title: Madagascar Marks One Year Since Uprising As Russia's Influence Grows
summary: _Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through
content:
_Madagascar marks one year on Saturday since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following weeks of youth-led protests that brought down elected president Andry Rajoelina. Over the past year, Russian influence has grown through closer military ties and weapons deliveries, while researchers have identified Moscow's interest in a strategic Indian Ocean port. Many of the political reforms demanded by protesters, however, remain unfinished._

Randrianirina was sworn in as president of the Refoundation of Madagascar on 17 October 2025, after a month of Gen Z protests demanding water, electricity, justice and transparency culminated in the ousting of Rajoelina.

[Russia](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/russia/) was quick to engage with the new leadership. Just four days after taking office, Randrianirina met the Russian ambassador in the Malagasy capital, [Antananarivo](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/antananarivo/).

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/) for the latest headlines

What followed was a rapid expansion of Moscow's presence on the island, researchers say.

An investigation published last month by [All Eyes On Wagner](https://alleyesonwagner.org/), a project that tracks Russian influence and security operations, traced the development of military, political and economic networks in [Madagascar](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/madagascar/) in the months after Randrianirina's inauguration.

"Madagascar has historical ties with Russia," explained Lou Osborn, co-author of the report.

"And Russia has had a discreet foothold on the island since the 2018 elections. But what is very striking is the speed with which the GRU [Russian military intelligence] has extended its networks in the country, through Africa Corps, African Initiative and various other activities."

[A year after Madagascar's Gen Z protests and Rajoelina's ouster, little promised change](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20261012-a-year-after-madagascar-s-gen-z-protests-and-rajoelina-s-ouster-little-promised-change)

A lightning offensive

The Russian presence soon became more concrete.

On 20 December 2025, two months after Randrianirina took office, a flight carrying 40 men led by Russian intelligence general [Andrey Averyanov](https://www.opensanctions.org/entities/Q100742758/) landed in Madagascar.

The investigation cites information collected by the Russian investigative unit of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. Averyanov is described by the researchers as the suspected supervisor of Africa Corps, the Russian paramilitary organisation that succeeded the Wagner group.

Malagasy authorities confirmed that same month that Africa Corps instructors were in the country training its military.

Then came the equipment. Helicopters, tanks, trucks, drones and rifles arrived in multiple shipments presented as donations, with deliveries continuing until April, the researchers said.

Averyanov also appeared at increasingly senior levels of the relationship.

In February, he was seen at a meeting in [Moscow](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/moscow/) between Russia's deputy prime minister and Madagascar's armed forces minister. Two weeks later, he was part of the delegation that welcomed Randrianirina on an official visit to the Russian capital.

The push has gone beyond military cooperation. Alongside Africa Corps, the researchers point to African Initiative, a Russian news agency with links to the state, as a key part of Moscow's influence campaign in Madagascar.

The agency has sought to reach young people through prizes and sporting events. It has also supported local media in exchange for coverage of Russian-Malagasy relations and organised trips to Moscow for media figures and influencers.

[Madagascar's wave of disappearances exposes 'deeper institutional failings'](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260720-madagascar-s-wave-of-disappearances-exposes-deeper-institutional-failings)

Influence at the top

Russia has also developed ties with senior Malagasy figures, including members of the political establishment who have remained influential despite last year's change of power, the investigation found.

"We are seeing figures from the old guard return," Osborn said. "These people have gained influence. And for some of them there is a kind of opportunism in playing the Russian card."

Among them is National Assembly speaker Siteny Randrianasoloniaiko, whom the investigation identifies as Moscow's most prominent supporter in Madagascar.

His connections with Russia have been fostered through his role as president of the African Judo Union. He confirmed the arrival of Africa Corps personnel and has spoken frequently about cooperation between the two countries.

Prime Minister Mamitiana Rajaonarison is also described as pro-Russian. A former head of Samifin, Madagascar's financial intelligence unit, he was involved in negotiations with Sber, Russia's main bank, which is under international sanctions, the investigation said.

Ny Hasina Andriamanjato, meanwhile, is a Russian-speaking former foreign minister whom the investigation places in former president Rajoelina's circle. He was appointed Madagascar's ambassador to Russia in May.

[Madagascar charts new course with France, after meeting Putin in Moscow](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20260225-madagascar-charts-a-new-course-with-france-after-putin-meeting-in-moscow)

Gateway to the Indian Ocean

Sitting at the entrance to the Mozambique Channel, Madagascar offers access to shipping routes linking southern Africa, the [Middle East](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/middle-east/) and the [Indian Ocean](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/indian-ocean/).

"Madagascar can give the Russians a sought-after access point to the Indian Ocean," Osborn said. "Potential access for their shadow fleet [of ships used to evade Western sanctions]."

Much of the attention has centred on the port of Antsiranana, also known as Diego-Suarez, at Madagascar's northern tip. A Russian delegation visited in April, and the following month Madagascar and Russia announced a joint economic zone, with fuel storage as its first project.

The authors of the investigation say the port's potential goes much further. They compare Diego-Suarez with Tartus, Russia's naval base in [Syria](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/syria/), arguing that its location could eventually make it a major military and economic logistics hub.

But the interest is not only military. "They are building a logistics platform and an information platform in Madagascar, but also setting up financial infrastructure, which is developing as in [Togo](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/togo/), with the A7 system," Osborn said.

A7 is a Russian cross-border payments network designed to allow international transactions outside conventional Western banking channels. The investigation says such a system could be used in Madagascar to finance arms deliveries, economic projects, security services and other areas of Russian cooperation.

Osborn sees a pattern in which Africa Corps and Russian military intelligence establish a foothold first, with the financial infrastructure following close behind to support business, potential arms sales and payments to Russian personnel.

"It didn't happen like that in [Mali](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/mali/), [Burkina Faso](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/burkina-faso/) or [Niger](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/niger/)," she said. "In fact, we hadn't seen Russia so firmly rooted since the [Central African Republic](https://www.rfi.fr/en/tag/central-african-republic/)."

[How Moscow is reinventing its influence machine across Africa](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20250819-how-moscow-is-reinventing-its-influence-machine-across-africa)

New words, old practices

Meanwhile, questions remain over how much has changed for the people of Madagascar. The authorities that emerged from last year's uprising have themselves faced accusations of repressing Gen Z activists, six of whom were arrested in April.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

"There has certainly been a political break since the previous regime fell," political scientist Ketakandriana Rafitoson, vice-chair of anti-corruption organisation Transparency International, told RFI. "But I would say the vocabulary has changed more than the practices."

Randrianirina's administration has promised to overhaul the state, strengthen national sovereignty and forge a new relationship with citizens. But Rafitoson argues that the concentration of power, weak checks and balances, impunity and a lack of transparency persist.

"That is why today I would speak of a real political revolution, but an institutional 'refoundation' that remains largely unfinished."

[Africa's Gen Z unrest shows 'generational divide' between people and politicians](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20251205-africa-s-gen-z-unrest-shows-generational-divide-between-people-and-politicians)

While changing political practices built up over decades can take time, Rafitoson said this could not justify a lack of progress. "The victims of last year's violence are still waiting for justice," she said.

For [the young people who drove the protests](https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20251101-madagascar-s-gen-z-uprising-as-told-by-three-young-protesters), there has been one significant shift. Gen Z has established itself as a political force capable of mobilising, shaping its own message and putting issues on the national agenda, Rafitoson said.

"But being heard does not yet mean having power."

Some young activists now speak of betrayal as they see practices they fought against beginning to reappear. That frustration is also rooted in how little influence they have gained since helping force political change, Rafitoson said.

"They were powerful enough to help bring down a regime, but they have not gained the same influence over decision-making in the transition."

_This article draws on reporting from [this story](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260924-madagascar-comment-la-russie-cherche-%C3%A0-s-imposer-dans-l-oc%C3%A9an-indien) and [this interview](https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-afrique-midi/20260925-un-an-apr%C3%A8s-l-insurrection-%C3%A0-madagascar-une-r%C3%A9volution-r%C3%A9elle-mais-une-refondation-institutionnelle-inachev%C3%A9e) by RFI's French service._

### Preventing the Next World War

Robert Peters & Wilson Beaver• RealClearDefense• October 15, 2026

It’s clear from the increasingly bellicose actions of the People’s Republic of China that the PRC seeks to return to its self-appointed role as the “Middle Kingdom” at the center of the world. To do this it must supplant the United States, both economically and militarily, by becoming the preeminent power on the world stage—at which point it will be able to rewrite the rules of the existing world order established by America after World War II.

### Why Taiwan May Need To Reconsider the Ultimate Deterrent

Lasse de Graaf• RealClearDefense• October 12, 2026

For decades, Taipei’s security has leaned on three pillars: its relationship with the United States, the Taiwanese armed forces, and the island’s renowned ‘silicon shield.’ However, as the global order shifts, the reliability of these safeguards is becoming increasingly uncertain. Decades after Taiwan ended its clandestine nuclear weapons program in 1988, the changing geopolitical environment raises questions on whether Taipei should reconsider nuclear deterrence.

The growing uncertainty surrounding U.S.-Taiwan relations is a clear warning sign for Taipei. Unlike South Korea and Japan, Taiwan lacks a formalized military alliance with Washington. Instead, U.S. policy toward Taiwan has traditionally rested on the Taiwan Relations Act of 1979 and a policy of strategic ambiguity. For Taipei this policy has been a double-edged sword, on the one hand serving as a potent deterrent by forcing China to weigh the high risk of a U.S. kinetic intervention without knowing the exact threshold or scale of that response, but simultaneously creating uncertainty for Taiwan’s strategic planning.

### Deterrence on Best Efforts: When Taiwan's Arms Come Without a Guaranteed Delivery Date

Hong-Yu Harper Chen• RealClearDefense• October 9, 2026

Taiwan’s arms contracts treat delivery dates as estimates, and Congress should require Washington to account for the major slips.

At a defense forum in Taipei in September, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey[said](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10879531)that the hold on a $14 billion Taiwan arms package is “definitely affecting the business,” and that “as long as that’s stuck, you don’t have continued forward progress in other areas.” He had raised it, he said, with the President. That is a hold before any sale. A different problem starts after Taiwan signs a sale agreement and waits for delivery. The standard terms in those agreements do not, as a rule, guarantee a delivery date, and if a date slips, any dispute over it goes to consultation between the two governments.

### Australia's Security Race in the South Pacific

Graeme Dobell• RealClearDefense• October 7, 2026

Waging a “permanent contest” with China in the South Pacific, Australia is building new alliances and a new security system. Treaties signed with Island states are driven by fear and shock in Canberra, yet also by a sense of responsibility — plus a determination to be the top regional power.

Prone to amnesia about its permanent Pacific interests, Australia has been given a jolting reminder by the permanent contest with China. content:
## 矽谷这座城市垃圾太臭居民受不了 就让科技来帮忙

图像来源，The Mercury News via Getty Images

图像加注文字，纽比岛垃圾掩埋场的营运方已被命令采取措施解决异味问题。

*       *   Author, 克里斯·马歇尔（Chris Marshall）
    *   Role, BBC科技记者

*   Published 2026年10月19日凌晨12点08分

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

美国加州矽谷（Silicon Valley；硅谷）科技中心的富裕城市米尔皮塔斯（Milpitas；苗必达）有个臭味问题。

数十年来，居民不得不忍受从工业场所飘来的难闻气味，其中包括一座占地342英亩的垃圾掩埋场。

“我刚搬来这里时，超过十年都不能开窗，”住在垃圾场约半英里外的科技公司工程师邝家玲（Chia-Ling Kong）说。

近年情况虽有改善，但邝家玲说她和邻居仍必须每天应付大约“两三小时的恶臭”。

或许符合矽谷的特质，这个社区把希望寄托在科技上。

当地当局已下令纽比岛（Newby Island）垃圾掩埋场的营运商使用无人机并安装监测器，以利系统性地追踪与测量造成恶臭的化学物质。掩埋场也被要求自动化收集造成气味的垃圾气体。

邝小姐对透过数据驱动的科学方法持乐观态度。她说：“希望透过这种持续监测，能更容易在问题刚开始时就精准定位。”

垃圾场营运商表示，他们致力于安全营运并保护空气品质。

就像在米尔皮塔斯，邝家玲参与公民反臭味运动一样，世界各地的社区也因恶臭让日常生活变得痛苦而发起抗议。有时是垃圾场，有时是污水处理厂，或是散发臭味的工厂。

当投诉不断累积时，解决问题并不总是简单。

而且，许多国家没有规范如何管理气味的法规。

譬如，美国环境保护署（Environmental Protection Agency, EPA）并不把环境臭味视为污染物来规范，让州与地方政府得处理这个问题。

城市扩张往往是问题的一部分，让社区更接近那些历史上可能被隔离在远处的臭味设施。

这创造了对监测与预防气味技术的更多需求。气味顾问迈克尔·布尔（Micheal Bull）对BBC说，人们越来越关注邻里的臭味。

他指出：“愈来愈多开发项目建在产生异味设施的附近⋯⋯随着土地变得更有价值，也出现更多填充式开发。”

他谈的是在英国的经验，但世界许多地方情况类似。

用来对付工业臭味的技术大致分为三类：吸收气味，透过化学反应转化成较不臭的物质，或烧掉它们。

处理工业气味的专家向BBC表示，最好的技术若正确使用，可去除90%或更多造成气味的目标化合物。

但这可能很昂贵，有些营运商选择更简单、便宜的解决方案。包括透过喷洒大量除臭剂来掩盖垃圾场或污水处理的气味。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，垃圾场的恶臭是最难解决的问题之一。

不过，记者联系的气味专家对这种工业规模空气清新剂的有效性持怀疑态度。

“在我看来，它们不太可能改变气味，”布尔把这些空气清新剂比作衣物柔软精。

此外，根据西班牙环境顾问迪亚兹（Carlos Diaz的）说法，废弃物场址的恶臭——投诉的常见原因——是最臭且最难解决的之一。他强调：“垃圾掩埋场很难处理，因为表面非常大。”

至少在某些地方，科技正在真正发挥作用。

譬如爱荷华州艾奥瓦州（Iowa；爱荷华／衣阿华）得梅因（Des Moines）的居民长期抱怨所谓的“城东臭味”（Eastside Funk），居民报告这种腐臭气味会飘过城市部分地区。

市政府委托的研究显示，三家工业肉品公司是元凶之一。

“方圆10英里（16.09公里）范围内大约有50万人，”在邻里服务部门工作的道尔顿·雅各布斯（Dalton Jacobus）向BBC说。他又说：“如果风向不对，10万人可能就处在那个气味羽流（Odor Plume）的中心。”

当局现在每年花费约24万美元（161万元人民币；779万元新台币）在追踪臭味的技术上，以便采取行动。他告诉BBC：“我们想做的是在我们怀疑排放气味的设施周围建立一圈气味监测器。”

这些监测器测量空气中化学化合物的浓度，与气象站结合，根据风向模式提供每个设施排放浓度的即时数据。

雅各布斯解释，这结束了每次气味引发投诉时互相指责谁该负责的情况。“现在我们可以相当有把握地说：‘这次气味事件确实来自你们的设施，当时发生了什么？’”

同时，得梅因一些被指控造成难闻气味的场址已花费数百万美元，升级自己的气味控制系统。

在得梅因经营肉品加工的史密斯菲尔德食品公司（Smithfield Foods）表示，已投资200万美元安装再生式热氧化器，摧毁与恶臭相关的化学物质。即便如此，该公司表示不认为自己是气味投诉的来源。

在安装监测器之前——部分当地公司协助出资——得梅因的官员会开车到投诉来源去闻空气。

图像来源，Kunak

图像加注文字，在得梅因，当局安装了“电子鼻”来精确定位异味。

依靠人类鼻子来嗅出工业气味仍很常见。

Kunak公司向得梅因供应了监测器。该公司的克劳蒂亚·巴里奥斯·奥布雷贡（Claudia Barrios Obregón）对BBC说：“目前，城市控制或测量气味的方式是嗅觉测定法：一个人类小组测量并给出对气味的意见。但这并不那么现实。”

这家西班牙公司的监测器是所谓“电子鼻”的例子，让侦测气味更容易。

无论使用什么技术，要让每个人都满意可能很难，因为气味非常主观。

“不幸的是，一般规则是我们觉得气味越难闻，我们对它就越敏感，”瑞典斯德哥尔摩卡罗林斯卡学院（Karolinska Institute）气味科学教授林德史东（Prof Johan Lundström）说。

*       *   Author, 杰克·伯吉斯（Jack Burgess）

*   Published 7 小时前

*   阅读时间: 3 分钟

法国总统马克龙（Emmanuel Macron；马克宏）呼吁民众保持“冷静与秩序”（calm and order）。此前，周六大规模示威演变成暴动和抢势，周日巴黎部分地区仍持续出现混乱情况。

马克龙在爱丽舍宫（Elysée Palace；总统府）发表全国讲话时警告参与骚乱者不要“进一步升级”，并表示：“我们所有人都感到愤怒和羞愧。”

约55万名示威者走上街头，参与主要以和平方式进行的抗议活动，诉求包括不满燃油价格上涨、生活成本高企，以及教育等公共服务质素恶化。

马克龙表示，必须区分示威者提出的“合理诉求”，以及那些“进行破坏、打砸和抢掠的人”。

根据法国内政部数据，警方至今已拘捕约2,400人。

马克龙表示，眼前出现的“失控”暴力行为“毫无正当理由”，并强调涉事者将被追究法律责任。

在巴黎、马赛及其他城镇和城市，大批暴动者走上街头，其中部分人身穿黑衣、戴上口罩及巴拉克拉瓦头套（balaclava）。部分人士更纵火焚烧汽车和建筑物。

视频加注文字，“非常令人痛心”：法国历史悠久的市政厅被纵火焚毁，居民震惊不已（英文影片）

周日，巴黎部分地区及里昂（Lyon）仍发生较小规模的抢掠事件及警民冲突。

法新社（AFP）报道，警方在巴黎向数百人施放催泪气体及震撼弹，示威者再次向警方投掷瓶子和石块。

随着这场动乱演变成法国现代史上最严重的社会骚乱之一，全国多个城市周日开始面对其造成的后果。

在利摩日（Limoges），当地一座建于19世纪、装饰华丽的市政厅于周六遭暴动者纵火焚烧，建筑严重损毁。当大火蔓延后，市政厅的钟楼和屋顶相继倒塌。

图像来源，Mairie de Limoge

图像加注文字，周日早上利摩日市政厅内部的受损状况

在这座满目疮痍的建筑物旁，名叫安妮丝（Annèyse）的居民说：

“这真的令人非常难过。我认为，仅仅因为对政府感到愤怒，就去破坏历史建筑是很自私的行为。这伤害的是所有人。”

自称热拉尔（Gerrard）的一名男子说：“这太糟糕，也太难以置信了。我们非常难过，我想要想恢复原貌需要很长时间。”

在巴黎，周日清晨可见商店东主清理散落一地的大块玻璃碎片，而垃圾车则在部分主要街道上清运瓦砾。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，周日，巴黎发生小规模骚乱，有人纵火，商店遭到抢劫。

巴黎、马赛（Marseille）、里尔（Lille）以及其他多个地区均发生大规模抢掠事件。

马克龙表示，各地省长（prefects）和市长将制定措施，以保护商店及公共建筑物。

总统还表示，警方应对示威的情况将“完全透明”。

在周末期间，警方曾向群众发射催泪气体及出动水炮车，而在多个地方亦有人目击防暴警察以警棍殴打示威者。

法国内政部表示，周六共有约1,000名警员受伤，其中7人伤势严重。

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，周日，一名男子在巴黎试图扑灭一场火灾。

上个月开始的学生抗议活动，在工会成员和其他反政府团体加入后，于周六显著升级。

法国政界的反应凸显了国家深刻的政治分歧。在法国准备迎接4月大选之际，极右翼与极左翼势力可能正面交锋。

法国内政部长洛朗·努涅斯（Laurent Nuñez）表示，虽然示威是基本权利，但有“数千名极左翼人士”实施了“令人发指的行为”，并蓄意将公共建筑作为攻击目标，同时与警方对抗。

他说，其后又有一批“不法分子（delinquents）”加入，在法国多个城市抢掠及破坏大量商舖。

极左翼政党“不屈法国”（La France Insoumise）领袖让-吕克·梅朗雄（Jean-Luc Mélenchon）则在社交媒体上猛烈批评努涅斯及警方高层。

他表示，他们在处理示威活动上“表现出彻底的无能”，并称他们是“制造有组织混乱的专家”。

另一方面，极右翼国民联盟（National Rally）领袖马琳·勒庞（Marine Le Pen）谴责有人利用民众的不满情绪，并批评“鼓励暴力的政治力量”藉此煽动局势。

# 乌克兰钢企老板称：欧盟对华关税殃及本国

图像来源，Getty Images

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 迈克尔·瑞斯（Michael Race）
    *   Role, BBC商业记者

     和
    *   Author, 西蒙·杰克（Simon Jack）
    *   Role, BBC商业编辑

*   Published 6 小时前
*   阅读时间: 2 分钟

乌克兰最大钢铁企业之一的负责人呼吁欧盟取消对乌克兰产品的进口限制，指乌克兰被“一并捆绑”进了旨在遏制来自中国等地廉价进口产品的措施之中。

美提投资集团（Metinvest）行政总裁尤里·雷任科夫（Yuriy Ryzhenkov）向BBC表示，欧盟近期对进口钢铁征收的关税“不公平”，是“完全没有考虑到乌克兰处境”而出台的措施。

他说，希望欧盟“至少作出例外安排”，让乌克兰钢铁产品能够进入欧盟市场。

欧盟委员会（European Commission）发言人则表示，欧盟在制定钢铁政策时，“已考虑到乌克兰面临的困难处境”。

欧盟近期收紧钢铁进口限制，以保护成员国钢铁制造商。

根据新措施，每年可免税进入欧盟市场的钢铁总量上限被设定为1,830万吨，较2024年水平减少47%。

虽然政策设有部分国别配额，但整体目的在于削减钢铁进口量，因为欧盟成员国的钢铁企业正难以与来自中国和土耳其等地的廉价进口钢铁竞争。

尽管欧盟与乌克兰之间已签订自由贸易协定（FTA），但该协定并不妨碍欧盟另行实施贸易保护措施。

雷任科夫表示：“乌克兰在这些措施中被一并纳入，却完全没有考虑到乌克兰目前所处的情况。”他指的是持续中的俄乌战争。

他表示：“进入欧洲市场对我们的生存至关重要。”

“欧盟当局实施的这些限制措施，并没有提供帮助。”

“我认为，乌克兰与其他所有向欧盟出口钢铁的国家被同等对待，是不公平的。”

乌克兰钢铁业估计，对欧盟的钢铁出口最终可能下跌约50%至60%。

欧盟方面则表示，专门为乌克兰设立的钢铁配额仍能确保乌克兰钢铁出口欧盟，但承认有关水平“低于过去数年”。

其发言人说：“即使在战争期间，乌克兰仍是欧盟重要的钢铁出口来源。”

发言人又补充，欧盟已向受影响最大的供应方提供“补偿安排”，当中包括乌克兰。

图像加注文字，美提投资集团行政总裁尤里·雷任科夫表示，欧盟钢铁配额对乌克兰“不公平”

钢铁产品是乌克兰经济的重要支柱。在俄罗斯于2022年全面入侵乌克兰之前，冶金和采矿业约占乌克兰国民收入的10%，并贡献约三分之一出口收入，而欧盟则是其最大的客户。

然而，持续不断的俄军轰炸已重创这个产业。

雷任科夫表示，自2022年战争爆发以来，乌克兰所有钢铁厂都曾遭受攻击，而最近空袭更是“明显加剧”。

他补充说，在9月份的某个时候，乌克兰更出现约150年来首次“一吨钢铁也没有生产出来”的情况。

自战争爆发以来，美提投资集团已有近800名员工丧生。

雷任科夫表示，公司已改善钢铁厂内可供员工在空袭期间避难的掩护设施。

他说：“我们唯一能做的，就是制定程序保障员工安全，遵守这些程序，并尽可能降低风险。”

“遗憾的是，你不可能把整座钢铁厂都覆盖起来，令它完全免受破坏。”

雷任科夫表示，他预计即将到来的冬季将是“我们历史上最艰难的冬天之一”。

他说：“我们正面对非常严峻的处境。除了欧盟市场之外，我们几乎没有物流条件进入其他市场，而如今可供进入的市场又被削减了60%，这无助于整个产业生存下去。”

# 中国三季度增长4.5%，但冷热不均：9月出口暴增三成，楼市新开工面积跌25%

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2026年3月16日，工人在江苏奥达康复合材料有限公司的车间里生产供出口的羽毛球拍，地点位于中国江苏省宿迁市。

Published 1 小时前

阅读时间: 4 分钟

中国国家统计局公布，2026年第三季度国内生产总值（GDP）同比增长4.5，比第二季度的4.3%回升0.2个百分点。这使前三季度累计增长4.6%，落在全年4.5%至5%的目标区间内。

星期一（10月19日）出炉的这一结果略胜于外界判断：路透社调查的50位经济学家预测均值为4.4%，财新调查的九家国内外机构均值也是4.4%，实际数字都高于预期。

宏观数据之外，普通人的生活感受上可能“冷热不均”：9月的汽油价格同比上涨16.6%；受人工智能热潮推动，数据存储设备价格同比涨46.7%，计算机涨21.8%，手机涨14.9%。而菜市场的猪肉，反而比去年便宜了一成多。

分析师普遍对BBC指出，当前经济呈现“外热内冷”：出口和高端制造撑住了增长，国内消费、投资和房地产市场仍然偏弱。他们同时提醒，依赖单一外需引擎的风险正在累积，北京的刺激空间有限，未必愿意、也未必有能力在这个时点大举加码。

## 谁在拉动，谁在拖累

撑住第三季度的是出口和高端制造。

出口的势头颇为显著：三季度整体出口增长28.4%，比上半年的17.5%明显加快，9月单月按美元计增长36.3%。

穆迪分析（Moody's Analytics）在给BBC中文的评论中说，这次回升的主要推手是出口。但同时指出：中国经济目前依赖单一的外部增长引擎，但这个引擎也出现了早期疲态。

不过出口的强劲，有相当一部分靠价格支撑。以9月为例，集成电路出口额同比增长136%，出口均价上涨133.7%，出口数量只微增1%，钱主要赚在了涨价上。

此外，前三季度，高技术制造业增加值同比增长14.3%，接近整体工业5.3%增速的三倍；3D打印设备、锂离子电池、工业机器人的产量分别增长62.5%、39.5%和29.1%。

但问题在于，“这种强劲暂时还没有真正传导到家庭消费和国内投资上”，牛津经济研究院高级经济学家余惠悦（Sheana Yue）向BBC表示，如果消费和投资持续疲弱，即使三季度GDP有所加快，“我们也会非常谨慎，不会轻易把它解读为经济全面复苏的证据”。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2026年1月12日，中国山东省青岛市，一台人形机器人在青岛人形机器人数据采集训练场学习零部件分拣。

如余惠悦所言，房地产仍在深度调整：前三季度房地产开发投资同比下降20.6%，降幅比上半年的18%更大，新开工面积下降近25%。穆迪提醒，新开工跌幅如此之大，意味着建筑活动在未来数月将持续收缩，进而拖累水泥、钢铁、家电等上下游产业。

投资整体在收缩。前三季度固定资产投资同比下降7.2%，比上半年的5.7%降幅更深；即使扣除房地产开发投资，仍下降4.2%。

消费有所回暖，但幅度有限。9月社会消费品零售总额同比增长1.1%，好于8月的0.4%。法国外贸银行（Natixis）亚太区首席经济学家艾西亚（Alicia García-Herrero）向BBC表示，对一个增长4.5%的经济体而言，零售只增长1.1%“仍然偏低”，这次回升“更多是因为之前的基数太低”。

服务业撑起了另外半边天：前三季度增加值增长5.2%，占经济比重接近60%，是增长的最大贡献者。但按穆迪的拆解，这部分增长由信息技术和商业服务带动，与居民日常消费关系不大。

## 政策为何不再加码

这样的成绩单下，官方定调积极。中国国家统计局副局长兼新闻发言人毛盛勇，星期一在国务院新闻办公室的发布会上说，前三季度4.6%的累计增速在全球主要经济体中保持领先，5.7万亿元人民币（8,533亿美元；27.7兆元新台币）的经济增量是过去五年同期最大。在中东冲突、国际油价上涨对全球增长影响加大的背景下，这一结果“来之不易、难能可贵”。

政策并非没有动作。9月底以来，中国人民银行（央行）下调了抵押补充贷款利率，扩大了面向科技和民营企业的再贷款额度；财政部等部门推出首套房购房者的按揭利息补贴；地方政府也被允许动用尚未使用的发债额度。

穆迪对这套动作的判断是，它们“依靠的是向特定借款人提供更便宜的信贷，而非直接广泛支持消费，因此难以迅速提振国内支出”。

艾西亚则说：政府这一轮的重点是基础设施而不是消费，这解释了为什么北京不愿在发放消费券上做更多文章。在她看来，政府对9月1.1%的零售增长“大概是满意的”，这个数字不高，但足以成为（政府）不再加码政策力度的理由。

她还把因素引向财政空间本身。她说，全世界都在问同一个问题：中国还有多少财政空间？而北京对自身的财政状况非常谨慎，“因为很清楚，能用上的空间已经非常有限了”。

图像来源，Getty Images

图像加注文字，2025年4月11日，在中国江苏省连云港市，工人在一家玩具公司的生产线上生产销往“一带一路”沿线国家的毛绒玩具。

## 唯一的引擎也在承压

但正在强劲拉动经济的出口和高端制造，未来也面临不确定性。

今年前8个月，全球存储芯片的新增营收里，涨价贡献了85%，出货量只贡献了15%。穆迪认为这是一处明显的转折点风险：由价格驱动的繁荣可以迅速逆转，一旦价格掉头，出口引擎就会受到冲击。

另一头是贸易壁垒。一年前在釜山与华盛顿达成的休战协议，目前只延长至明年1月10日，距离到期不足三个月。欧盟方面，10月15日的欧盟领导人峰会上，欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩把化工和工业机械列为需要优先保护的行业，建议尽快研究进口配额、关税等保障措施；法国和德国还联合提出一项“紧急切断开关”机制，允许欧盟在认定市场扭曲时迅速限制相关企业进入。该机制尚未获批。

中国国内也有一个正在成型的隐患。艾西亚把通缩问题摆到了台面上：尽管全球油价高企，中国通胀率依然很低，国内激烈的市场竞争正在形成一种“结构性通缩”。她认为这个风险真实存在，而要走出通缩需要大规模刺激，问题恰恰在于刺激需要空间。

至于前景，穆迪的最可能情形是，北京不会推出大规模新刺激，而是继续以定向工具维持增长，2026年国内生产总值增长4.6%：完成目标的方式将更加单调，即靠出口一项对冲内需的疲软。

余惠悦预计，中国的出口顺差还会继续扩大，真正的挑战在于关税等外部环境如何演变，以及中国与主要经济体关系的前景。这与艾西亚的判断一致：观察接下来的中国经济，不能只看增速的标题，更要看这个增速由什么构成。

# Finance minister leads Taiwan delegation to APEC meeting in Hong Kong

Taiwan's Ministry of Finance. CNA file photo

Taipei, Oct. 19 (CNA) Finance Minister Chuang Tsui-yun (莊翠雲) is leading a delegation to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) finance ministers' meeting in Hong Kong, which begins Tuesday, according to the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

The delegation includes Financial Supervisory Commission Vice Chairman Chen Yen-liang (陳彥良) and other financial officials, the MOF said in a press release on Sunday.

When the two-day meeting starts Tuesday, representatives from the participating APEC economies will discuss global and regional economic and financial outlook, among other issues, the ministry said.

The delegates will also hold discussions with representatives from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), and the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC), the MOF said.

At the meeting, Chuang and her delegation will share Taiwan's policy experience in promoting economic growth, easing household burdens, and improving tax administration, including through the use of artificial intelligence, according to the finance ministry.

Finance Minister Chuang Tsui-yun. CNA file photo

The delegation will also discuss Taiwan's plans to encourage private investment in digital infrastructure, as well as its efforts to promote financial innovation and financial inclusion, the MOF said.

The ministry said Taiwan will continue to participate in regional financial policy discussions and strengthen cooperation with other APEC economies to promote economic resilience and sustainable growth in the Asia-Pacific region.

Taiwan participates in APEC as a full member under the name "Chinese Taipei."

This year's APEC meeting, themed "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," includes some preliminary discussions on Monday.

(By Su Ssu-yun and Ko Lin)

Synopsis

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defence has reported heightened military activity from China around the island recently. Five Chinese military aircraft, six naval vessels, and nine official ships were detected until early Monday. This follows multiple incursions by Chinese military aircraft and vessels into Taiwan's Air Defence Identification Zone. Taiwanese armed forces have been actively monitoring and responding to these developments as tensions escalate.

Taiwan detects 5 PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels operating around island

Taipei: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defence detected five Chinese military aircraft, six naval vessels, and nine official ships operating around the island until 6 AM (local time) on Monday.

According to a security update released by the defence ministry in a post on X, three of the five detected aircraft crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait and breached Taiwan's northern, central, and southwestern Air Defence Identification Zone (ADIZ).

"5 sorties of PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships operating around Taiwan detected up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) today," Taiwan's Ministry of National Defence stated, adding, "3 out of 5 sorties crossed the median line and entered Taiwan's northern, central and southwestern part ADIZ."

# 王赫：債務利息支出大於新增GDP 中共危險

[![Image 6: 王赫：債務利息支出大於新增GDP 中共危險](https://www.epochtimes.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fi.epochtimes.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F10%2Fid14872028-4560150881.jpeg&w=1200&q=75)](https://i.epochtimes.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/id14872028-4560150881.jpeg)

示意圖。最新研究顯示，中國不斷增加的債務令人警惕。 (Johannes Eisele/AFP/Getty Images)

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=www.epochtimes.com%2Fb5%2F26%2F10%2F18%2Fn14872024.htm)[](https://line.me/R/msg/text/?Check%20this%20out%3A%20www.epochtimes.com%2Fb5%2F26%2F10%2F18%2Fn14872024.htm%3FopenExternalBrowser%3D1)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Check%20this%20out!&via=dajiyuan&url=www.epochtimes.com%2Fb5%2F26%2F10%2F18%2Fn14872024.htm)[](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/26/10/18/n14872024.htm#)[](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/26/10/18/n14872024.htm#)[](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/26/10/18/n14872024.htm)[](https://www.epochtimes.com/gb/26/10/18/n14872024.htm)

【大紀元2026年10月18日訊】中共財政報表極其複雜，不僅有官方正式的「四本帳」，還有「二財政」、「准財政」等。其真實、全部債務，讓人眼花繚亂（也是當局有意不讓人看懂）。本文嘗試捋一捋，以2025年為例，且只討論債務利息支出，不談償還本金，因為付息都已困難，償還本金就更不可能、只能「借新還舊」苟且而已。

在捋之前，先計算一下官方數據中的中國2025年新增GDP（且不論其真假）。2024年GDP，經最終核實為1,348,066億元；2025年全年初步核算為1,401,879億元，較2024年增加53,813 億元。這個數據是全文比較的基準。

## （一）法定顯性政府債付息（中央國債+地方一般債+地方專項債）

（1）中央政府國債付息為8,193.61億元，其中，中央政府國內債務付息支出8,110.43 億元（比上年增長8.0%），中央政府國外債務付息支出83.18 億元。（2）地方政府一般債券付息為5,292.87億元。（數據源自2025年全國一般公共預算決算表）

（1）+（2）合計13,486.48億元。這就是官方常規口徑公布的政府債務付息支出。但還有大頭在後面。

（3）地方政府專項債：9,550.13億元。根據財政部2025年12月地方政府債券還本付息情況，全國地方政府債券在2025年全年累計支付利息14,843億元。扣除列在一般預算裡的一般債利息5,292.87億後，剩下的9,550.13億全部在「政府性基金預算」中由土地出讓金和項目收益去消化。它雖然不顯示在常規的「債務付息支出」科目中，但它也屬於法定的顯性的政府債務付息。

小結：2025年法定顯性債務總利息為23,041.13億元，而非13,491億元。對應的債務規模：截止2025年末，國債餘額41.2萬億元，地方政府法定債務餘額54.8萬億元（其中一般債務餘額17.5萬億元、專項債務餘額37.3萬億元）。

## （二）地方政府隱性債務付息

中共地方政府隱性債務問題非常繁雜，可分為城投債務和非城投債務，城投債務是主體。估測2023年末至2024年底，城投債務約60萬億至68萬億元，非城投債務10萬億至15萬億，合計70萬億至83萬億。

其中，獲得中央承認的地方政府隱性債務，只是極小一部分（14.3萬億），絕大部分中央不承認，認為它是由借款者作為獨立企業/單位自主承擔的債務，是經營性債務（當然，IMF等並不接受這種說法，因為融資主要投向城市公用事業）。

根據各券商固收團隊對部分省份穿透審計樣本的測算，在中央承認的地方政府隱性債務（14.3萬億）中，非城投類隱性債務占比大約在15%至25%，也就是在2.145萬億至3.575萬億之間，其餘的是城投債務。

自2015年後，中共財政部和國家審計署不再公開城投的總債務數據。金融市場主要通過市場上公開發行過債券（如中票、短融、企業債）的城投公司（約3,000至4,000家），進行「全樣本掃描」，這些平台由於有發債合規要求，必須定期披露資產負債表。把這些平台財報裡的「短期借款」「長期借款」「應付債券」「一年內到期的非流動負債」以及「長期應付款（往往包含非標、信託）」全部相加，計算出城投總有息負債規模（約60萬億至68萬億元）。拆解城投平台的有息負債，行業長期的統計共識是，銀行貸款占比通常在60%上下，城投債占比約23%至25%，非標及其它占比約15%。

**（1）中央承認的地方政府隱性債務的利息支出：約4,600億元**

當局宣稱：2023年末，經過逐個項目甄別、逐級審核上報，全國隱性債務餘額為14.3萬億元；2024年通過「增加地方政府債務限額置換存量隱性債務」方案，截至2025年末，已大幅壓降至6.5萬億元，兩年間累計減少了7.8萬億元。（1）根據財政部在國新辦發布會等渠道披露的數據，地方隱性債務置換前的平均年化綜合利息成本大約在4.5%至7%之間；（2）2025年隱債規模的平均占用額約為8.5萬億元（2024年末約10.5萬億元 + 2025年末6.5萬億元，再除以 2）；（3）若按5.5%的保守平均綜合利率測算，2025年地方政府對這部分尚未被置換或正在置換中的存量隱性債務，仍需實際支付的利息額4,600億元。

**（2）城投債券付息：約4,800億元。**2025年公開發行存續的標準化城投債，中樞規模在15萬億左右；2025年信用債利差經歷劇烈震盪，城投標準化債券的平均發行和加權成本維持在3.2%左右。以此計算，利息為4,800億元。

**（3）城投平台經營性金融債務（約31萬億）付息：**約12,400億元**。**2025年，全國城投總有息負債中，未納入隱債、但實際上屬於基建和地方項目的銀行貸款規模約為31萬億元（剔除中央承認部分）。雖然央行連續下調LPR，但由於存量項目貸款展期和中西部高風險地區平台較高的風險溢價，城投平台銀行貸款的年化加權平均利率在4.0%左右。據此計算，2025年城投貸款總利息約12,400億元。

**（4）城投高息非標影子融資付息：約6,400億元。**前面說的城投債權，公開發行，屬於標準化融資，而信託/租賃/地方定向融資計劃等等，則屬於非標融資，利息高，屬於高位資金。根據粵開證券與標普研究模型，2025年未出清的全口徑非標影子資金池存量中樞在8萬億元左右，年化加權成本在8.0%左右，據此計算，2025年高息非標影子融資付息約6,400億元。

**（5）非城投地方政府隱性債務付息：約2,700億至4,200億元。**

城投平台外，還有許多種類的隱性債務，它們廣泛散落、隱藏在地方行政事業單位、普通國有企業、偽裝的項目合資公司以及對實體企業的工程欠款中。根據財政部以及國家審計署的甄別和通報，主要集中在以下五大核心領域：

A、PPP（政府和社會資本合作）項目中的「明股實債」；
B、違規的「政府購買服務」與延期付款；
C、政府引導基金、投資基金中的兜底承諾；
D、行政事業單位、公立醫院及學校的直接借款；
E、普通國有企業和民營企業的「墊資與欠款」。

它們的總規模有多大？沒有官方數據。經濟學家和券商固收研究機構通過「分項剝離法」和「應付帳款穿透法」倒推，2023年末至2024年底，宏觀估算區間為10萬億到15萬億：包括：全國企業應收帳款中的「政府拖欠款」（5萬億至8萬億元）；公立醫院與高校負債（2萬億至3萬億元）；被清理的民間定融與灰色財富產品（全國殘存規模估計在 2萬億至3萬億元）；偽裝的PPP與產業引導基金「暗債」（1萬億至2萬億元）。

2025年，由於全面啟動「10萬億一攬子化債」，估測非城投債務的整體存量被打掉接近一半，縮減至5萬億至6.4萬億元（剔除中央承認部分）。利息支出也暴跌，約2,700億至4,200億元。

**（6）小結：****全部的2025年地方政府隱性債務付息約30,900億元至32,400億元之間。**

截至2025年末，地方政府隱性債務規模：中央承認的6.5萬億元+標準化城投債存量餘額16.36萬億元+城投平台經營性金融債務約31萬億元+城投高息非標影子融資8萬億元+非城投地方政府隱性債務5萬億元至6.4萬億元，合計66.86萬億元至68.26萬億元。當然，這些都是大致估算，並不精確。

## 結語

根據上述，法定顯性政府債付息+地方政府隱性債付息，2025年政府債務付息為53,941億元至55,441億元之間，就已超過了2025年的新增GDP（53,813億元）。

這還沒包括複雜的中央隱性債務付息，諸如政策性金融債、PSL（抵押補充貸款）、國鐵集團的「准主權鐵道債與貸款」、國有大型銀行及AMC表內的「政策性不良資產與資本補充永續債」等等。

2025年政府債務付息為53,941億元至55,441億元之間。而（1）2025年全國一般公共預算收入216,045億元、全國政府性基金預算收入57,704億元，合計273,749億元，付息占比在20%上下；也就是說，中共廣義財政收入中，每5元錢就有約1元錢需要拿去付利息。（2）2025年全國一般公共預算支出287,395億元、全國政府性基金預算支出112,874億元，合計400,269億元，付息占比在14%左右；中共廣義財政收入中，每7元錢就有約1元錢是付利息的。

而且，利息大於新增GDP可是一個極其危險的信號——整個國家一年辛苦創造的新增財富，連償還當年債務的「財務成本（利息）」都不夠，意味著國家經濟正走入危機。政府賺到的新錢不夠付利息，為了不違約，就必須借新債來還舊債的利息，債務滾雪球的速度會失控，可能最終觸發「明斯基時刻」，引發債務危機。例如，20世紀80年代的拉美經濟體（「失去的十年」）， 2010年前後歐債危機中的重災國等等。

## 2026年10月19日星期一

### 中國來港讀博士生 被訛稱入境處來電騙走500萬元

[](https://lingbaxianzhang.blogspot.com/2026/10/500.html)追光者報道

一名中國來香港攻讀博士的大學生，接獲假冒入境處的電話，最終被騙走500萬港元。

警方指，假客服、假官員騙局飆升，尤其是首年來港的中國學生已成為詐騙集團的重點目標，主要涉及假冒官員及假冒客服的騙局。

最新公布的一宗案例指，一名博士生8月接到自稱入境處的來電，稱其身份被盜用作申請電話號碼並發騷擾訊息，要求他報案，緊接將電話轉駁至騙徒，期間引導他下載Teams應用程式、簽署密承諾書和接受24小時監聽，再以赴美交換為由，促他向家人借錢，全程共享屏幕監視，結果被騙走500萬元。

根據警方統計，今年累計逾729宗相關個案，按年增140%；而涉及中國新生墮假官員騙局的案件，則共涉800萬元。警方提醒，切勿點擊短訊內的連結或回撥電話號碼，如接獲任何自稱公安的來電，應立即掛斷。

title: Chinese maritime control a growing issue
summary: ## STRENGTH FROM THE SEA: As China is in the process of trying to pull the entire western Pacific into its sphere of influence, other nations must be wary, an academic said * By William Hetherington / Staff writer, with CNA * * [Add TT as P
content:
## STRENGTH FROM THE SEA:  As China is in the process of trying to pull the entire western Pacific into its sphere of influence, other nations must be wary, an academic said

*   By William Hetherington / Staff writer, with CNA

*       *   [Add TT as Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=taipeitimes.com)
    *   [_![Image 1](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/x.png)_](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Chinese+maritime+control+a+growing+issue%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F19%2F2003866215)
    *   [_![Image 2](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/facebook.png)_](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F19%2F2003866215&t=Chinese+maritime+control+a+growing+issue)
    *   [_![Image 3](https://www.taipeitimes.com/assets/images/line.png)_](https://lineit.line.me/share/ui?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.taipeitimes.com%2FNews%2Ftaiwan%2Farchives%2F2026%2F10%2F19%2F2003866215?utm_medium=P&utm_campaign=SHARE&utm_source=LINE)

China’s efforts to expand its maritime activities in waters east of Taiwan are a shared concern for Taiwan, Japan and the Philippines, a Japanese specialist on China’s maritime policy said.

The three sides should cooperate to assess Beijing’s intentions and protect their respective interests, Chisako Masuo, a professor at Kyushu University’s Graduate School of Social and Cultural Studies, said in an interview on Wednesday last week.

Masuo said Taiwan and Japan lack close cooperation, while concern in Japan over a contingency involving Taiwan has faded amid growing optimism that an armed invasion would not occur. Such views have spread following the removal of senior Chinese military officers from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), she said. Attention to maritime issues has also slackened under Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government.

## An undated photo shows a Japan Coast Guard cutter and a China Coast Guard ship.

Photo courtesy of Japan Coast Guard via AFP

However, China’s maritime “law enforcement patrols” east of Taiwan could become more sophisticated and would “absolutely not disappear,” Masuo said.

She added that Japan’s and the Philippines’ exclusive economic zones overlap in the same maritime area, connecting it to Japan’s interests.

Taiwanese and Japanese generally view each other favorably but “surprisingly do not know each other well” and make little effort to understand one another, Masuo said. Both sides assume they understand the other, yet have not exchanged views on some of the most important issues. The two sides need to deepen their mutual understanding, she said.

Chinese President Xi Jinping’s (習近平) top priority was domestic politics, while he sought to fulfill two missions: reshaping the international political order and unifying Taiwan with China, Masuo said. Military unification was not a predetermined course of action, she said, but Beijing would “absolutely not abandon this option.”

China would likely increasingly combine “gray zone” tactics that stop short of triggering armed conflict, she added.

Since becoming CCP general secretary and Chinese president, Xi has launched various reforms that have expanded the tools available to him, Masuo said. In maritime policy, these include fisheries reform, port development and marine environmental protection, as well as a system for using people in the fishing industry as maritime militia members.

China has gained new partners by strengthening its scientific and technological capabilities and rebuilding its socialist system, while more people at home have recognized its new missions and fallen in line, she said.

These developments have given Xi more ways to pursue “gray zone” operations, while his growing incentive to use them has made China’s activities increasingly apparent, she added.

Masuo said China wants to break away from the US-centered international system and establish a separate regional order in Asia anchored in Beijing. Its activities in the Pacific suggest it means to bring the western half of the ocean under its hegemony.

To achieve this, China is preparing to respond, even in a worst-case scenario of an armed conflict with the US, she said.

“The Taiwan issue is not an isolated one and could become a flashpoint for a future war between the US and China,” Masuo said.

In the event of a war in Taiwan, the Japanese Self-Defense Forces would have difficulty directly assisting Taiwan under Japanese domestic law. However, Masuo said that “the continued functioning of the Japan-US alliance is also extremely important to Taiwan in practice.”

title: Pax Silica needs a ‘follow the money’ reality check
summary: _The Pax Silica’s promised economic returns cannot be demonstrated by political rhetoric. They must be credible, financeable, environmentally sustainable and institutionally deliverable. That's the necessary empirical test._ LAST week, the
content:
_The Pax Silica’s promised economic returns cannot be demonstrated by political rhetoric. They must be credible, financeable, environmentally sustainable and institutionally deliverable. That's the necessary empirical test._

LAST week, the Philippines and the US signed a framework agreement for the planned “AI industrial hub” under the US-led Pax Silica initiative. It is targeted before the end of the year.

Nonetheless, Pax Silica is likely to multiply Philippine geopolitical and, thereby, economic risks, as I argued half a year ago.

*   [Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

According to its proponents, Pax Silica — the US-led international strategic initiative to build secure supply chains for advanced technologies — could become an important opportunity for the Philippines. And the country does possess some comparative advantages in electronics, English-speaking technical labor, services, geographic location and mineral resources.

Yet that is very different from proving that the proposed 4,000-acre (about 1,619-hectare) hub at New Clark City will attract $40–70 billion, create 130,000–190,000 jobs and transform the country into an AI industrial power. These remain projections, not observed economic outcomes.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

**Pax Silica claims****— and realities**

First, $40–$70 billion is not a demonstrated investment commitment. The Philippines signed the Pax Silica Declaration in April 2026, but the declaration is a cooperation framework, not a guarantee of _Philippine_ investment, technology transfer or market access.

On Oct. 13, the government said the BCDA had submitted a proposed legal framework to the president and that BCDA and its US development partner were still discussing the partnership; signing was expected before year-end. Distressingly, the terms were not public. A framework agreement, even when signed, would not itself prove that investors have committed or financed projects.

*   ![Image 1: ‘We are fed up with old and low tricks’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265074.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘We are fed up with old and low tricks’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/national/we-are-fed-up-with-old-and-low-tricks/2448199)

Second, the job projections require much greater scrutiny. The implied capital intensity is extraordinary. The headline figures imply roughly $210,000–$538,000 of capital per projected job. That may be possible in capital-intensive semiconductor or advanced manufacturing, but the project cannot be judged mainly by job totals. Officials must distinguish direct jobs from indirect jobs and disclose assumptions behind any employment multipliers.

Third, “AI hub” is too elastic to support a credible cost-benefit calculation without a defined industrial mix. Semiconductor assembly, chip testing, equipment manufacturing, mineral processing, logistics and data center operations have very different requirements for skills, capital, energy, water and environmental safeguards.

In September, the Palace said no data centers were planned at the Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park, describing its role instead as producing equipment and components for AI data centers and AI-enabled products. That clarification makes it even more important to state precisely which industries the project will actually host.

Fourth, basic environmental due diligence remains unresolved. In August, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources told Congress that no project-specific environmental impact assessment had been applied for or processed and that it lacked a clear project description.

*   ![Image 2: Prosecution’s withdrawal of impeachment articles is swindling the people and VP Sara](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/19/1265115.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Prosecution’s withdrawal of impeachment articles is swindling the people and VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/opinion/columns/prosecutions-withdrawal-of-impeachment-articles-is-swindling-the-people-and-vp-sara/2448232)

An Environmental Compliance Certificate for BCDA’s broader development plan is not equivalent to an assessment of the actual industrial hub. Publicly available project-specific water-balance, grid-adequacy and cumulative-impact studies also remain essential before the project’s requirements can be credibly judged.

**Contested claims, concerns****of flood control scandal déjà vu**

The most vulnerable headline claims are $70 billion, 190,000 jobs, enormous export gains and “AI powerhouse” status.

Scale matters. Industry sources put Philippine electronics exports at about $49.6 billion in 2025, although official trade classifications differ. A new zone generating exports worth tens of billions would be a major transformation, not a routine investment cycle.

*   ![Image 3: More criminal cases seen vs VP Sara](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/19/1265093.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More criminal cases seen vs VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/more-criminal-cases-seen-vs-vp-sara/2448202)

Additionality matters, too. Some activity may relocate or expand production that would otherwise happen elsewhere in the Philippines. The question is how much new Philippine output the project creates. Nor does $1 billion in semiconductor exports add $1 billion to Philippine GDP: imported inputs, equipment and foreign intellectual property can account for substantial value. The government should publish domestic value added, wages, productivity, technology spillovers and tax receipts — not just gross exports.

Fiscal costs must also be counted. Tax incentives, public infrastructure, utility investments and environmental externalities should be deducted from the benefits. The proper test is incremental domestic value added and public revenue, net of public costs and tax expenditures.

The issue of foreign versus domestic value added is vital. A semiconductor exported for $1 billion does not necessarily add $1 billion to Philippine GDP. Imported wafers, equipment, components, energy and foreign intellectual property may constitute substantial portions of gross export value. Government projections need therefore to report domestic value added, not merely exports.

Nor can fiscal leakage be ignored. Large strategic investments commonly receive tax incentives. The proper calculation is consequently: incremental GDP, wages, taxes plus technology spillovers _minus_ infrastructure costs, tax expenditures, environmental costs and externalities.

Finally, the flood-control scandal makes independent verification especially important. Government estimates put losses from defective or fictitious projects at tens of billions of pesos, while auditors documented substandard, overpriced, duplicated or nonexistent works. This does not prove Pax Silica will be corrupt. But it does show why announcements and project totals cannot substitute for contracts, financing, transparent procurement and independent audit.

**Bottom line: the climate****and geological test**

The Philippines is highly exposed to typhoons, flooding, earthquakes, liquefaction, landslides, tsunamis and volcanic hazards. World Bank analysis warns that climate change could materially reduce GDP without adaptation; historical typhoon losses have been estimated at around 1.2 percent of GDP. For an energy- and water-intensive industrial project, resilience is an economic input, not a public-relations label.

The correct sequence is hazard and cumulative-impact assessment; a credible water balance and power plan; economic feasibility and full fiscal costing; public disclosure and consultation; binding investment and financing commitments; _then_ construction and measured results. Independent studies should assess not only the site boundary but also the connected power, water, transport and industrial infrastructure.

**Follow the money**

Pax Silica is an opportunity to test whether the Philippines can move up the technology value chain — not yet proof that it has done so.

The standard should be neither anti-American nor anti-Chinese, pro- nor anti-Marcos. It should be empirical: Show us the contracts, financing, feasibility studies, environmental assessment, water and power plans, tax costs, verified jobs and domestic value added — and then let the empirical record decide.

_Dr. Dan Steinbock is an internationally recognized strategist of the multipolar world and the founder of Difference Group. He has served at the India, China and America Institute (USA), Shanghai Institutes for International Studies (China) and the EU Center (Singapore). For more, see https://www.differencegroup.net_

title: Even Marcos wouldn’t want Chinese envoy expelled
summary: [![Image 1: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265053.png)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265053.png) * [Prosecution’s withdrawal of impeachment articles is swindling th
content:
[![Image 1: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265053.png)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265053.png)

*   [Prosecution’s withdrawal of impeachment articles is swindling the people and VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/opinion/columns/prosecutions-withdrawal-of-impeachment-articles-is-swindling-the-people-and-vp-sara/2448232)

IF our diplomatic row with China escalates, this would result in the final push that could send an already fragile Philippine economy over the edge. That would unleash so much outrage that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. would be toppled, just as his father was, before his term ends in 2028.

Let’s ignore the pretended, for-the-headlines indignation against the Chinese ambassador of infantile and ignorant senators Erwin Tulfo and Risa Hontiveros, as well as of Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., and soberly assess the consequences of kicking the diplomat out of the country.

China's first response would almost certainly be reciprocal. If Manila expels Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan, Beijing could order the Philippine ambassador to leave China. The two governments could subsequently downgrade diplomatic contacts, suspend consultations and reduce cooperation on issues ranging from trade to maritime incidents.

China, however, could respond more forcefully: the Philippines would appear to be the first country in six decades to expel a serving Chinese ambassador — a rare and momentous escalation as Beijing increasingly contests American economic and military primacy.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

The comparable recent precedent, but with an important difference, is the China-Canada spat in 2023. Canada in May 2023 — when Justin Trudeau was prime minister — expelled Chinese consul Zhao Wei over alleged interference targeting the family of legislator Michael Chong. Beijing denied the allegations, and the next day ramped up the response by expelling the consul at Canada’s consulate-general in Shanghai, an important diplomatic post.

Canada in 2024 imposed tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, steel and aluminum, and China in 2025 restricted Canadian agricultural and seafood exports. After Trudeau was replaced by Mark Carney as prime minister in March 2025, high-level contacts resumed and relations between the two countries normalized.

*   ![Image 2: OFW arrested at NAIA for estafa](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265067.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[OFW arrested at NAIA for estafa](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/ofw-arrested-at-naia-for-estafa/2448191)

Canada removed a consul, not China’s ambassador. Ordering Jing out of Manila would be a far more serious escalation, in a relationship already burdened by dangerous maritime encounters and far greater Philippine dependence on Chinese trade.

**Indonesia**

Indonesia expelled two Chinese diplomats in 1967 in the wake of the Suharto-orchestrated massacres of 1965 and 1966, which killed hundreds of thousands of Indonesians alleged to be supporters of the Indonesian Communist Party, and the anti-Chinese frenzy that came with them. Relations between the two countries were normalized only after **23 years**, in 1990.

The big difference in Indonesia’s rift with China and ours if it escalates is that the China that Indonesia confronted in 1967 was a poor country and cutting trade with it hardly affected its economy.

*   ![Image 3: SC asked to stop courts from blocking wage orders](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265081.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[SC asked to stop courts from blocking wage orders](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/sc-asked-to-stop-courts-from-blocking-wage-orders/2448206)

Now, China is the largest, or second largest (depending on the metric used), economic superpower today. China’s total trade with the world in 1967 was barely $4 billion. Last year, it was **$6 trillion**. China is the world’s largest goods exporter and second-largest goods importer, behind the United States.

China is one of the Philippines' largest trading partners and its **biggest** source of imported goods. It is a major market for Philippine agricultural and industrial products, an important participant in regional manufacturing supply chains, and a potentially significant source of tourists and investment.

Beijing would not have to announce a sweeping economic embargo to hurt the Philippine economy. It could simply tighten inspections of agricultural imports, slow customs clearances, restrict selected commodities, discourage Chinese tourists from visiting the Philippines or postpone economic cooperation projects.

**Administrative**

*   ![Image 4: ‘We are fed up with old and low tricks’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265074.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘We are fed up with old and low tricks’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/national/we-are-fed-up-with-old-and-low-tricks/2448199)

Each measure could be defended as a regulatory, commercial or administrative decision. Proving that a particular restriction constituted retaliation would be difficult. Reversing the resulting economic damage could be even harder.

China in the past did apply economic pressure in diplomatic disputes. Its restrictions on Australian commodities during the deterioration of Sino-Australian relations showed how trade could become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation. The restrictions affected products including barley, wine and coal, although their consequences varied considerably across industries and many were subsequently lifted.

During our “Scarborough Standoff” with China in 2012, China stopped banana imports as they landed on its ports, on the grounds that these needed to be checked for infestations. The bananas rotted, and then-president Benigno Aquino III was more than willing to believe an American diplomat’s claim that Beijing had agreed to withdraw its vessels from the shoal. That was a lie, but it gave Aquino the excuse to order our vessels out of the area, in effect abandoning the disputed shoal to China.

In 2025 China supplied $38.4 billion worth of goods to the Philippines, representing 28.6 percent of our total merchandise imports. Philippine exports to China amounted to $9.3 billion, or 11 percent of total exports.

Now examine the same trade relationship from Beijing's perspective. The $38.4 billion in Chinese goods bought by the Philippines in 2025 represented barely **one**percent of China's worldwide exports. The $9.3 billion in Philippine goods sold to China amounted to only 0.36 percent of China's worldwide imports.

**Blow**

This means that if China were to halt trade with the Philippines, its citizens would hardly notice it. By contrast it could be a body blow to our economy. Go to a supermarket: my estimate is that half or more of the nonperishable goods there are made in China; so are the inexpensive products sold in online stores Lazada and Shopee. In 2023, China even supplied a quarter of our imported petroleum products.

Cut off in a quarrel with China would be goods that sustain factories, construction projects, transportation, agriculture and countless small businesses. China supplies machinery, electronics, industrial components, vehicles and other products indispensable to Philippine economic activity. A serious deterioration in relations could disrupt supply chains, increase costs and discourage investment.

Of course, not all these goods would suddenly disappear if diplomatic relations deteriorated. Trade is conducted almost entirely by private businesses, and Chinese firms also benefit from selling to the Philippine market. But Beijing possesses considerable administrative power over access to its own market, particularly for agricultural exports that require sanitary approvals, customs clearances and other government authorizations.

Economic retaliation is not the only possible consequence. China could intensify its coast guard operations around Bajo de Masinloc and other contested areas, increase patrols, or adopt a less accommodating position in negotiations over maritime incidents.

Such measures would not necessarily be announced as retaliation for the ambassador's expulsion. Beijing could describe them as revitalized enforcement of its territorial and maritime claims. The Philippines would then confront the familiar difficulty of responding to a much larger power whose coast guard and naval capabilities substantially exceed its own.

**Escalation**

We should not assume, as our defense secretary seems to firmly believe, that an escalation at sea would produce direct American military intervention. In 2012 President Aquino went to Washington to beg then-president Barack Obama to intervene militarily in the Scarborough standoff. Obama told him to just file a case against China at an international venue, which turned out to be merely with an arbitral panel.

There is a disturbing tendency in Philippine political discourse to equate hostility toward China with patriotism. For the sake of being viewed as committed nationalists, senators and presidential wannabes like the defense secretary compete to issue the harshest statements, while anyone advocating negotiations is accused of weakness or subservience to Beijing.

English writer Samuel Johnson was referring to that kind of scoundrel when he said back in the 18th century: “Patriotism is the last refuge of a scoundrel.” These scoundrels reverse the meaning of patriotism. The obligation of political leaders and bureaucrats is not to demonstrate how loudly they can denounce another country. It is to protect the security, welfare and prosperity of their own people.

For all their pretended patriotism, the likes of Tulfo and Hontiveros, these ignoramuses — or worse, American puppets — want the country to gamble with Filipino livelihoods just for the sake of their grabbing headlines. Shame on these two senators, shame on the Yellows who are trying to build an anti-China frenzy in our country — in the service of the US.

**PS:** What exactly did the Chinese ambassador say to push the likes of these two ignorant senators and Defense Secretary Teodoro into an anti-China paroxysm? The ambassador made the statement in response to a media query on the sidelines of the second Diliman Dialogue, on his reaction to Teodoro’s characterization of China as the region’s “troublemaker.” Here is his response verbatim:

“That’s nonsense. Who’s the troublemaker? Look at who go after Chinese teachers. They’re innocent. Who led the army to arrest Chinese innocent workers? Who every day smear, attack China? We should feel fortunate enough that you have a neighbor like China in this region. If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not choose force, and we love peace.”

title: ‘We are fed up with old and low tricks’
summary: THE Chinese Embassy in Manila on Sunday dared lawmakers to act on their threat to declare China’s Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan persona non grata, saying it has grown tired of such repeated warnings. “Some anti-China politicians t
content:
THE Chinese Embassy in Manila on Sunday dared lawmakers to act on their threat to declare China’s Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan persona non grata, saying it has grown tired of such repeated warnings.

“Some anti-China politicians talked about declaring the Chinese ambassador persona non grata. Over the past 30 years, anti-China forces have been repeatedly doing the same thing to threaten our embassy. We are fed up with these old and low tricks,” the embassy said in a statement on Facebook.

“If they really want to do something, do it quickly and immediately please,” it added.

*   [Free trade deal with Canada pushed](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/free-trade-deal-with-canada-pushed/2448208)

The embassy said that it would not welcome lawmakers calling for the ouster of the ambassador to China.

“While diplomacy is based on reciprocity, we will not welcome them to China. Simple and fair enough,” it added.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

More senators on Sunday called on the ambassador to leave the Philippines, saying China could easily defeat the country in a military conflict.

Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito and Sen. Francis Pangilinan were among the lawmakers who criticized Jing after the Chinese Embassy challenged Philippine officials to declare the envoy persona non grata.

In a video posted on his Facebook page, Ejercito addressed Jing in Mandarin, telling the ambassador the West Philippine Sea belongs to the Philippines and urging him to go home.

*   ![Image 1: OFW arrested at NAIA for estafa](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265067.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[OFW arrested at NAIA for estafa](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/ofw-arrested-at-naia-for-estafa/2448191)

In separate radio interviews, Ejercito described the envoy’s remarks as hostile, arrogant and undiplomatic, and could further inflame tensions between Manila and Beijing.

He said the Philippines should pursue diplomacy to improve bilateral relations, but Jing’s statements were undermining those efforts.

“He is adding fuel to the fire,” Ejercito said, adding that Manila did not want a war with China but expected Beijing to respect Philippine sovereignty.

“We do not want war. We do not want to fight China. They are super powerful, while we are only a Third World country,” he said.

*   ![Image 2: SC asked to stop courts from blocking wage orders](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/18/1265081.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[SC asked to stop courts from blocking wage orders](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/sc-asked-to-stop-courts-from-blocking-wage-orders/2448206)

Ejercito noted that the two countries have longstanding economic and cultural ties, including through the Filipino-Chinese community and bilateral trade.

Interviewed on DWIZ, the senator said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was right to summon Jing but added the government must exhaust diplomatic means in addressing the dispute.

“Given his attitude, I think he should be declared persona non grata, and Beijing should replace him. If they want to improve our relationship, this ambassador will not help,” he said.

Ejercito said the Senate could consider a resolution condemning Jing’s remarks when sessions resume.

*   ![Image 3: More criminal cases seen vs VP Sara](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/19/1265093.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[More criminal cases seen vs VP Sara](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/19/news/more-criminal-cases-seen-vs-vp-sara/2448202)

He backed the continued modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and the strengthening of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), saying the country needed a minimum credible defense capability to protect its territory.

Ejercito said his criticism was directed at China’s policies, not its people.

“I am not pro-America or pro-war. I am pro-Filipino,” he said.

Pangilinan criticized what he described as the envoy’s arrogant and condescending attitude.

“By way of diplomatic language, you can please easily leave Manila and go back to China,” Pangilinan said in a post on his Facebook page.

On Friday, Sen. Risa Hontiveros described Jing’s remarks as a form of “gray-zone” aggression intended to intimidate the Philippines without triggering outright conflict.

Hontiveros said summoning the ambassador was not enough, calling on the government to demand a formal retraction and an apology from Beijing.

If China refused, she said, the Philippines should declare Jing persona non grata and raise the issue before Asean and the United Nations General Assembly.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian called on Jing to apologize, describing his remarks as undiplomatic and uncalled for.

“It is not correct that a foreigner inside our country is threatening us. That’s undiplomatic and uncalled for,” Gatchalian said.

Sen. Erwin Tulfo, vice chairman of the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, said the Philippines will not back down in the face of threats.

“Nobody in this world can bully the Philippines — whether through words or by force. Our sovereignty is not negotiable, our dignity is not for sale, and our resolve must never be mistaken for weakness,” Tulfo said.

Sen. Jinggoy Estrada urged caution on calls to declare Jing persona non grata, saying the Philippines should defend its sovereignty while keeping diplomatic channels open.

“While I share the concern and indignation his words have stirred, we must protest strongly and demand respect, without closing the doors of dialogue,” Estrada said.

“There is nothing to be gained from acting hastily in response to the Chinese envoy’s remarks,” he said.

# 美国中国研究生涉嫌毒害越南同学：大学与受害者家属怎么说？

图像来源，Getty Images/University of Wyoming/BBC

**Article Information**
*       *   Author, 黎爱（Thuong Le）
    *   Role, BBC越南语记者

*   Published 2026年10月18日
*   阅读时间: 4 分钟

美国怀俄明大学（University of Wyoming）一名越南籍研究生的家属表示，受害人在办公室咖啡机内发现神经毒剂后，至今仍出现疲倦、食欲不振及睡眠欠佳等健康问题。

怀俄明大学表示，校内一名研究生因涉嫌使用某种物质伤害一名同实验室同事，被控加重伤害重罪（felony aggravated assault and battery）。

主修微生物学的32岁中国籍女研究生王艾莉（Aili Wang；音译，又译王爱丽），[于10月6日在洛杉矶国际机场被捕](https://bbc.com/vietnamese/articles/c63r58gd4lwzo)。此前，她因涉嫌毒害一名越南籍同事而接受调查，当时正试图离开美国。

王艾莉被指于今年年中两度透过 eBay 购买化学品丙烯醯胺（acrylamide），其后要求平台删除其帐户。

之后，她被怀疑将上述神经毒物混入一名越南籍研究生的咖啡机中。该名研究生在法庭文件中被标示为“K.T.”。

执法人员在洛杉矶国际机场拘捕她时，检取了其手提电脑、电子储存装置及手写文件。

根据法庭文件，王艾莉于10月5日接受校园警察盘问时声称，自己“已有多年未使用丙烯醯胺”。

一天后，即10月6日，王艾莉在机场被捕。检察官指控她当时正试图返回中国。

截至10月13日，王艾莉仍被羁押于洛杉矶，不得保释候审。

怀俄明大学市场推广及传讯副校长查德·鲍德温（Chad Baldwin）在发给BBC越南语（BBC News Vietnamese）的电邮中表示，相关指控已于上星期提交至奥尔巴尼县巡回法院（Albany County Circuit Court），此前怀俄明大学警察局（University of Wyoming Police Department, UWPD）已完成调查。

UWPD 的调查结果已移交奥尔巴尼县检察官办公室，由该办公室正式提出控罪。

与此同时，校方亦正进行学生纪律程序。

不过，怀俄明大学强调，目前仍仅属指控阶段。任何人在法院作出有罪裁决前，均应被视为无罪。

## “异常苦涩的味道”

受害人的姐姐在越南接受BBC采访时表示，其弟弟自8月起饮用办公室内咖啡机冲泡、带有“异常苦涩味道”的咖啡后，开始出现健康问题。

她说：“喝了几天咖啡后，他出现身体疲倦、手脚骨头疼痛、无法进食和睡眠等症状，曾就医检查但未能查出病因，之后经化验才得知原因。”

她表示，K.T. 有每天喝咖啡的习惯，而咖啡机设于他的实验室内，因此主要由他使用及饮用。

姐姐表示：“那位同学（王艾莉）因为一起做研究，可以自由进出实验室。”

一名化学教授在水样中发现丙烯醯胺。这种化学物质在高剂量接触下可能具有毒性。

其后，怀俄明大学校园警察在两人工作的办公室安装监控摄影机。警方表示，9月27日拍摄到王艾莉翻查受害人的办公桌。

到了10月1日，监控画面再次显示她拍照、翻动桌上的笔记本，并将自己杯中的液体倒入同事的杯中。

调查人员亦指控她曾两度透过 eBay 购买丙烯醯胺，并在事后试图要求平台删除其帐户。

图像来源，GummyBone / iStock / Getty Images Plus

图像加注文字，怀俄明大学创校至今已有140年历史。

End of content

直接指导 K.T. 与王艾莉的微生物学教授马克·戈梅尔斯基（Prof Mark Gomelsky）向美联社表示，受害人是一名表现非常出色的学生。

家属表示，K.T. 于2022年获博士奖学金赴美深造，此前曾就读河内理工大学，并在韩国（南韩）攻读硕士学位。

这名越南籍研究生的研究项目获美国联邦政府资助，并正等待一项涉及癌症、神经疾病及遗传病治疗新技术的专利批准。

根据调查文件，王艾莉在赴美前亦曾于中国从事类似研究。

戈梅尔斯基教授在回覆BBC电邮时表示：“这对我而言是一段可怕且难以置信的经历，尤其对受害人及其家人更是如此。”

此前，戈梅尔斯基教授向美联社表示，王艾莉首次论文答辩未获通过，而对同事成功发现利用细菌将核糖核酸（RNA）导入人体细胞的方法，可能产生嫉妒心理。

戈梅尔斯基教授亦表示，自6月起，王艾莉已不再参与实验室工作，以专注完成论文。

姐姐亦表示，目前受害人仍受到健康问题困扰，“身体依然感到疲惫、食欲不振，而且睡不好”。

戈梅尔斯基教授向美联社表示：“丙烯醯胺是一种神经毒物，无法被中和，因此会留存在神经细胞中并导致其死亡。所以，目前仍不清楚他是否能完全康复。”

丙烯醯胺是一种可能致癌的物质，可在高温烹调富含淀粉的食物时形成，也存在于烟草烟雾中。

该物质在高剂量下可引起急性中毒，亦可用于涉及蛋白质或 DNA 的微生物研究。

## 接下来会怎样？

王艾莉面临加重伤害重罪指控；该罪名在怀俄明州最高可判处10年监禁及罚款1万美元（6.69万元人民币；32.45万元新台币）。

目前尚不清楚王艾莉何时会被押解回怀俄明州。奥尔巴尼县法院法官罗伯特·桑福德（Judge Robert Sanford）已批准检方要求，将保释金由20万美元提高至150万美元，且须以现金缴纳。

在回覆BBC的置评请求电邮中，查德·鲍德温引述怀俄明大学校长尚恩·里夫斯（Shane Reeves）的声明表示，校方“严肃看待所有涉及校园社群健康与安全的问题，并致力为学生、教师、员工及访客维持安全及受保障的环境”。

校方亦表示，将持续评估与事件相关的资讯，并在有需要时采取适当措施，以保障校园社群安全。

声明指出：“怀俄明大学正与执法部门合作，并将就任何后续资讯作出回应。”

戈梅尔斯基教授向BBC表示：“最好的做法是让调查程序按照既定程序进行，而我不再作进一步评论。”

受害人家属K.T. 的姐姐表示：“健康是最重要的事，家人希望他能够康复。”

她说：“家人亦希望越南有关部门能协助保护在美国的越南人，尤其是我的弟弟。K. 的妻子和儿子也十分担心，不知道背后是否还有其他人参与这件事。”

# Takaichi defies Korea, China as Yasukuni offerings escalate and tensions rise

Tokyo's autumn shrine rites stir fresh backlash as Takaichi persists with personal tributes

By

Published 2026.10.19. 08:55

[Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com)

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan sent an offering on the 17th to Yasukuni Shrine, where Class-A war criminals from the Pacific War are enshrined, and on the 19th additionally dedicated payment for the offering. Even though the Korean and Chinese governments strongly protested the offering earlier and expressed regret, she again used personal funds three days later to show sincerity. As Japanese Cabinet ministers and ruling party executives have also been visiting to pay respects one after another, diplomatic friction with neighboring countries is expected to intensify further.

On the 17th, Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae sends a wooden offering plaque (left) to Yasukuni Shrine. /Courtesy of Yonhap News

According to a compilation of reports by Kyodo News and other Japanese media on the 19th, Prime Minister Takaichi, marking the Yasukuni Shrine autumn festival (ritual) in Kudankita, Tokyo, dedicated at personal expense the payment for an offering called tamagushi-ryo through Liberal Democratic Party General Council Chair Hiroshi Kajiyama. After paying his respects at the shrine, General Council Chair Kajiyama met with reporters and disclosed this fact.

Located in central Tokyo, Yasukuni Shrine is a facility that commemorates the more than 2.46 million people who died in major wars waged by modern Japan. Fourteen Class-A war criminals from the Pacific War, including former Prime Minister Hideki Tojo, who were executed under the International Military Tribunal for the Far East, are also enshrined there, making it regarded as a symbol of Japanese militarism.

On the 17th, when the autumn festival began, Prime Minister Takaichi also dedicated, in the name of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, a wooden potted-plant-type offering called masakaki. The Korean government immediately expressed regret when Prime Minister Takaichi sent the first offering on the 17th, and the Chinese government also condemned it as a provocation targeting the postwar international order. However, Prime Minister Takaichi pressed ahead with an additional dedication two days later, undeterred by opposition from neighboring countries.

Considering the diplomatic fallout, Prime Minister Takaichi plans to hold off on a schedule to visit Yasukuni Shrine in person to pay respects during this autumn festival period. During the spring festival in April, she also chose to dedicate masakaki and tamagushi-ryo in succession instead of paying respects in person. On Aug. 15, Korea's Liberation Day and the anniversary of Japan's defeat, she paid the offering fee out of pocket and performed a yohai—bowing toward the shrine from afar—instead of going to the shrine. According to Kyodo News, when asked whether she also performed a yohai on the 17th, Takaichi's aides said, "We refrain from answering." It is seen as a dual strategy to avoid negative effects on Korea-Japan and China-Japan relations while appeasing a hardline conservative base at home.

While the prime minister moved to make a second dedication, sitting Cabinet ministers and political figures have been lining up to pay respects in person. On the first day of the festival, the 17th, Economy and Fiscal Policy Minister Minoru Kiuchi and ruling Liberal Democratic Party policy chief Takayuki Kobayashi visited Yasukuni Shrine to pay respects. Then on the morning of the 19th, Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism Minister Tatsunori Ibayashi additionally visited the shrine as a sitting Cabinet minister. Lawmakers belonging to a cross-party group called the Parliamentary Association for All to Visit Yasukuni Shrine also planned a group visit the same day, suggesting that Northeast Asia's diplomatic tensions over historical issues are unlikely to subside for the time being.

title: Chinese embassy slams Japan’s Takaichi over Yasukuni ritual offering
zh_title: 中国大使馆批评日本高市参拜靖国神社
summary: 中国谴责日本首相高市早苗向与战争有关的东京靖国神社[送上祭品](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3371219/japans-takaichi-sends-offering-controversial-yasukuni-war-shrine?module=inline&pgtype=article)，此举有可能进一步加剧中日关系紧张。邻居。周六，在靖国神社为期三天的秋季祭典开始时，高市以首相的身份向靖国神社送去了祭树祭品，尽管她没有亲自参拜。木内稔（Minoru Kiuchi），经济增长担当大臣
content:
中国谴责日本首相高市早苗向与战争有关的东京靖国神社[送上祭品](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3371219/japans-takaichi-sends-offering-controversial-yasukuni-war-shrine?module=inline&pgtype=article)，此举有可能进一步加剧中日关系紧张。邻居。

周六，在靖国神社为期三天的秋季祭典开始时，高市以首相的身份向靖国神社送去了祭树祭品，尽管她没有亲自参拜。

据日本共同社报道，负责经济增长战略的大臣木内稔当天访问了这个有争议的地点。

中国驻日本大使馆在周六晚间发表声明强烈谴责此举。

中国大使馆将靖国神社描述为“日本军国主义的精神工具和象征”，并表示，日本政治人物任何以任何借口参拜靖国神社的企图，都等于粉饰战争罪行，为加速“重新军事化”铺平道路。

正确认识和对待历史，是日本战后重返国际社会的重要前提，是日本与周边国家关系的政治基础，也是日本是否恪守和平发展承诺的标杆。
北京对外经济贸易大学日本研究研究员吴英杰表示，高一正在追随她许多政治人物的脚步](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3322141/china-complains-about-japanese-ministers-tribute-war-criminals-yasukuni-shrine?module=inline&pgtype=article)前辈。

“高市的做法遵循了大多数前任日本首相所坚持的平衡做法——避免亲自访问以避免严重的国际反弹，同时进行祭祀以满足国内右翼盟友的要求，”吴说。

靖国神社供奉着约 246 万日本战死者，其中包括二战后被国际法庭定罪的 14 名甲级战犯。遭受日本战时侵略的亚洲国家，特别是中国和韩国，一直抗议日本领导人的访问和提供。

06:06

争议地点：日本靖国神社

吴指出，北京的最新谴责符合其既定的外交立场，并呼应了其[8月份的批评](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3364135/china-blasts-japanese-officials-visit-yasukuni-shrine-wwii-anniversary?module=inline&pgtype=article)，当时北京指责日本挑战二战后国际秩序。
8月15日，即日本二战投降纪念日，尽管防卫大臣小泉进次郎和其他三名内阁成员亲自参拜了靖国神社，但高市同样没有亲自参拜，而是送去了祭品。

作为对这些供奉和参拜的回应，中国外交部明确将靖国神社称为“战犯靖国神社”。

周四，国防部发言人毛宁在评论日本公共广播公司 NHK 的一部新纪录片时，再次将该遗址描述为“事实上的战犯祠堂”，该纪录片详细介绍了 1960 年代祭祀甲级战犯的秘密决定。

最近的摩擦加深了去年 11 月高市在议会中提出的建议时开始的关系冰冻

【原文 English Original】
China has condemned Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for [sending a ritual offering](https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/east-asia/article/3371219/japans-takaichi-sends-offering-controversial-yasukuni-war-shrine?module=inline&pgtype=article) to Tokyo’s war-linked Yasukuni Shrine, a move that threatens to further strain ties between the neighbours.

At the start of Yasukuni’s three-day autumn festival on Saturday, Takaichi sent a ritual tree-stand offering to the shrine in her capacity as prime minister, although she did not visit in person.

Minoru Kiuchi, minister in charge of economic growth strategy, visited the controversial site the same day, Japan’s Kyodo News reported.

In a statement late on Saturday, the Chinese embassy in Japan strongly condemned the move.

Describing the shrine as a “spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism”, the embassy said that any attempts by Japanese political figures to pay homage at Yasukuni – under whatever pretext – amounted to an effort to whitewash war crimes and pave the way for accelerating “remilitarisation”.

Properly understanding and treating history was an essential prerequisite for Japan’s post-war return to the international community, the political foundation for its relations with neighbouring countries and a benchmark for whether Japan abided by its commitment to peaceful development, the embassy said.

Wu Yingjie, a Japanese studies research fellow at the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing, said Takaichi was [following in the footsteps](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3322141/china-complains-about-japanese-ministers-tribute-war-criminals-yasukuni-shrine?module=inline&pgtype=article) of many of her political predecessors.

“Takaichi’s approach follows the balancing act maintained by most previous Japanese prime ministers – abstaining from personal visits to avoid severe international backlash while making ritual offerings to satisfy domestic right-wing allies,” Wu said.

The Yasukuni Shrine honours around 2.46 million Japanese war dead, including 14 Class-A war criminals convicted by international tribunals following World War II. Asian nations that suffered under Japanese wartime aggression, notably China and South Korea, have consistently protested against visits and offerings by Japanese leaders.

06:06

Place of controversy: Japan’s Yasukuni Shrine

Wu noted that Beijing’s latest condemnation aligned with its established diplomatic position and echoed its [criticisms in August](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3364135/china-blasts-japanese-officials-visit-yasukuni-shrine-wwii-anniversary?module=inline&pgtype=article), when it accused Japan of challenging the post-World War II international order.

On August 15, the anniversary of Japan’s surrender in World War II, Takaichi similarly skipped a personal visit and sent an offering instead, although Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and three other cabinet members visited the shrine in person.

In response to those offerings and visits, China’s foreign ministry explicitly branded Yasukuni a “war criminal shrine”.

On Thursday, ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning again described the site as a “de facto war criminal shrine”, while commenting on a new documentary by Japanese public broadcaster NHK detailing the covert 1960s decision to enshrine Class-A war criminals.

The latest friction deepens a frost in relations that began last November, when Takaichi suggested in parliament that a military attack on Taiwan could constitute a “survival-threatening situation” for Japan, potentially justifying military intervention.

High-level governmental dialogues between China and Japan have largely ground to a halt since.

Japanese PM ‘open’ to talks with China

Beijing sees Taiwan as part of China to be reunited by force if necessary. Most countries, including the United States and Japan, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, but Washington is opposed to any attempt to take the self-ruled island by force and is committed to supplying it with weapons.

However, Takaichi has signalled her willingness to visit China despite the diplomatic strain.

She said on Friday that she intended to be in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen next month, parliament permitting.

However, Wu cautioned that a high-level bilateral meeting was unlikely to materialise unless Tokyo made a fundamental shift in its rhetoric on Taiwan.
