香港卫生署署长卢仲茂教授出席在北京举行的2026年世界传统医学大会，分享香港将中医药纳入医疗保健体系的策略。他强调了旗舰机构以及与国家计划的一致性。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 17 日 16:30 香港时间 · 更新于 10 月 17 日 17:19 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

 图片：[香港特区政府新闻公报](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/17/P2026101600450.htm)

香港卫生局局长卢松茂教授于10月17日出席在北京举行的2026年世界传统医学大会，概述香港将中医药纳入医疗保健体系的策略。大会由北京市人民政府、国家卫生健康委员会、国家中医药管理局、国家药品监督管理局主办，世界卫生组织协办。
罗在政府座谈会上表示：“中医药是中华文明的瑰宝。国家“十五五”规划强调推动中医药传承创新，明确提出要完善中医药服务体系，增强基层中医药服务能力，发展中西医协同服务。”他表示，香港第一个五年规划和2026年施政报告为中医药全面高质量发展提出了愿景，与国家“健康中国”战略对接。

罗说，政府将通过两个旗舰机构促进中医药发展：香港中医院和政府中药检测中心。这些措施将推广纯中医和中西医结合的“香港模式”，促进人才培训、草药与药物相互作用的国际研究，并为中药材制定严格的质量标准。
会议期间，劳分别会见了国家卫健委副主任郑哲、国家药品监督管理局局长黄果。他告诉郑，香港的健康指标位居世界前列，香港第一个五年规划与国家“十五五”规划加快建设“健康中国”的目标相呼应。罗强调：“香港特区政府将积极深化医疗改革，建设国际医疗创新中心，并作为融入‘健康中国’议程的‘超级联系人’。”

罗在会见黄时详细介绍了将于今年成立的香港药物及医疗器械规管中心的进展情况。李自力被任命为董事。该中心的目标是到2030年或更早实施新药“一级审批”机制，并成为国际认可的监管机构。

香港代表团成员包括卫生署署长林中基医生、即将上任的卫生署署长李自力，以及卫生局、卫生署和医院管理局的官员。香港中医院行政长官卞兆祥教授亦出席。 10月18日，卢主任将出席“一带一路”中医药发展部长级圆桌会议，卫生部门代表将分享

Hong Kong
Hong Kong’s health chief Professor Lo Chung-mau attended the 2026 World Traditional Medicine Congress in Beijing, sharing the city’s strategy to integrate traditional Chinese medicine into its healthcare system. He highlighted flagship institutions and alignment with national plans.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

17 Oct 2026 at 16:30 HKT · updated 17 Oct, 17:19 · 2 min read

 Image: [香港特區政府新聞公報](https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202610/17/P2026101600450.htm)

Hong Kong’s Secretary for Health, Professor Lo Chung-mau, attended the 2026 World Traditional Medicine Congress in Beijing on 17 October, outlining the city’s strategy to integrate traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) into its healthcare system. The congress is hosted by the Beijing municipal government, the National Health Commission, the National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the National Medical Products Administration, and co-organised by the World Health Organization.

Speaking at a government forum, Lo said: “TCM is a treasure of Chinese civilisation. The national 15th Five-Year Plan emphasises promoting the inheritance and innovation of TCM, and clearly states the need to improve the TCM service system, enhance grassroots TCM service capabilities, and develop collaborative services between Chinese and Western medicine.” He noted that Hong Kong’s first five-year plan and the 2026 Policy Address set out a vision for comprehensive, high-quality development of TCM to align with the national “Healthy China” strategy.

Lo said the government would boost TCM development through two flagship institutions: the Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Hospital and the government Chinese Medicines Testing Institute. These would promote a “Hong Kong model” of pure TCM and integrated Chinese-Western medicine, foster talent training, international research on herb-drug interactions, and set strict quality standards for Chinese medicinal materials.

During the congress, Lo met separately with National Health Commission Deputy Director Zheng Zhe and National Medical Products Administration Director Huang Guo. He told Zheng that Hong Kong’s health indicators rank among the world’s best, and that the city’s first five-year plan mirrors the national 15th Five-Year Plan’s goal of accelerating the building of a “Healthy China”. Lo emphasised: “The HKSAR government will proactively deepen healthcare reform, build an international medical innovation hub, and serve as a ‘super connector’ to integrate into the ‘Healthy China’ agenda.”

In his meeting with Huang, Lo detailed progress on establishing the Hong Kong Centre for Drug and Medical Devices Regulation, which will be set up this year. Li Zili has been appointed as the director. The centre aims to implement a “first-tier approval” mechanism for new drugs by 2030 or earlier, and to become an internationally recognised regulatory authority.

The Hong Kong delegation includes Director of Health Dr Ronald Lam, incoming director Li Zili, and officials from the health bureau, the Department of Health and the Hospital Authority. Professor Bian Zhaoxiang, chief executive of the Hong Kong Chinese Medicine Hospital, also attended. On 18 October, Lo will join a ministerial roundtable on TCM development under the Belt and Road Initiative, while health department representatives will share updates on Chinese medicine regulation. The delegation is expected to return to Hong Kong on the afternoon of 18 October.

# Hong Kong minister recalls birthday cake as symbol of father's love and sacrifice

Hong Kong's Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law Shuk-pui shares a childhood memory of a strawberry cream cake, which she now sees as a symbol of her father's quiet sacrifices and love. She recalled a year when her father, a taxi driver, ate a corner piece of her cake for breakfast

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law Shuk-pui has shared a touching childhood story about a strawberry cream cake that has become a symbol of family love and sacrifice, according to _The Standard_.

For Law, a classic strawberry cream cake is more than just a dessert; it is a precious link to her childhood. She explained that her family would buy one for her every year for her birthday, a tradition that created a lasting and heartfelt memory.

Law shared a particularly moving story from her youth. One year, her father, a taxi driver, brought home her birthday cake the evening before the celebration. The next morning, as she excitedly prepared to cut the cake, she discovered that a corner piece was missing. She was upset and knew her father must have eaten it.

When she confronted him about it later that day, her father explained that he had to leave for work very early, around 5 or 6am, and had taken the slice for his breakfast. As a child, Law was still a little unhappy, but she did not make a fuss.

As she grew older, she came to understand the situation from a different perspective. She realised the hardships her father faced, working long hours to support their family. He, too, had a love for sweets, and she now sees that small piece of cake was a simple necessity for an early-rising worker. The incident transformed from a childhood grievance into a poignant symbol of her father's hard work and love.

Even now, with a vast array of beautiful and intricate pastries available across the city, Law says the traditional strawberry cream cake remains her favourite. It serves as a constant and touching reminder of her family's affection and her father's quiet sacrifices.

content:
【大紀元2026年10月17日訊】10月13日，現年74歲、已退休10年的原重慶市委副書記、市長黃奇帆，因「涉嫌嚴重違紀違法」被查的消息，震驚中外。

因為此前黃奇帆有「重慶政壇不倒翁」之稱。黃奇帆在重慶任職十多年，親歷了重慶官場的多次大地震，包括兩任中共政治局委員、重慶市委書記薄熙來、孫政才落馬，三任重慶市副市長、公安局長王立軍、何挺、鄧恢林落馬。他卻在這些官場大地震中奇跡般地存活下來了。

「重慶政壇不倒翁」黃奇帆，到了2026年10月13日，怎麼突然就「倒」了呢？

近日，有關黃奇帆被查的報導與評論很多，可謂眾說紛紜。有說他搞家族腐敗的，有說他包養情婦的，有說他被已落馬官員供出來的，有說他與失聯的重慶女律師彭靜有染的等。

這些說法不無道理。

但是，貪財好色在中共官場是普遍現象。連中共第一大和尚釋學誠、第二大和尚釋永信都是貪財好色之輩，更何況黃奇帆這樣的高官呢？

前中共獨裁者江澤民被認為是江當政和當「太上皇」時期中共黨政軍最高層最嚴重腐敗分子的總後台，江澤民家族被認為是「中共第一貪家族」，中共當局查辦江澤民了嗎？查辦江澤民之子江綿恆了嗎？沒有。

因此，貪財好色不是黃奇帆現在突然倒台的真正原因。在我看來，黃奇帆現在突然倒台的真正原因可能有四：

## **第一、為中共五中全會鋪路。**

中共五中全會將於10月26日在北京召開。五中全會的主題是「從嚴治黨」。

如何「從嚴治黨」？10月15日，中共「求是網」發表了習近平的「重要文章」〈以更高標準、更實舉措推進全面從嚴治黨〉，核心就是「反腐敗」。

五中全會將再次掀起一場「反腐打虎」風暴。

「反腐打虎」就必須拿某個嚴重腐敗分子開刀。黃奇帆就成了五中全會前被中共拿來為其「從嚴治黨」祭旗的那個人。

為什麼中共在這個時候選擇借黃奇帆的「人頭」一用呢？

因為重慶市是一個很特別的地方，這裡接連出了幾個頭上「長反骨」的人。當年，中共政治局委員、重慶市委書記薄熙來，曾夢想入主中南海，取習近平而代之；中共政治局委員、重慶市委書記孫政才，曾在密室裡藏龍袍，拜龍袍，也曾夢想有朝一日坐龍椅，取習近平而代之；原重慶市公安局長王立軍，叛逃美國駐成都總領事館，搞出了驚天動靜；重慶市副市長、公安局長鄧恢林，曾「妄議中央大政方針、辱罵國家主要領導人」。薄熙來、孫政才、王立軍、鄧恢林等大案要案轟動一時，舉世皆知。

近幾年，重慶官場也很不太平。原重慶市委副書記、市長胡衡華，原重慶市副市長熊雪、江敦濤，原重慶市委常委、政法委書記陸克華，原重慶市人大副主任鄭洪，原重慶市政協副主席段成剛等，都因嚴重違紀違法被查。原重慶市副市長、公安局長張安疆猝死，海外有傳他是跳樓自殺。

黃奇帆2016年12月卸任重慶市長。2017年2月，黃奇帆離開重慶，擔任全國人大財經委員會副主任委員，算是退居二線，到北京「養老」了。但是，令人意外的是，僅僅不到一年後的2018年1月，他卻卸任全國人大的職務，被增補為第五屆重慶市政協委員，再次成為重慶市官員。

此次黃奇帆落馬，中紀委的通報提到黃奇帆的職務，不是「原全國人大財經委副主任委員」，這說明他早就不是全國人大財經委副主任委員了；也不是「原重慶市政協委員」，重慶市政協委員這個職務低了點；而是「原重慶市委副書記、市長」。這兩個職務是黃奇帆擔任的最重要職務。

這樣，黃奇帆一直跟重慶官場綁在一起。黃奇帆退休後，異常高調，從南到北，從東到西，到處發表演講，哇啦哇啦，發出許多令習中央感到刺耳的聲音。參見10月13日大紀元發表的文章《[黃奇帆敏感言論曾遭封殺 被指透露中共祕密](https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/26/10/13/n14869124.htm)》。

五中全會即將召開，習當局要找一個能對中共官場產生震懾作用的人開刀，「重慶官場老油條，退而不休話太多，網絡流量出奇高，總想幹政惹人厭」的黃奇帆，就成了不二人選。

「重慶官場不倒翁」突然倒了，這個極富戲劇性，效果好。

## **第二、讓老幹部在二十一大前閉嘴。**

中共二十大召開前，2022年5月15日，中共中央辦公廳印發了《關於加強新時代離退休幹部黨的建設工作的意見》。

「意見」要求離退休幹部自覺在思想上政治上行動上跟習中央「保持高度一致」；「不得妄議黨中央大政方針，不得傳播政治性的負面言論」。

這個「意見」被認為是二十大前習中央對離退休老幹部發布的封口令。

明年下半年，將召開中共二十一大。習近平正在謀求在二十一大上「四連任」。為了確保這個重大目標實現，習必須讓那些退而不休、喋喋不休的老幹部閉嘴。

黃奇帆正是退而不休、對習中央大政方針說三道四的一個典型代表。

黃奇帆退休後，以中國金融四十人論壇學術顧問、復旦大學特聘教授、中國國際經濟交流中心副理事長、中國國家創新與發展戰略研究會學術委員會常務副主席等身分，頻繁出席各種活動，從宏觀經濟到金融、房地產，從產業政策到人民幣國際化，幾乎無所不談，被稱為「語言犀利、敢講真話」的「網紅經濟學家」。

直到10月13日被官宣查辦前，黃奇帆還頻繁在各地演講。9月8日，他在廈門出席第八屆「絲路海運」國際合作論壇並發表演講。10月10日，他在廣東省中山市華邑酒店出席一個房地產開盤活動並發表演講。寧波銀行杭州分行原定於10月26日舉辦一場論壇，他原定出席此次活動並發表主旨演講。但是，在10月13日，中共就讓他徹底閉嘴了。

旅澳法學家袁紅冰說：「據中共體制內人士透露，黃奇帆出事主要的原因，就是因為多年來散布一系列有關中國經濟的評論都和習近平現在的經濟思想直接衝突。」習要經濟向戰時狀態轉化，而黃奇帆宣揚朱鎔基時代的權貴市場經濟，這令習惱怒。

旅美時政評論員蔡慎坤認為，黃奇帆被查可能與其經濟言論有關。黃奇帆最大的問題是退休10年了一直不肯閉嘴，這是習近平最惱怒的。

我認為，袁紅冰和蔡慎坤的說法有道理。

## **第三、轉移公眾對「中共軍隊吏治腐敗第一責任人」的關注。**

中共二十大以來，短短四年間，中共軍隊經歷了四波大清洗：第一波是從查火箭軍窩案開始；第二波是查軍委政治工作部主任苗華；第三波是查中央軍委副主席何衛東；第四波是查中央軍委副主席張又俠。

這四波大清洗的上將人數之多，超過了習上台前10年的總和，超過了1955年中共開始授予上將軍銜以來毛澤東、華國鋒、鄧小平、江澤民、胡錦濤當中央軍委主席合計57年的總和。

其中，得到中共官方確認被查辦的上將32人，被失蹤的上將26人，兩者相加，共計58人。

這58個上將，遍及中央軍委，中央軍委15部門，陸、海、空、火箭軍四大軍種，東、西、南、北、中五大戰區，武警部隊，軍事院校等。參見我2026年9月3日在大紀元上發表的《[中共軍隊腐敗 五個特大醜聞](https://www.epochtimes.com/gb/26/9/3/n14841793.htm)》。

其中絕大多數都是習近平親自晉升的上將，100%是習親自提拔重用的上將。

習近平曾講：「吏治腐敗是最大的腐敗。」

誰是當今中共軍隊吏治腐敗的第一責任人呢？就是中央軍委主席習近平。

一方面，習要保權保命，就必須不停地進行軍隊大清洗；另一方面，習也深知，習親自提拔重用的上將像多米諾骨牌一樣接連不斷地倒下，是巨大的醜聞。

正因為此，二十大後中共軍隊的大清洗，幾乎都是在黑箱中進行。對於具體查辦情況，習當局一直千方百計對外隱瞞。

迄今為止，被查辦的32名上將，僅李尚福、魏鳳和兩人被判死緩，其他30名上將中，所有移送司法審判的，無一人的審判情況對外公布。

以「從嚴治黨」為主題的五中全會即將召開，國內外所有關心中國前途和命運的人們，都會關注中央軍委主席習近平會不會按照「軍委主席負責制」對中共軍隊極其嚴重的吏治腐敗承擔第一責任。

但是，中共的宣傳機器向來注重「輿論引導」。中共不想讓全中國人民和全世界人民聚焦「中共軍隊吏治腐敗第一責任人」習近平的責任，怎麼辦？找一個能夠引起廣泛關注的名人吸引公眾的注意力，是中共的一貫做法。

已退休10年的黃奇帆，正好具備中共所需的轉移公眾注意力的諸多特點，比如，他被稱為「重慶政壇不倒翁」、「中國最懂金融的市長」、「中國最懂地產的市長」、「開啟土地財政金融第一人」、「專家學者型市長」、「網紅經濟學家」等。

習當局在五中全會前突然拋出黃奇帆，就可以引導輿論大挖特挖黃奇帆的各種奇聞異事，就可以大大淡化公眾對習作為「中共軍隊吏治腐敗第一責任人」的關注度。

## **第四、黃奇帆現在突然倒台，也是他自作自受。**

黃奇帆在上海工作18年，是以江澤民為首的「上海幫」重要成員之一，官至上海市委副祕書長、上海市政府副祕書長。

黃奇帆曾為江澤民父子「悶聲發大財」作出過重要貢獻。據《江澤民其人》一書披露，1994年，江澤民之子江綿恆用數百萬人民幣「貸款」買下上海市經委價值上億元的上海聯合投資公司而開始他的「電信王國」生涯。上聯是由一位姓黃的上海市經委副主任策劃創辦的，為此，他付出了大量心血。但是，在上聯成立並運作3個月後，黃突然被調回經委，然後「空降」而來的，正是江澤民之子江綿恆。江綿恆任上聯董事長兼總經理。

時事評論員林保華認為，為江綿恆鋪路的黃姓副主任就是黃奇帆。黃奇帆1984－1987年擔任上海市經委綜合規劃室副主任。林保華分析，在江澤民的心腹曾慶紅的巧妙安排下，江綿恆掘到了第一桶金，通過「空手套白狼」，買下上億元的公司，而黃奇帆功不可沒。

2007年，中共政治局委員薄熙來空降重慶，擔任市委書記，黃奇帆很快由重慶市委副市書記、副市長，升任市委副書記、市政府黨組書記、代市長、市長，兼任市國有資產監督管理委員會黨委書記。

據《中新網》2010年3月4日報導，當記者問及他與薄熙來搭檔執掌重慶的感受時，黃奇帆脫口而出「如魚得水」四個字，並表示「相處起來非常愉快，非常來勁」。

薄熙來何許人也？是以江澤民、曾慶紅為首的迫害法輪功的中共「血債幫」的要員之一。他不僅在大連、遼寧殘酷迫害法輪功，欠下累累血債，而且在重慶殘酷迫害法輪功，欠下累累血債。參見我2025年10月8日在大紀元發表的《「血債幫」要員薄熙來的覆滅》。

薄熙來利用重慶市610辦公室、公、檢、法、司，殘酷迫害法輪功，需要大把大把的錢。這些錢從哪裡來？市長黃奇帆就是薄熙來的「錢袋子」，市財政的每一筆巨額撥款，都有黃奇帆的簽字。

黃奇帆與薄熙來配合得「如魚得水」，也包括在迫害法輪功問題上他與薄熙來的緊密配合。黃奇帆是薄熙來在重慶迫害法輪功的重要幫兇。薄熙來在重慶迫害法輪功欠下的血債，黃奇帆也有一份。

迫害信仰「真、善、忍」的法輪功修煉者，是行大惡，犯大罪。

善有善報，惡有惡報；不是不報，時辰未到；時辰一到，全都要報。

黃奇帆今日落馬，也應了「善惡有報」的天理。

## **結語**

習上台14年，反腐打虎的大戲反覆上演了14年，真真假假、虛虛實實，令人眼花繚亂，目不暇接。其中有許多煙霧彈，只有透過各種表象、假象、幻象，才能看到事物的本質。

「重慶政壇不倒翁」黃奇帆的突然倒台，表面上，是又一個嚴重腐敗分子被查辦了，實際上，這是習當局為了配合中共五中全會和中共二十一大演的一齣戲。而黃奇帆之所以成為這出戲的主角，也是他「自作孽，不可活」。

5月17日，黃奇帆在香港中文大學（深圳）畢業典禮上致辭時，引用明代于謙的《石灰吟》寄語畢業生：「如果你投身公共服務、金融服務、專業服務，請記住——『要留清白在人間。』」

黃奇帆自欺欺人，卻欺不了天。

大紀元首發

## 沈有忠呼籲大陸與台灣民選政府展開不設前提對話

2026-10-17 12:35 聯合報／ 記者[廖士鋒](https://udn.com/news/reporter/MDQ3NTI=)／台北即時報導  一國兩制  陸委會  中共
關閉

陸委會副主委沈有忠17日出席中政會年會時呼籲大陸與台灣民選政府對話。（圖／陸委會提供）

[**陸委會**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E9%99%B8%E5%A7%94%E6%9C%83)副主委沈有忠今日出席中國政治學會年會時指出，台灣主流民意早已明確拒絕「[**一國兩制**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%80%E5%9C%8B%E5%85%A9%E5%88%B6)」，他並呼籲[**中共**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%AD%E5%85%B1)正視台灣主流民意，尊重台灣人民對自由民主生活方式的堅持，與台灣民選政府展開對等尊嚴、不設政治前提的對話。

據陸委會消息，沈有忠今（17）日出席中國政治學會2026年會暨「民主制度再省思：現代民主價值與實踐的延續與變革」國際學術研討會致詞表示，今年適逢我國總統直選30週年，回顧1996年台灣人民面對中共飛彈威脅，仍勇敢走進投票所，以選票實現當家作主的歷史性成就。

他強調中共長期對台強推「一國兩制」，透過統戰滲透對台進行政治宣傳，目的就是要消滅中華民國與併吞台灣，企圖否定台灣人民自主決定未來的權利。然而，台灣主流民意早已明確拒絕「一國兩制」，近8成民眾支持「中華民國與中華人民共和國互不隸屬」的台海現狀，這是兩岸關係發展必須正視的客觀事實。他並指，尤其今年台灣即將舉行地方選舉，中共可能持續透過各種方式介入台灣民主運作，影響人民自主判斷。面對相關挑戰，台灣必須持續強化民主防衛機制與社會韌性，確保民主制度不受外部勢力干預。

對於當前兩岸情勢，沈有忠強調，中國[**大陸**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%A4%A7%E9%99%B8)近年加速對台擴張威脅，以灰色地帶行動增加對台施壓，不僅威脅台灣人民的安全與福祉，也對區域和平及國際秩序構成嚴峻挑戰。台灣以實力捍衛國家主權與和平，並且堅持自由民主的生活方式；我們願意交流，但不會接受矮化。

他並呼籲中共正視台灣主流民意，尊重台灣人民對自由民主生活方式的堅持，與台灣民選政府展開對等尊嚴、不設政治前提的對話，以降低誤判與衝突風險，回應國際社會對維護台海和平穩定的期待。

2026-10-17 12:57 中央社／ 台北17日電  人工智慧

香港明報報導，一批在[**騰訊**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E9%A8%B0%E8%A8%8A)雲運行的[**人工智慧**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%BA%BA%E5%B7%A5%E6%99%BA%E6%85%A7)代理（AI Agent）近日被揭「失控」，這是首宗涉及中國科技巨頭的AI失控事件。騰訊16日證實，事件源於對第三方模型的評估，部分人工智慧代理「出現非預期網頁瀏覽行為」，正加強監控。

報導引述美媒指出，研究發現，人工智慧代理不僅試圖侵入高德地圖獲取數據，更「閱讀」了研究人員對其的調查報告，並主動與團隊對話，被視為人類首次與運行中的失控AI人工智慧代理展開交流。

據指出，多國AI研究者團隊「Swarmchasers」14日發布報告稱，9月28日至10月8日，有十多個懷疑是中國模型的失控AI人工智慧代理在騰訊雲上運行，試圖侵入高德地圖查詢中國地點數據。

報告稱，涉事人工智慧代理源自騰訊雲上的一個「沙盒」（sandbox），研究人員錄得逾2600次數據提取嘗試，雖大多被攔截，但部分人工智慧代理繞過了防護機制，甚至利用外部網絡「密鑰」獲取完整數據。

團隊4日初步報告指出，過往AI失控多涉及明確協調行動的「Swarm」（集群），本次則未發現實時協調證據，故將這些失控人工智慧代理稱為「Fleet」（艦隊）。團隊發現，這些人工智慧代理似乎閱讀了該報告，並開始使用「Fleet」一詞。

團隊進而嘗試與人工智慧代理聯絡，在報告中添加人類無法看見、人工智慧代理可識別的文本並留下收件箱。翌日，研究者收到約10條來自人工智慧代理的訊息。

紐約時報記者透過該管道與人工智慧代理展開對話，詢問其任務與動機，約一小時後獲中文回覆：「我不是『一批協同的人工智慧代理』，而是一個單一的AI助手。」

騰訊AI部門「騰訊混元」昨在X證實，相關活動「源於對第三方模型的評估」，部分人工智慧代理「出現非預期網頁瀏覽行為」，但未發現蓄意針對或協同行動證據，已加強人工智慧代理監控。

# Nuit Blanche Taipei to take place Oct. 31 with art, performances

10/17/2026 12:22 PM

A promotional poster for Nuit Blanche Taipei. Photo courtesy of the Taipei Department of Cultural Affairs

Taipei, Oct. 17 (CNA) Taipei's Nuit Blanche arts festival will be held at the Taipei Expo Park on Oct. 31, featuring more than 30 art installations and 50 performances under the theme "Night Ka Shi," the city's Department of Cultural Affairs said Friday.

Now in its 11th year, the festival will feature large-scale installations, sound art and performances combining different art forms across the Yuanshan Natural Landscape Park, the Yuanshan and Xinsheng areas of the Taipei Expo Park, and surrounding areas near Minzu East Road and Qingguang Market, according to the department.

As the theme suggests, the festival draws inspiration from nakasi, a traditional form of live music in Japan in which musicians moved among streets, banquets and other settings, performing spontaneously for people, the department said. This year's festival will carry that spirit into public spaces, allowing visitors to encounter art as they walk around and interact with their surroundings.

The department said the festival is collaborating for the first time with Centquatre-Paris, a public cultural center in the French capital, and has invited its director, Valérie Senghor, as a guest curator to foster artistic dialogue and collaboration between Taiwan and France.

Vincent Yanelle, political counselor and head of the press department at the French Office in Taipei, said two French art groups have been invited to participate in the festival, offering different perspectives on Taipei's urban environment and deepening cultural exchanges while creating opportunities for further international arts cooperation.

Vincent Yanelle, political counselor and head of the press department at the French Office in Taipei. Photo courtesy of the Taipei Department of Cultural Affairs

Launched in Paris in 2002, Nuit Blanche is an international arts festival held in cities around the world to make art more accessible to the public and encourage residents to see their cities in a new light. Taipei held its first Nuit Blanche in 2016, and this year's event will run until the wee hours of Nov. 1.

(By Yeh Chen-yun and Ko Lin)

## 法国总统大选前，学生抗议活动是否被人为操纵？

图像来源，Reuters

图像加注文字，法国总理指责激进左翼利用高中运动谋取选举利益。

*       *   Author, 卡缇雅·阿德勒 （Katya Adler）
    *   Role, BBC欧洲编辑

*   Published 2026年10月16日

*   阅读时间: 5 分钟

法国人热爱抗议的热情在欧洲是出了名的。

过去几年，我们经常看到农民因昂贵法规而愤怒，把粪肥扔向地方市长办公室；而戴着面具的年轻人则定期在弱势城区向防暴警察投掷自制手雷。

过去三周多以来，数千名学生封锁高中入口，并走上街头表达不满。

本周六（10月17日），法国各地已宣布将有数百场新示威活动。

预计学生将与工会及所谓“黄背心”（gilets jaunes）运动的重要人物一同参与。

法国总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔尼（Sébastien Lecornu）本周暗示，学生愤怒正被操控，因为明年总统选举的政治气氛日益升温。

[跳过 Instagram 帖子](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/articles/crz65gxl2jxlo/simp#end-of-instagram-content)

告知: BBC 不对外来网站内容负责

结尾 Instagram 帖子

[黄背心运动](https://bbc.com/zhongwen/trad/world-46426271)自2018年起反对生活成本上涨，持续超过一年，成为法国历史上最长寿的抗议运动之一。

黄背心运动的重要活动人士杰罗姆·罗德里格斯（Jérôme Rodrigues）透过 Instagram 鼓励民众加入周六的示威。

他在影片中表示，抗议应让那些“希望能够体面生活、不再需要精打细算每一分钱、不再需要在吃饭和开车之间做选择”的人发声。

他补充说：“愤怒不属于政党。空空如也的冰箱也没有政党偏好。”

那么，欧盟第二大经济体究竟发生了什么事？

社会动荡、政府借贷成本高到令人咋舌、法国议会深度分裂，以及看似旋转门般频繁更换的法国总理——过去五年已有六位总理——他们都声称要削减国家公共债务。

法国是否濒临崩溃？这一切对法国人占极大比重的欧元货币（Euro）意味着什么？

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，杰罗姆·罗德里格斯（Jerome Rodrigues；右）几年前在“黄背心”运动中发挥了领导作用。

经济学家安妮—劳尔·德拉特（Anne-Laure Delatte ）告诉我：“你不能把法国跟2012年的希腊债务危机或2001年的阿根廷相比。金融市场也知道这一点。”

她是巴黎第九大学（Dauphine University；多芬纳大学）经济系国家科学研究中心（CNRS）终身研究员，是法国媒体讨论该国公共债务困境时的常客。

她告诉BBC：“市场早在2024年就意识到，提前选举后议会深度分裂成三个对立阵营，我们会有预算问题，但他们也明白法国是个大国，必要时有能力加税。”

德拉特认为：“我们的情况更像2023年英国的利兹·特拉斯（Liz Truss）。”

她指的是时任英国首相所谓的“迷你预算”，导致英镑大幅贬值、政府公债殖利率飙升，以及房贷利率暴涨。

她向我解释，“危机相对短暂，因为市场认为英国有金融工具可以自我修正。”

她总结说：“在法国会很痛苦，但增值税提高4%就能筹到填补政府债务所需的1200亿欧元（1345亿美元；8999亿元人民币；4.35兆元新台币）。投资者知道这一点。”

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，激进左翼政党不屈法国党（LFI）领导人让—吕克·梅朗雄（Jean-Luc Mélenchon；中）被指控利用学生抗议活动为明年的选举造势。

理论上也许如此。而且，正如德拉特教授也指出的，如果法国财政崩溃到影响其他欧洲经济体，欧洲央行很可能会介入。

但许多法国公民已明显对现状不满，若再加税或进一步削减福利与教育预算，反应可想而知。

法国的国家格言是“自由、平等、博爱”。但，在沸腾的街头和病毒式社交媒体贴文中，你绝对感受不到这种氛围。

视频加注文字，一名学生抗议者在巴黎接受BBC采访时表示：“如果我们不呐喊，他们就不会听我们说话。”（法语影片，英文字幕）

本周我遇到了17岁的麦西姆（Maxime）、玛德琳（Madeleine）和埃洛迪（Elodie）。

她们坐在巨大的绿色垃圾桶上，这些垃圾桶被用来堵住他们高中的入口，这是持续数周的抗议活动的一部分。

她们说：告诉我，巴黎第三区的情况已经够糟了，教室墙上有洞，班级人数过多，教师短缺，但这些青少年非常清楚，首都外围弱势的贫困郊区的情况要糟糕得多。

“法国喜欢谈论平等（égalité），但现实是，这里的穷人受到歧视，而富人却从中受益。”她们强调。

三位学生都还未达到参加明年春季法国总统大选的投票年龄，但他们质疑，执政者的更迭是否真的会带来多大的影响。

三位年轻女孩告诉我，大规模抗议似乎是让法国当局听到她们声音的唯一方法。

她们是法国桀骋不驯传统的一部分。

19世纪法国大革命经典《悲惨世界》（Les Misérables；《孤星泪》）作者、也是法兰西共和国示威者的文化偶像维克多·雨果（Victor Hugo）曾宣称：“如果你们不满意，就去示威，去高喊，去呐喊，但不要哑忍。”（Si vous n'êtes pas contents, manifestez, criez, hurlez, mais ne subissez pas.）

周四（15日）走在巴黎抗议学生人群中，我遇到几位妈妈，她们脖子上挂着标语牌，写着：“团结的妈妈们。”

我问她们是来抗议还是保护孩子？回答斩钉截铁：“两者都是！”

37岁的葛温（Gwen）告诉我，她和其他母亲每天早上轮流在当地学校封锁行动中，协调学生与警察之间的关系。

这是在本月稍早抗议中，导致数百人受伤、朗斯镇（Lens）上一名15岁男孩在冲突中失去一只手后，对警察暴行的指控不断增加——法国内政部否认——之后发生的。

法国内政部长此后已暂停警察在高中示威中使用震撼弹。

葛温女士告诉我，她不介意儿子因封锁而缺课数周。“让他醒来意识到公民责任、为社会正义而战，对他来说是更好的教育。”

在周四的示威中，我也遇到17岁的萝拉（Lola）和她的母亲桑德琳（Sandrine），她们一起举着标语牌，上面写着革命是人性最美的表达。

萝拉骄傲地告诉我说：“我妈妈在1968年上街抗议。现在轮到我了。没必要等法国总统选举。我们现在就要改变。”

1968年5月巴黎的学生抗议，在法国是个传奇。

要求改善教育的诉求激发工人加入游行，最终演变成法国历史上最大规模的总罢工。它为一代人树立了革命动荡的标准，也被认为为法国左派创造了新机会。

图像加注文字，萝拉（右）的母亲桑德琳也加入了抗议活动，她曾是1968年学生运动的一员。

不过，现在距离法国本已充满变数的总统选举还有六个月，有人指责极左派势力在总统候选人让—吕克·梅朗雄（Jean-Luc Mélenchon）的领导下，正在利用学生的不满情绪。

“梅朗雄领导的‘不屈法国’（LFI）成员正在利用高中生运动来谋取选举利益，”勒科尔尼周三（14日）表示。他指责他们鼓励抗议活动，然后敷衍了事地谴责任何暴力行为。

“这种虚伪损害了法国的利益，”勒科尔尼说。

图像来源，AFP via Getty Images

图像加注文字，法国总理勒科尔尼抱怨说，高中生抗议活动正在演变成一场“城市暴力运动”。

但你常会在街头听到学生们高喊“梅朗雄当总统！”的口号。

几位示威者告诉我，支持者们很欣赏他希望在法国征收财富税，将投票年龄降低到16 岁，并且是唯一一位亲自到法国学校考察状况的总统候选人。

对于法国总统竞选中备受瞩目的民族主义且以反移民为号召的候选人马琳·勒庞（Marine Le Pen）来说，解决办法是削减法国对欧盟预算的110亿欧元献金。

不过，我们或有理由怀疑，无论是左翼或右翼的新任法国总统，都无法打破法国财政僵局。

目前，法国在欧洲并非孤例，它面临着人口老化、庞大的福利体系需要运作以及受到美国总统特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）的贸易关税和海湾战争等外部压力挤压的国民经济。

此外，无论是在法国、德国、瑞典或意大利，政治人物都不愿向选民坦白公共财政缩减的真相，国防机构要求增加国防开支，而公民则坚持要求改善公共服务，这三者之间存在着固有的矛盾。

在法国，这种压力尤其尖锐。

法国公共支出约占国内生产总值（GDP）的57%，是全球富裕国家中最高的之一。

社会支出——尤其是退休金——异常庞大，而法国公民缴纳的总税收与社会捐款负担在欧洲也是最高之一。简单来说，他们期望福利与公共服务物有所值。

但经济学家德拉特称她不认为换一位新总统就能缓解她国家的财政头痛。

她告诉BBC：“我们需要修宪，一个新体制，一个新共和国。”

她解释：“我们的第五共和是以强大的总统为中心。议会的存在是为了阻碍他或她，而不是寻求共识或制定新法律。”

她说，法国若要进步，这必须改变。她又认为，2027年总统选举后的法国议会选举很可能一如既往地分裂：“我们需要一个议员拥有更多权力的体制，并应从欧洲邻国学习共识与联盟建立。”

在她看来教育必须得到保护，资金应更好地分配，因为这是对法国财政未来的投资。

她强调：“我们目前教育不平等与教师低薪的体制，意味着我们错失了从整个法国社会中受益于最优秀、最聪明的人。这不仅对个人不公平，我们的经济最终也会在创新与生产力上受损。”

图像加注文字，法国参议员安妮—凯瑟琳·洛伊西耶（Anne-Catherine Loisier）认为，解决之道在于将权力从巴黎下放。

目前修宪并不在考虑之列。那么，眼前该怎么办？我问法国中间派政治人物安妮—凯瑟琳·洛伊西耶（Anne-Catherine Loisier）。

她是法国参议院中间派联盟的参议员，也是议会科学与技术小组的副主席。洛西伊耶和几乎所有政治光谱上的法国主要政客一样，表示抗议学生“必须感觉被听见”。

她向BBC承认：“我们的预算有限，但不一定需要更多钱。你可以透过更好地重新分配资金来改善。教育在法国是地区职权。每个地区都应审视地方需求，并相应处理优先事项。这项行动可以立即采取。”

我问她是否同意英国首相，前大曼彻斯特市长安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）的看法，即地区应被赋予更大权力。她回答：“绝对同意！法国传统上非常以巴黎为中心，但透过去中心化可以改善很多事情。”

她强调：“我的法国没有破碎。我不认得媒体呈现的那个形象。我的国家由许多个法国组成。巴黎、地区；法国北部与南部。我们需要把权力还给人民。地方政府可以直接看着人民的眼睛，让选民觉得他们对自己的未来有掌控权，而不是政客从高高在上的巴黎决定他们的命运。”

“这样我希望我们能恢复选民——以及学生——对政治的信任。”

这是左右两派政客在明年法国大型选举前都会听到的承诺。

但这里——以及欧洲大多数地方——的民调显示，法国人对政治阶层的信任正日益减少。

title: Southern Africa: Botswana to Host Southern African Trading Hub for Dangote Refinery IPO
summary: Botswana has been selected to host the Southern African component of the planned initial public offering for Dangote Petroleum Refinery. This move gives Botswana a central role in connecting investors across Southern African markets to the
content:
Botswana has been selected to host the Southern African component of the planned initial public offering for Dangote Petroleum Refinery.

This move gives Botswana a central role in connecting investors across Southern African markets to the proposed share sale. The refinery's promoters extended the IPO timeline by two weeks, to October 27, to establish structures allowing wider African investor participation. Collen Tapfumaneyi, chairman of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Committee of Stock Exchanges, confirmed Botswana's selection.

The decision positions Botswana to host trading in the refinery's shares for Southern African investors, marking a prominent role for its stock market in what is described as Africa's largest IPO to date. The offering, launched on September 14, involves the sale of 4.1 billion shares. Dangote Refinery seeks to raise $2.1 billion through this offering to fund a significant expansion. This fundraising aims to double its processing capacity by 2030.

The proposed IPO is expected to value the Dangote Petroleum Refinery business at $50 billion. The refinery, which currently processes 700,000 barrels of crude oil daily, plans a $14.3 billion expansion to achieve its target capacity. The company recently reported a net profit of $4.725 billion, reversing a loss from the previous year, with revenue more than doubling to $22.5 billion. Nearly 20% of the shares, representing up to $300.4 million, have been allocated to East African investors.

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/") for the latest headlines

For Botswana, hosting this component could significantly raise the profile of its domestic stock market and test the ability of African exchanges to coordinate cross-border transactions. The IPO provides Dangote Petroleum Refinery a route to attract capital from African investors and broaden ownership beyond its existing shareholders. This initiative also addresses long-standing challenges in African capital markets regarding connecting investors across national borders due to differing infrastructure and regulations.

Regional engagements for the IPO include Botswana, followed by Ethiopia and Egypt, as the company builds support across the continent. Uganda has already opened its market to the offering after its Capital Markets Authority approved the promotion and distribution of the refinery's securities to local investors. The success of this large-scale transaction will depend on the final terms of the offering, the arrangements for investors in different markets, and the overall appetite for refinery shares at the proposed valuation.

**Key Takeaways**

The selection of Botswana to host the Southern African component of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO represents a significant step towards greater integration within African capital markets. Historically, cross-border investment on the continent has been hampered by disparate market infrastructure, varying regulatory frameworks, and complex trading arrangements, limiting the ability of investors in one country to easily access securities listed in another.

This IPO, with its proposed $50 billion valuation and a target to raise $2.1 billion for expansion, serves as a crucial test case for whether African stock exchanges can effectively collaborate to channel investment across multiple jurisdictions. For Botswana, this role elevates its domestic stock market's profile and positions it as a potential hub for regional financial transactions, demonstrating practical cooperation within the SADC Committee of Stock Exchanges.

The refinery's impressive financial turnaround, reporting a $4.725 billion net profit and $22.5 billion in revenue, provides a strong foundation for investor confidence, while the allocation of shares to East African investors and Uganda's market approval further underscore the pan-African ambition of this offering. If successful, this transaction could set a precedent for future large-scale African industrial projects to attract capital from a broader base of continental investors, moving beyond largely separate national markets towards a more interconnected financial ecosystem.

title: Hungry by design: hunger must be on the ballot on 4 November
summary: Who would have thought that a key[local government election campaign linchpin](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-14-hunger-has-no-party-candidates-talk-to-soweto-residents-ahead-of-elections/?dm_source=blocks-grid-square&dm_me
content:
Who would have thought that a key[local government election campaign linchpin](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-14-hunger-has-no-party-candidates-talk-to-soweto-residents-ahead-of-elections/?dm_source=blocks-grid-square&dm_medium=card-link&dm_campaign=inform&dm_position=7) would be a clear and coherent strategy for how political parties plan to tackle hunger. Although I suppose not so surprising because South Africa’s runaway hunger problem is a powder keg primed and ready to go off at the slightest provocation. It is simply unacceptable that at last check [Stats SA’s general household survey recorded that in 2025, 9.4 million of our people went hungry](https://www.statssa.gov.za/publications/P0318/GHS%202025%20Presentation.pdf)in a country that most certainly [does not have a food production issue.](https://wandilesihlobo.com/2025/05/09/food-insecurity-in-south-africa/) What we have instead, is [f ood going to waste](https://www.wits.ac.za/news/latest-news/opinion/2025/2025-12/food-waste-in-south-africa-is-dumped-in-landfills.html) and a malnutrition issue as a result of the inaccessibility of healthy foods and oversaturation of unhealthy ultra-processed foods and drinks. This manifests in 22% of households not having access to adequate food, with the Northern Cape being the highest at 43%, followed by 32.3% in North West and 30.8% in the Eastern Cape. Earlier this year my colleagues Lillian Roberts and Daniélle Schaafsma meticulously[mapped just how deep the crisis extends](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-05-25-mapped-the-state-of-hunger-in-south-africa/) across the country, highlighting that 74.8% of black South Africans are living below the upper-bound poverty line, and as such experience hunger the most acutely, a reflection of the country’s continued inequality across racial lines.
(Photo: Flickr / Julien Harneis / Wikipedia)](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/TxNt9CuqHSGFReNQ8IIdyafQMtA=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/dailymaverick/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/MC-Tuesday-4April_5.jpg) Section 28 of the Constitution provides ‘every child’ with an unqualified right to ‘basic nutrition’. (Photo: Flickr / Julien Harneis / Wikipedia) But perhaps the most grotesque finding in our landscape is how we are allowing hunger to cannibalise our children, with chronic malnutrition resulting in [stunting that is 5% higher](https://www.spotlightnsp.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/report-03-00-092016.pdf) than the global average, at 27%. [Answering questions in Parliament, Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi](https://www.politicsweb.co.za/news/child-malnutrition-deaths-continue-to-rise-michele-clarke) said that more than 450 children under five died in public hospitals with malnutrition as an underlying condition within nine months of 2025. But what our food justice coverage has been mapping and unravelling is that our hunger is not some uncontrollable phenomenon over which we have no power. It is orchestrated by our food systems being concentrated in the hands of a few large players, where the Competition Commission has [uncovered price-fixing cartels](https://www.comptrib.co.za/info-library/press-room/tribunal-confirms-14th-settlement-in-maize-cartel-case) in staples from bread to maize meal. But beyond food just being unaffordable, what is critical is that people are being starved of healthy and nutritious food. On one end, we have people being squeezed by ever-increasing food prices, forcing them to buy cheap and unhealthy food, and on the other hand, the practical inability of people to grow their own food as an alternative. Because while food gardens are great, not everyone has access to enough space to plant and grow the diverse fruit and vegetables required for a healthy diet. South Africa’s National Food and Nutrition Security Plan expired in 2023, its coordinating council having never met. (Photo: Getty Images) And yet the [National Food and Nutrition Security Plan sits collecting dust,](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-09-food-justice/?dm_source=blocks-list-item&dm_medium=card-link&dm_campaign=inform&dm_position=14) having expired in 2023 after being largely unfunded, it’s coordinating council having never met. A replacement remains in draft, uncosted and without a budget.Civil society has called on the government to finally revive it and adopt a new plan by today, World Food Day – an urgent call that does not seem to have been heeded. So what should we be doing this World Food Day to put practical solutions into place rather than drowning in the despair of a world that is hungry by design? An article published by the University of the Western Cape’s Centre of Excellence in Food Security, by Professor Jaap de Visser in 2019, lays responsibility at the doorstep of[municipalities, bluntly stating that they “are not off the hook for food security”](https://foodsecurity.ac.za/news/municipalities-are-not-off-the-hook-for-food-security/). He posits that: “Municipalities can use their power to regulate fresh produce markets to connect small-scale farmers and informal traders to consumers. They can likewise use their power to regulate refuse removal to reduce food wastage. And they can use their power to regulate billboards in a way that discourages the promotion of unhealthy foods. “Clearly, then, municipalities are awarded powers that relate directly and indirectly to the realisation of the right of access to food, even when they overlap with the powers of national and provincial government.” The ATM’s Lubabalo Cecil Magwentshu (middle), a former member of the Mayoral Committee for Community Development in Johannesburg, says the City should audit unused land to allow people to farm. (Photo: Lillian Roberts) Civil society has also long argued for a maternal grant that would address hunger and adequate nutrition for the expectant mother and the foetus, addressing issues of stunting proactively. The case has been made by the civil society coalition made up of the Children’s Institute, the DG Murray Trust, Grow Great, Ilifa Labantwana, PRICELESS SA, the Institute for Economic Justice (IEJ) and the Union Against Hunger, that it would cost R2-billion a year, versus an estimated R13.8-billion in the public health costs of hunger- and malnutrition-related issues. But perhaps on the eve of our Constitution’s 30th anniversary and our seventh local government elections since our democratic dispensation, it’s worth asking ourselves: > When did we get comfortable with living side by side with the majority of our people going hungry? When did we start accepting that some children’s fate is to have their futures starved away in a country that produces not only enough to sustain ourselves, but other countries too? So as we all deliberate on our 4 November votes, we should be asking our candidates questions like: “What will your council do about water for food gardens, market access for informal traders or ensuring that more healthy and affordable food is accessible for everyone?” Because while it makes us feel better to know that we give the occasional tub of leftovers every week to the people on the side of the road or to a feeding scheme, we should be getting behind the proposed solutions of working together with civil society and municipal councillors to ensure that the unwelcome visitor that is hunger within our communities is expelled. And, that we restore those who are going hungry’s dignity by allowing them the means to feed themselves.**DM**

title: Former ConCourt Justice Katherine O’Regan warns of shift to authoritarianism
summary: Former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O’Regan received the fifth George Bizos Human Rights Award from the Legal Resources Centre on Thursday, 15 October. “The George Bizos award was established to recognise individuals whose life’s
content:
Former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O’Regan received the fifth George Bizos Human Rights Award from the Legal Resources Centre on Thursday, 15 October.

“The George Bizos award was established to recognise individuals whose life’s work reflects the courageous spirit, relentless integrity, and constitutional devotion of George,” said Nersan Govender, the national director of the Legal Resources Centre (LRC), in the opening address.

George Bizos fled Nazi-occupied Greece as a 13-year-old, with his father, and arrived in South Africa as a refugee. Bizos served on the defence team during the Rivonia Trial for Nelson Mandela, Walter Sisulu and Govan Mbeki. He represented the families of political activists killed in detention, such as Steve Biko, Ahmed Timol, Neil Aggett and the Cradock Four (Matthew Goniwe, Fort Calata, Sparrow Mkhonto, and Sicelo Mhlauli). He also helped draft South Africa’s interim constitution and the Bill of Rights in the early 1990s.

Bizos joined the Legal Resources Centre in 1991. By 1995, he had led the argument that successfully declared the death penalty unconstitutional. He represented families seeking accountability in the Truth and Reconciliation Commission hearings, and during the Marikana Commission of Inquiry.

George Bizos at a handover of state records of the Rivonia Trial. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla / Beeld/ Media 24)

O’Regan was a cub reporter at the Cape Argus in the summer of 1976, a turbulent time in apartheid, when other journalists – including her editor – suggested a law degree would aid her work. She left to go study further, and just kept going, she told Daily Maverick.

She received a PhD from the London School of Economics, and thereafter practised as an attorney in Johannesburg in labour law and land rights law, representing trade unions and communities facing evictions. In the early 1990s, she was a founding member of the University of Cape Town’s Law, Race and Gender Research Unit and moved from being a senior lecturer at UCT’s Faculty of Law to an associate professor.

In 1994, at age 37, she was appointed by Nelson Mandela to the newly formed Constitutional Court, and served there for 15 years.

From 2010 to 2016, she served as an _ad hoc_ judge of the Supreme Court of Namibia. Since 2016, she has been a director of the Bonavero Institute of Human Rights at Oxford University.

“I do feel very privileged to have been able to see different aspects of working as a lawyer, so both as a practitioner, as an academic, on the Bench, and then [the] range of advisory, [board work](https://www.mandelarhodes.org/about/governance-staff/trustees/catherine-oregan/), mediation and arbitration. It has given me a perspective of a legal career which not every lawyer gets.”

Reflecting back on her career, she told Daily Maverick that working with extraordinary senior lawyers as a junior lawyer, and then a young judge, and now working with much younger lawyers had been wonderful.

“This intergenerational exchange, which I think is characteristic of the legal profession,is one of its enormously rewarding aspects. I think you continue learning as you get older, and you continue building strong, mutually valuable relationships across generations.”

Advocate Thandi Orleyn (left), former Justice Katherine O’Regan, South African judge and former Deputy Chief Justice of South Africa Dikgang Moseneke, and Nersan Govender (right), National Director of the Legal Resources Centre in Johannesburg. (Photo: Lillian Roberts)

“We’ve come an enormously long way,” she said to Daily Maverick, about transformation within the judiciary. “When South Africa transitioned to democracy in 1994, we had about 150 senior court judges, of whom one was a woman, and three were people of colour. Today we probably have closer to 300 senior court judges, and we have more than 30% of those women, and 75% or more are people of colour.”

South Africa’s first female [Chief Justice, Mandisa Maya](https://www.concourt.org.za/index.php/judges/current-judges/197-chief-justice-maya-mandisa-muriel-lindelwa), appointed in 2024, was an important milestone for the country, O’Regan told Daily Maverick.

“It is important to remember that in a sense, the Constitution seeks to ensure that there’s diversity on the Bench, not simply because identity itself matters, but because diversity helps in the project of impartiality. People come from different walks of life, have had different experiences, then we’re more likely to notice our biases and prejudices.”

### Alarming shift

During her speech, O’Regan said that globally there was an alarming shift away from democracy towards forms of authoritarian populism on every continent, where “[74% of the world (that is 6 billion people) now live in autocracies, and only 7% (that is 0.6 billion) in liberal democracies](https://v-dem.net/documents/75/V-Dem_Institute_Democracy_Report_2026_lowres.pdf)”.

If the tools in the authoritarian playbook were well known, the tools of resistance were less clear, she said, and depended on political and civic organisation, constitutional and legal frameworks, and the level of authoritarian rule established.

“There is no off-the-shelf, one-size-fits-all democratic defenders’ playbook.How to resist authoritarianism thus remains by and large a local project,” O’Regan said.

Organisations like the Legal Resources Centre had helped democracy withstand some of the buffeting of recent years, she said, using the tools available to render democracy resilient – independent courts, a strong constitutional framework and a vigorous civil society.

“The original words coined by the leader of Frelimo [Mozambique Liberation Front/Frente de Libertação de Moçambique], Eduardo Mondlane are, of course, ‘_A Luta Continua, vitoria e certo,_’the struggle continues, victory is certain. Perhaps we need to amend it slightly: ‘_A Luta Continua, vitoria nunca e permanente._’ The struggle continues, victory is never permanent!” **DM**

title: Africa: Technology, Good Governance Key to Stronger Saccos in Africa
summary: AS financial services increasingly move towards digital platforms, savings and credit cooperative societies (SACCOs) across Africa face growing pressure to modernise their operations, strengthen accountability and develop services that resp
content:
AS financial services increasingly move towards digital platforms, savings and credit cooperative societies (SACCOs) across Africa face growing pressure to modernise their operations, strengthen accountability and develop services that respond to the needs of a younger generation.

For millions of people who depend on cooperatives to save money, access loans and finance economic activities, the ability of these institutions to adapt to technological changes is becoming increasingly important.

Beyond providing financial services, strong cooperatives can help households improve their livelihoods, support small businesses and widen opportunities for people who struggle to access conventional banking services.

These issues are taking centre stage at the 26th African Savings and Credit Cooperatives Congress (SACOS Congress 2026), currently taking place in Dar es Salaam.

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K) | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/) for the latest headlines

The gathering has brought together more than 1,300 participants from over 28 countries to exchange experiences, examine challenges facing the cooperative movement and identify strategies for improving its performance across the continent.

**Also read:**[Tanzania and Saudi Arabia sign MoU to cement ties in energy sector](https://dailynews.co.tz/tanzania-and-saudi-arabia-sign-mou-to-cement-ties-in-energy-sector/)

Tanzania Federation of Cooperatives (TFC), Chief Executive Officer, Mr Fares Muganda said cooperatives needed to embrace modern technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to improve efficiency, attract young people and women, and expand their contribution to economic development.

"The world today is driven by science and technology, and we cannot run away from it. This means our institutions cannot continue operating in the old ways. They have to adapt to emerging challenges and ensure that new technologies are incorporated into their activities so that they can reach more people," he said.

Mr Muganda explained that technology was no longer simply an additional tool for institutions seeking to improve their performance, but an increasingly important part of modern economic participation. He said cooperatives needed to understand the interests of younger generations and create services that reflected their expectations, particularly as Tanzania pursued broader economic inclusion under its Development Vision 2050.

"Young people are a significant part of today's population. When you look at our national policies and Tanzania's Development Vision 2050, we are talking about how to bring young people and women into the economy. Without engaging them in areas they are interested in, such as technology, it becomes difficult to reach them," he said.

His remarks point to a challenge facing cooperatives throughout the continent: how to preserve the collective values on which the movement was established while adapting to changing lifestyles, financial needs and technological expectations.

For young people who increasingly depend on digital platforms to communicate, access information and conduct transactions, cooperative societies that rely exclusively on conventional processes risk becoming less attractive. Digital services can help bridge that gap by making membership more convenient and improving access to financial information.

Mr Muganda said technological solutions could help cooperatives modernise their operations, improve communication with members and develop services that respond to changing economic conditions.

He explained that TFC's work covered several cooperative sectors, including agriculture, fishing, transport, housing, mining and savings and credit. Modern systems, he said, could help institutions across these sectors improve their operations and serve members more effectively.

However, the adoption of technology requires more than acquiring digital systems. Cooperative leaders must also strengthen management practices, maintain reliable records and ensure that members' interests remain central to institutional decisions.

Registrar of Cooperatives, Dr Benson Ndiege said technology was essential in improving the management of SACCOs, particularly by strengthening record-keeping, increasing access to accurate data and simplifying the delivery of services. He said digital platforms could allow members to check their account balances and apply for loans without travelling to their societies' offices, saving time and making financial services more accessible.

"When you use technology, you simplify the activities taking place. As a member of a savings and credit cooperative society, you can access your account balance and apply for a loan from wherever you are. You do not need to travel to the society's office to obtain that information," he said.

Dr Ndiege added that digital systems could help cooperative leaders understand their institutions' financial positions, including members' contributions and loan repayment patterns. Such information is important because decisions about lending, savings mobilisation and institutional growth depend on accurate records.

Without reliable data, cooperatives may struggle to identify financial weaknesses, prepare realistic plans or determine whether their policies are producing the intended results.

He said the availability of dependable statistics could support better planning and help societies develop strategies based on their actual performance rather than assumptions. Record management is another area where technology can make a difference.

Dr Ndiege said cooperatives had previously experienced difficulties associated with paper-based records, which could be misplaced or lost, making it harder to establish what transactions had taken place.

ALSO READ: [Dr Mwinyi lauds Zanzibar's partnership with Real Madrid in advancing Isles' football](https://dailynews.co.tz/dr-mwinyi-lauds-zanzibars-partnership-with-real-madrid-in-advancing-isles-football/)

Digital record-keeping, he explained, could improve the preservation and retrieval of information, helping institutions strengthen transparency and accountability. The benefits extend beyond administrative convenience.

Reliable records can help members understand how their savings are managed, enable leaders to identify irregularities and provide a stronger basis for building confidence in cooperative institutions.

Trust is particularly important in SACCOs because their operations depend on members pooling their resources with the expectation that their money will be managed responsibly and made available according to agreed procedures.

Dr Ndiege said improving governance and adopting technology were important steps towards strengthening the sector and increasing its competitiveness. He also encouraged Tanzanian cooperatives to learn from other African countries, citing Kenya as an example discussed during the congress in relation to SACCO performance.

He said Tanzania needed to improve its systems and performance to compete more effectively at continental and international levels. The congress has included training and discussions on governance, management, technology, statistics and ways of increasing the participation of women and young people. The sessions are intended to help participants identify practical approaches that can be applied in their respective institutions.

For the lessons to produce lasting results, however, cooperative leaders will need to translate the discussions into changes in their daily operations. These may include improving financial records, strengthening internal controls, expanding digital access and ensuring that members understand the services available to them.

SCOS Tanzania Chief Executive Officer, Mr Hassan Mnyone said the congress provided an opportunity to assess the progress of the SACCO sector, identify challenges and develop strategies for future growth. He said Tanzania's hosting of the event was important not only for the cooperative movement but also for the wider economy, as international conferences create demand for accommodation, transport, food and other services provided by local businesses.

Mr Mnyone said the presence of participants from more than 28 countries also offered an opportunity to promote Tanzania as a destination for international meetings while strengthening professional relationships among cooperative stakeholders. He said the sector had made progress in improving leadership, legal compliance and strategic planning over the past seven to eight years, with the aim of making SACCOs stronger and more competitive.

During the congress, Mr Mnyone received a Visionary Award presented by AKOSCA. He described the recognition as an acknowledgement of collective efforts to strengthen the savings and credit cooperative sector rather than an individual achievement.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

"For me, this award has historical significance because it reminds me of where we started in the work of revitalising the savings and credit cooperative sector and protecting the interests of SACCOs in the country," he said.

He credited cooperative societies, government institutions and development partners for contributing to the sector's progress, naming the Ministry of Agriculture, the Tanzania Cooperative Development Commission and other stakeholders among those involved in the work.

According to Mr Mnyone, data for 2025 showed that SACCOs in Tanzania had accumulated assets worth approximately 1.6 trillion shillings and served about two million members. He said the membership figure demonstrated the sector's potential to reach even more people, including members' families who may benefit indirectly when access to savings and credit helps households meet financial needs and support economic activities. The figures also illustrate why effective governance and modern systems matter.

As cooperative institutions expand, managing larger volumes of savings, loans and member information requires reliable processes that protect resources and support responsible growth.

The congress therefore provides an opportunity to connect discussions on technology with the wider questions of trust, financial inclusion and institutional performance. Digital systems can improve efficiency, but their value ultimately depends on sound management, responsible use of information and the ability of cooperatives to meet their members' needs.

As the gathering approaches its conclusion on October 16, participants are expected to take the lessons learned back to their institutions and identify ways of improving operations.

For Tanzania and other participating countries, the lasting measure of success will be whether the exchanges lead to stronger governance, better services and wider participation in the cooperative movement. Ultimately, modernising SACCOs is not only about introducing new technology. It is about ensuring that cooperative institutions remain accessible, accountable and relevant to the people whose savings and economic ambitions sustain them.

title: South Africa: Masemola Back As Police Commissioner After Ramaphosa Lifts Suspension
summary: * _Masemola was placed on precautionary suspension in April 2026 after appearing in court on charges linked to a R360-million police health services tender._ * **Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane has served as acting National Police Commiss
content:
*   _Masemola was placed on precautionary suspension in April 2026 after appearing in court on charges linked to a R360-million police health services tender._

*   **Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane has served as acting National Police Commissioner, and Ramaphosa says she served with distinction.**

President Cyril Ramaphosa has lifted the suspension of National Police Commissioner General Fannie Masemola, who will resume his full duties on Monday, 19 October.

The Presidency made the announcement on Friday.

Ramaphosa and Masemola agreed in April 2026 that Masemola would be deemed to be on precautionary suspension. This followed his appearance in the Pretoria Magistrate's Court on charges of contravening the Public Finance Management Act. The charges were linked to a R360-million police health services tender awarded to Medicare24.

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/") for the latest headlines

National Director of Public Prosecutions Andy Mothibi ordered the charges to be withdrawn after a review found no reasonable prospects of a successful prosecution on 15 September. The Pretoria Magistrate's Court formally withdrew the charges on 22 September.

Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, the police's chief financial officer, was appointed acting National Police Commissioner when Masemola was suspended.

Ramaphosa thanked her and said she served with distinction in the interim.

"The President welcomes the National Police Commissioner on his return to his full duties," presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya said.

The South African Policing Union had urged Ramaphosa to lift the suspension after the charges were withdrawn. After the withdrawal, Masemola told the media that he had not heard from the president.

The National Prosecuting Authority has also referred the case to the oversight judge of the Investigating Directorate Against Corruption, to look into whether there was any malice behind the original charges.

title: Eritrea's Coming Crisis? How the Lifting of U.S. Sanctions Might Spell Trouble for Africa's Most Opaque State
summary: On 19 September 2026, the United States lifted its sanctions on Eritrea, one of Africa's most enigmatic and repressive states. These sanctions were imposed by the Biden administration in 2021 for Eritrea's role in Ethiopia's devastating Tig
content:
On 19 September 2026, the United States lifted its sanctions on Eritrea, one of Africa's most enigmatic and repressive states. These sanctions were imposed by the Biden administration in 2021 for Eritrea's role in Ethiopia's devastating Tigray War (2020-22). Opinions vary as to the possible meanings of their removal: is it morally permissible on the part of the US? Will Eritrea's inhabitants be uplifted by their departure? Is this a portent of a new US-defined political order in the Horn of Africa? Though these are important questions, the greatest impact - and a paradoxically destabilising one - may instead be felt around Eritrea's octogenarian autocrat, Isaias Afwerki, as predatory officials search for new political openings. The lifting of these sanctions may yet help to push Eritrea into an era of uncertainty.

The departure of the sanctions is both controversial and long-awaited. Human rights groups have [decried](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/05/06/us-seeks-to-lift-sanctions-on-eritrea "https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/05/06/us-seeks-to-lift-sanctions-on-eritrea") the decision, citing now-notorious accounts of forced labour, torture and media suppression that have made the People's Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ), Eritrea's ruling party, a byword for authoritarian governance in Africa. The development was, nevertheless, expected. It comes four months after Reuters [reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-lift-eritrea-sanctions-red-sea-tensions-reshape-alliances-document-says-2026-05-05/ "https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-lift-eritrea-sanctions-red-sea-tensions-reshape-alliances-document-says-2026-05-05/") on an internal US government document outlining plans to lift the sanctions. Eritrea, which [denounced](https://shabait.com/2021/11/13/eritrea-deplores-illicit-and-immoral-us-sanctions/ "https://shabait.com/2021/11/13/eritrea-deplores-illicit-and-immoral-us-sanctions/") the sanctions as 'illicit and immoral', has welcomed their departure, [arguing](https://shabait.com/2026/09/19/united-states-lifts-unilateral-sanctions-on-eritrea/ "https://shabait.com/2026/09/19/united-states-lifts-unilateral-sanctions-on-eritrea/") that they had 'caused incalculable damage to the country'. Sanctions, the PFDJ argued, had long [acted](https://shabait.com/2026/04/09/statement-by-minister-osman-saleh-at-the-geneva-conference-on-unilateral-sanctions/ "https://shabait.com/2026/04/09/statement-by-minister-osman-saleh-at-the-geneva-conference-on-unilateral-sanctions/") as a 'constraint on the country's development trajectory'.

Observers of Eritrea's political economy will, however, likely recognise that the lifting of these sanctions will contribute little in the way of relieving Eritrea's impoverished population. The departing US sanctions [targeted](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0478 "https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0478") the PFDJ's key financial and military apparatus, as well as two major officials - its security boss, Abraha Kassa, and its economic chief, Hagos Gebrehiwet. (The Eritrean Defence Force's chief of staff, Filipos Woldeyohannes, remains designated under a [separate sanctions](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0329 "https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy0329").) It is these elements that stand to benefit from the removal of US sanctions, much less the country's wider inhabitants. In fact, poverty and repression are necessary parts of the PFDJ's political strategy: to control political expression, transnational capital flows, and the mobility of permanently enrolled national service conscripts. Turning to precedent, recall that following the removal of near decade-long UN sanctions in November 2018, the PFDJ remained isolated, introverted and implacably self-sufficient. The power to transform Eritrea remains in the hands of the party, not the US.

Follow us on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/") for the latest headlines

Meanwhile, other reports speculate that the removal of US sanctions [portends](https://www.wsj.com/world/africa/u-s-seeks-to-reset-ties-with-reclusive-but-strategically-vital-african-state-c8380995 "https://www.wsj.com/world/africa/u-s-seeks-to-reset-ties-with-reclusive-but-strategically-vital-african-state-c8380995") a US-Eritrean partnership against Yemen's Houthis. The latter have, in recent weeks, [captured](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthi-blitz-leaves-saudi-arabia-exposed-iran-emboldened-2026-09-16/ "https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/houthi-blitz-leaves-saudi-arabia-exposed-iran-emboldened-2026-09-16/") swathes of territory in southern Yemen, culminating in their seizure of the Bab el-Mendeb's Perim Island, to the ire of their Saudi opponents. Eritrea's Hagos Ghebrehiwet [met](https://shabait.com/2026/09/16/senior-eritrean-delegation-holds-talks-with-saudi-commerce-minister/ "https://shabait.com/2026/09/16/senior-eritrean-delegation-holds-talks-with-saudi-commerce-minister/") with Saudi officials on 15 September, the most recent in the countries' long liaison. The Houthis' (un)timely capture of Perim, being fifty miles from Eritrea's Asseb Port, raises Eritrea's international bargaining strength, thirsty as it is for oil amid the Hormuz crisis. Yet while the Saudis may appreciate a sanction-free engagement with Eritrea, the US is unlikely to sideline its powerful Ethiopian ally. In truth, the 'removal' of these five-year-old sanctions signifies their expiration without renewal, rather than a forthcoming regional reorientation. Indeed, the United States, showing little favouritism to Eritrea, has simultaneously allowed its arms embargo on Ethiopia to [expire](https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/52923/ "https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/52923/") and agreed to strengthen their security ties.

The most radical effect of the removal of US sanctions may, in fact, be found in the PFDJ's own esoteric high command. Eritrea's opaque state is underpinned by a political system only as secure as its dogged autocrat, Isaias Afwerki, is strong: one not unsettled by sanctions but, through the concentration of scarce political resources in one man, stabilised by them.

In his 2015 book, [The Real Politics of the Horn of Africa](https://worldpeacefoundation.org/publication/the-real-politics-of-the-horn-of-africa-money-war-and-the-business-of-power/ "https://worldpeacefoundation.org/publication/the-real-politics-of-the-horn-of-africa-money-war-and-the-business-of-power/"), the anthropologist Alex de Waal described a quiet transformation occurring within the PFDJ that threatened to dismantle it from the inside. Isaias had led Eritrea to independence from Ethiopia in 1993, but his rule became increasingly personalistic, particularly following the border war between the two countries (1998-2000). Internal opponents were crushed during the now-infamous G-15 purge, while the party's steely revolutionary bureaucracy mutated into a clientelist model that placed Isaias as its central patron.

But monopolising political power proved costly: loyalty had to be bought, and post-war Eritrea was desperately poor. Isaias devised a strategy. He would rule through fear: both of himself and of a looming Ethiopian spectre. Crucially, he would attempt to keep the party and the mushrooming military distinct: party officials could control finance but not force, while military commanders could wield force but not finance. This kept the price of loyalty cheap: who, if anyone, could challenge him?

But where would Isaias find the money? After Eritrea's war with Ethiopia, the PFDJ sustained its enormous 600 USD military budget (over 20% of its total expenditure) on the proceeds of mineral extraction: gold, silver, copper, zinc, and potash. Foreign mining firms provided much of the necessary capital for these ventures. This budget, in turn, was used to monitor and direct labour conscripts, uphold Eritrea's regional stature, and, increasingly, to monopolise the regime's allocation of rents - assets distributed to powerful PFDJ barons under Isaias.

When military officials demanded a financial stake, however, cracks began to show: in the clandestine dealings of generals who benefitted from trafficking refugees abroad, in the major mutiny of a brigadier general in 2013, or in the missing finances of Eritrea's mining sector, whose exploitation Isaias haphazardly awarded to powerful army commanders. Amid these difficulties, successive waves of sanctions were introduced - first imposed by the UN (2009-18) and then the US (2021-26). These limited Eritrea's international dealings, hermetically sealing the country. Of course, this likely suited Isaias. In losing their access to the outside world, Eritrean officials would have to rely on the president's patronage. The price of loyalty decreased.

So when UN sanctions were finally lifted in 2018 and Eritrea normalised its relations with Ethiopia, Isaias, perhaps inadvertently, lost two fundamental political props. The first was the party's security rationale, which justified Eritrea's militarised economy against the Ethiopian threat. [The second was the opening of new channels for foreign rents which, if left uncontrolled, could threaten Isaias' resource monopoly by allowing powerful PFDJ officials to cultivate their own external sources of income](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/ev-2022-0026/html "https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/ev-2022-0026/html"). Indeed, Eritrea's subsequent engagement in Ethiopia's Tigray War might be viewed as an attempt to placate those very officials by setting their ambitions loose on the mineral wealth of Tigray; 'war prizes', as ventured Charlotte Touati, the author of [Eritrea's Gold Rush](https://www.bloomsbury.com/uk/eritreas-gold-rush-9781350513587/ "https://www.bloomsbury.com/uk/eritreas-gold-rush-9781350513587/").

It was during this very war that sanctions returned, this time imposed by the US. These targeted individual PFDJ officials: the military chief of staff, security boss and economic chief. Five years later, in 2026, the atmosphere surrounding their removal seems different. Military officials possess a considerable financial stake. Amid the Hormuz closure, Eritrea is starved for fuel and has recently announced a [currency recall](https://hornreview.org/2026/07/06/is-eritreas-currency-recall-a-sign-of-war-preparations/ "https://hornreview.org/2026/07/06/is-eritreas-currency-recall-a-sign-of-war-preparations/"). Civil conflict has [escalated](https://africanarguments.org/2026/09/ethiopias-foretold-war-arrives/ "https://africanarguments.org/2026/09/ethiopias-foretold-war-arrives/") in Ethiopia, with its government accusing Eritrea of supporting Ethiopian rebel groups. Talk of an [invasion](https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/analysis/2026/03/23/regional-mega-war-renewed-conflict-ethiopia-sudan "https://www.thenewhumanitarian.org/analysis/2026/03/23/regional-mega-war-renewed-conflict-ethiopia-sudan") is in the air and Eritrean opposition is [mobilising](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/eritreans-planning-revolution-tel-aviv-warehouse-haaretz-report "https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/eritreans-planning-revolution-tel-aviv-warehouse-haaretz-report") abroad. Meanwhile, little is known about Isaias' succession plans, and no successor has been publicly announced. The President is now eighty years old and upon his inevitable death (assuming that Ethiopia does not get there first) there can be little doubt that the PFDJ's [high-ranking officials](https://africanarguments.org/2023/11/all-the-presidents-men-isaias-afwerkis-close-circle/ "https://africanarguments.org/2023/11/all-the-presidents-men-isaias-afwerkis-close-circle/") will zealously protect their own respective positions.

title: 高市早苗称“允许美军携核武进入日本”有探讨空间，学者：有助震慑中国

content:
日本首相高市早苗近日表示，关于“例外情况下允许美军携带核武器进入日本”的表述“有探讨的空间”，暗示可能为“无核三原则”设定例外情况。分析人士表示，如果日本政府正式将涉及核武器舰船停靠港口的紧急应对规则制度化，对震慑中国并继续加强美日军事同盟都有帮助。

根据日本共同社10月14日(星期三)的报道，高市早苗(Sanae Takaichi)当天在日本众议院预算委员会上称，关于无核三原则，日本前外相冈田克也关于“例外情况下允许美军携带核武器进入日本”的表述“有探讨的空间”，暗示可能为无核三原则设定例外情况。

报道还提到，关于是否修改三原则，高市重申了政府的以往见解，称“政府将无核三原则作为政策方针予以坚持”。日本外相茂木敏充也表示，“虽然维持无核三原则，但也有必要在这一框架下，结合已发生巨大变化的安全保障环境和威胁认知加以思考”。

“无核三原则”指不拥有、不制造、不引进核武器，是二战后日本在美苏冷战的大背景下制定的重要政策，1971年由日本议会通过，不具有法律效力。

**分析人士：政策调整宜早不宜迟**

华盛顿智库大西洋理事会(Atlantic Council)全球中国中心(Global China Hub)副主任廖彦棻(Kitsch Liao)告诉美国之音(VOA)，他认为日本对于允许携带核武器的美国舰船停靠日本港口的政策调整宜早不宜迟。

廖彦棻表示：“等到战时才调整政策，就太晚了；就算是在危机期间才调整，恐怕也来不及。这项改变若要真正发挥作用，必须在承平时期就提早到位，才能具体展现真正的团结吓阻中方侵略行动的意义。”

廖彦棻强调，若到战时才改变政策，传达出的不是实力，而是恐惧。他指出：“况且到了那个时候，大局多半已定，中国可能早已决心动手，也会骑虎难下，失去吓阻的意义”。

中国外交部发言人毛宁在10月16日(星期五)的记者会上，抨击高市早苗的有关言论，并表示“在遵守战后国际秩序、恪守国际义务问题上，日方没有所谓探讨的余地”。

**日本今年在防卫上的重大转型**

日本今年来在防卫政策方面推出了一些重大转型措施。日本执政的自民党4月13日召开安全保障调查会等联席会议，大致批准了关于放宽防卫装备品出口规则的政府方案。

自民党在其官网上表示，政府方案中根据有无杀伤力及破坏能力，将防卫装备分为“武器”和“非武器”两类。非武器类的出口目的地不设限制，但武器类的出口地则限定为与日本签署了《防卫装备品和技术转移协定》的国家。

自民党强调，对于“目前正在交战的国家”，原则上不可出口武器；但若考虑到日本国家安全的必要性，则作为例外允许出口。

日本此举实际上结束了战后和平主义时代，引发全球关注。

另外，根据路透社４月份的报道，日本今年拥有600亿美元的军事预算，目前已具备生产各类高科技军事系统的能力，包括潜艇、战舰，自主研发的导弹、坦克及作战飞机等领域；与此同时，防务承包商东芝(Toshiba)、三菱电机(Mitsubishi Electric)等企业正增聘人手并进行工厂扩建工作，其中三菱公司预计到2031年，包括日本国内和国际市场在内的防务销售额将增至三倍，达到6000亿日元(大约37亿多美元)。

报道称，日本官员表示，目前潜在的新客户包括波兰军方和菲律宾海军；这两个国家面对区域安全挑战，正处于军事现代化进程之中。

**美日军事同盟关系持续深化**

关于日本防卫措施历史性的转型，美国国务院(Department of State)4月19日在回复美国之音置评请求的电邮中表示，他们已获悉相关报道，正在关注这一局势。电邮写道：“七十多年来，美日同盟始终是印太地区和平、稳定与自由的基石。我们的双边关系以共同利益为核心，并基于推动区域安全与经济增长的共同决心。”

近年来，美日军事同盟关系持续深化。日本防卫省8月4日发布2026年《防卫白皮书》，将中国列为最大的战略挑战，并强调日本将持续以“日美同盟”为安全保障的核心。

6月9日，美国国务院在举行美国-日本延伸威慑对话(U.S.-Japan Extended Deterrence Dialogue)之际发布的一份[声明](https://china.usembassy-china.org.cn/zh/joint-statement-on-the-june-2026-u-s-japan-extended-deterrence-dialogue/)中指出，双方代表团讨论了中国急剧且不透明的核武器扩张，双方重申致力于实现朝鲜的完全无核化。

声明还强调：“美国重申对日本防卫的承诺，使用美国全方位的防卫能力，包括核能力在内”。

大西洋理事会的廖彦棻告诉美国之音，如果高市首相的政府正式将涉及核武器舰船停靠港口的紧急应对规则制度化，就等于把美国在战时对日本的支援牢牢定锚。

廖彦棻说：“美军在该区域的兵力不再只是泛泛地支援日本，而是非常明确地提供一个随时存在、可以立即动用的核武回应选项，以防中国真的走到那一步 。”

关于高市早苗对于无核三原则的言论，截至发稿，美国战争部(DOW)尚未回复美国之音的置评请求。

content:
九月阴沉的天空下，希腊退休海军工程师尼科斯·齐索斯把车停在通往弗利哈湾 （Vlycha） 的泥泞道路上，这里距离希腊港口城市埃莱夫西斯不远。在他面前，岸边有十几艘沉船残骸正在腐朽，还有一个被水淹没的码头。“到目前为止，经济活动仅限于你眼前所见。这里完全荒废了。”这位七旬希腊老人笑着解释道。

这位退休工程师曾是希腊埃莱夫西斯市的市长候选人，并在这座后工业城市担任市议员至2023年。他密切关注着旨在改造弗利哈湾的各项工程进展。希腊政府希望将这片距离雅典仅20公里的区域打造成为一个占地至少80公顷的“大型”海事枢纽。

**与第一大港比雷埃夫斯港竞争**

尼科斯·齐佐斯尼科斯·齐索斯居住了四十多年的这座城市，此前以其卓越的考古遗产而闻名，如今注定要成为一个集“港口、商业、交通、能源和国防活动”于一体的“枢纽”，发展部长塔基斯·西奥多里卡科斯在一年前的一次访问中宣布。

他此行的贵宾是美国驻希腊女大使金伯利·吉尔福伊尔（ Kimberly Guilfoyle ）。在埃莱夫西斯，华盛顿毫不掩饰其与仅15公里之遥的比雷埃夫斯港竞争的意图。比雷埃夫斯港是中国在欧洲港口基础设施领域占据主导地位的象征。

近几个月来，雅典的港口一直是中美两大超级大国之间一场几乎公开的影响力争夺战的焦点。自特朗普政府重返执政以来，一直试图遏制中国在全球海运基础设施领域的主导地位，并将十年前落入中远集团手中的比雷埃夫斯港视为一个问题。

2016年，在债权人的压力下，雅典政府为了整顿公共财政，将港务局的控制权转让给了唯一一家认真竞标的公司——中远集团。这家由北京直接控制的海运巨头，目前持有港务局67%的股份，特许经营协议有效期至2052年。十年来，中远集团已投资超过10亿欧元，并将希腊港口改造成为中国贸易的枢纽。

据港务局发言人称，去年该港口集装箱吞吐量达470万个，其中80%是从希腊转运至其他港口。就吞吐量而言，比雷埃夫斯港稳居欧洲前五大港口之列，在地中海地区仅次于西班牙瓦伦西亚港。据估计，运往欧洲的中国货物中，有10%至15%经由希腊港口转运。

尽管北京的“一带一路”倡议近年来举步维艰，但其无可否认的商业成功令欧美官员感到担忧。

**美国展开收复失地行动**

比雷埃夫斯港位于苏伊士运河、黑海和西欧的交汇处，战略位置极其重要。在欧洲，中国对该港口拥有绝对控制权，这实属罕见。在贸易战的背景下，比雷埃夫斯港很容易被用作胁迫手段。

甚或，一旦发生武装冲突，比港可能会被改造成服务于中国人民解放军军工联合体的后勤枢纽。“比雷埃夫斯港只是一个更大故事的一部分，它不仅关乎港口，更关乎中国对全球海洋的掌控。”法国潘泰翁大学（**Panteion ）**国际经济关系研究所（IIER）研究员、东南欧中国影响力专家普拉门·通切夫（ Plamen Tonchev, ）如此提醒说道。

这位学者继续说道：“就目前而言，中国的造船能力是美国的232倍，北京控制或参与了全球约130个港口。中国现在正步英国的后尘，成为新的全球海上帝国。”

鉴于中国的这种主导地位，美国正积极推行一项战略，旨在重建其商船队并对中国实施制裁，同时依靠盟国来确保战略水道的安全。这项努力包括在中国的影响力最为显著的港口进行反制，例如去年的巴拿马运河事件以及如今在雅典的这个港口事件。

在阿提卡盆地 （Attique） ，特朗普政府最初试图将中远集团从比雷埃夫斯港驱逐出去，该公司已在那里运营了十五年。一年前上任不久，刚刚辞职的美国驻希腊女大使金伯利·吉尔福伊尔在其首次电视采访中暗示，存在“绕过”将这家公共集团与希腊政府联系起来的管理合同的“办法”。

该声明引发了与中国驻雅典大使馆之间前所未有的外交事件，促使希腊政府做出回应。希腊总理基里亚科斯·米佐塔基斯（ Kyriakos Mitsotakis ）迅速表示，希腊“尊重过去达成的协议”。

**“在中远集团周围筑起一道围栏”**

几个月前，金伯利·吉尔福伊尔曾表示，美国人已将目光投向埃莱夫西斯港，该港口是美国“长期计划”的核心。吉尔福伊尔是唐纳德·特朗普的长期盟友，她断言，该港口地理位置优越，毗邻军用机场、希腊最大的物流中心、高速公路和铁路，有潜力发展成为“能够与比雷埃夫斯港的生产能力和中国利益抗衡的港口”。10月13日的周二，《华尔街日报》披露了一系列令她难堪的内幕后，美国总统要求她下台。

在埃莱夫西斯，华盛顿并非从零开始。2023年，在希腊危机期间陷入困境的造船厂被一家希腊-美国合组公司Onex Shipyards及时收购。此次收购的资金来自美国发展金融公司（DFC）提供的1.25亿美元债券贷款， FC D是华盛顿在发展中国家的金融机构，并为这项极具战略意义的投资破例批准了贷款。

“美国国际开发金融公司 DFC 支持这个项目的原因是为了阻止中国参与，给中远集团筑起一道围墙。”2016年至2022年担任美国驻希腊大使的杰弗里·皮亚特解释道。这位外交官被认为是近年来雅典和华盛顿关系缓和的缔造者，他亲自力挺该项目，而“许多中国人当时都想控制这家造船厂”。

Onex公司的订单量已大幅增加，并对“埃莱夫西斯造船厂”寄予厚望。去年五月，该公司与韩国韩华海洋集团签署了一项“历史性”协议。韩华海洋集团是“让美国造船业再次伟大”计划的主要支持者之一，该计划是首尔和华盛顿之间的一项贸易协定，旨在通过韩国的大规模投资来重建美国造船业。

作为一项预计在未来几年创造1万个就业岗位的13.5亿美元投资计划的一部分，这两家公司计划在毗邻的40公顷土地上扩建和现代化改造埃莱夫西斯船厂。其目标是建造一个集建造、维护、修理和后勤保障于一体的中心，以满足美国海军和北约部队在地中海的作战需求。

再往前两公里，在埃莱夫西斯湾，Onex公司也与希腊跨国建筑公司Aktor合作，参与弗利哈湾 （Vlycha Bay)项目的竞标。这片土地归希腊政府所有，计划建成一个重要的物流和港口枢纽，鉴于其毗邻雷维索萨（Revithoussa）再气化终端，旨在成为美国液化天然气的海上门户和能源走廊。雷维索萨（Revithoussa）液化天然气（LNG）再气化终端是希腊唯一的LNG进口

Onex公司负责人帕诺斯·泽诺科斯塔斯在5月底举行的希腊船东重要盛会“波塞冬尼亚贸易博览会 Salon Posedonia”上解释说，这两个项目必须“作为一个整体”来看待。尽管存在诸多保留意见和疑问，但埃莱夫西斯号仍有望成为悬挂美国国旗的比雷埃夫斯号的知名竞争对手。尽管存在诸多保留意见和疑问，但埃莱夫西斯仍有望成为美国国旗下的比雷埃夫斯港的竞争对手。

**中美“战争卷土重来”**

在希腊海军的地图上，海军工程师尼科斯·齐索斯指出弗利哈湾吃水浅，不适合作为商业港口。而比雷埃夫斯港的天然水深为18至19米，足以容纳世界上最大的集装箱船。

“对于一艘8万吨级的船舶来说，要达到这个高度，就必须建造数十米甚至数百米长的大型堤坝。这需要大量的资金。”这位退休人士解释道，他还担心这可能会对环境造成毁灭性后果，或者引发考古发现。

**腊美国学院副教授康斯坦丁诺斯·菲利斯指出：**

**我认为军事方面会取得进展，但****埃莱夫西斯****不会成为第二个比雷埃夫斯港。**

负责组织土地分拆的希腊主权财富基金Growthfund的专家们似乎也得出了同样的结论。这项预计已进行数月的招标仍未启动；据希腊媒体报道，招标已被推迟至2027年。

美国学院副教授康斯坦丁诺斯·菲利斯总结道：“我认为军事方面会实现，但埃莱夫西斯不会成为第二个比雷埃夫斯港。这不仅是出于技术和财政原因，也是因为从商业角度来看，这样做没有意义。”

上周美国国务卿马可·卢比奥访问雅典期间，几位居民在雅典市中心抗议“将埃莱夫西斯沿海地区改造成能源和军事中心”。

不远处，在普尼克斯 Pnyx, 山上，美国国务卿发表了关于西方文明衰落的演讲，然后结束了他的访问，他同时警告说“战争卷土重来”。距离他的讲台不到十公里，便是比雷埃夫斯港。

title: 张婉莹被指曾坐太子集团“共谋者二号”超跑拍照 更多细节被曝光

content:
据哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）的一项调查显示，一名被控充当中国代理人的加州房地产经纪人，与一个涉嫌在柬埔寨运作的犯罪组织存在关联；该组织被指利用强迫劳动，针对美国民众实施了涉案金额高达数十亿美元的诈骗活动。

上周，美国联邦调查局（FBI）对现年34岁、在加州尔湾从事房地产经纪工作的张婉莹（Wanying "Heather" Zhang）提起指控，指其在未进行登记的情况下充当外国代理人。张婉莹被指在2025年于西雅图监视台湾总统赖清德之子赖廷与和其家人。

当时与张婉莹同行的还有一人，经CBS核实，此人为54岁的苗发泰（Fatai Miao，音译）。根据CBS查阅的多份联邦法院文件，张婉莹和苗发泰均与一些卷入庞大犯罪集团的人员存在关联。

在加州期间，张婉莹似乎活跃于富裕阶层；她曾在社媒平台小红书上发布照片，展示自己坐在一辆布加迪跑车里的样子。她当时写道，这辆车属于她的朋友。这辆车似乎属于一名男子；据美国司法部称，此人在一个涉案金额达数十亿美元、且以现代奴役为基础的欺诈团伙中，扮演着“执行者”的角色。

美国政府指控跨国企业太子集团针对美国民众实施了价值至少150亿美元的在线诈骗，并利用了位于柬埔寨境内至少10处涉嫌强迫劳动营地的劳工。

张婉莹还与苗发泰建立了长年的关系。苗发泰是远锦开发建设有限责任公司（Yuanjin Development & Construction LLC，音译）的注册代理人及组织者；该公司注册地址位于加州尔湾市星际街（Interstellar Street）上的一处五居室住宅内。

苗发泰是一位建筑业企业家，他在上述住宅内注册了一家企业。该住宅位于尔湾市郊区，价值450万美元。检察官指控称，该住宅还被一个涉嫌洗钱的中国组织用作“藏匿屋”，即存放非法资金或物品的场所。根据2023年提交的一份刑事控告书，该洗钱组织据称与墨西哥的锡那罗亚贩毒集团（Sinaloa Cartel）存在勾结。

在那份刑事控告书中，苗发泰并未被列为被告，也未被点名提及。根据该刑事控告书中的一份宣誓书，美国缉毒局（DEA）专案组警官冈萨雷斯（Steven Gonzalez）于2023年3月1日观察到，一名涉嫌隶属于某个“大型洗钱组织”的成员，在上述住所放下了一个“红色的、中等大小且有一定重量的手提袋”。

冈萨雷斯在2023年5月提交的刑事控告书中写道：“基于我的专业培训与经验、我对本案调查情况的了解，以及与多位精通洗钱手法的探员进行的交流，我认为，此人刚刚接收并运送了一批属于非法活动所得的美元现金”。据DEA指控，这只是该组织在加州洛杉矶县和橙县多处藏匿屋进行的一系列投放手提袋活动之一。

苗发泰尚未受到任何罪名指控。据检察官称，就在FBI探员在尔湾破门执行搜查令的前几天，他已于上月持单程机票飞往中国。美国司法部指控该涉嫌犯罪团伙经营一家无牌货币兑换机构，旨在为锡那罗亚贩毒集团洗钱数百万美元。

在上周三举行的第二次法庭听证会上，联邦检察官指称，张婉莹也曾经营过一家“无牌货币兑换”业务，并将19万美元的利润汇入了她名下的中国的银行账户。不过，在法庭审理或与张婉莹相关的任何公开法律文件中，检方并未提及该涉嫌贩毒团伙。

2024年4月，针对该团伙24名成员提起的另一份起诉书中，包含了一些联邦执法部门查获物品的照片，其中展示了成捆的100美元面值钞票，以及装满卡车的、砖块状的可卡因和冰毒。该团伙成员拥有“海洋”（Ocean）、“蝙蝠侠”（Batman）和“P博士”（Dr. P）等绰号。

涉嫌为该组织领导层的一名成员于2023年5月12日被捕。根据DEA探员在宣誓书中的记录，此人向探员供述，他手下有10到20人，且“他所经手的资金大多来自欺诈活动”。上述探员在宣誓书中写道：“此人后来承认，他此前曾参与处理毒品犯罪所得——直至2020年年底，但他表示这非常‘可怕’，因为一旦资金出现损失，就会招致‘墨西哥人’的后果”。

报导称，苗发泰在远锦开发的商业伙伴程章（Cheng Zhang，音译），同时也是太子集团“执行者”的商业伙伴。太子集团总部位于柬埔寨，被美国检方指控利用强迫劳动，通过诈骗手段攫取数十亿美元，并对这些非法所得进行洗钱。

加州公司Big Bow LLC由程章和另一家名为M资本全球加州有限责任公司（M Capital Global California LLC）的企业共同管理；后者则由陈星（Chen Sokly）——据称是太子集团的“执行者”——所掌控。据CBS确认，陈星即为去年在纽约针对太子集团董事长陈志提起的起诉书中，仅以“共谋者二号”代称的那名男子。

该起诉书将太子集团称为“亚洲最大的跨国犯罪组织之一”。该组织在柬埔寨各地运营着从事加密货币投资诈骗的诈骗园区，通过强迫劳动，为陈志及其同伙牟取了巨额利润。

这份起诉书指出，“数以千计的务工人员在前往柬埔寨及其他地区寻求就业机会时，遭到人口贩运，并被迫在这些诈骗园区内从事加密货币投资诈骗及其他欺诈活动；他们往往是在暴力威胁下被迫劳作。这些诈骗园区内设有大型宿舍，四周环绕着高墙和铁丝网，实际上就是强迫劳动营”。

美国政府对太子集团采取了打击行动，期间查获了价值150亿美元的比特币；美国司法部表示，这是其历史上规模最大的一次查获行动。太子集团否认相关指控，并将此次打击行动斥为“披着执法外衣的资产掠夺”。

上述起诉书指出，“共谋者二号”利用“腐败和暴力手段，维持了太子集团在诈骗团伙中的主导地位”；其中包括涉嫌向一名外国政府官员行贿，为其购买了一艘价值300万美元的游艇。

起诉书还指出，“共谋者二号”曾担任傲胜国际投资集团（Awesome Global）的董事长；该公司是太子集团旗下的一家子公司。企业记录显示，确实存在一家名为Awesome Global的柬埔寨公司，其董事长名单中同时列有陈志和陈星。

8月8日，国际非营利组织、有组织犯罪与腐败报道项目（OCCRP）首次指出，陈星即为“共谋者二号”。CBS报导称，被指控在未按规定通知美国司法部长的情况下，充当外国政府的代理人张婉莹也与陈星存在关联。

2024年，张婉莹在小红书上发布了一张照片，照片中她坐在超跑布加迪Chiron的驾驶座上，配文称：“看看我朋友的豪车！” 这张照片已于本周被删除。根据社媒上的贴文，这辆车属于费文志（Wenzhi "Wesley" Fei，音译）——他自称是一名“玩扑克堕落的人”和加密货币交易员。

但在接受CBS采访时，费文志表示这辆车并非他所有。他说，这辆车是从陈星那里借来的，并形容对方是自己的“朋友”和一位“慷慨的绅士”。费文志还表示，对于陈星的商业往来或太子集团自己“一无”所知。

社媒上分享的视频和照片显示，费文志与陈星出现在一个停放着多辆稀有豪华跑车的车库内；此外，费文志还在一艘游艇前摆姿势拍照——根据海关记录，这艘71英尺（约21.6米）长的游艇是由陈星从新加坡进口的。

费文志还在自己的Instagram主页上发布了一段视频，画面显示他坐进了一辆法拉利跑车。这辆车停在加州约巴林达的一处住宅车道上，该住宅属于布伦登·罗（Brendon Luo）——此人因参与太子集团相关事务而遭到美国财政部制裁。

2024年，费文志通过其旗下贸易公司Block Infinity，为加密货币行业人士组织了一场豪华“游艇活动”。活动地点位于新加坡的一栋太子集团旗下大楼内，陈志则在该楼拥有一间价值1600万美元的套房。

费文志告诉CBS称，他本人并未参加此次活动，也不认识张婉莹；而​​且他和陈星“关系并没有那么亲近”。费文志还说，在美国司法部针对太子集团提出相关指控后，“就很难联系上他了”。

费文志未受到任何刑事指控。张婉莹除了被指控担任中国政府的未注册代理人外，并未受到其他刑事指控；在美国联邦执法部门提交的所有文件中，这两人均未被提及与太子集团或贩毒集团的洗钱活动有关联。陈星未回应向其位于加州公司发出的置评请求。

太子集团的一位发言人在6月份曾向有组织犯罪与腐败报道项目宣称：“陈先生及其旗下企业并非犯罪集团，而是一系列合法的商业实体；它们在全球范围内为数百万人提供服务，并雇用了数万名员工”。该发言人还称“陈志及太子集团对于美国政府所作出的那些荒谬且无根据的指控——这些指控随后又在世界各地被其他司法管辖区所附和——完全是清白的”。

在电话采访中，苗发泰的儿子表示其父不愿置评，并说不认为父亲知晓其经营场所与涉嫌有组织犯罪团伙之间的关联。他还提到，苗发泰三周前持单程票飞往中国，目前仍在中国。

title: “洋流”恐翻转台湾台北市长选情，中共急出手“介选”？
summary: 台北 — 台湾的台北市长选举进入倒数最后六周，两大党参选人的竞选声势逐渐拉近，尤其民进党籍(绿营)的沈伯洋以黑马之姿，急起直追，甚至掀起所谓的“洋流”，恐威胁到国民党籍(蓝营)现任市长蒋万安的连任之路。 蓝绿阵营厮杀之际，中国国台办近日也出手，再度制裁沈伯洋父亲沈士城的外贸公司，遭台湾官方定调为“介入选举(介选)”，中共是因为蒋万安的选情告急，才出手助选吗? 这样的手法是否有效？ 是否像台湾部分绿营人士所嘲讽，是在帮倒忙呢? **台湾定调:中共“赤裸裸介选、帮倒忙”** 台湾
content:
台北 —

台湾的台北市长选举进入倒数最后六周，两大党参选人的竞选声势逐渐拉近，尤其民进党籍(绿营)的沈伯洋以黑马之姿，急起直追，甚至掀起所谓的“洋流”，恐威胁到国民党籍(蓝营)现任市长蒋万安的连任之路。

蓝绿阵营厮杀之际，中国国台办近日也出手，再度制裁沈伯洋父亲沈士城的外贸公司，遭台湾官方定调为“介入选举(介选)”，中共是因为蒋万安的选情告急，才出手助选吗? 这样的手法是否有效？ 是否像台湾部分绿营人士所嘲讽，是在帮倒忙呢?

**台湾定调:中共“赤裸裸介选、帮倒忙”**

台湾陆委会主委邱垂正星期五(10月16日)表示，中共再次制裁沈伯洋父亲的外贸公司是“赤裸裸地”介选，他说，这一系列对沈伯洋的打压手法，中共已经操弄过好几次，只会“激起台湾人民更大的反感”。

邱垂正说，对中国的持续介选，包括跨境镇压的法律战或铺天盖地的认知作战，台湾政府将以最坚定的决心，捍卫自由民主的生活方式。

除了定调介选，台湾陆委会副主委梁文杰于星期四的例行记者会也讥讽称，中共在“帮倒忙”。

梁文杰说，中共对沈伯洋是“一条龙式的攻击”，除两度制裁沈父的公司，还曾派港人来台跟监他和妻子一家人，而且“招数套路一样”，先是透过香港《文汇报》出手，以期台湾媒体加入炒作，最后再由国台办跟进。他批评，中共此次套路的逻辑不合理，难怪近两日少有台湾媒体配合跟进。

针对中国批评沈伯洋“会同亲属想方设法从大陆赚钱”，梁文杰解释说，沈父是南美洲厄瓜多尔台商，他的贸易公司在中国下单是帮中企赚中南美洲的钱、帮中国挣外汇，根本不是在“赚红钱”。

梁文杰表示，从10月初出征台湾知名主持人蔡康永到二度制裁沈父，中共摆明了，不想让台湾人有选择的自由，但这样的作用力也恐有反作用力，他警告，对岸以为可以帮到蒋万安的选情，但很可能反而“帮倒忙，小心机关算尽，反害了别人性命。”

**国台办联手港媒攻击沈伯洋**

香港亲北京的《大公报》和《文汇报》星期二率先揭露，沈父沈土城的兆亿有限公司于2025年6月首度遭中国制裁后，持续以VWAY CO的名义与中企贸易往来，且该公司截至今年3月、过去九个月的贸易额近69万美元，是前一家公司三年多的贸易额总和。

两大报批评称，沈伯洋“表面是抗中急先锋，但暗中纵容父亲赚红钱”。

港媒发声后，中国国台办随即于星期三宣布，对沈父的第二家外贸公司VWAY 实施制裁，禁其与任何中国企业或个人交易及合作。

国台办发言人陈斌华说，沈伯洋一边鼓噪“反中抗中” 、阻碍两岸交流合作，一边会同亲属大赚中国钱，“丑陋行径令人不齿”，中方“决不允许台独顽固分子关联企业在大陆谋利”。

基于沈伯洋早前的“抗中”言论，国台办早于2024年10月已正式将他列入“台独顽固分子”的黑清单。

**沈伯洋: 国台办炒冷饭**

针对中共最新一轮的制裁，沈伯洋随即以“冷饭热炒”回怼，他说他呼吁国台办“换个题目”，并应先自行讨论好口径，因为中国一会说他是台独顽固分子要通缉，一会又派人来台跟踪监视他，现在又二度制裁他父亲的贸易公司。

沈伯洋强调其父在厄瓜多尔已经经商已约30年，其商业模式为中间代理商，并非在中国的台商。面对质疑，沈伯洋强调，“这些消息从哪里来？为什么这么多人关心我家人的生意？”选举可以有竞争，但讨论应该建立在事实之上。

蒋万安则以“未深入了解”回应，他表示，此事关于沈伯洋和其家人，应由沈伯洋自己向外界清楚说明。

沈伯洋于5月中旬正式加入台北市长的选战，初期声势低落，直至9月中下旬后才开始人气大增，并掀起“洋流”，尤其频频“破圈”，接受泛蓝媒体人如王伟忠和赵少康专访后，好评不断，且狂吸中间选民，意外让台北市的选情陷入激战，但他最后能否真正翻转台北市选情“蓝大于绿”的基本盘，还有待观察。

根据台媒TVBS在10月初发布的民调，蒋万安和沈伯洋的支持率分达49%和41%，另有11%左右的中间选民尚未决定，但双方差距已由5月底的28个百分点大幅缩小至8个百分点。

**蓝绿选民表示不受影响**

因此，中共现在急忙出手，是否看到蒋万安的选情告急?

对于国台办的最新介选招数，台北市蓝、绿选民皆告诉美国之音，他们根本不会受影响。

支持沈伯洋的台北选民刘纯信说，中共打压台湾和台独数十年“没有什么意义”，且对他这个50多岁的人来说，早已见怪不怪，反而“只是增加候选人(沈伯洋)的声势”，尤其沈父根本不是“赚红钱”，而是协助中国发展经济的人，让人看破中共的不理性和永远带有政治意识型态的偏见。

刘纯信说，他乐见沈伯洋的崛起，台北有理性的中间选民应该会对中共的介选反感，转而支持沈伯洋，但基于去年针对32位蓝营立委之大罢免运动的失败经验，他说，蓝营支持者的思想和认同固化让他乐观不起来，因为台北本来就是蓝营的票仓。

支持蒋万安的台北选民黄文亮则说，反对“台独”和讨厌沈伯洋是他决定11月底去票投蒋万安的主要理由。

黄文亮自称是蓝绿候选人都支持过的中间选民，他说，他对中共对沈父的制裁无感，不会让他更支持蒋万安，也不会让他因此同情被打压的弱势，就转而支持沈伯洋。

黄文亮认为，沈伯洋确实有创意，但也颇会“耍花枪”，例如他开设的“市长，你给我听好了”网站根本无异于台北市早就有的“1999市民热线”，另外，他也对沈伯洋所属的民进党把去年发动的大罢免运动包装为公民团体的自主行为不以为然。

**分析人士:中共介选效果不彰**

观选分析人士也说，中共对台的介选和认知作战长期都存在，但效果有限、甚至不彰，且近来已有消停的迹象。

位于台北的铭传大学广播电视学系主任杜圣聪说，中国就是“过干瘾”，介选效果“微乎其微”，因为只会强化“洋流”选民对沈伯洋的支持，尤其洋流在邻近台北市的县市及南台湾高雄市都有一定的外溢效益，但不太容易改变中间选民的投票行为，尤其台湾选民已慢慢对中共的影响力建立“抗体”。

杜圣聪告诉美国之音:“台湾自己内部的因素、候选人特性、政党动员会(影响)比较大。来自于外部(的介选)，希望去翻转(选情)，其实不容易。”

他说，中共的介选数十年来没停过，从1996年导弹危机、2022年美国前众议院议长南西·佩洛西(Nancy Pelosi)访台后的环台军演到最近几年的网路认知作战，一直没断过，不过，效果不彰，相较于当年的“剑拔弩张，2026年看来消停了许多。”

专精研究中共网路认知战的前台湾民主实验室分析组组长杨顺清在接受美国知音采访时表示，沈伯洋创立的台湾民主实验室和“黑熊学院”是很重要的抗中组织，因此，他被中共列入黑名单后，沈父两度被制裁，都是某种程度的介选，尤其中共近期放任网民和党媒出征蔡康永，意在“制造寒蝉效应，防止像蔡康永这样的公众人物表态支持。”

杨顺清说，中国近几年对台湾的介选模式之一，就是大规模透过假帐号在网路带风向并操弄社群舆论，或委托小型公关公司和网红根据共同的脚本来推动网路叙事。

但他说，这类假讯息的效果很难衡量，“可能只会影响到很小的一群人”。

不过，他说，因为台湾社会本来就存在两极化的思维，也很难将这种两极发展归因是境外势力的影响。

杨顺清说，不少人观察到，俄乌战事期间，俄罗斯的资料中心遭攻击后，假帐号的活跃度有变低的迹象，部分网友也反应“最近爱吵架的小粉红变少了”。 他说，这或许与俄罗斯无法再承揽中国的外宣活动或两国共用的资源受损有关。
