content:
英国贸易大臣萨瓦尔（Anas Sarwar）在受访时表示，英国与欧盟必须“携手合作、行动一致”，以应对中国在汽车领域的主导地位。这些言论释放出一个迄今为止最明确的信号：英国政府准备在针对中国电动汽车进口的关税问题上与欧盟保持一致，从而争取参与欧盟的“欧洲制造”（Made in Europe）产业计划。

在伦敦市长官邸举行的英德商业峰会期间，当被政客新闻网欧洲版问及英国是否会考虑对中国电动汽车加征关税时，萨瓦尔指出，与欧洲伙伴的讨论“仍在进行中”。

萨瓦尔在采访中说道：“汽车行业及合作关系依然稳固，但我们难道不需要应对中国市场迅速扩张所带来的挑战吗？当然需要；英国与欧盟之间的合作越紧密、行动越协调一致，对双方就越有利”。

英国正与欧盟委员会展开磋商，旨在避免从明年年初起对电动汽车征收10%的关税——届时，根据英国脱欧贸易协议，更严格的原产地规则将正式生效。此外，英国也在积极争取让本国企业能够被纳入欧盟的“欧洲制造”相关政策框架中。

英国官员认为，在应对中国不公平竞争的贸易行为方面，伦敦与布鲁塞尔面临着共同的挑战；通过政策协调采取联合应对措施，是处理对华关系的最佳途径。欧盟的《工业加速法案》在部分公共采购项目中给予欧盟本土产品优惠待遇；若英国被排除在外，其制造商可能会因此处于不利地位。

德国政府及部分欧盟官员指出，英国不愿在针对中国电动汽车的关税问题上与欧盟保持一致，这削弱了其争取被纳入相关政策框架的理由。萨瓦尔在发表主旨演讲时向德国商界领袖和决策者表示，英国及其欧洲邻国面临着相似的挑战。

萨瓦尔指出：“一方面是强硬的保护主义，另一方面是急剧的扩张主义；而德国等与我们经济规模相当的国家，其政府正不得不审视这种局面会对各自的供应链意味着什么”。

萨瓦尔补充道：“我并不是说我们的欧盟同事不该开展‘欧洲制造’（Made in Europe）运动，我们自己也有‘英国制造’（Made in U.K.）的运动……但我想说的是，我们应当避免因反应过度而引发无意的后果，以免在这一过程中损害到我们自身的企业”。

英国商业、创新、科学与贸易大臣雷诺兹（Jonathan Reynolds）此前曾表示，他对针对中国电动汽车征收关税持相对审慎的态度。上月在接受政客新闻网采访时，雷诺兹指出，英国在决定是否征收关税时的考量与欧盟有所不同。

雷诺兹于周日说：“我们是一个出口导向型行业。因此，显然不应采取任何可能危及出口市场的举措；而且一旦实施关税，就必须时刻警惕可能招致的报复行动”。他将英国在对待中国电动汽车问题上的立场形容为“精细平衡”。

另据英国《金融时报》所见的一份协议草案，法国和德国愿意将英国汽车行业纳入欧盟的“欧洲制造”公共采购计划——这是英国政府长期以来的诉求——但前提是英国必须使其对华关税与欧盟保持一致。

该协议草案明确指出，“欧洲制造”相关规则——旨在将补贴和公共合同的获取权限限定在欧洲企业范围内——将涵盖欧盟27个成员国以及英国的汽车制造商；其具体方式是将“在2020年1月1日属于欧盟单一市场的其他欧洲伙伴”也纳入其中。

然而，若要从这一地位中获益，英国就必须与“欧盟贸易保护措施”，例如针对中国电动汽车征收的关税保持一致，而这对英国政府而言恐怕难以接受。至于其他曾要求将其汽车制造商纳入其中的欧盟贸易伙伴——如日本、韩国和土耳其——则不会被涵盖在内。

这项尚未最终敲定的协议，不仅满足了德国提出的放宽欧盟2035年起停止销售内燃机汽车这一要求，还包含多项可能削弱欧盟气候雄心的提议。

自今夏以来，法国和德国一直在就汽车相关政策进行谈判。这些措施旨在为淘汰内燃机汽车制定规则，并针对汽车及其零部件——包括电池——引入新的欧洲优先准则。与欧盟不同，英国迄今为止并未对中国进口产品采取同样严格的限制措施，因此其汽车市场中中国品牌车辆的占比要高得多。此外，英国还需对进入本国的外商直接投资设定更严格的条件。

法国曾力推一种仅限欧盟27国参与的方案，旨在重振欧洲陷入困境的汽车产业；而德国则主张将英国及其他贸易伙伴也纳入其中。这一折中方案让伦敦方面陷入了两难境地：它虽然实现了英国首相伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）所要求的市场准入，但代价却是必须与欧盟的贸易措施保持一致。

据悉，目前，英国对中国电动汽车仅征收10%的标准进口关税。相比之下，欧盟自2024年起已对中国纯电动汽车征收最高达45%的关税，而美国则征收100%的关税。雷诺兹曾表示，正在“评估”提高针对中国电动汽车关税的可能性；但他对此持谨慎态度，担心此类措施可能招致中方的对等关税，进而影响对华出口汽车的英国车企——尤其是捷豹路虎。

报导指，伯纳姆政府获得的一项突破是，周四，法国最终转而支持德国——德国一直支持英国关于在欧盟《工业加速法案》框架下将其列为欧洲的呼吁。该法案目前尚处于草案阶段，旨在保护欧盟制造业免受中国廉价竞争的影响。根据英国《卫报》看到的法德联合文件，两国现在提议，特别是在汽车行业，英国可以被纳入“欧洲制造”。

文件写道：“对于汽车行业，‘欧洲制造’应涵盖欧盟27国，并允许自愿加入，以进一步纳入截至2020年1月1日属于欧盟单一市场的欧洲合作伙伴，但须达成关于完全对等协议——即采用适用于汽车行业的欧洲优先方案”。这段表述显然是指英国，因为在2020年1月，英国作为欧盟成员国，当时仍处于单一市场之内。

这也将涵盖挪威——该国虽非欧盟成员国，但属于欧洲单一市场的一部分。文件补充称，这种“选择加入”机制附带若干条件，包括在贸易防御措施方面保持一致。

这些措施既涵盖欧盟已于2024年对中国纯电动汽车加征的关税，也包括未来可能设立的任何贸易壁垒——例如目前正处于最终敲定阶段的、针对中国混合动力汽车出口的配额协议。

文件指出，除了“相关的反规避措施”外，这些选择加入的国家还必须接受“在欧盟针对第三国投资的相关条件，以及欧盟各项贸易防御措施方面，与欧盟保持动态一致”。

周三，梅赛德斯-奔驰负责人恳请欧盟领导人允许英国加入“欧洲制造”计划。梅赛德斯-奔驰负责人表示，如果将英国排除在欧盟旗舰级的“欧洲制造”产业立法之外，那将意味着欧盟领导人“蓄意选择”去“伤害”整个欧盟地区的汽车产业。

数周以来，英国一直面临压力，被要求在针对中国汽车的关税问题上与欧盟保持一致；但本周，雷诺兹强调，不会在胁迫下与欧盟的政策保持一致。然而，英国政府极力争取加入欧盟的“欧洲制造”计划，因为他们担心，如果英国被排除在欧盟供应链之外，可能会导致英国汽车行业数十亿英镑的贸易额损失。

title: 环境与发展 - 第17届生物多样性峰会看点与中国立场
summary: 联合国《生物多样性公约》第17次缔约方大会（CBD COP 17）将于 本月的19日至30日 在 亚美尼亚首都埃里温（Yerevan） 举行， 此次峰会的着重点是要对 “昆明—蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架”（简称“昆蒙框架”）达成后的全球履约情况进行审查。评估各国在“保护30%的陆地和海洋”等核心目标上的进展。那么，除此之外，还有一些什么别的看点？另外，中国作为“昆蒙框架”的主要推动国，中国的表现如何？法广就此电话采访了法国智库，法国可持续发展与国际关系学院（IDDRI）的生物
content:
联合国《生物多样性公约》第17次缔约方大会（CBD COP 17）将于 本月的19日至30日 在 亚美尼亚首都埃里温（Yerevan） 举行， 此次峰会的着重点是要对 “昆明—蒙特利尔全球生物多样性框架”（简称“昆蒙框架”）达成后的全球履约情况进行审查。评估各国在“保护30%的陆地和海洋”等核心目标上的进展。那么，除此之外，还有一些什么别的看点？另外，中国作为“昆蒙框架”的主要推动国，中国的表现如何？法广就此电话采访了法国智库，法国可持续发展与国际关系学院（IDDRI）的生物多样性项目负责人Juliette Landry 女士，她的中文名字叫做兰朱莉：

**法广：**非常感谢兰朱莉女士接受法广的采访，这您看来，下周即将举行的峰会的最大的看点是什么？

**Juliette Landry****：**对我们来说基本上有四个关键的议题： 全球评估、资源调动、遗传资源数字序列信息（Digital Sequence Information，简称 DSI）以及土著人代表机制。 当然，峰会届时 会有其他的一些发布，例如，亚美尼亚也会提出一些关于山地生态系统，以及利用高科技更好地监测自然状况的倡议。 此外，还有一些国家希望联合起来，共同应对有害补贴问题。我们需要审视所有这些，看看《生物多样性公约》将如何与其他正在进行的国际倡议相契合。

**法广：**联合国已经综合了来自各国的更新报告，发表了一份全球报告，那么这份报告总的来说究竟是喜是忧？

**Juliette Landry****：**首先可以说好消息是各方对《昆明——蒙特利尔框架》的承诺已达到前所未有的程度。 与其他以往的全球框架，特别是《爱知目标》相比，各国从未作出如此多的承诺，也从未见过如此多的进展迹象。 可以说，各国在诸如入侵物种和目标四等目标上都取得了进展。 事实上，当我们把各国的雄心加总起来时，我们就更接近于我们在全球层面需要共同努力的目标。不过，另一方面，我们也意识到，其他一些全球目标的实现则要困难得多。我对这份全球报告做了一些分析，我的 结论 是： 对于那些几十年来一直以传统方式实施的目标——也就是与保护、保育以及更传统的生物多样性目标相关的目标——我们取得了一些进展， 但是，对于那些更具社会和经济性质、针对特定领域的目标——我们看到存在一些不足，也看到实现这些目标并不容易。尤其是在将生物多样性纳入部门政策、改革和取消对生物多样性有害的补贴方面。 因此，我们也希望第十七届联合国气候变化大会能够在这方面发挥作用，重新推动相关的行动。

**法广****：**中国是否已经递交评估报告，内容又如何呢？

**Juliette Landry****：**是的。 就中国而言，情况比较复杂， 很多国家都提交了报告。 中国的国家报告指出，如果将“生态红线”政策纳入30%的目标，那么， 他们得出的结果是已经达到了30%的目标。 这些区域的划界是在2023年确定的。当然，这30%的目标是可以因国家的具体国情而定的，也就是说，这是一个全球目标，并不意味着每个国家都必须执行30%。 因为这取决于各国的具体情况，取决于各国的生态系统，取决于它们面临的压力，不能要求小型的发展中的岛国必须保护其30%的领土。 但有些国家可以做得更多，总而言之，中国在其国家报告中指出，如果将“红线”的七项空间规划政策也包括在内，那么，这个保护范围则为30%。

**法广****：**当然，这里的30%涉及的仅仅是对陆地的保护，而对海洋的保护则相对要落后得多。另外，关于贫困国家关注的有害补助问题，中国政府在 报告中怎么说？

**中国声称完成改革有害补贴数字为****O****元**

**Juliette Landry****：** 是的，关于这一点，我建议你去看一下[中国递交的报告](https://ort.cbd.int/national-reports/nr7/A9FC4580-5596-C3FE-8FCC-0159C843EB2C)。 也许我的翻译有误。 中国表示，到2024年，不再有任何对生物多样性有害的补贴和激励措施。 也就是说，中国已经完成了改革。必须指出的是， 联合国的全球评估是基于各国报告的基础而进行的，但这些报告未必经过核实。因此 ，公民、民间社会和专家也需要关注这些报告。 的确，从二月份到现在，我们没有太多时间阅读150份国家报告，并逐条核查是否真正达到了报告所列水平，总之中国政府在其报告中指出：“中国已完成有害生物多样性的补贴改革，有害生物多样性的补贴和其他激励措施的价值为0元。中国政府已系统性地识别、评估并改革了那些原本可能鼓励过度开发、导致栖息地破坏或加剧环境污染的财政补贴政策。例如，在农业领域，调整了客观上导致农药化肥过度使用，进而影响土壤健康和周边生态系统的补贴方式；在林业领域，改革了可能诱导天然林转化为单一经济林的补助政策；在能源领域，逐步取消了对化石燃料中不利于环境保护的补贴部分。从源头上消除了公共资金对生物多样性的潜在负面影响。“

所以，当你读到这些时，你可能会想：“哇！ 这个国家为实现目标 18做出了巨大贡献。” 但仍然值得更深入地研究一下。 只是目前我们还没有掌握如此详细的信息。

**法广：**另外，融资问题一向是多边谈判的一个老大难的问题，发达国家曾经承诺到2025年每年应向发展中国家提供至少2000亿美元，到2030年增加到每年3000亿美元，因而这7000亿美元的缺口如何获得填补？

**Juliette Landry****：**首先，从数字上来看，7000亿美元是我们所说的总体资金缺口。 它并不一定是 指南北资金流动， 而是涵盖所有方面。但是 ，关于南北资金流动，我们在《昆蒙议定书》框架内规定的数字约为200亿美元。 这就是2025年的目标；我们正朝着这个目标不断迈进。根据最新数据，这个数字已经达到180亿， 到2030年，目标是达到300亿。 中国实际上是捐助方，这意味着，通过昆明基金中国也为其他国际机制做出了贡献 。 但在 计算这200亿美元的方案中，中国并没有被包括在内，因为它是基于经合组织（OECD）的方案，事实上，中国在某种程度上是个例外。 不过，这目前是谈判中的一个因素，因为一些国家—— 特别是那些预算正在大幅削减的西方国家——会说，实际上，我们需要更新南北融资和《生物多样性公约》（CBD）的捐助国名单。 关于这一点的谈判 已经于今年夏天在内罗毕开始，而且进展非常艰难。 在这一点上，中国的立场明确而坚定：中国确实为南南合作做出了贡献。 中国愿意提供援助。 但绝对不想被列入贡献国名单。 所以今年夏天有几个讨论方案摆在桌面上： 例如加拿大、日本、欧盟等国提出需要根据客观标准，比如世界银行的标准，来审查这份名单。但遭到中国、巴西等国的反对， 还有其他方案，提出集体反思共同审查这份名单的标准。 但也遭到中国和其他一些国家的反对。这份名单自2006年以来就维持不变，所以，第十七届缔约方大会将要谈判一个折中的方案，也就是花两年时间来考虑一下被列入这份名单的后果。要知道，这对沙特阿拉伯和卡塔尔等国来说，是一条不可逾越的红线，他们根本不想讨论这个问题。 因此，扩大援助国范围问题将在第十七届联合国气候变化大会（COP17）上成为一个非常重要的议题 。

**同在联合国气候峰会上一样，中国始终坚持自己发展中国家的地位，拒绝加入援助国的行列，不过，与此同时，中国也确实通过南南合作的渠道向贫困国家提供援助，在生物多样性领域，也同样如此，中国在****2022****年中国率先出资****15****亿元人民币设立了****“****昆明生物多样性基金****”****，据中方介绍，已在****40****多个发展中国家落地项目，不过，兰朱莉女士表示，对类似的项目进行评估目前还为时过早。**

**法广：**去年峰会设立了“卡利基金”（Cali Fund）以及有关遗传资源数字序列信息的共享机制，下一步要看的是如何明确全球企业因使用DSI应向该基金支付多少，以及这些资金如何公平分配给发展中国家和原住民？那么，中国政府是否关注此一问题？

**Juliette Landry****：** 是的，这确实是一个重要问题。 因为卡利基金和多边机制，是卡利峰会（COP16）上通过的一项有趣的创新，它允许调动私人资金。我认为这是《生物多样性公约》的一项非常有趣的创新，至于中国的立场。 总体而言，中国支持这一机制。 我上次参与谈判时，中国表达的观点是关于一些大家可能不太关心的话题。 例如关于计划在COP18上评估该机制的问题，中国会说，还为时过早，不过中国仍然支持该机制， 总之，所有国家都同意，目前这个基金资金仅有6000美元，但这是因为各国没有义务向该基金捐款。 而这最终也将在峰会上决定， 例如，能否提出某种证书制度？ 如何实施？ 我们如何测试激励企业通过该基金分享利润的方案？但可以说，中国不会阻挠它。 关于对这个议题的讨论相当有建设性，就如同对其他议题一样。

**中国声称：土著土地利用保有权不适用于中国国情而未应用**

**法广：**最后，去年的峰会还设立了一个新的保障土族居民参与的机制，中国媒体对此鲜有报道，[中国递交给联合国的报告](https://ort.cbd.int/national-reports/nr7/A9FC4580-5596-C3FE-8FCC-0159C843EB2C)中在此一栏目上是一片空白，相关的解释是： 土著人民和地方社区传统领地上的土地利用变化和土地保有权）因不适用于中国国情而并未在国家监测和报告体系中得到应用。如何解释北京拒绝纳入第22 个目标。它的具体内容又是什么？

**Juliette Landry****：**两年来，一个新的机构成立了，专门负责传统知识的研究，尤其包括土著居民和当地社区的传统知识。 这个机构是与DSI共同创建的，也是卡莉的两项创新之一。 因此，除了现有的框架之外，还有一个负责处理生物多样性传统知识的新附属机构，这必然会在文本起草等方面赋予土著人民和地方社区重要的地位。 关于这一点，第十七届缔约方大会（COP17）需要决定他的运作模式，议程上的问题包括：该机构将由两位共同主席负责起草缔约方大会的决定。 其设想是由缔约国指定一位共同主席，另一位共同主席则直接由土著人民和地方社区通过其自身的代表机制选出。 然而，这引发了一个关于主权的问题。我们想强调的是，这是一个附属机构。 所以，土著人民和当地社区的参与度会更高，但最终决定文本的仍然是缔约方大会（COP）。 因此，各国显然仍然有权改变他们对将在缔约方大会上提交的文本的看法，但就多边主义而言，这也是一项有趣的创新，因为我们不再总是处于纯粹的政府间框架内。 还有其他一些群体正在组织起来，他们也应该得到更好的代表， 所以这将是一个重要的问题。 我们知道，有些国家，例如俄罗斯，完全反对赋予土著居民和当地社区在多边主义中更直接的作用。 中国自然也非常关注国家主权。 所以，主要就是以上这些关键的问题。

非常感谢法国可持续发展与国际关系学院的生物多样性项目负责人Juliette Landry 兰朱莉女士接受法广的采访。

title: China-North Korea border bridge may do little to spur trade, experts say
zh_title: 专家表示，中朝边境大桥可能对刺激贸易无济于事
source: 菲律宾在中国紧张局势中加强其最北端的防御
summary: 本周，随着中国和朝鲜新鸭绿江大桥的剪彩，官员们用重要的措辞描述了新的过境点。中国总理李强表示，这座连接中国丹东和朝鲜新义州的 3 公里（1.9 英里）大桥将“大力促进”贸易并“加强情感纽带”。 ## 推荐故事列表，共 4 项 * 列表 1（共 4 项）[曼联的马丁内斯在与卡里克会谈后为自己的爆发道歉](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/15/martinez-apologises-for-man-united-outburst-after-carrick-talks) * 列表 2（共 4 项）[以色列停止从以色列进口商品]
content:
本周，随着中国和朝鲜新鸭绿江大桥的剪彩，官员们用重要的措辞描述了新的过境点。

中国总理李强表示，这座连接中国丹东和朝鲜新义州的 3 公里（1.9 英里）大桥将“大力促进”贸易并“加强情感纽带”。

## 推荐故事

4 项清单
* 清单 1（共 4 项）[曼联球员马丁内斯为与卡里克会谈后的爆发道歉](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/10/15/martinez-apologises-for-man-united-outburst-after-carrick-talks)
* 4 项中的第 2 项[以色列停止商业货物进入加沙；哈马斯否认税收索赔](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/15/israel-halts-commercial-goods-from-entering-gaza-hamas-denies-tax-claims)
* 列出 4 项中的 3 项[三名儿童、一名教师在俄勒冈州学校枪击事件中丧生](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/15/at-least-4-include-3-children-killed-in-us-elementary-school-shooting)
* 列出 4 条中的 4 条[两条叙利亚管道在能源基础设施遭受一系列袭击中受损](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/10/15/two-syrian-pipelines-damaging-amid-spate-of-attacks-on-energy-infrastruct)

列表末尾
朝鲜总理朴太成表示，相信该过境点将“加速两国繁荣的进程”，并为两国经济合作“增添新的活力”。

对于中朝关系的分析人士则要谨慎得多。

North Korean Premier Pak Thae-song expressed his belief that the crossing would “accelerate the advance for the prosperity of the two countries” and “add fresh vigour” to their economic cooperation.

Analysts on China-North Korea ties are much more circumspect.

While the bridge is a concrete symbol of China and North Korea’s efforts to revitalise relations that have waned from their Cold War-era peak, the prospects for trade are hindered by obstacles ranging from international sanctions to a North Korean leadership that prioritises security above all else, experts say.

“It reflects China’s renewed effort to strengthen its relationship with North Korea at a time of changing regional alignments,” Phillip Park, a professor at the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, South Korea, told Al Jazeera.

“But whether this leads to substantially deeper economic integration, greater North Korean dependence, or a significant shift in Pyongyang’s strategic orientation remains an open question.

“The bridge could facilitate trade and logistics, but it does not remove international sanctions,” Park added.

China, whose troops fought alongside Pyongyang in the 1950-53 Korean War, has long been North Korea’s most crucial economic benefactor.

China accounts for as much as 95 percent of official trade with the secretive country, which is among the world’s most diplomatically and economically isolated states.

Before the four-lane New Yalu River Bridge officially opened on Thursday, road and rail freight between Dandong and Sinuiju, the main route for China-North Korea trade, travelled exclusively via the ageing Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge.

Opened in 1943, the bridge, which has a single-lane road and a rail track, can only carry vehicles weighing a maximum of 20 tonnes.

Jae-woo Joo, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Kyung Hee University in Seoul, said the new bridge could “tremendously” boost trade between the sides, including the transfer of components banned under sanctions against Pyongyang’s nuclear and missile programmes.

“It is therefore really significant to open this bridge with China,” Joo told Al Jazeera.

After coming under strain from North Korea’s nuclear weapons tests in the mid-2000s, Beijing-Pyongyang ties have warmed under Chinese President Xi Jinping and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

At Xi and Kim’s most recent meeting in June, their seventh summit since 2018, the leaders pledged to enhance cooperation in areas spanning trade, defence, agriculture, law, science and technology.

Analysts have, in part, cast Beijing’s deepening engagement with Pyongyang as a response to the latter’s growing ties with Moscow, which have included the deployment of thousands of North Korean troops to the front lines of Russia’s war in Ukraine.

Last month, North Korean and Russian officials opened the first road bridge linking their countries across the Tumen River.

Chinese President Xi Jinping walks with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, right, to a reception following a military parade to commemorate the 80th anniversary of Japan’s World War II surrender held in front of Tiananmen Gate in Beijing, China, on September 3, 2025 [Mahesh Kumar/AP]

North Korea and China’s two-way trade grew 25 percent in 2025 to reach $2.74bn, according to figures from China’s General Administration of Customs.

Bilateral trade has continued to grow in 2026, jumping nearly 20 percent to reach $1.5bn in the first half of the year, putting it on track to reach its highest volumes since the COVID-19 pandemic.

But while growing, trade remains relatively minuscule in the context of global commerce.

With China’s overall trade hitting $6.36 trillion in 2025, North Korea’s contribution to the total was a little more than 0.04 percent.

Official trade between the neighbours also remains substantially below its 2010s heyday.

Trade hovered around $5-6bn throughout much of the decade, peaking at $6.45bn in 2013.

Economists have offered explanations for the slowdown that range from tightened sanctions to China’s waning reliance on imports amid its efforts to boost economic self-reliance.

Christopher Green, a senior consultant for the Korean Peninsula at International Crisis Group, said the new border crossing’s significance should not be overstated, considering that China-North Korea trade “is fundamentally driven by politics”.

“Lack of cross-border transit routes is not the main obstacle,” Green told Al Jazeera.

“If the bridge opening signifies a political desire on both sides to give political cover to rising trade volumes, then a boost to trade should follow,” Green said, describing ties up until now as “steady-as-she-goes” economic engagement.

“Time will tell. But the key is the politics of national security, not economics.”

Vehicles drive through a new bridge linking China and North Korea as it opened in North Phyongan province, North Korea, on October 15, 2026 [Cha Song Ho/AP]

As much as officials have hailed the New Yalu River Bridge as a reflection of Chinese-North Korean cooperation, the project had a long and torturous road to completion.

Construction began in 2011 and was finished on the Chinese side in 2014.

But North Korean authorities only completed roads and customs facilities on their side of the river this year following repeated pauses in construction amid tensions with Beijing.

“The 12-year delay certainly suggests that economic cooperation is more conditional than the language of friendship might imply,” Marco Mari, a PhD researcher at Bocconi University in Italy who studies China-North Korea economic ties, told Al Jazeera.

“The bridge can facilitate supplies and economic activity, while Russian support gives North Korea alternatives that diminish Beijing’s leverage,” Mari added.

“This does not necessarily imply broader economic reform or a comparable improvement in ordinary people’s lives.”

Chinese Premier Li Qiang, on screen, makes a speech through video conference as a new bridge linking China and North Korea opens in North Phyongan province, North Korea, Thursday, October 15, 2026 [Jon Chol Jin/AP]

Weiqi Zhang, an associate professor at Suffolk University who studies relations between North Korea and China, said the history of China-North Korea economic ties is littered with abortive projects, such as the Hwanggumpyong Special Economic Zone, a North Korean-Chinese development near Dandong.

“There were cases, like the Hwanggumpyong Special Economic Zone – established by China and North Korea – where China built infrastructure on its side, but North Korea didn’t even pave the road on their side,” Zhang told Al Jazeera.

“One reason is that, unlike its neighbours, North Korean government doesn’t really pay much attention to trade for economic development,” Zhang said.

“International trade is used by North Korea more like a foreign policy tool.”

With China wishing to demonstrate its “indispensability” as a trade partner and North Korea eager to strengthen their economic ties, trade is likely to grow, said Edward Howell, a lecturer in international Relations at the University of Oxford.

Even so, economic engagement will be subject to political considerations, Howell said.

“North Korea will obviously want to avoid facing any Chinese influence to change its economic model, but Pyongyang will want to reap the economic benefits of trade with its principal economic benefactor,” Howell told Al Jazeera.

**台湾 取消“社保等级制”的艰辛历程**

来源：https://qitongshe.com/article/5630427278639081

编者按：近日，中国官方表示要动员未参保人员加入社保体系，做到“应保尽保”，社保再次成为热议话题。本篇简略讲述了台湾国民年金的改革历程，或可为中国未来的社保改革提供某种参考。

**台湾“社保”，其正式名称叫：国民年金。**

台湾年金制度是一个非常复杂的系统，具体包括军人保险、军人退抚、公教人员保险(公务员、公私校教职员)、公务人员退休、学者教职员退休、私校退抚、政务人员退职、法官退养金、劳工保险、劳工退休、民众年金、老农津贴、农民健康保险等13种制度。

当时的年金制度确实对军公教群体有利，特别是18%的优惠存款利率，让军公教群体在退休后每月可以领取丰厚的退休金并享受较好的福利。这在岛内年轻人失业率颇高，工资水平连年未涨的背景下，确实显得十分“扎眼”。

可见的忧患就是：**按当时费率与给付水平，各行年金制度正面临收支失衡，且随着财政不断恶化，迟早要破产。**

首先要说的是，在马英九执政初期，台湾“社保”资金不足的压力就越来越大，到了2014年，台湾的退抚基金收支出现逆转，有人甚至预估10年后将会破产。

**年金改革势在必行，这也得到岛内主流民意认同。**

之前，历届台湾当局也曾对军公教群体的福利进行过改革，马英九当局于2012年直接取消了军公教的年终慰问金，引发该群体的强烈不满，而军公教群体政治意识形态普遍偏蓝，是国民党的“铁票仓”，这导致国民党在2014年的“九合一选举”中遭遇惨败。

长期以来，军公教群体一直被视为国民党坚定支持者、蓝营“铁票”，且迄今仍是“忠贞”国民党员的集结地。**国民党要改革当时的年金制度，必须刀口向内动基本盘**，也注定其年金改革必然成为短命动作。

**蔡英文上任之前，台湾这种长期实行的三六九等的社会保障制度，已经饱受诟病！**

公务员、军人、教师的社保待遇位于最高层，甩工农民众八条街。一直以来，实行退休金双轨制，吃皇粮人群的退休金是普通工人农民的3到5倍。

劳工与公务员同样工作30年，劳工退休后只能月领2.5万元左右，而公务员每月可以领到6万元，另外还有一笔一次领取的124万元公保养老金，由此不难看出劳工与军公教人員退休所得存在天壤之别。

台湾中底层民众怨声载道，苦不堪言，而国民党利益集团成员却享受着高高在上的特权，吃香喝辣，骄奢贪腐，因此台湾省内社会矛盾日益扩大，社会动荡不安！

**2016年蔡英文上任之后随即着手拆除不合理的等级制，大胆触动利益集团的蛋糕，发起“年金制度改革”。**

蔡英文任命陈建仁为年金改革委员会召集人、民进党智囊林万亿为副召集人兼执行长，全面推动改革事宜。他们接连召开20次年金改革座谈会;于当年12月31日和次年1月7日、8日、14日分别召开北中南东四区分场会议。按计划，行政机构与“考试院”要于5月20日前完成相关改革方案，提交给立法机构审议。

军公教群体成为此次改革的焦点，主要包括：一、是否继续维持军公教18%的优惠存款利率，即“18趴”;二、是否降低所得替代率，即员工退休后领取的给付与退休前薪资所得的比值;三、是否延迟退休到65岁;四、如何提升基金经营绩效，增加基金总额;五、特殊对象，如党职并公职、法官与检察官、公营行库职工、政务人员等这些人的退抚金计算与领取到底该如何处理。

**无论如何，军公教都是“改革”主要对象，****是最大的利益受损者****。**

动人利益，无异于“杀人父母”，按鲁迅的说法，搬张桌子都要流血，何况是这样大刀阔斧的砍别人的实打实的收入。

2017年的9月3日，军公教人员就开始了游行示威活动，参与人数出人意料地多达近15万人(警方保守估计)，成为蔡英文执政后首场规模最大的街头抗争活动。

针对年金改革方案，蓝绿双方在台立法机构曾大打出手；中华统一党等台湾党派还曾打出五星红旗，反对民进党当局推行的年金改革。

于是，我们有幸看到大陆各大媒体有关台湾军公教上街抗议蔡英文政府的消息，并配有大篇幅图文并茂的内容以及耸人听闻的标题，媒体集体得出的结论是：蔡英文政府完了！

然而，蔡英文并没有被军公教上街抗议所吓倒，她公开回应称：“我也理解，在改革的过程里，难免有些冲击。但是我要再一次强调，年金改革最重要的意义，就是要保障我们每一个人的下一代、保障世世代代台湾人都能够拥有安定的退休生活。我们这一代人的牺牲，是为了让下一代更好。如果我们不改革，我们就对不起下一代”。

经过反复沟通和不懈坚持，台湾的军公教利益群体在蔡英文及其团队的感召下终于理解并接受了政府的年金制度改革方案，从此台湾社会走向了人人平等，民安省富的时代！

现在，台湾各界退休人员的保障水平基本公平。以农民为例，65岁起领到的老农津贴加上退休储金每个月可以领到37027元（人民币8516.21元）。

## 香港新推工業品牌、廟宇文化等四個旅遊熱點項目

2026-10-16 17:10 聯合報／ 香港特派員[李春](https://udn.com/news/reporter/MDM4NjY=)/即時報導  香港

[**香港**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF)發展旅遊熱點，年底起再推出四個項目，包括九龍巴士車廠、廟宇漫遊等，為觀光客提供更多香港特色的多元化旅遊體驗。

[**港府**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E6%B8%AF%E5%BA%9C)政務司副司長卓永興領導的「發展旅遊熱點工作組」，首階段已推出九個旅遊熱點項目，包括香港工業[**品牌**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E5%93%81%E7%89%8C)旅遊、維園市集、紫花風鈴木園、舊城中環深度遊等，港府說這些項目受到歡迎，決意推出更多熱點項目。

卓永興說，港府要透過加強跨部門統籌並結合社會各界力量，在今年底起，分階段推出涵蓋工業品牌、微型藝術、宗教文化及地區風貌等主題的旅遊熱點項目，向旅客展現香港獨特的文化底蘊及城市面貌。

新的四個項目包括第二階段香港工業品牌旅遊，新增項目涵蓋九龍巴士車廠、港鐵「載遇‧站見」鐵路展，以及北京同仁堂香港生產研發基地等；

第二個項目是香港微型城市展，香港杜莎夫人蠟像館將於今年第四季起，於山頂凌霄閣重塑香港微型城市展。新展覽將加入全新精緻的微型藝術展品，立體展現香港的地標建築、地道習俗及生活特色；

第三個項目是推廣宗教文化深度遊，港府會進一步研究以廟宇為核心，串連各區具文化價值的歷史建築及古蹟，打造廟宇文化深度遊的漫遊路線；

第四個項目是元朗民政事務處將與地區團體合作，推出「元朗好時節」項目，鼓勵旅客全年按不同主題探索元朗地區特色，例如於天后誕到元朗市中心觀賞盛大的會景巡遊，以及於秋冬季節走訪自然生態景點，尋紅葉、覓候鳥等。

另外香港的「粵艇南下」項目，即廣東遊艇南下香港今日首航，首批五艘遊艇中午起駛入香港水域，並陸續進入大嶼山遊艇會停泊，香港海事處船隻鳴笛迎接。五艘遊艇分別來自深圳、珠海及南沙，將在香港休閒和購物數日。

title: 澳洲初步裁定中国进口铝制门窗存在倾销 立即开征最高73.3%临时保证金

content:
澳大利亚贸易救济委员会（Australian Trade Remedies Commission，前身为反倾销委员会）初步认定，中国生产的铝制门窗以倾销价格进入澳大利亚市场，大幅压低本地产品价格，对澳大利亚相关产业造成损害。从10月15日起，以保证金的形式对中国铝制门窗征收临时反倾销税和反补贴税。这一规定引发了建筑成本可能上涨以及中国可能采取反制措施的警告。

澳大利亚贸易救济委员会在[初步报告](https://www.industry.gov.au/sites/default/files/atrc/public-record/2026-10/691-501-report-statement-of-essential-facts-sef-691.pdf)中认定，除一家中国出口商外，所有接受调查的中国出口商在2024年7月1日至2025年6月30日的调查期内均存在倾销行为。

委员会发现，根据不同出口商的情况，这些产品的倾销幅度介于正常价格的5.3%至70.4%之间，部分出口商获得了中国各级政府提供的少量补贴。

委员会认定，中国进口产品已经对澳大利亚相关产业“造成实质性损害”。

委员会估计，在调查期内，澳大利亚铝制门窗市场的价值约为28亿澳元，中国进口产品占总销售额的19%，澳大利亚本土产品约占79%，其余2%来自其他国家。

委员会估计，中国进口产品已导致澳大利亚相关产业损失3.5亿澳元。(ABC News: Yiying Li)

报告指出，从2021年7月至2025年6月，澳大利亚本地制造商的销售量下降了约19%，销售额从2023财年的峰值下跌了约14%。

委员会发现，在其审查的相关铝制门窗招标和报价中，有一半的报价比预期价格低约30%；超过四分之一的报价则低了40%或以上。

委员会估计，由于“来自中国的倾销和／或获得补贴的进口产品”压低价格，澳大利亚相关产业损失了约3.5亿澳元。

委员会已提议建议工业与创新部长蒂姆·艾尔斯（Tim Ayres）发布反倾销税公告，对来自中国的相关进口产品征收反倾销税。

根据《中澳自由贸易协定》，目前中国制造的铝制门窗不需要缴纳关税。

艾尔斯的一名发言人表示，阿尔巴尼斯政府支持自由、公平的贸易。

发言人说：“澳大利亚贸易救济委员会根据业界提出的申请，开展严格、以证据为依据的调查。”

“任何实施的贸易救济措施都完全符合澳大利亚在贸易协定下承担的义务。”

## 保证金可能“实际上导致价格上涨”

委员会专员表示，在调查继续进行期间，有必要要求进口商交纳保证金，以“防止澳大利亚相关产业受到实质性损害”。

从10月15日起，进口商必须提供相当于产品价值5.3%至73.3%的临时保证金，每家企业的具体缴纳比例基于其倾销幅度而不同。

这些保证金用于确保进口商能够支付未来可能需要缴纳的反倾销和反补贴税。是否最终征税，将由澳大利亚工业与创新部长作出决定。

专家表示，征收临时保证金可能推高铝制门窗价格。(ABC News: Lily Nothling)

新南威尔士大学国际经济法教授周围欢表示，贸易救济委员会发布的初裁结论“很难改变”，因此最终实施反倾销和反补贴税的可能性很大。

他说，中国铝制门窗的进口商要交纳保证金可能会“实际上导致价格上涨”，因为进口商会将保证金成本考虑在定价之中。

周教授说：“价格受到的影响将体现为进口铝制门窗价格上涨，进而推高商业和住宅建筑项目的建造成本。”

## “维护公平竞争，抵制不正当贸易”

这项调查于2025年11月25日启动，由澳大利亚建材商文托拉集团（Ventora Group）和澳大利亚玻璃与门窗协会（Australian Glass and Window Association，AGWA）提出申请。

申请方指称，本地产业因销售流失和价格受到压制而“遭受实质性损害”。

澳大利亚玻璃与门窗协会首席执行官克林顿·斯基奥克（Clinton Skeoch）告诉澳大利亚广播公司（ABC）：“我们并不是要求政府保护澳大利亚企业免受竞争。”

> "我们要求政府维护公平竞争，免受不公平贸易行为影响。"

该协会对收取保证金的措施表示欢迎，并称对于一个长期承受倾销进口产品巨大压力的产业而言，这是“一项重要且积极的进展”。

ABC已向中国商务部和中国驻澳大利亚大使馆寻求回应。

周教授表示，中国会采取报复措施的可能性不大，因为从历史上看，中国针对澳大利亚采取的反倾销和反补贴措施，远少于澳大利亚针对中国采取的同类措施。

但他说：“这并非完全不可能。而如果中国决定采取行动，澳大利亚的农产品出口可能成为目标。”

调查期间，媒体报道对中国铝制门窗的质量提出了质疑。(ABC Central West: Luke Wong)

文托拉集团曾委托对中国铝制门窗进行检测，澳大利亚玻璃与门窗协会随后公开了检测结果。

委员会表示，在作出初步裁定时，并未考虑这些检测结果，也没有考虑有关产品质量或合规性的其他指控。

## 建筑商担忧成本上涨

澳大利亚建筑商协会（Master Builders Australia）代理首席执行官梅丽莎·伯恩（Melissa Byrne）表示，该协会将“仔细审查委员会的调查结果”。

> "与此同时，任何导致建筑成本上升的措施，都恰逢住房可负担性和项目可行性仍面临巨大压力的时期。"

她表示，澳大利亚“绝不能限制高质量、符合规定的建筑产品和材料的流通”。

贸易救济委员会将于12月16日前提交最终建议。预计工业与创新部长将在收到建议后的30天内作出决定。

最终报告将在部长作出决定后公布。

人工智慧世代到來，許多人遇到疑難雜症時，第一時間都是求助AI，但也有人把AI的話當成聖旨，甚至要求專業人士照AI做。近日專精於椎間盤突出與坐骨神經痛的醫師徐國峰分享自己遇到的奇葩案例，有位病患上門時，把整疊AI診斷砸到桌上，要求按照上面進行治療，讓他傻眼「當我得來速嗎」。

徐國峰日前在[臉書粉專發文](https://www.facebook.com/msnhsu/posts/pfbid0UfGzg8jR2zwEynjw41LHuz2ZQbNGKBd4HG3dSmMhzXw4QhKcxy1Ur2VLWrKTQF4Al?locale=zh_TW)「資料印了整整十五頁，結果只准林北回答一個好字？」表示近來有位初診患者一坐下來，就把整疊比論文還厚的A4紙砸到桌上，除了MRI報告外，還有10幾頁的ChatGPT對話紀錄，上面甚至用螢光筆與紅筆標好重點，讓他一時以為是大學指考衝刺筆記。

患者開口說「AI說我腳麻是因為椎間盤突出、椎管狹窄，加上第二級滑脫害的，你照這個方向處理就好」，當他詢問是小腿哪邊、走幾步會麻？下樓梯會不會踩空時，患者竟露出不耐表情，「上面不都寫了嗎，就是神經壓迫啊」，徐國峰解釋，需要敲反射、測肌力，確認症狀跟片子有沒有對上，話音未落，患者就不客氣打斷詢問「AI都交叉比對完了，你照上面處置很難嗎」。

徐國峰形容，當下心裡真的是有1萬隻「草泥馬」狂奔而過，花貴鬆鬆的掛號費進來是來看病還是點得來速的？直言真的很賭爛，對連人長什麼樣都不知道的伺服器代碼虔誠得像在拜北港媽祖，卻百般質疑眼前的活人醫師。徐國峰強調，自己也天天用AI，但脊椎這檔事從來就不是報告有名詞就代表抓到病因，感嘆AI很會說，但隔著螢幕有辦法檢測到患者肌肉萎縮嗎？敲得出膝反射嗎？連患者坐在診間翹二郎腿都看不到。

文末徐國峰表示，患者可以帶十頁資料來考試，也可以帶一百個問題來抬槓，但走進診間，請留一點空間縫隙，讓檢查跟專業說話，「身上的病痛，真的不會因為你辯贏了就自己痊癒，相信醫生，相信專業好嗎」，並貼出一張告示「已經在GPT獲得診斷的患者，請勿再向我們尋求意見，請改向Google查詢，但Threads真的不建議」。

title: Impeachment as democracy’s necessary check
summary: THE latest Pulse Asia survey, conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, places Sara Duterte at 50 percent in presidential preference for 2028. For those troubled by the allegations against her, this is a sobering reminder that electoral popularity and
content:
THE latest Pulse Asia survey, conducted from Sept. 17 to 24, places Sara Duterte at 50 percent in presidential preference for 2028. For those troubled by the allegations against her, this is a sobering reminder that electoral popularity and fitness for public office can travel in opposite directions.

A survey measures preference. It cannot certify honesty, reconcile financial records or absolve constitutional violations. Yet Duterte’s defenders treat her continuing popularity as though millions of supporters could collectively erase questions that demand documentary answers. When loyalty becomes a substitute for accountability, democracy risks becoming an elaborate mechanism for rewarding impunity.

This is why impeachment matters. It provides a constitutional means of protecting the republic when electoral judgment fails. The Senate can prevent irrational political allegiance from returning a demonstrably unfit official to power, provided it establishes impeachable wrongdoing through a fair examination of evidence. Popularity must never become immunity.

*   [Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

Political theory gives us reasons to question the comforting assumption that voters reliably make informed, rational choices. Anthony Downs’ concept of rational ignorance explains why people may invest little effort in learning about politics. Acquiring information takes time, while one individual’s vote has an exceedingly small chance of deciding an election.

What makes sense for an individual can produce disastrous collective consequences. A citizen may find it easier to repeat a slogan than understand a financial disclosure. Multiply that shortcut across millions and an election can reward the candidate with the strongest emotional appeal rather than the strongest record of honesty.

Bryan Caplan goes further in “The Myth of the Rational Voter.” His concept of rational irrationality explains how voters can indulge comforting political beliefs because the personal cost of doing so appears negligible. People gain emotional satisfaction from believing what they want, while the consequences of misguided choices are shared by society.

Caplan’s principal evidence concerns economic policy. Applying his framework to unconditional loyalty toward a political personality is therefore an interpretation, rather than a finding about Duterte’s supporters. Nevertheless, the mechanism is recognizable. Admitting that one’s political idol has failed can be emotionally expensive. Dismissing inconvenient evidence can feel reassuringly cheap.

The resulting harm extends beyond the loyalist. Citizens who never supported that politician must also live under the administration that electoral devotion helps produce. Irrational voting carries a public cost. The satisfaction of defending an idol is privately enjoyed; the damage from installing an unfit leader is collectively endured.

*   ![Image 1: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

Geoffrey Brennan and Loren Lomasky’s theory of expressive voting adds another explanation. Voting can function as an expression of identity, belonging, resentment or solidarity. A ballot may resemble cheering for a team. Supporting the candidate communicates who the voter is and which community the voter considers home.

This helps explain why damaging information can fail to weaken political allegiance. A supporter who experiences criticism of Duterte as an attack on personal identity may defend her more fiercely. The question shifts from whether she has answered the evidence to whether one’s political camp will be humiliated by conceding anything.

Christopher Achen and Larry Bartels, in “Democracy for Realists,” likewise challenge the picture of citizens calmly comparing policies before choosing leaders. They emphasize social identities and partisan attachments. Political loyalties can shape how people perceive facts, enabling the same conduct to appear unforgivable in an opponent and excusable in an ally.

These theories cannot establish that every Duterte supporter is irrational. Nor does one survey reveal what each respondent knows or believes. They do explain why counting preferences cannot settle questions of competence and integrity. Persistent refusal to confront substantiated wrongdoing deserves criticism, regardless of how numerous or enthusiastic its defenders become.

*   ![Image 2: ‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260179.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/news/our-soldiers-are-not-troublemakers/2445870)

The argument for impeachment becomes stronger when supporters openly declare that no revelation could change their minds. Such loyalty abandons democratic scrutiny. It turns public office into a personal entitlement and makes constitutional accountability indispensable to the republic.

Constitutional democracy anticipates that popular judgment may falter. It distributes authority among institutions and imposes obligations that public enthusiasm cannot cancel. Article XI declares public office a public trust and identifies grounds for impeachment, including culpable constitutional violations, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust.

Impeachment is political because it addresses the abuse of public power through constitutionally designated political institutions. Its political character binds it to the protection of the republic. Alexander Hamilton’s discussion in “Federalist No. 65” links impeachment to violations of public trust and injuries to society, while warning against decisions governed by factional strength.

That warning applies directly to senators who might confuse Duterte’s survey numbers with a reason to excuse proven misconduct. Their obligation is to examine the charges, hear the defense and decide whether the evidence establishes constitutional grounds for conviction. Electoral calculations cannot discharge that obligation.

*   ![Image 3: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

Questions about asset declarations, unexplained wealth or the misuse of public funds require answers on their merits. If the evidence establishes impeachable wrongdoing, senators must act despite the respondent’s popularity. If it fails, they must decline to convict. The integrity of this check depends on principled judgment.

The Constitution permits impeachment judgments extending to removal and disqualification from public office. That power has a protective purpose: An official found culpable need not remain available for another electoral rehabilitation. Voters retain the right to choose among qualified candidates. Public support cannot compel institutions to disregard constitutionally established disqualification.

Senators are also vulnerable to irrationality, ambition and partisan attachment. Their election does not confer monopoly on wisdom. Robinhood Padilla is exhibit No. 1. This makes their conduct under oath especially consequential. They must demonstrate that constitutional responsibility can prevail over personal loyalty, anticipated electoral rewards and fear of offending a powerful political following.

The Senate can save irrational voters from making a mockery of democracy by enforcing accountability against proven abuses of public trust. Refusing that duty because an accused official remains popular would surrender constitutional government to political fandom.

Democracy deserves citizens willing to reconsider their loyalties and institutions willing to uphold their obligations. When voters will not confront proven unfitness, impeachment becomes a necessary check. Senators must have the courage to use it.

The author is a professor at the University of the Philippines Los Baños and vice chairman of the board of the People’s Television Network Inc.

title: BARMM coalition gets majority with 46 MPs
summary: **DAVAO CITY**— Not just 41 as earlier expected, but 46 Members of Parliament signed the coalition documents, which, in the words of Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, would pave the way for an inclusive government that br
content:
**DAVAO CITY**— Not just 41 as earlier expected, but 46 Members of Parliament signed the coalition documents, which, in the words of Bangsamoro Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, would pave the way for an inclusive government that bridges political divisions and serves all BARMM communities.

In a press briefing in this city, Macacua said the coalition would prioritize unity among the Bangsamoro people after the region’s first parliamentary elections, stressing that the incoming government must serve constituents regardless of their political affiliations or electoral choices.

“After the formal assumption of the Government of the Day, we will pursue a program for the unity of all Bangsamoro,” Macacua said.

*   [More complaints filed vs Magalang mayor](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/12/regions/more-complaints-filed-vs-magalang-mayor/2443357)

Macacua described the coalition as broad and inclusive, reflecting the diversity of the region and the need for political leaders to work together beyond the divisions created during the election campaign.

Macacua emphasized that the responsibility of the new government would extend beyond those who voted for its members, encompassing every community, province and sector across the Bangsamoro region.

According to Macacua, the coalition would reach out to other groups, heal divisions and build a government capable of responding to the needs of the entire Bangsamoro population.

The commitment to inclusive governance comes as the newly elected Parliament prepares to organize the region’s first fully elected parliamentary government, marking a significant stage in BARMM’s transition from an interim administration.

*   ![Image 1: Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/13/1258203.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Marcos’ impeachment plot backfires](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/opinion/columns/marcos-impeachment-plot-backfires/2444878)

[![Image 2: No Image](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260105.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1260105.jpg)

The 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament emerged from the Sept. 14 elections, in which no single political party secured the 41 seats needed to command a majority. The coalition arrangement is therefore central to efforts to establish a working parliamentary majority. The 46 lawmakers who signed the coalition documents exceed the 41-member threshold required for a majority in the 80-seat Parliament, providing the coalition with a numerical basis to organize the incoming government.

The Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), chaired by Macacua, emerged as the largest party in the elections, securing 31 seats when party and district seats were combined, according to election reporting. The United Bangsamoro Justice Party and the BARMM Grand Coalition also secured substantial representation in the new legislature.

Macacua thanked the 46 elected lawmakers for their trust and commitment, as well as the national government for respecting BARMM’s institutions and political processes.

*   ![Image 3: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

He said the coalition was prepared to move forward once Parliament convenes, with its members united by the objective of serving the Bangsamoro people.

The coalition’s formation comes at a crucial point in the region’s political transition, as elected lawmakers prepare to assume their responsibilities and determine the leadership and direction of the incoming parliamentary government.

The 80 newly elected members are scheduled to assume office on Oct. 30, when Parliament is expected to organize the new government and elect a chief minister.

[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

title: Haze worsens air quality in Singapore, East Timor
summary: **SINGAPORE** — Air pollution in one part of Singapore hit the city-state’s “very high” band on Wednesday while East Timor shut schools, as haze from forest fires in Indonesia is causing a regional crisis. The blazes have burned through hun
content:
**SINGAPORE** — Air pollution in one part of Singapore hit the city-state’s “very high” band on Wednesday while East Timor shut schools, as haze from forest fires in Indonesia is causing a regional crisis.

The blazes have burned through hundreds of thousands of hectares of forest and plantations on the Borneo and Sumatra islands, sickened residents in Indonesia and sent thick haze across Southeast Asia.

Air pollution in western Singapore on Wednesday hit “very high” — the country’s top level — the National Environment Agency said.

*   [Japan’s PM: Household duties make me busier](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/world/asia-oceania/japans-pm-household-duties-make-me-busier/2445488)

It recorded levels of tiny particulates capable of penetrating the bloodstream and lungs, known as PM2.5, at 288 micrograms per cubic meter, vastly exceeding the World Health Organization’s recommended average annual exposure of five micrograms.

Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, but has seen stronger-than-usual blazes this year as a powerful El Niño cycle brings drought.

Experts also point to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape of Sumatra and Borneo.

The haze has drifted into neighboring Singapore, Malaysia and East Timor, which said it would shut schools nationwide for three days from Thursday, and as far afield as the Philippines.

The closures in East Timor were necessary “as a preventive measure to protect the health of students, teachers and other members of the educational community, given current air quality conditions,” the government said.

*   ![Image 1: Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259220.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Eala eyes fresh start at Ningbo Open](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/15/sports/eala-eyes-fresh-start-at-ningbo-open/2445560)

It urged families to keep children indoors and to use “respiratory protection” if going outside.

Singapore rolled out subsidies for haze-related medical treatment from Monday, a measure last activated in 2015, when similar blazes in Indonesia cloaked Southeast Asia in toxic smoke for weeks.

The city-state has also begun distributing N95 masks to eligible residents when pollution reaches very unhealthy levels.

Singapore’s National Trades Union Congress said on Monday that public transport workers and delivery riders could receive free N95 masks, but Agence France-Presse (AFP) found that uptake was slow.

*   ![Image 2: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

“It’s a little bit uncomfortable to wear a mask, and some orders we have to walk around blocks, or park outside,” a delivery rider, who gave his name only as Daniel, told AFP.

“With the mask, I will have to breathe heavier,” the 27-year-old said.

[![Image 3: BURNING UP Soldiers and firefighters work on containing a wildfire in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan province, Indonesia, on Oct. 13, 2026. AFP PHOTO](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259331.jpg)](https://manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1259331.jpg)
BURNING UP Soldiers and firefighters work on containing a wildfire in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan province, Indonesia, on Oct. 13, 2026. AFP PHOTO

*   ![Image 4: 44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258812.jpeg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

Homes razed,

diplomatic calls

Ong Kwang Wei, 57, who has asthma, said he wore an N95 mask outdoors and carried his inhaler and medication with him at all times.

He was accompanying his 88-year-old mother — also masked — for a health checkup after a recent bout of the flu.

“Once the flu kicks in, my asthma is exacerbated ... I get breathless, I cough, I get phlegm, so I need to use my inhaler,” Ong said.

In Indonesia, tens of thousands of people have sought treatment for respiratory illness linked to haze from fires burning in Borneo, South Sumatra and Papua regions.

On Sumatra island, a fire razed nearly 300 homes, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate, an official said on Tuesday.

Residents first spotted the fire approaching their village in Bangka Belitung province on Saturday and tried to put it out themselves with portable water pumps.

But the fire continued to smolder underground in peatland, and when the wind shifted, the flames moved toward their homes.

The local disaster agency said nearly 1,000 people fled the village.

“My house is gone,” Leni, a 55-year-old villager now staying at a shelter with her family, told AFP.

“There’s nothing left. I could only save myself and take my kids with me ... I panicked and didn’t have the time to grab anything,” said Leni, who, like many Indonesians, has one name.

President Prabowo Subianto on Monday ordered the government to mobilize maximum efforts, with officials saying more than 60,000 personnel had been deployed to combat fires on the ground.

But efforts so far, including cloud seeding and water-bombing, have had limited success.

The haze has prompted Malaysia to request a meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), and on Tuesday Malaysian parliamentarian Syed Saddiq Rahman urged a “diplomatic protest.”

“We must send a diplomatic protest note, not just on behalf of Malaysia, but the Asean. You need to treat them as an outcast in the region,” he said.

title: ‘Our soldiers are not troublemakers’
summary: DEFENSE Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. blasted Vice President Sara Duterte for saying the Philippines is “becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia,” and made clear that the source of all troubles in the region is China. “Can you say that
content:
DEFENSE Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. blasted Vice President Sara Duterte for saying the Philippines is “becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia,” and made clear that the source of all troubles in the region is China.

“Can you say that our soldiers who sacrifice there [in the West Philippine Sea] are troublemakers, when we are only fighting for our rights over the sea that is the future of our country’s sustainability?” Teodoro said in Filipino.

Duterte had made the comment after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called alleged remittances from a Chinese state-owned firm into a company linked to the vice president’s husband a potential national security issue.

*   [44% expect Sara Duterte’s conviction in impeachment trial — survey](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/44-expect-sara-dutertes-conviction-in-impeachment-trial-survey/2445251)

“Is doing business with China really prohibited because it’s a national security risk?” Duterte had said in Filipino. ”We are becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia.” Teodoro made it clear that engaging with the Chinese in business is not prohibited. What’s in question rather is how a public official is allowed to enter into such transactions.

“Filipinos are not prohibited from doing business with China, but the question is, is a public official, first and foremost, allowed to have any business transactions on a certain level? Some are not, some are. That is a question which has to be determined by the proper investigative authorities,” Teodoro said.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

Teodoro cited as an example China-owned or linked businesses in the Philippines that were proven to be illegal or flawed such as the alleged substandard steel, illegal mining and the offshore gaming operations which he said “did not benefit the overall integrity of the Philippines.” “If you are a public official, you have a voice in the stability of our national territory and integrity; if you have transactions with China, these should be studied to determine if they are, above all, legitimate and proper,” the Defense chief said.

Teodoro emphasized that it is China who is the troublemaker and not the Philippines, citing as proof the intention of the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (Asean) member countries to finalize a long-awaited South China Sea Code of Conduct with China.

“China is clearly the troublemaker here, crystal clear, and I will not accept any other narrative on that. It’s obvious; nobody can say that the Philippines is the one causing trouble,” Teodoro said.

*   ![Image 1: Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1258438.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Pangilinan seeks reversal of ruling on Duterte’s dropped charges](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/news/pangilinan-seeks-reversal-of-ruling-on-dutertes-dropped-charges/2445025)

**Chinese talking point**

Vice President Duterte’s use of the word “troublemaker” mirrors Chinese talking points against the Philippines.

China has repeatedly used the label “troublemaker” against the Philippines over the years to describe Manila’s actions in the West Philippine Sea.

In July 2026, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian labeled the Philippines a “troublemaker” in the South China Sea after Manila embedded journalists on resupply missions and patrols, accusing the Philippines of provoking maritime confrontations to “stir up tensions.” In July 2015, following the Philippines’ legal challenge against China’s expansive maritime claims at the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued an official statement explicitly referring to the Philippines as the “real troublemaker in the region.”* China accused Manila of deliberately escalating tensions and violating bilateral agreements.

*   ![Image 2: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

During early disputes following the Scarborough Shoal standoff in July 2013, Maj. Gen. Luo Yuan of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army publicly stated: “The role of the Philippines in the South China Sea is actually, in my view, a troublemaker.” Beijing routinely uses this narrative whenever the Philippines asserts its sovereign rights or brings international visibility to maritime disputes, portraying Manila’s defense measures and joint security partnerships as disruptive to regional peace.

title: Inadmissible evidence may be admitted if not challenged

content:
**_Dear PAO,_**

**_I filed a data privacy case before the National Privacy Commission (NPC), and the said office ruled in my favor. However, the appellate court overturned the NPC’s decision, stating that the text messages I attached to my complaint were unauthenticated and thus inadmissible. This is surprising because the respondent did not even contest the admissibility of the text messages. Can I still elevate the case to the higher court?_**

**_Syl_**

*   [The ‘captain of the ship’ doctrine](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/legal-advice/the-captain-of-the-ship-doctrine/2444935)

Dear Syl,

Yes, you may still elevate the case in the higher court, subject to the prescription period provided for by the Rules of Court.

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

As ruled in the case of Trimillos v. Fcash Global Lending Inc., GR 271360, Aug. 13, 2025, penned by Associate Justice Henri Jean Paul Inting, inadmissible evidence may be admitted if not challenged at the proper time, and such issue may not be raised for the first time on appeal, saying:

“However, in the same case, the Court also recognized that inadmissible evidence may be admitted if not challenged at the proper time and such issue may not be raised for the first time on appeal, viz.:

“In any case, it bears pointing out that petitioner failed to raise his objection to the admissibility of the photos during the proceedings in the RTC. Basic is the rule that in order to exclude evidence, the objection to admissibility of evidence must be made at the proper time, and the grounds therefore be specified. Objection to evidence must be made at the time it is formally offered. In case of documentary evidence, offer is made after all the witnesses of the party making the offer have testified, specifying the purpose for which the evidence is being offered. It is only at this time, and not at any other, that objection to the documentary evidence may be made. When a party failed to interpose a timely objection to evidence at the time they were offered in evidence, such objection shall be considered as waived. This is true even if by its nature the evidence is inadmissible and would have surely been rejected if it had been challenged at the proper time.

*   ![Image 1: Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://miopia.newsroom.bi/statics/i/ps/manilatimes.net/manilatimes/uploads/images/2026/10/14/1257533.jpg?width=113&crop=113:85)
[Laguna mayors rally behind Aragones](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/14/regions/laguna-mayors-rally-behind-aragones/2444954)

“As a complimentary principle, it is well-settled that no question will be entertained on appeal unless it has been raised in the proceedings below. Points of law, theories, issues and arguments not brought to the attention of the lower court, administrative agency or quasi-judicial body, need not be considered by a reviewing court, as they cannot be raised for the first time at that late stage. Basic considerations of fairness and due process impel this rule. Any issue raised for the first time on appeal is barred by estoppel.”

In your case, the respondents did not even contest, in any stage of the proceeding, the admissibility of your evidence. Thus, you can argue before the higher court that by failing to timely raise any objection to the admissibility of the text messages you have attached, the respondent is deemed to have already waived the same. Hence, the text messages are admissible in evidence by virtue of estoppel.

We hope that we were able to answer your queries. This advice was solely based on the facts you have narrated and our appreciation of the same. Our opinion may vary when other facts are changed or elaborated.

Thank you for your continued trust and support.

# Taiwan Plans to Invest $4.4B in Alaska LNG, Subject to Negotiations

The proposed Alaska LNG liquefaction plant on Cook Inlet (Alaska LNG)

By **[The Maritime Executive](https://maritime-executive.com/author/marex)** 2026-10-14 20:15:36

On Wednesday, Taiwan's government confirmed that it currently plans to buy six million tonnes per annum of LNG from the Alaska LNG megaproject, and it intends to make a $4.4 billion investment in the construction of the system, subject to further negotiations.

In a statement on his social media platform on Wednesday, President Donald Trump confirmed that Taiwan had agreed to an "offtake commitment" equaling 30 percent of the plant's output "because this is now a U.S. federal government project." New York-based investment company Glenfarne Group and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation are the project's sole owners, holding equity stakes of 75 percent and 25 percent respectively.

Taiwan's energy ministry couched its commitment in terms of an ongoing negotiating process, pledging "an estimated maximum" investment amount only after further study and budgeting. "Specific investment arrangements, shareholding ratios, and related conditions will be handled according to subsequent negotiations and commercial contract procedures," the ministry said.

Alaska LNG is a longstanding proposal for an infrastructure network to pipe abundant North Slope gas resources across the state to Cook Inlet for liquefaction and export. It would require construction of an 800-mile line connecting gas fields on the Artic tundra to an LNG plant rated at 20 million tonnes per annum.

At one time, Alaska LNG had support from BP, ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips and was advancing steadily as a private-sector venture. All three oil majors backed out in 2016 following an independent assessment of the [project's economics](https://www.offshore-energy.biz/2016/08/30/exxonmobil-bp-conocophilips-back-out-of-alaska-lng). At present, a New York-based investment company and the state-owned Alaska Gasline Development Corporation own the equity in Alaska LNG.

With the need to construct a $9 billion gas treatment plant at the Arctic northern side, then build an 800-mile overland supply pipeline through rugged wilderness, the megaproject is expected to cost $45-55 billion for 20 mtpa of capacity. This works out to as much as $2.7 billion per mtpa, much higher than the $1.6 billion per mtpa capex cost for the LNG Canada Phase 2 project in Kitimat, British Columbia. About 900 nautical miles apart, the two sites are natural competitors: they target the same East Asian market, and at similar scale. Two weeks ago, LNG Canada got the green light from private investors for its $23 billion Phase 2 expansion, which will double its capacity to 28 mtpa.

title: ‘Agriculture minister sounds El Niño warning
summary: As a [super El Niño](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-07-09-godzilla-el-nino-what-it-is-why-it-matters-and-our-complete-coverage) threatens South Africa’s farming sector and the wider economy with drought and potential water sho
content:
As a [super El Niño](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-07-09-godzilla-el-nino-what-it-is-why-it-matters-and-our-complete-coverage) threatens South Africa’s farming sector and the wider economy with drought and potential water shortages, Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp has warned against complacency.

Much of South Africa’s summer rainfall region got decent rains in September, an additional layer of security to good soil moisture and dam levels. But El Niño only typically gains traction here once summer is fully under way.

“We are very much concerned. We had a bit of rain now in September, but I tell farmers, ‘Please, do not be deceived that this is not going to happen.’ Some of our farmers are planting now, and I think we are going to have a very hot and dry November, December and January,” Aucamp told Daily Maverick on the sidelines of the AgriSA congress on Wednesday in Irene.

“We’ve got early-warning systems, but this is going to be next level.”

El Niño usually triggers drought in this region, and the latest event is widely regarded as the strongest on record. It is [expected to last until at least February](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-10-08-el-nino/).

Aucamp is concerned about the timing of water-use restrictions.

“We should not wait for this to be declared a disaster before municipalities put in water restrictions, and then it spills over and farming communities get less water. I think we need to be proactive in implementing water restrictions from the municipalities’ side,” he said.

> “Every municipality will have to decide that on their own, because they know their own resources. But we cannot have a situation where municipalities wait too long to implement what is required, and then water restrictions might have to be implemented on the farming community. We can’t get to a point where they can't irrigate their crops.”

With municipal elections looming, it may be the case that water restrictions before 4 November are not seen as politically wise in some municipalities – but the consequences could be dire. It’s also the case that many South Africans already experience frequent and unintended “water restrictions” because local government failures lead to dry taps.

### A game of yields

Aucamp said the department was advising farmers to focus on their most fertile sections of land and not plant in marginal areas.

Most commercial farmers are probably doing so anyway, guided by high-tech and capital-intensive tools such as precision farming, which enables the precise distribution of inputs based on soil quality using GPS. This is a [key reason behind the surge in South African crop yields](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-08-01-gmos-and-precision-farming-bring-food-prices-down/), rain or shine, in recent decades.

The first indication of the amount of land that will be devoted to summer grain crops, including maize, will come on 27 October when the government’s Crop Estimates Committee will provide its first estimate on farmers’ planting intentions.

Maize fields face a crucial season ahead as South Africa braces for a potentially severe El Niño-induced drought. (Photo: iStock)

Surging fuel and fertiliser prices triggered by the Ukraine and Iran wars will be a constraint. Aucamp said that fertiliser prices had soared by more than 300% since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Turning to livestock, Aucamp said farmers would have to reduce their herd numbers to prevent overgrazing.

A smaller national cattle herd will also reduce the number of vaccines required to contain the foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) outbreak. On that front, Aucamp said that 70% of the national herd of more than 13 million animals has been vaccinated to date and that the goal of 80% by the end of this year was in reach.

> “If you’ve got a cow that’s not giving you a calf any more, or a cow that’s not giving the proper amount of milk any more, get rid of that animal. Rather have less stock but stock of good quality. We can always build up that stock again.”

Amid all the focus on El Niño and FMD, other agriculture issues such as the politically thorny one of land reform have faded on the public’s radar screen. But Aucamp, who assumed the agriculture portfolio 3½ months ago, said it was a priority of his.

“We are busy with a project where we are identifying 100 farms per province, black farmers who are currently renting their farms from government, to transfer the land into their names, and this is just the start,” he said.

“They must have title deeds. We must see that land gets out of the hands of the government. You’re not going to invest in a farm if it’s not yours. You can use it as collateral to obtain finance,” he said. **DM**

title: Uganda's Sugarcane Boom Leaves Families Hungry - What Needs to Change
summary: Busoga, in eastern Uganda, is a low, fertile plateau [surrounded](https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture "https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture") on three sides by [Lake Victoria](https://www.britannica.com/place/Lake-Victoria "https
content:
Busoga, in eastern Uganda, is a low, fertile plateau [surrounded](https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture "https://jinja.go.ug/lg/population-culture") on three sides by [Lake Victoria](https://www.britannica.com/place/Lake-Victoria "https://www.britannica.com/place/Lake-Victoria"), the [River Nile](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/nile-river/ "https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/nile-river/") and [Lake Kyoga](https://wldb.ilec.or.jp/Lake/AFR-15 "https://wldb.ilec.or.jp/Lake/AFR-15"). Most of its [4.3 million people](https://www.ubos.org/ "https://www.ubos.org/") farm small, rain-fed plots. Yet hunger is common: in the 2024 census, about a third of Busoga households reported going [whole days](https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/3-in-10-ugandans-going-without-food-daily-4795334 "https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/3-in-10-ugandans-going-without-food-daily-4795334") without food.

Sugarcane has been grown commercially here [since the 1920s](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210"), when one family established a large sugar processing facility. New investors followed after the government stopped setting sugar prices and [opened the industry](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/249121468110056798/pdf/multi-page.pdf "https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/249121468110056798/pdf/multi-page.pdf") to the private sector in 1991.

**Read more: [South Africa's small sugar farms are producing less than they could: study finds ways to boost them](https://theconversation.com/south-africas-small-sugar-farms-are-producing-less-than-they-could-study-finds-ways-to-boost-them-285098 "https://theconversation.com/south-africas-small-sugar-farms-are-producing-less-than-they-could-study-finds-ways-to-boost-them-285098")**

[Seven mills now operate](https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/growth-of-sugar-mills-in-busoga-threatens-wetlands-4724652 "https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/growth-of-sugar-mills-in-busoga-threatens-wetlands-4724652") in and around the Busoga region, with the amount of sugar cane planted tripling in size between [2000 and 2024](https://www.newsecuritybeat.org/2026/08/unenforced-rules-in-ugandas-sugar-sector-food-insecurity-and-climate-change/ "https://www.newsecuritybeat.org/2026/08/unenforced-rules-in-ugandas-sugar-sector-food-insecurity-and-climate-change/"). Tens of thousands of families also grow cane on their own land as "outgrowers", [selling this](https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/2020/13 "https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/2020/13") on contracts to the sugar mills.

Keep up with the latest headlines on [WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K "https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaIdDi8Bqbr263erhw1K") | [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/ "https://www.linkedin.com/company/allafrica/")

I spent over 20 years working in Uganda's civil service before becoming an academic. For my [doctoral research](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210"), I set out to understand why decades of sugarcane growth had not reduced hunger in Busoga. I visited two parts of Busoga - the Jinja and Buyende districts - and interviewed 27 officials, local leaders and farmer representatives. I also asked four groups of farmers for their views.

I asked who decides how land is used, who signs contracts, who receives the money, and how households eat while waiting for the harvest.

[My research found](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210") that the hunger in Busoga isn't caused by farmers not growing enough sugarcane to sell. [The prices](https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-busoga-sugarcane-farmers-fume-as-prices-drop-for-seventh-year/ "https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-busoga-sugarcane-farmers-fume-as-prices-drop-for-seventh-year/") of sugarcane [are dropping](https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-sets-minimum-sugarcane-price-to-protect-farmers-in-busoga/ "https://www.chinimandi.com/uganda-sets-minimum-sugarcane-price-to-protect-farmers-in-busoga/"), but my research found that the main problem is that sugar mills mainly sign contracts with men.

This means that decisions about what to use land and cash for are solely in the hands of the men. They don't always use the cash to feed their families. The work of feeding families falls mainly on women, who are left only with the option of planting what little land is left with food crops.

**Read more: [Child labour, poverty and terrible working conditions lie behind the sugar you eat](https://theconversation.com/child-labour-poverty-and-terrible-working-conditions-lie-behind-the-sugar-you-eat-95242 "https://theconversation.com/child-labour-poverty-and-terrible-working-conditions-lie-behind-the-sugar-you-eat-95242")**

To solve the problem, the government and sugar companies all need to end the practice of only contracting with men, set up contracts with women farmers too and make sure that women from sugarcane farming families inherit contracts automatically when their husbands die.

**One fifth of the land, all the responsibility**

[Only about 20%](https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210 "https://scholarworks.umb.edu/doctoral_dissertations/1210") of the available farmland in the Jinja and Buyende districts of Busoga is available to grow food crops. Up to 80% of farmland owned by families is used to grow sugarcane to sell.

Mills recruit sugarcane farmers through male household heads, whose names appear on the contracts. In one focus group, women described husbands signing multi-year contracts covering the family's entire land without consulting them. When they questioned this, the women were told the decision was not theirs.

**Read more: [Why Ethiopia's showcase sugar projects face huge challenges](https://theconversation.com/why-ethiopias-showcase-sugar-projects-face-huge-challenges-122871 "https://theconversation.com/why-ethiopias-showcase-sugar-projects-face-huge-challenges-122871")**

The payment, a lump sum at harvest, is made to whoever signed the contract. A political leader in Buyende, speaking anonymously, told me that many men now keep the cane money and don't use it to buy food for the home.

[Uganda's Land Act](https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1998/16/eng@2023-12-31 "https://ulii.org/akn/ug/act/1998/16/eng@2023-12-31") says family land cannot be sold, leased, or mortgaged without a spouse's written consent. But cane deals rarely go through a land office, so no one checks if consent is being given.

**A widow inherits the cane, but not the contract**

[Uganda's constitution recognises](https://ulii.org/en/akn/ug/act/statute/1995/constitution/eng@2023-12-31 "https://ulii.org/en/akn/ug/act/statute/1995/constitution/eng@2023-12-31") the right of women to inherit land. Yet my research found that when an outgrower dies, the contract usually remains in his name, and his widow has no standing with the mill.

The mill's recruitment agent, who signs up farmers, might decide not to allow her to take over her husband's contract. A clan meeting may instead hand the land to a male relative. A bank may refuse her credit without a man's signature. Although this is not legal, my research found that it is common practice and the government hasn't put in place any way of stopping it.

**Read more: [33 million women grow food on plots in sub-Saharan Africa. Greener farming can boost their earnings - study](https://theconversation.com/33-million-women-grow-food-on-plots-in-sub-saharan-africa-greener-farming-can-boost-their-earnings-study-261880 "https://theconversation.com/33-million-women-grow-food-on-plots-in-sub-saharan-africa-greener-farming-can-boost-their-earnings-study-261880")**

Government extension officers, who advise farmers, visit only registered contract holders, and don't advise the wives of contract holders. [Researchers call this](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1549-0831.2003.tb00133.x "https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1549-0831.2003.tb00133.x") the gap between holding a right and being able to use it.

In some cases, young men inherit the family's land but then sell it to pay for a motorcycle, school fees, or a family obligation. With the land gone, many end up cutting and loading cane for daily wages. A technical officer in Buyende told me that most of those workers are children. Uganda's [employment law](https://mglsd.go.ug/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Employment-Act.pdf "https://mglsd.go.ug/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Employment-Act.pdf") bars this, but enforcement is weak: one study found that there were only [83 labour officers](https://globalmarch.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Policy-Brief_s.pdf "https://globalmarch.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Policy-Brief_s.pdf") in Uganda, but that 1,344 were needed to make sure that labour laws were not being broken.

**What needs to happen next**

All the different organisations in the sugar industry have a role to play in protecting the rights of women in sugarcane growing families.

#### Sign up for free AllAfrica Newsletters

Get the latest in African news delivered straight to your inbox

First, the sugar mills should stop signing contracts with males only. Kidera Sugar, a new mill in Buyende that [opened in 2026](https://worldbusinessjournal.com/4385-2/ "https://worldbusinessjournal.com/4385-2/"), is now recruiting outgrowers, and has not set its contracting rules yet, so there's an opportunity for at least this sugar mill to introduce practices where women benefit equally.

**Read more: [How harvesting natural products can help rural people beat poverty](https://theconversation.com/how-harvesting-natural-products-can-help-rural-people-beat-poverty-108271 "https://theconversation.com/how-harvesting-natural-products-can-help-rural-people-beat-poverty-108271")**

Second, [the Sugar Industry Stakeholders Council](https://allafrica.com/stories/202512190520.html), the sugar industry regulator, gives mills their licences. It could change the situation by refusing to approve contracts without both spouses' signatures in the case of married couples. It could also start a new practice of requiring that all contracts pass on to widows. It could even make a rule that widows should retain a share of each farm's food crops.

Third, district land offices could register cane agreements so the Land Act's consent rule applies. Fourth, the labour ministry should fund the jobs of more inspectors in cane-growing areas.

As contract farming spreads, who signs the contract can determine who controls the income and whether the family has enough to eat.

_[James Kintu](https://theconversation.com/profiles/james-kintu-2730455 "https://theconversation.com/profiles/james-kintu-2730455"), Postdoctoral Research Fellow, Centre for Governance and Sustainability, UMass Boston_

# China Spied on Taiwanese President’s Son – in the US

The incident shone a spotlight on China’s growing repertoire for transnational repression targeting Taiwanese leaders.

By [Brian Hioe](https://thediplomat.com/authors/brian-hioe/)

October 15, 2026

[](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F&title=China+Spied+on+Taiwanese+President%E2%80%99s+Son+%E2%80%93+in+the+US "Share on LinkedIn")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F "Share on Facebook")[](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=China+Spied+on+Taiwanese+President%E2%80%99s+Son+%E2%80%93+in+the+US%0Ahttps%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F "Share on Bluesky")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=China+Spied+on+Taiwanese+President%E2%80%99s+Son+%E2%80%93+in+the+US&url=https%3A%2F%2Fthediplomat.com%2F2026%2F10%2Fchina-spied-on-taiwanese-presidents-son-in-the-us%2F "Share on X")

Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te

Credit: [Official Photo by Liu Shu fu / Office of the President, ROC (Taiwan)-8a90004bfc-k](https://www.flickr.com/photos/presidentialoffice/54502930988/in/dateposted/)

Ad

News broke earlier this month that the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had arrested real estate agent Wanying “Heather” Zhang for spying on Lai Ting-yu, the eldest child of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te. Zhang lived in Irvine, California, where she worked as a real estate agent. She was originally from Changsha, China, before emigrating to the United States and naturalizing.

Lai Ting-yu is not a political figure – members of the Lai family tend to keep a low profile. Lai Ching-te’s wife, First Lady Wu Mei-ju, does not often make public appearances with her husband. Arguably, the most famous members of the Lai family outside of Lai Ching-te himself are the family dogs, Murphy, Banban, and Luke, though Luke has since [passed away](https://tw.news.yahoo.com/%E7%8B%97%E6%B4%BE-%E7%B8%BD%E7%B5%B1%E8%B3%B4%E6%B8%85%E5%BE%B7%E7%B1%B2%E9%A0%98%E9%A4%8A%E4%B8%8D%E6%A3%84%E9%A4%8A-%E6%9B%AC%E5%85%A8%E5%AE%B6%E7%A6%8F%E7%85%A7%E4%BB%8B%E7%B4%B9%E6%84%9B%E7%8A%ACmurphy-%E7%9B%BC%E7%8B%97%E7%8B%97%E9%83%BD%E8%83%BD%E5%9C%A8%E6%84%9B%E8%88%87%E7%90%86%E8%A7%A3%E4%B8%AD%E6%89%BE%E5%88%B0%E6%AD%B8%E5%B1%AC-075324709.html). Banban in particular [is best known](https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/life/breakingnews/5422777) as a dog that had lost a leg to a wild boar trap before being adopted by the Lai family.

Lai Ting-yu, who [holds a doctorate](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/suspected-chinese-agent-taiwan-president-son-los-angeles-federal-court/) in bioengineering from the University of Washington, works for electronics company Philips and lives in Seattle with his wife and son.

The FBI alleged that Lai was being surveilled by Zhang, along with other accomplices, in September 2025. It is unclear what Zhang was attempting to accomplish, given Lai Ting-yu’s lack of a political background.

There could be a domestic political angle. Lai Ching-te has long been criticized by members of the pan-Blue camp over allegations that his son lives in the United States. The suggestion is that Lai is hypocritical in calling for Taiwan to increase defense spending to ward off Chinese threats, even as his own children live abroad.

Alternatively, China may have sought to project its reach, or possibly to threaten Lai Ting-yu in order to have leverage over Taiwan’s president. Indeed, the idea that China might seek to kidnap the children of influential government officials in the course of an invasion, so as to blackmail political leaders during the turmoil of armed conflict, has occasionally been raised. This sort of political kidnapping is a plot thread that comes up in several episodes of “[Zero Day Attack,](https://nomanisanis.land/zero-day-attack-overall-review/)” the hit 2025 television show dramatizing a Chinese invasion.

Whatever the motive, according to the FBI, Zhang was working in coordination with Chinese handlers and demonstrated [signs of tradecraft](https://udn.com/news/story/6656/9796629) to cover her tracks, such as renting vehicles for several hours then returning them, or booking short-range flights with little notice. It is unclear how evidence of her activities was detected, but Zhang was arrested in October 2026 while attempting to board a flight to Shanghai.

The FBI did not comment on when Zhang was recruited, or her motivations, seeing as she lived in [a $6 million home](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wanying-heather-zhang-china-surveillance-arrest-los-angeles/) and handled real estate transactions that were in the millions. Though there have been reports of China increasingly recruiting “disposable” agents that are used temporarily and then cast aside, tradecraft by Zhang may indicate professional training.

The Taiwanese government has criticized such actions as Chinese transnational repression. This is not the first case occurring in the United States. [Individuals](https://www.justice.gov/usao-cdca/pr/political-operative-sentenced-4-years-federal-prison-acting-covert-agent-peoples) allegedly working for China’s government were arrested for surveilling Taiwan’s then-President Tsai Ing-wen’s travels in California in 2023. Reports indicate that Taiwanese government officials such as Joseph Wu were [surveilled](https://newbloommag.net/2021/10/31/wu-european-visit/) during past trips to Europe.

Most famously, news broke in June 2025 of [an attempt](https://thediplomat.com/2025/07/china-car-crash-plan-targeting-hsiao-bi-khim-shocks-taiwan/) by the Chinese military attaché in Prague to ram a vehicle into the motorcad

# Typhoon Champi unlikely to hit Hong Kong, Observatory says

China's weather agency says a tropical depression east of Guam is set to become Typhoon Champi within 24 hours, possibly reaching super typhoon strength. The Hong Kong Observatory says a direct hit on the city is unlikely, with tropical cyclones not expected to affect Hong Kong for the rest of Octob

[![Image 4: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

 By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

 15 Oct 2026 at 17:54 HKT · 1 min read

Share:

[](https://wa.me/?text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says%20https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea "WhatsApp")[](https://t.me/share/url?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea&text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says "Telegram")[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A//clb.org.hk/en/hong-kong/Typhoon-Champi-unlikely-to-hit-Hong-Kong-Observatory-says-0b47ea&text=Typhoon%20Champi%20unlikely%20to%20hit%20Hong%20Kong%2C%20Observatory%20says "X")[](https://clb.org.hk/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection# "Email")

China's National Meteorological Center said a tropical depression east of Guam is forecast to become this year's 30th typhoon, Champi, within 24 hours, and it could develop into a super typhoon as it moves west-northwest.

The Hong Kong Observatory said the city is less likely to be hit directly, and tropical cyclones are unlikely to affect Hong Kong for the rest of October. The storm may move toward waters east of Luzon early to mid next week. Its later track remains uncertain, but there is a higher chance it will turn north and pass through waters east of Taiwan.

AI weather models all show Champi making a 90-degree northward turn near eastern Taiwan. Model Pangu forecasts the storm will cross Japan on October 26, while Fuxi and Fengwu show it passing near Tokyo between October 25 and 26.

Separately, Typhoon Koguma in the western North Pacific weakened into an extratropical cyclone on October 14.

Locally, the Observatory said a fresh easterly airstream will bring stronger winds and one or two showers to the Guangdong coast over the next two or three days. As an upper-air anticyclone strengthens, the South China coast should be generally sunny and dry early to mid next week, with hot daytime weather. A northeast monsoon is expected to affect southern China late next week.

The Observatory predicted mostly sunny weather over the next nine days. Saturday will be mostly cloudy with one or two showers, and Sunday will start mostly cloudy with one or two light showers.
