summary: 首尔无法承担裂痕 驻美国大使将情报共享异常视为主要挑战 统一部长官郑东泳周一在首尔政府大楼对记者表示，在华盛顿限制与首尔共享情报的争议中，韩美同盟没有问题。郑先生拒绝了华盛顿方面的评估，即他有关朝鲜平安北道久城核设施的言论泄露了美国机密情报，称这是“误解”，并坚称“美国错了”。在国家A级
content:
首尔无法承受的裂痕
驻美大使认为情报共享异常是主要挑战

统一部长官郑东泳周一在首尔政府大楼对记者表示，在华盛顿限制与首尔共享情报的争议中，韩美联盟没有问题。郑先生拒绝了华盛顿方面的评估，即他有关朝鲜平安北道久城核设施的言论泄露了美国机密情报，称这是“误解”，并坚称“美国错了”。

同一天在华盛顿举行的国会审计中，韩国驻美国大使康京和表示，两国之间的高层磋商次数如此之少，以至于局势令人沮丧。 “我承认与白宫的沟通是有限的，”她补充道。当被问及双边关系中最困难的悬而未决的问题时，康还指出“情报合作”是一个重大挑战。

在周二的内阁会议上，韩国总统李在明表示，韩美同盟非常重要，但他补充说，在国家关系中应避免顺从和屈从的态度。他还强调，韩国是一个主权独立的国家，处理好与周边大国的关系很重要。
美国的任何盟友都无法幸免于与唐纳德·特朗普政府在安全和贸易方面的摩擦。然而，大多数盟国领导人都考虑到华盛顿的影响力，寻求通过幕后谈判解决争端。李明博关于维护国家尊严的言论，原则上是完全合理的。但刻意宣称韩国不会屈服在外交上是不明智的。现在的问题是华盛顿将如何解读他的话。

朝鲜战争期间，美国向半岛部署了近180万军队，其中3.6万多人阵亡。目前，仍有超过2.8万美军驻扎在韩国，帮助维护朝鲜半岛的稳定与和平。韩国还严重依赖美国的延伸威慑，包括核保护伞，来应对朝鲜核武库构成的威胁。在此背景下，将美国与中国、俄罗斯等邻国置于同等地位根本站不住脚。

李明博的言论似乎强化了郑先生的主张，即韩美同盟没有任何问题。但总统和统一部长是否充分认识到联盟的重要性？

郑在三月份揭露了龟城核设施的存在后，华盛顿对该地点的机密情报被泄露感到愤怒，开始限制其卫星收集的一些有关朝鲜的情报。
美国军方通过数百颗侦察卫星和其他监视设备监视朝鲜的核活动。它收集的图像和信号情报对于韩国应对拥有核武器的朝鲜威胁的能力至关重要，特别是考虑到首尔自己没有核武器。因此，任何对此类情报共享的限制都是令人严重关切的问题。

最重要的是，情报和军事合作取决于相互信任。对情报共享的限制发出了一个令人不安的信号，即人们之间的信心

【原文 English Original】
A rift Seoul cannot afford
Ambassador to US identifies abnormality in intelligence sharing as major challenge

Unification Minister Chung Dong-young told reporters at Government Complex Seoul on Monday that there is no problem with the South Korea-US alliance amid controversy over Washington's restrictions on sharing intelligence with Seoul. Chung rejected Washington's assessment that his remarks about nuclear facilities in North Korea's Kusong, North Pyongan Province, had disclosed classified US intelligence, calling it a "misunderstanding" and insisting that "the US is wrong."

At a National Assembly audit in Washington on the same day, South Korean Ambassador to the United States Kang Kyung-wha said high-level consultations between the two countries were taking place so infrequently that the situation was frustrating. "I acknowledge that there are limits to communication with the White House," she added. Asked about the most difficult outstanding issues in bilateral relations, Kang also identified "intelligence cooperation" as a major challenge.

At a Cabinet meeting on Tuesday, President Lee Jae Myung said the South Korea-US alliance is very important, but added that submissive and subservient attitudes should be avoided in relations between countries. He also stressed that South Korea is a sovereign, independent nation and that managing relations with the major powers surrounding it was important.

No US ally is immune to friction with the Donald Trump administration over security and trade. Yet most allied leaders seek to resolve disputes through behind-the-scenes negotiations, mindful of Washington's influence. Lee's remarks about the need to maintain national dignity are perfectly reasonable in principle. But going out of one's way to declare that South Korea will not submit is diplomatically unwise. The question now is how Washington will interpret his words.

During the Korean War, the United States deployed nearly 1.8 million troops to the peninsula, more than 36,000 of whom were killed in action. Today, more than 28,000 US troops remain stationed in South Korea, helping maintain stability and peace on the Korean Peninsula. South Korea also relies heavily on US extended deterrence, including the nuclear umbrella, to counter the threat posed by North Korea's nuclear arsenal. Against this backdrop, putting the United States on the same footing as neighboring powers such as China and Russia is simply untenable.

Lee's remarks appear to reinforce Chung's assertion that there is nothing wrong with the South Korea-US alliance. But do the president and the unification minister fully appreciate the alliance's importance?

After Chung exposed the existence of nuclear facilities in Kusong in March, Washington, angered by what it regarded as a leak of classified intelligence about the site, began restricting some intelligence on North Korea gathered by its satellites.

The US military monitors North Korea's nuclear activities through hundreds of reconnaissance satellites and other surveillance assets. The imagery and signals intelligence it collects are vital to South Korea's ability to counter the threat from a nuclear-armed North Korea, especially given that Seoul has no nuclear weapons of its own. Any curtailment of such intelligence sharing is therefore a matter of grave concern.

Above all, intelligence and military cooperation depend on mutual trust. Restrictions on intelligence sharing send a troubling signal that confidence between the two sides has been eroded.

The two countries also face a host of major unresolved issues, including tariffs, South Korean investment in the United States and nuclear energy cooperation. If Seoul cannot maintain effective communication with key decision-makers in the White House, its national interests risk being pushed aside.

The US alliance remains a lifeline for South Korea. The stark reality is that Seoul still has much to seek from Washington on a range of issues. It cannot afford to let rifts in the alliance deepen and then pay the price in both security and economic terms.

The government must act swiftly to restore trust and resolve the intelligence-sharing dispute through concrete confidence-building measures. This should include reviewing personnel arrangements where necessary to address US concerns. Reassuring Washington that Seoul takes the alliance seriously is not a matter of submission; it is a matter of protecting South Korea's national interests.
(END)

title: “Last Year We Needed Volunteers, This Year We Need Tourists”: Reviving Post-Disaster Tourism in Eastern Taiwan
zh_title: “去年需要志愿者，今年需要游客”：复兴台湾东部灾后旅游业
summary: 下载整期 PDF 城镇重建很久之后，它的形象可能仍停留在过去。潜在的游客可能会通过过时的图像和以前的灾难头条新闻来查看这个地方。如果没有足够的保证或激励，他们会比必要的时间更长时间地避开，忘记这个地方曾经是，而且仍然可以是一个度假胜地。这种现象给依赖旅游业为生的居民和企业带来了一场延迟的、不太明显的灾难。花莲县横跨台湾东北海岸和山谷。该地区经济依赖旅游业
content:
下载整期 PDF 城镇重建很久之后，它的形象可能仍停留在过去。潜在的游客可能会通过过时的图像和以前的灾难头条新闻来查看这个地方。如果没有足够的保证或激励，他们会比必要的时间更长时间地避开，忘记这个地方曾经是，而且仍然可以是一个度假胜地。这种现象给依赖旅游业为生的居民和企业带来了一场延迟的、不太明显的灾难。花莲县横跨台湾东北海岸和山谷。该地区的经济依赖旅游业，但由于历史上的自然灾害而遭受重挫。对于花莲来说，该行业约占全县就业和产值的40%。该县的光福镇经历了 2024 年地区性地震对旅游业的影响和 2025 年洪水造成的自然破坏，目前正在努力应对游客量长期低迷的问题。本文通过对当地人的采访和第一手研究，探讨了居民在灾后努力重建城镇吸引力的经历，并探讨了政府迄今为止为支持旅游业恢复所做的努力。它还详细说明了政府应采取哪些进一步措施来真正重振经济。本案例研究揭示了灾后重建的长期现实以及重振当地经济所需的政府干预规模。
这也对台湾在国际舞台上的韧性提出了更广泛的问题：当自然灾害和更广泛的危险认知威胁到旅游业时，目的地如何保持游客的信心？由头条新闻定义的小镇光复镇坐落在台湾花莲县花东裂谷，长期以来以其田园风光、自行车路线和原住民文化而闻名。花莲北部该地区的主要旅游景点太鲁阁峡谷吸引的国际游客会顺着峡谷而下，在光复寺停留欣赏风景并在附近的温泉休息。但近两年来，该地区的旅游业经受了严峻考验。 2024年4月，花莲地震给我们带来了第一波打击。太鲁阁峡谷在地震中受损严重，连接台北和花莲的高速公路暂时被封锁。花莲市一栋倒塌建筑物的图片出现在全球主要新闻媒体的头版上。来台国际游客数量锐减，国内游客将假期从花莲转移到其他地方。峡谷以南的所有乡镇都受到旅游业下降的影响。尽管如此，光复并不是受灾最严重的地区之一，它位于花莲市以南一小时车程的地方。居民经历了强烈的震动，建筑物遭受了结构性影响，但受损程度并不像北部城市地区那么严重。
花莲县的大部分地区都是低层房屋，周围环绕着连绵起伏的农田和山脉。该地区很幸运，基本上避免了新闻报道中花莲市的破坏场景。然而，广泛传播的这座城市的图像让人感觉整个县都遭到了破坏，因此参观不安全。在高速公路再次向游客开放后，这个观点仍然存在很长一段时间。图片：X 上危险倾斜的天王星大厦附近的救援人员和设备

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Long after a town rebuilds itself, its image can remain stuck in the past. Potential visitors may view the place through outdated images and previous disaster headlines. Without enough reassurance or incentives, they steer clear for longer than necessary, forgetting that the place was, and still can be, a holiday destination. This phenomenon results in a delayed, less visible disaster for residents and businesses whose livelihoods depend on tourism. Hualien County stretches over the northeastern coast and valleys of Taiwan. The area’s economy relies on the tourism industry, which has been set back due to a history of natural disasters. For Hualien, that sector accounts for around 40 percent of the county’s employment and output value. A township within this county, Guangfu, is grappling with a particularly prolonged downturn in visitors, having weathered both the tourism fallout of a regional earthquake in 2024 and the physical devastation of floods in 2025. Through interviews with locals and first-hand research, this piece explores the experiences of residents struggling to rebuild a town’s appeal post-disaster, and examines the government’s efforts to support tourism recovery to date. It also details what further steps the government should take to genuinely revive the economy. This case study reveals the long-term realities of post-disaster reconstruction and the scale of government intervention needed to re-energize a local economy. It also raises wider questions for Taiwan’s resilience on the international stage: how can a destination maintain visitor confidence when natural disasters—and broader perceptions of danger—threaten tourism? A Township Defined by Headlines Guangfu Township, nestled in the East Rift Valley of Hualien County, Taiwan, was long known for its rural scenery, cycling routes, and indigenous culture. International tourists drawn in by Taroko Gorge, the region’s main tourist attraction in north Hualien, would make their way down the valley, stopping by Guangfu to enjoy the view and rest in the nearby hot springs. But in the last two years, the area’s tourism industry has been severely tested. In April 2024, the Hualien earthquake dealt the first blow. Taroko Gorge was considerably damaged by the earthquake, and the highway connecting Taipei and Hualien was temporarily blocked. Images of a collapsed building in Hualien City were displayed on front pages of major global news outlets . The number of international visitors to Taiwan plummeted and domestic visitors redirected their holidays away from Hualien. No township south of the gorge was spared the impact of the drop in tourism. This said, Guangfu was not amongst the most severely damaged areas, being situated one hour south of Hualien City by car. Residents experienced strong tremors and buildings sustained structural impacts, although the extent of the damage was not as severe as in the urban areas to the north. Much of this part of Hualien County is made up of low-rise houses surrounded by rolling farmland and mountains. The region was fortunate to largely avoid the scenes of destruction in Hualien City that dominated the news. Nevertheless, the widely broadcasted images of the city contributed to a perception that the whole county was devastated and therefore unsafe to visit. This viewpoint remained long after the highway was opened to visitors again. Image: Rescue workers and equipment near the dangerously-leaning Uranus Building on Xuanyuan Road in Hualien City, in the immediate aftermath of the April 3, 2024 Hualien earthquake. (Image source: ROC Presidential Office / Wikimedia Commons ) In 2024, the National Tourism Administration (交通部觀光署) offered subsidies for six months following the earthquake , in order to stimulate tourism recovery in Hualien. This included the “Hualien Independent Travel Accommodation Subsidy” (花蓮自由行住宿補助) , featuring an NTD 1000 (around USD 30) rebate on the first night, with an additional NTD 1500 (around USD 47) provided on the second. This was combined with discounts on charter flights , shuttles , amusement parks and local products. With Taroko Gorge still shut, the county government diversified regional branding, releasing the video, “ On the Way to Eastern Taiwan: Travel Freely with Peace of Mind , ” and hosting international marketing shows alongside local spotlight events such as the 2024 World Bicycle Day. These initiatives reportedly helped tourism activities in Hualien reach pre-earthquake rates from 2025 , though it is unclear what proportion of these numbers trickled down to townships in the south, such as Guangfu. However, in September 2025, just as tourists were returning to the region, Guangfu Township faced a second blow which left a more devastating impact to the community. The overflowing of a nearby barrier lake caused flash floods, which sent mud and debris into homes and businesses. The floods also left many stranded after a lack of comprehensive evacuation notices caught locals off guard. Fellow citizens arrived in extraordinary numbers to aid in cleanup efforts, with an estimated 30,000 volunteers appearing on September 27, and tens of thousands more in the following weeks. Li Jen-i (李仁義), the owner of breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿) in Guangfu, recalls their arrival after his shop’s cooking equipment had been washed away: “It brings tears to my eyes to remember. The warmth of Taiwanese people, you never forget that.” [1] The government emergency response was swift. The Legislative Yuan (立法院) passed a NTD 27 billion (USD 859 million) special budget to rebuild parts of the township damaged by the floods, and offered temporary housing, reconstruction loans, and cleanup subsidies to victims. The county government dispatched 790 mud removal trucks and cooperated with the bike rental company YouBike to temporarily install bike stations . When I visited a year later, the relief efforts of both government and private charities had significantly reduced the physical damage of the floods. Many businesses have reopened and locals await the return of visitors. But now, a less visible crisis is unfolding in Guangfu. Many tourists still skip the township, deterred by the lingering perception that conditions there are wet and muddy at best, or dangerous at worst. Ongoing disaster-related reporting continues to dominate the media, re-enforcing the perception of Guangfu as a township still in devastation. Locals are therefore struggling to keep their businesses afloat. Rebuilding public confidence in the township as a tourist destination is a challenge residents cannot shoulder alone. It will require a different kind of targeted, strategic support from the government. Image: An ant art installation in Danongdafu Flatland Forest Park (Image source: Author’s photograph) Tourist Restoration Policies Beyond Physical Recovery Two challenges remain when it comes to sustainably revitalizing Guangfu’s economy. First, government funding in Guangfu has so far prioritized the concrete efforts of physical restoration over the more abstract needs of tourism recovery. The initial response to the floods by both the central and county governments was remarkable in both speed and scale, with much of Guangfu’s physical infrastructure restored in under a year. Now, government support should extend beyond emergency relief and employ a strategic approach to sustaining the long-term survival of local industries. “People might have their homes again, but what can they do with no livelihood? We need further government support to promote the township and help our businesses get back on their feet,” says “Uncle Tien” ( 田克靚 ), owner of Uncle Tien’s Guesthouse ( 見青小築民宿) , whose monthly revenue has been down by 50-80 percent since the autumn of 2025. [2] Second, Guangfu has received limited visibility within Hualien’s wider tourism promotion efforts. The county government has continued since 2024 to launch tourism marketing campaigns to attract international and domestic visitors to the region. However, initiatives tend to be concentrated on north Hualien County and Hualien City. A staff member managing tourism affairs at the Guangfu Township Office (光復鄉公所) confirmed to me that while the office is keen to promote Guangfu’s tourism assets, there are currently no county-level initiatives aimed at helping Guangfu boost the industry. Local officials are committed to revitalizing tourism but seemingly lack the resources and funding required to conduct sustained, large-scale promotional efforts. [3] It is understandable that Hualien’s tourism efforts were focused elsewhere while Guangfu was still undergoing extensive physical restoration. With the township now largely cleared, though, there is a stronger case for requesting additional funding from the county or central governments for campaigns that put Guangfu at the center of tourism promotion. A Focused Strategy for Restoring Tourist Confidence With the help of county and central government, a tailored tourism-recovery framework could be coordinated for the township. This could include: More accurate, balanced information on conditions and daily life on the ground. Coordinated travel campaigns and incentives. Investment in tourism infrastructure. First, more widely publicized information on the township’s recovery and travel conditions will help accelerate the shift in perceptions. Clear, sustained, and positive communication about regional safety and accessibility, as well as regular local government broadcasting of daily life and cultural events will rebuild the public’s trust. This includes both earthquake-related safety assurances and post-flood recovery stories. “Many people worry that it is unsafe here. But the government has done a great deal to ensure our buildings are secure. Clearer public information on this would help reassure visitors,” says breakfast shop owner Li Jen-i. [4] “Guangfu has recovered quickly from the floods, and life has largely returned to normal for many residents. We hope that coverage of the township can better reflect that reality,” say Laoye (盧政惠) and Juju (陳慧秋), guesthouse owners of Breadfruit B&B (麵包樹舍). They add: “People forget how accessible and peaceful this part of Taiwan is as a holiday destination.” [5] Indeed, despite media coverage focusing primarily on areas under construction, a notable portion of the township was not touched by the floods. The main tourist attractions remain open here, such as the Matai’an Xinlü Farm (馬太鞍欣綠農園 ), where visitors can learn about the indigenous ecological knowledge of the Amis indigenous people (阿美族) ; and the Guangfu Sugar Factory (光復糖廠 ), which dates back to the Japanese period . Without this information to counter negative news coverage, many continue to assume Guangfu is a no-go zone. Second, to effectively promote the township nation-wide and beyond, Guangfu needs the resources of a coordinated government-backed tourism promotion program. Eye-catching marketing campaigns showcasing the area’s rural charm and scenery could be rolled out on social media and displayed in trains, underground (MRT) stations in cities nationwide, and international airports in both Taiwn and abroad. To provide additional financial incentives for people to visit, subsidized travel packages and discounted transport tickets, akin to Hualien County’s post-earthquake discounts, could be reintroduced and adapted for Guangfu. Image: “Laoye” (盧政惠) and “Juju” (陳慧秋), the proprietors of “Breadfruit B&B” (麵包樹舍) in the town of Guangfu (Hualien County) (July 2026). (Image source: Author’s photograph) If the county’s existing tourism campaigns elsewhere in Hualien County are indeed proving effective, the wheel does not need to be reinvented. Government officials can build on existing initiatives and direct them where the region requires further support. Policy lessons can also be taken from abroad. Following the 2019-2020 bushfires in Australia, tourism hotspots across New South Wales struggled with avalanches of cancellations for months . Similarly, f ollowing the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes , towns in Japan experienced protracted slumps in tourism. In both cases, government-funded campaigns and incentives helped boost the recovery of the tourism industry, which encouraged people to travel in an ordinary fashion, rather than to see residents solely as victims needing support . Third, travel promotion and incentives in Guangfu could be matched with continued investment in tourism infrastructure. While the township is easy to reach by direct train and car hire is convenient, the government can pursue further investment in a number of transit methods to enhance the township’s accessibility. These include expanding bike hire options, improving bus services, and introducing shuttle buses between local attractions. Taiwan already boasts 84 shuttle bus routes country-wide. Until Guangfu enjoys better transport services, reliance on car travel will create barriers for those who cannot drive or who do not hold driving licenses. Taiwan has a strong track record of strategic tourism promotion and infrastructure development. A clear tourism roadmap would build on the government’s existing strengths, putting its tools to work for a township in need of greater support. Lessons in Post-Disaster Recovery for Taiwan and the World Cases of natural disasters in Guangfu have shown that while physical restoration can take place remarkably quickly, the harder task is ensuring that local industries recover long-term. This experience can offer lessons that extend well beyond Taiwan. As climate change intensifies the frequency and severity of extreme weather worldwide, governments will increasingly be required to consider the protracted effects of these occurrences on local communities. Building strong strategies to ensure long-term recovery is crucial. Taiwan, meanwhile, has particular reasons to strengthen its capacity for resilience. Its exposure to natural disasters, as well as ongoing concerns over geopolitical tensions in the Taiwan Strait, means that the government is constantly contending with international perceptions of a nation in danger. Taiwan needs to be able not only to rebuild industries after crises, but also to continuously reassure visitors that the country remains a safe and appealing destination. Guangfu offers a smaller-scale opportunity to test how strategic information sharing, combined with promotional tourism campaigns and incentives, can help reshape perceptions of a disaster-affected destination. The main point: Effectively reviving a local economy post-disaster and rebuilding its appeal to tourists requires a long-term, targeted approach from government. This includes strategic information sharing, promotional tourism campaigns and incentives, and infrastructure building. This case study of Guangfu, Hualien County—one year after devastating floods—sheds light on the necessary scale of government intervention and the pertinence of strengthening Taiwan’s tourism resilience both regionally and nationally. [1] Author’s interview with Li Jen-i (李仁義), the owner of breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿), July 25, 2026. [2] Author’s interview with Uncle Tien ( 田克靚 ), owner of Uncle Tien’s Guesthouse ( 見青小築民宿) , July 26, 2026. [3] Author’s informal interview with Guangfu Township local official, July 24, 2026. [4] Author’s with Li Jen-i (李仁義), the owner of breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿), July 25, 2026. [5] Author’s interview with Laoye (盧政惠) and Juju (陳慧秋), guesthouse owners of Breadfruit B&B (麵包樹舍), July 25, 2026. Acknowledgments: The author thanks Uncle Tien (田克靚), owner of Uncle Tien’s Guesthouse見青小築民宿; Laoye (盧政惠) and Juju (陳慧秋), owners of 麵包樹舍 Breadfruit B&B; and Li Jen-i (李仁義), owner of a breakfast shop Yonghe Doujiang (永和豆漿) for their time and insights during interviews for this article. The post “Last Year We Needed Volunteers, This Year We Need Tourists”: Reviving Post-Disaster Tourism in Eastern Taiwan appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

title: Fruit at the Forefront of a Trade and Diplomatic Push
zh_title: 处于贸易和外交推动前沿的水果
summary: 下载全文 PDF 今年，来自台湾的新鲜水果首次出现在英国和法国的超市货架上，这让英国和法国的购物者大饱眼福。第一批来自台南的优质欧文芒果和来自台中的黑叶荔枝混合装运，已于六月初在英国曼彻斯特清关。此后不久，台湾芒果也抵达法国，尽管每颗芒果的售价高达29美元，但仍深受法国消费者的欢迎。不到一个月的时间，超过四吨的水果被运走。
content:
下载全文 PDF 今年，来自台湾的新鲜水果首次出现在英国和法国的超市货架上，这让英国和法国的购物者大饱眼福。第一批来自台南的优质欧文芒果和来自台中的黑叶荔枝混合装运，已于六月初在英国曼彻斯特清关。此后不久，台湾芒果也抵达法国，尽管每颗芒果的售价高达29美元，但仍深受法国消费者的欢迎。不到一个月的时间，四吨多的水果就被卖光了。获得将台湾产品运送到欧洲高度保护的关税区的官方许可是一个复杂的过程。该地区与农产品相关的进口法规具有严格的限制性，因为它们涵盖了从标签和农药暴露到农产品如何销售的方方面面。因此，经过“多年的谈判和技术准备”，台北驻欧盟和比利时代表处于2025年宣布获得芒果和番石榴进口清关，这是一项伟大的成就。八个月后，荔枝和火龙果获得批准。欧洲并不是台湾水果出口唯一面临挑战的目的地。台湾农业部门的官员也寻求向新西兰出口菠萝。
这一努力始于2013年新西兰与台澎金马单独关税区经济合作协定（ANZTEC，纽西兰与台澎金马关税领域经济合作定）的签署。经过八年的ANZTEC修正案双边谈判，新西兰终于打开了优质台湾菠萝的大门。 2025年5月，即ANZTEC修订案获得批准两年后，第一批台湾菠萝抵达新西兰市场。减少对单一市场的依赖 2010 年，台湾加入世界贸易组织 (WTO) 前后，台湾的水果开始在许多传统市场失去竞争力，其中包括日本和菲律宾。随着台湾农业面临新的国际竞争，海峡两岸经济合作框架协议（ECFA，海峡两岸经济合作架构协议）为台湾水果创造了机会，导致对单一市场中国的出口大幅增长。 ECFA是送给台湾农民的一份礼物。颁布两年后，台湾农产品出口总额增长了百分之八以上。其中，对中国的水果出口增长了42%；香蕉、哈密瓜、柠檬、红火龙果等早期收获清单上的农产品比2007年猛增42%。然而，受ECFA保护的农产品贸易并没有持续太久。
2021 年 2 月和 9 月，中国突然停止从台湾进口——首先是菠萝，然后是糖苹果和莲雾——声称检查中在多批货物中发现了柑橘粉蚧。 ECFA 批评者表示，中国本来就不是一个可行的长期市场。中国开始种植和培育曾经是台湾标志性水果的水果，侵蚀了对台湾出口的需求。此外，北京开始利用进口水果作为象征性的大棒来迫使台湾就范。中华经济研究院颜慧欣曾警告台湾有必要减少对中国市场的依赖，她写道：“

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Shoppers in the United Kingdom and France got a treat when supplies of fresh fruit from Taiwan found their way onto their supermarket shelves for the first time this year . The first batch, a mixed shipment of premium Irwin mangoes from Tainan and black-leaf lychees from Taichung, cleared customs in the British city of Manchester in early June. Taiwan’s mangoes also arrived in France shortly thereafter , enjoying overwhelming popularity among French consumers despite the astonishing price tag of $29 USD per fruit. In less than a month, more than four tons of the fruit were sold out. Getting an official permit to send Taiwan produce into Europe’s highly protected customs area is a complicated process. The region’s produce-related import regulations are highly restrictive, as they cover everything ranging from labelling and pesticide exposure, to how the produce can be marketed . Therefore, it marked a great achievement when the Taipei Representative Office in the European Union (EU) and Belgium announced in 2025 that it had received clearance for mango and guava imports , after “years of negotiations and technical preparations.” Approvals for lychees and dragon fruit followed eight months later. Europe was not the only challenging destination for Taiwan’s fruit exports. Taiwan’s officials in agricultural sectors also sought to export pineapples to New Zealand. The endeavor began with the signing of the Agreement between New Zealand and the Separate Customs Territory of Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen, and Matsu on Economic Cooperation (ANZTEC, 紐西蘭與臺澎金馬個別關稅領域經濟合作協 定) in 2013. Eight years of bilateral negotiations on the amendments to ANZTEC finally opened New Zealand’s doors to premium Taiwan pineapples. In May of 2025—two years after the ANZTEC revisions were approved—the first batch of Taiwan’s pineapples arrived in the New Zealand market. Reducing Dependence on a Single Market In 2010, around the time of Taiwan’s accession into the World Trade Organization (WTO), the island’s fruit began losing competitiveness in many of its traditional markets, which included Japan and the Philippines . As Taiwan’s agricultural industry scrambled in the face of new international competition, the Cross Straits Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA, 海峽兩岸經濟合作架構協 議) created an opportunity for Taiwan’s fruit, resulting in a huge jump in exports into a single market : China. ECFA was a gift for Taiwanese farmers. Two years after it was promulgated, Taiwan’s total agricultural exports increased more than eight percent. Particularly, fruit exports to China grew 42 percent; and produce on the early harvest list, such as bananas, hami melons, lemons, and red dragon fruits, surged 42 percent compared to 2007. Nevertheless, the agricultural trade protected by ECFA did not last. In February and September 2021, China abruptly ended its imports from Taiwan—first pineapples, then sugar apples and wax apples—claiming that inspections had discovered citrus mealybugs in a number of shipments. ECFA critics say China was not a viable long-term market to begin with. China started growing and cultivating what used to be Taiwan’s signature fruits, eroding demand for Taiwan’s exports. Additionally, Beijing began to use fruit imports as a figurative stick to bring Taiwan to heel. Huai-Shing Yen (顏慧 欣 ) of the Chung Hua Institution for Economic Research (中華經濟研究 院 ) had warned of the need to reduce Taiwan’s reliance on the Chinese market, writing that: “The high concentration structure (of exports to China) makes it certain that the import restrictions will have a commercial impact on relevant farmers in Taiwan. As such, China’s actions to restrict imports are loud reminders of the vulnerability that this ‘export dependence’ causes for these agricultural products.” Yen also warned that even if Taiwan had sought to seek redress for China’s actions through the WTO, China “would not be obliged to enter consultations or negotiations with Taiwan.” Instead, Taiwan should seek alternatives, more reliable markets for its products. Weeks after China’s sugar apple and wax apple ban, the then-Council of Agriculture (COA, 行政院農業委員會 ) announced a strategy that sought to capitalize on existing and potential demand for Taiwanese fruit both inside and outside the country. Image: Local officials in Pingtung County (southeastern Taiwan) pose with a shipment of various fruits— mangoes, lychees, and dragon fruit—bound for shipment to Europe under the terms of new trade agreements with the European Union (June 2026). (Image source: Central News Agency ) Cold Chain Logistics: The Unsung Hero Today, Taiwanese fruit is sold at a premium in supermarkets and specialty retailers in numerous countries, such as Japan, South Korea, Australia, Canada, Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Brunei and Palau—but the produce would not have made it beyond its shores without advancements in Taiwan’s cold chain logistics industry. The Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI, 工業技術研究 院) , a non-government R&D organization that incubated Taiwan’s semiconductor industry , has been dedicated to the development of cold chain logistics since the 1990s . Janet Chen (陳慧 娟) , General Director of ITRI’s Service Systems Technology Center, told this author that there are similarities to transporting fruit and semiconductors, as they both have strict requirements in temperature, humidity, and cleanliness: “Agricultural products must be kept within appropriate temperature and humidity ranges to slow deterioration and preserve freshness and nutritional value. Semiconductor components may also be sensitive to temperature and humidity. Clean storage and transportation environments help prevent cross-contamination and microbial growth in agricultural cold chains. Semiconductor manufacturing requires exceptionally clean environments because even microscopic particles can cause defects.” Chen adds: “Freshness is a major source of value for agricultural products, making timely delivery essential. Semiconductor supply chains also require fast and reliable transportation because delays may lead to missed business opportunities, inventory shortages, or production disruptions. Agricultural cold chains require traceability from farm to table to support food safety and quality control.” [1] Government Ensures Taiwan’s Fruit is Compliant The Ministry of Agriculture (MOA, 農業部) has also ensured that fruit exports comply with regulations that differ from territory to territory. For instance, mangoes heading to Europe must be subjected to heat treatment to kill off any pests or microbial hitchhikers, while pineapples bound for New Zealand must be harvested at a specific life stage . This is not to mention the various pesticide standards set in overseas markets. To support Taiwan’s farmers, the MOA and local governments in 2024 inaugurated a processing park in Yujing District in Tainan , which can process mango and pineapple to meet international standards. Its Produce Processing and Cold Chain Logistics Center ( 玉井農產加工及冷鏈物流中心) is equipped with pre-cooling, processing, refrigeration, and freezer zones capable of processing as much as 800 tons of mangoes a year. External uncertainties highlight the significance of transport quality control. Kris Tang, General Manager of fruit exporter Sunray Fresh ( 昇睿鮮 農) , revealed to this author that during their first commercial shipment, fruit travelled via Frankfurt in the midst of a staffing shortage and a heat wave. “The mango and lychee could not be placed on the same onward flight to the UK and had to arrive separately. (By then), our priority was not simply to preserve the original schedule, but to protect the quality and integrity of the products.” [2] Gaining entry into Europe’s market is a good start—but more needs to be done if Taiwanese farmers are to cut their reliance on the Chinese market entirely. Focus Taiwan has reported that the Taiwan still sold USD 370 million worth of fresh fruit to Hong Kong and China from 2020 to May 2026, while exports to Japan totaled USD 199.4 million during the same period. But exporters know that getting a foothold is just the first, albeit critical step. Tang told this author: “The first shipment was important, but it was only the beginning. What matters is whether we can create a repeatable and commercially sustainable route that allows more Taiwanese fruit and agricultural products to enter the UK and, eventually, the wider European market.” [3] The main point: Taiwan’s move away from relying on a handful of traditional export markets like China has opened new doors for its fruit exports. That pivot, which also resulted in new technological innovation within Taiwan’s cold-chain logistics system, opened new markets in Europe for Taiwan’s mangoes and lychees. Developing its fruit market has also paved the way for Taiwan’s exports beyond high-tech products. [1] Author’s interview, summer 2026. [2] Author’s interview, summer 2026. [3] Ibid. The post Fruit at the Forefront of a Trade and Diplomatic Push appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

【大纪元2026年10月11日讯】（大纪元记者林丹纽约报导）10月10日是中华民国115年双十国庆，一群来自中国大陆的移民一早在纽约法拉盛图书馆前，举行庄严的“青天白日满地红旗”升旗仪式，庆祝中华民国成立115周年。他们挥舞中华民国国旗与美国国旗，表达盼望中国大陆早日实现民主、自由与宪政的心声。 2026年10月10日，大陆移民在纽约华人社区法拉盛庆祝中华民国115年国庆，举行庄严的升旗仪式，盼中国大陆有一天实现宪政民主。（中华民国国军老兵关爱中心提供） 大陆移民在纽约法拉盛举行中华民国115年国庆升旗典礼，盼中国大陆实现宪政民主。（中华民国老兵关爱中心提供） 活动由中华民国公民联盟、中华民国国军老兵关爱中心主办，参加的有中国新时代人民党、基督徒公义联盟、中国民主人权联盟等团体，这些团体的成员多为大陆新移民。参加者打出横幅：“中华民国才是我的国，中共国是非法国”、“解散中国共产党，台湾接管新中国，恢复中华民国，普用台湾宪法 ”。众人高喊口号：“结束中共暴政！中华民国万岁！” 在美国国歌和中华民国国歌之后，在中华民国国旗歌声中，青天白日满地红旗冉冉升起。 活动主持人、中华民国国军老兵关爱中心执行长王莉在开场时表示，升起中华民国国旗，“是对自由中国的希望，对民族共和的信念，对中华民国未来的期待。” 她说，中国大陆不仅要结束中共一党专政，更重要的是建立一个自由、民主、法治的国家，“中华民国的历史与宪政制度，可以为中国大陆未来的政治转型提供重要参考。” 中华民国海外公民委员会执行长曹胜华表示，根据《中华民国宪法增修条文》的表述，在国家统一前，中华民国分为大陆地区和自由地区（台湾）。他说：“中国大陆是战区、是匪区、是敌占区、是沦陷区”，庆祝双十国庆之际，不应忘记中国大陆的同胞，期盼中国大陆早日结束中共统治，走向民主宪政。 曹胜华并指出，台湾（中华民国）因此不仅在地缘政治上是美国的战略重地，也是美国反共产主义意识形态的前线，他说：“2026 年美国独立 250 周年庆典上，川普总统将共产主义对美国与世界的危害当成演讲的核心主题：‘共产主义是世界上一切自由人民的敌人，是美国宪法的敌人，更是 1776 年 7月4日的敌人。’美国永远不会成为共产主义国家，而中华民国大陆沦陷区必将终结共产主义的奴役，回归民主宪政道路。” 中华民国国军老兵关爱中心董事长胡福庆表示，他长期坚持街头宣讲国军在抗日战争中的贡献，是希望更多华人，尤其是被中共洗脑的大陆移民重新认识中华民国的过去、现在与未来。他也希望大陆民众看到，中共政权结束之后，中国并非只能面对混乱、分裂或另一场专制，“回归共和、重建宪政的中华民国，是可以追循的一条道路。” 中国新民党创办人杨茂森则以“民国魂”为主题发言，回顾中华民国建立及抗日战争的历史，他并批评中共对台湾的施压与跨国镇压行为。 针对近日发生的加州华裔房产中介张婉莹监控台湾总统赖清德长子一案，杨茂森表示：“这不是一般的跨国镇压案件，如果中共不承认台湾是一个国家，承认它属于中华民国管辖，那么这个案件是跨国镇压；但如果中共认为台湾是一个主权国家，那么对台湾这个主权国家的总统的儿子的监控，那属于侵略行为，性质就不一样了。所以，我们要把中共的残暴、反人类揭露出来，同时要终结它。” 中华民国公民联盟总协特助凯武说，民主的先驱不是哪些老而腐朽的人，他们是年轻、正直、能明辨是非的人；现在的年轻人也应该挺身而出，成为中国民主的栋梁。而当今的中国，人民不能自由表达意见、没有选举权，正如孙中山先生所说的：“革命尚未成功， 同志仍须努力”。 中国民主人权联盟纽约副主席钱家发回顾历史说：“中共邪党为了阻止蒋委员长‘攘外必先安内’的剿共策略，竟然诱骗张学良发动西安事变，此后，中共邪党在共同抗日的幌子下，‘七分发展，二分应付，一分抗日’，利用国民党在抗战中的军力消耗，在苏俄的支持下，再一次发动内战，将中华民国政府逼退至台湾。” 来自南京的钱家发说，他对中华民国的记忆刻在骨子里，“从总统府、国民大会堂、内政部、外交部、中山陵，以及道路两旁高大的梧桐树，总想像着中华民国有那么一天会还都南京。” 他表示，中华民国在台湾维持民主制度，成为中国大陆民众向往自由的一座灯塔。 基督徒公义联盟代表赵西玲说：“我们希望有一天，中国人民能够自由表达意见、自由选择信仰，能够在法律面前人人平等，让权力受到制度的约束，让公义成为社会的根基。” 国军老兵关爱中心代表杨家儒表示，当中国大陆迎来政治转型的历史时刻，重新走上中华民国的宪政道路，是值得考虑的选择。 众人在赵西玲的带领下大合唱《中华民国颂》。法拉盛缅街熙熙攘攘，升旗仪式吸引众多大陆移民驻足观看。 责任编辑：黄小堂

# “捂嘴” 、“洗

# 脑” : 中国人工

# 智能审查能否

第 4 卷 第 4 期

CC-BY-NC-ND

汉娜 · 西贝里

钟伟锋 访谈 31

> 钟伟锋 Hannah Cyberey

编按 ：“完全跳过思考过程，直接给出答案——要么拒绝回答，要么

顾左右而言他，要么给你一句党的口径”，Hannah Cyberey（汉娜 · 西

贝里）这样描述 DeepSeek 模型内置的审查机制。Cyberey 是弗吉尼亚

大学数据科学学院博士后研究员，她与导师埃文斯（David Evans）教

授合著的论文《操控审查之舵》，在大语言模型内部找到了控制审查

程度的 “引导向量”，可以像拧旋钮一样把审查调高或调低；论文还发

现，DeepSeek-R1 系列推理模型遇到“台湾独立”、“六四”等敏感话题

时，会完全跳过思考过程，作者称之为 “思维压制”。

Cyberey 在台湾出生、长大，2025 年获弗吉尼亚大学计算机科学博士学

位，研究人工智能模型的评测与审计。2026 年 9 月 15 日，钟伟锋博士

对 Cyberey 博士进行了专访。钟伟锋是乔治 · 梅森大学默卡特斯中心学

者、《中国民主季刊》顾问编辑。访谈探讨了中国大语言模型内置的

审查机制、白盒与黑盒两种审计方法、所谓 “无审查” 模型、西方模型

的安全限制与审查的异同、放慢人工智能发展之争，以及威权政府在

人工智能时代如何控制信息等问题。 32

钟伟锋（以下简称钟）： Hannah，我们在今天之前其实从没见过

面，但我读过你那篇精彩的论文《操控审查之舵》（Steering the

CensorShip）（英文原题把“审查”一词 censorship 中的 ship 大

写，ship 即“船”，steer 即“掌舵”，一语双关——编者。），由

此知道了你的研究。论文是你和合作者埃文斯（David Evans）教授

去年发表的，非常有意思。不过在进入正题之前——因为论文涉及很

多技术性的内容——我想先请你介绍一下自己，以及你目前在弗吉尼

亚大学从事什么研究。

Hannah Cyberey （以下简称 Cyberey）： 其实我是在台湾出生、

长大的，后来到美国读研究生，去年夏天拿到了计算机科学博士学

位。我的博士论文主要研究“可信自然语言处理”（trustworthy

natural language processing）。自然语言处理关注的是处理文本

的模型，ChatGPT 就属于这一类。我研究的是如何提高模型的可靠

性，怎样确保它们按我们希望的方式运作。我的大部分工作集中在

评测（evaluation）和审计（auditing） 1 上，这是我研究的主线。

不过我也研究过其他一些相关问题，比如对抗鲁棒性（adversarial

robustness），也就是模型能不能抵御对抗攻击（“对抗攻击”指故

意构造特殊的输入来诱使模型出错，例如在提问中加入精心设计的干

扰文字，让模型绕过安全限制。——编者）；还有偏见与公平性；还

有审查，就是《操控审查之舵》那项研究。最近我在做的是审计：怎

样拿出证据，证明模型的实际表现确实与我们所声称的相符。

钟： 先给读者交代一下背景。正如你刚才提到的，我最早是通过《操

控审查之舵》这篇论文了解你的研究的。我先说说我的理解，不准确 访谈 33

的地方请你指正。我读完论文的印象是：如果把 DeepSeek 模型——

或许也包括其他中国开发的模型——看成一个受到审查的人脑，那么

你们设法弄清了这个“大脑”内部发生的某些事情。那里似乎有一个

旋钮，可以调高调低，以此纠正，或许该说是操控——这个人工智能

模型“嘴”里说出来的话。这个比喻准确吗？

Cyberey ：是的。这种技术叫作“激活引导” （activation steering），

它 借 助 的 是 所 谓 的“ 引 导 向 量”（steering vector） 2。 我 们 在 模

型内部找出与某个特定概念——比如审查——相对应的内部表征

（representation）。同样，你也可以找出与性别相对应的表征，操

控模型中的性别信号，从而在一定程度上控制模型的行为。我那篇审

查论文就是基于激活引导这种技术。就像你描述的那样，你可以把它

调高或调低，来提高或者降低这种行为出现的概率。

钟： 说到审查，我能理解。我是在中国出生长大的，那里的审查多得

不得了。我最熟悉的模式其实是“捂嘴”。在我成长的过程中，这种

事没发生在我身上，但发生在我认识的人身上：你上百度这样的搜索

引擎，输入“台湾独立”之类的词，国安人员就会找上门来。这就像

捂住你的嘴。从这样的例子里，我学到的就是：那种东西千万别搜。

在公共场合，有些话就不说了。我不知道你的研究能不能拿这个来类

比：如果你在手机上用 DeepSeek，输入某些内容，有时会看到人工

智能开始回答，然后一下子答案全都没了。那算不算“捂嘴”？你研

究的东西和它有什么不同？

Cyberey： 我相信他们肯定有多个层面的审查，不只是嵌在模型里的 34

那种。我研究的是通过训练嵌入模型内部的审查。他们大概还有一些

“事后分类器” （post hoc classifier；指在模型之外另设的自动检测

程序，在模型生成内容的同时或之后进行筛查，一旦发现违规内容即

中断输出——编者），检测模型的思考内容或者用户输入的内容，一

旦发现敏感话题，就当场停下来。所以是的，我觉得那和你描述的差

不多，就像有什么东西拦着，不让你把信息说出来。

钟： 对。那么你的研究——是不是可以说，你的研究之所以可行，是

因为你能下载它的开放权重模型（open weight） 3 ？起码是其中某个

版本？

Cyberey： 对，是的。这种方法只适用于我们所说的“白盒模型” 4，

也就是我们能拿到权重、可以操控其内部参数的模型。

忧：如果中国政府不断加大力度，提高模型里的审查程度——不只是

通过训练把某种审查机制嵌进模型，他们可能会开始从训练数据里删

除信息。那样的话，我们目前的去审查技术可能就不够用了，因为模

型是用训练数据训练出来的，如果中国政府开始筛选这些数据，我们

就没法规避那些审查了。

钟： 我倒是能想到——当然不是要给中共出主意——我能想到一个可

能：如果他们出台一项规定，要求所有人工智能公司都必须用中国互

联网上的数据来训练模型，那所有模型都会是“干净”的，对吧？因

为中国的互联网本身已经经过审查。你不能用任何不是 .cn 结尾的网

站，也就是非中国域名网站的数据。那么，中国互联网全都是“干净”

的，你的模型最后也会非常“干净”，尽管它可能能力不太强，因为 46

没有学到世界其他地方的很多东西。

Cyberey： 是的。我还在想，政府会不会也限制——现在的模型需要

获取较新的信息时，往往不会只依赖自己内部的知识，而是会上网搜

索其他信息。我在想，中国政府是不是也需要限制这些模型可以查哪

些网站。

钟： 对。但那也很难做到吧？因为那几乎是即时的。根据查询的不同，

模型会启动网页搜索功能，从世界上任何地方引入内容，然后模型得

当场实时决定让哪些内容进来。

Cyberey： 是啊，不知道那要怎么过滤。

钟： 对。所以我真希望这能给中国那些以审查为业的人添很多活儿，

让他们没法控制一切。这确实让我对人们手里能多一点自由抱有一点

希望。这些讨论都非常有意思。我也很想知道——你现在是弗吉尼亚

大学的博士后，最近写了这些很精彩的论文，我都读过——那你接下

来要做什么？你的研究路线图上有什么？

Cyberey： 我马上要去一个新的职位，是在太平洋西北国家实验室

（美国能源部下属的国家实验室）做研究。我将从事人工智能保障（AI

assurance；指通过测试、评估和审计，确保人工智能系统安全可靠、

符合预期的研究领域——编者）研究，这是我一直在做的研究的自然

延续：审计，怎样控制模型的行为，确保它们可靠。所以我会继续这

方面的研究。接下来我最想做的是改进我们评测模型的方式。我认为 访谈 47

这是很多机器学习工作的基础：我们怎样确定模型在进步，或者训练

方法是否有效？我们需要有更好的评测基础，才能确保我们开发的这

些方法都真的有效。

钟： 祝贺你找到新工作。

Cyberey： 谢谢。

钟： 那么说到评测，具体指的是什么？你想的是一个产品，还是一套

别人会遵循的行业标准流程？最后成形的东西会是什么样子？

Cyberey： 是的，我认为在国家实验室肯定会有很好的机会，我们可

以研究如何建立评测人工智能模型的标准方法，或者如何以更系统的

方式进行审计。

钟： 我很期待在你去国家实验室之后继续关注你的研究。

Cyberey： 好的。

钟： 谢谢你。我希望我们的读者也会喜欢今天的对谈。这是《中国民

主季刊》 系列访谈的一部分， 我们请来嘉宾， 谈论包括人工智能在内的

各种热门话题， 以一种有助于我们了解这个行业、 也有助于我们理解和

认识中国未来实现民主的可能的方式来谈——希望那一天不会太远。

如果读者想进一步了解你的研究，他们可以在搜索引擎上输入你的名

字 Hannah Cyberey。你在 GitHub 上也有一个网站： hannahxchen. 48

github.io 。

我推荐大家去看看 Hannah 的研究，非常精彩。再次感谢你接受《中

国民主季刊》的专访。

Cyberey： 好的，谢谢。

huggingface.co/spaces/hannahcyberey/Refusal-Censorship-Steering。这

两个演示都放在 Hugging Face 平台上，大陆读者可能需要翻墙才能打

开。她还写了一篇比论文通俗的英文博客文章介绍这项研究：https://

hannahxchen.github.io/blog/2025/censorship-steering/。

title: 要闻分析 - 在俄导弹袭乌的轰炸中 俄中美“联盟”显形了?
summary: 周一19日凌晨俄罗斯发射多波导弹袭击基辅，至少造成1人死亡、8人受伤。乌克兰总统泽连斯基就此表示：虽然俄罗斯以弹道导弹攻击基辅及周边地区的能源设施，但乌方事前并未收到盟国的预警。所谓的盟国指的当然是美国 泽连斯基指出，俄罗斯19日向基辅及周边地区发射16枚弹道导弹，并向乌克兰各地出动了200架以上的无人机。法新社记者报道说：在首都基辅可以听到空袭警报与爆炸声。 乌克兰总统19日在社群媒体发文表示：俄罗斯再次发动弹道飞弹攻击，一整夜分多次袭击，而我们的伙伴又一次没有事先发出预警
content:
周一19日凌晨俄罗斯发射多波导弹袭击基辅，至少造成1人死亡、8人受伤。乌克兰总统泽连斯基就此表示：虽然俄罗斯以弹道导弹攻击基辅及周边地区的能源设施，但乌方事前并未收到盟国的预警。所谓的盟国指的当然是美国

泽连斯基指出，俄罗斯19日向基辅及周边地区发射16枚弹道导弹，并向乌克兰各地出动了200架以上的无人机。法新社记者报道说：在首都基辅可以听到空袭警报与爆炸声。

乌克兰总统19日在社群媒体发文表示：俄罗斯再次发动弹道飞弹攻击，一整夜分多次袭击，而我们的伙伴又一次没有事先发出预警。基辅方面上周就曾经指出，美国先前也未针对类似攻击发出预警，使居民几乎没有时间躲进避难设施。

但美国国务卿卢比奥19日稍早否认美国曾暂停与乌克兰分享情报。

美国总统特朗普近日数次就俄乌战争批评泽连斯基。他曾表示，美国已与俄罗斯达成协议，以放宽制裁换取俄国出口燃料。

特朗普18日在自家社群平台“真实社群”（Truth Social）发文称，他在推动俄乌和平谈判方面正取得“重大进展”，但泽连斯基既“不在乎”也“不希望结束这场战争”。

于是泽连斯基19日在贴文中反驳特朗普以上说法，他强调：“乌克兰从来就不想打这场战争，也一直欢迎合作伙伴为使战争有尊严地落幕所付出的一切努力。”

他还说：俄罗斯的回应，就是一次又一次的弹道导弹、见证者（Shahed）无人机与杀戮。

他补充道：“当对乌克兰的防空导弹供应受阻，俄罗斯却获得了制裁放宽或延后实施的待遇，很遗憾，这显示我们有些伙伴不愿正视现实。”

美国特朗普政府用断供防空导弹和星链不灵等方式逼迫乌克兰放弃袭击俄罗斯能源目标，就在双方矛盾公开化的节点上，普京在加大打击乌克兰的同时，又抛出外交武器，提议要在中国深圳亚太经合会峰会期间，与习近平和特朗普共商：如何在对俄罗斯有利的情形下结束俄乌战争？

一名前俄国情报官员向华尔街日报透露，普京是在10月9日与特朗普通话时提出的这个构想，当天的通话还促成了美俄柴油协议，让美国得以购买俄罗斯柴油，并协助俄方将柴油销往全球市场。

克里姆林宫发言人则证实这一消息属实，并且相关各方的确在讨论举行这类会晤的可能。虽然目前对于会晤本身及可能讨论的议程，尚无明确共识，“但3方都承认，举行这类会晤在理论上可行”。

报导还引述一名美方高层表示，特朗普虽尚未同意举行这场峰会，但特朗普希望兑现竞选承诺、结束俄乌战争，因此推测特朗普很可能对这项提议抱持开放态度。

据报俄方已透过外交管道向北京提出这项构想，中方则表明只要特朗普同意，中方不反对举行会晤。

报导还引述前俄国情报官员表示，普京过去就曾分别向特朗普和习近平提议举行3方峰会，不过这次提出时机正逢美俄关系回温，目前态势的天秤正朝有利俄国倾斜。

莫斯科盼促成美俄中3方对话，将欧洲排除在外；克里姆林宫认为，欧洲是阻碍俄乌战争结束的背后力量。

这名前俄国情报官员甚至表示，普京有意将可能的美俄中3国领袖会形塑成第二次雅尔塔会议，接此重新划分彼此的全球势力范围。华尔街日报认为如果这场峰会在排除欧洲与乌克兰参与下登场，等于开创罕见先例，势必引发欧洲各国高度警戒。

**同一天10月19日的另一条消息也令人生疑：**

自己发动对乌克兰战争快5年，需要习近平特朗普加持的普京现在试图扮演调解伊朗战事的角色，他派俄国外交部长拉夫罗夫19日抵达伊朗进行访问，这是中东战争爆发以来俄外长首度到访伊朗。

法新社报导，本月初，俄罗斯总统普京曾告诉伊朗总统裴泽斯基安（Masoud Pezeshkian），俄国准备为中东地区的战争调解工作贡献心力。

拉夫罗夫预计将与伊朗外交部长阿拉奇（Abbas Araghchi）会面，他表示，俄国的努力“旨在防止重返大规模战争”。目前伊朗与美国的谈判处于僵局状态。

最近特朗普公开展示对普京的友好和对乌克兰的背叛，已经引发舆论对特朗普动机的怀疑。特朗普逼迫泽连斯基单方面停止轰炸俄罗斯能源设施，说是为了降低油价，人们无法相信但找不到真实原因。

**部分答案现在显现了：其实是特朗普在与普京做交易，他对普京高抬贵手，普京则可以发挥对伊朗政权的影响力，最终让特朗普更体面地从海湾战争泥潭中脱身。**

**被牺牲的当然就是乌克兰，而能阻止这一切的最重要力量也只能来自美国内部。即将到来的中期选举重要性毋庸置疑。**

title: 一文看懂：美中俄或举行乌克兰问题会谈 大国外交能否推动战争终结？
summary: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期一(10月19日)针对美中俄三方可能就乌克兰战争举行高层会谈表示，“只要我能做任何事来结束战争，我都会去做。”特朗普总统也在回答美国之音中文部记者提问时表示，他会与中国国家主席习近平商谈乌克兰问题。 与此同时，国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)星期一表示，目前尚未最终确定会谈细节，有关会谈可能在11月举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会期间进行。 这场潜在会谈的背后，是三个大国不同的战略考量，以及乌克兰在持续战争
content:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期一(10月19日)针对美中俄三方可能就乌克兰战争举行高层会谈表示，“只要我能做任何事来结束战争，我都会去做。”特朗普总统也在回答美国之音中文部记者提问时表示，他会与中国国家主席习近平商谈乌克兰问题。

与此同时，国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)星期一表示，目前尚未最终确定会谈细节，有关会谈可能在11月举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会期间进行。

这场潜在会谈的背后，是三个大国不同的战略考量，以及乌克兰在持续战争压力下面临的艰难抉择。若会谈成行，能否推动俄乌战争走向结束？当乌克兰的未来成为大国谈判议题时，基辅又将面临怎样的处境？

**美国：推动停火，同时控制战争风险**

特朗普总统星期一在白宫玫瑰园签署了一项聚焦女性健康的行政命令，在签署仪式结束后面对记者询问时，他表示，愿意做任何事帮助结束乌克兰战争。

“我对俄罗斯和乌克兰的唯一希望就是他们停止这场愚蠢的战争。无论有人在场与否，只要我能做任何事情来结束战争，我都会去做。”特朗普说。

当美国之音中文部记者黄耀毅询问特朗普总统，是否会与中国领导人习近平谈乌克兰问题时，特朗普给予一个肯定的答案。

“我会的。不过，到目前为止，我认为他(习近平)在乌克兰问题上一直非常公平。他并没有过多介入，对俄罗斯方面也是如此。他们的介入程度远没有达到本来可以达到的程度，我对此表示赞赏。他们知道我对此表示赞赏。”

星期一稍早，国务卿马尔科·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)在访问乌兹别克斯坦期间说，美国将尽一切努力达成解决方案。“在过去近两年时间里，我们多次进行接触，试图促成或推动这场战争的结束；我认为，如果有可能，总统愿意采取任何他能做的事情来帮助结束这场战争。我们将继续寻找这样做的机会。”他说。

特朗普政府可能试图利用其对乌克兰的长期支持，以及与俄罗斯直接沟通的渠道，推动双方达成停火或政治协议。与中国展开沟通，也有助于美国探索更广泛的外交解决路径。

然而，如何平衡尽快结束战争与维护乌克兰安全，是美国面临的核心难题。

如果美国过于强调迅速达成协议，乌克兰可能被迫接受不利的领土安排，或者在缺乏可靠安全保障的情况下停火。近期美国取消部分对俄罗斯能源的制裁，也引发基辅对华盛顿是否会继续对莫斯科施压的担忧。

**俄罗斯：将战场成果转化为政治利益**

对俄罗斯而言，与美国直接讨论乌克兰问题，有助于莫斯科争取将战场上的既得利益转化为外交成果。

自2022年全面入侵乌克兰以来，俄罗斯一直试图巩固对乌克兰部分领土的控制，并要求西方重视其安全诉求。莫斯科希望未来的安排能够涉及领土问题、乌克兰的军事与外交方向，北约扩大，以及涉俄制裁。

与美国和中国领导人举行会谈，也能提升俄罗斯的国际地位，表明莫斯科仍是国际安全事务无法绕开的参与者。

但俄罗斯面临的难题是，如何在不作出重大让步的情况下结束战争。若停火无法满足其核心诉求，莫斯科可能缺乏妥协动力；而战争持续带来的军事和经济消耗，也使其必须权衡继续作战的成本。

**中国：主张政治解决，争取外交主动权**

中国一直主张通过对话谈判解决乌克兰危机，强调尊重各国主权和领土完整，同时重视各方合理安全关切。

中国与俄罗斯保持密切的政治和经济关系，也与欧洲及乌克兰维持外交联系。

对中国而言，参与三方会谈既可能为政治解决提供新的沟通平台，也有助于提升中国在欧洲安全事务和全球外交中的影响力。乌克兰战争持续影响能源、粮食、贸易及大国关系，北京也有动力推动局势降温。

不过，中国的角色面临争议。美国及部分西方国家批评中国与俄罗斯的经济和工业联系有助于俄罗斯维持战争能力，北京则否认支持俄罗斯的军事行动，并强调政治解决。

中国外交部发言人毛宁星期一被记者问到可能的三方会谈时回答说：“这个问题目前我没有可以提供的信息。”

**乌克兰：战争当事方，却面临话语权受限**

对乌克兰而言，最大的担忧是，三个大国讨论乌克兰的未来，却未必充分考虑乌克兰自身的诉求。

经过多年战争，乌克兰面临人员伤亡、基础设施受损和经济压力。随着冬季临近，能源设施及供电、供暖保障也成为现实挑战。与此同时，乌克兰的防御能力仍高度依赖美国等西方国家的军事、情报和经济支持。

基辅面临两难：接受以现有战线为基础的停火，可能意味着俄罗斯继续控制部分乌克兰领土；拒绝不利条件，则可能让战争继续消耗国家资源。

更重要的是，即使达成停火，乌克兰仍需要可靠的长期安全保障，以防俄罗斯未来再次发动进攻。

因此，乌克兰希望确保自己能够直接参与谈判，并坚持任何和平协议都必须考虑国家主权、领土完整和未来安全。欧洲国家的参与同样重要，因为欧洲既是乌克兰的重要支持者，也是战争长期影响的直接承担者。

title: China protests after Japanese premier sends monetary offering to war-linked Yasukuni shrine
summary: Aamir Latif and Riyaz ul Khaliq 19 October 2026•Update: 19 October 2026 Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a monetary offering Monday to the war-linked Yasukuni shrine in Tokyo, prompting “strong protests” from China, according to
content:
Aamir Latif and Riyaz ul Khaliq

19 October 2026•Update: 19 October 2026

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a monetary offering Monday to the war-linked Yasukuni shrine in Tokyo, prompting “strong protests” from China, according to local media.

The shrine has long been a source of diplomatic friction between Japan and its neighbors, including China.

Takaichi sent the offering out of her own pocket for the shrine’s autumn festival, Kyodo News reported.

Takaichi, as the leader of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, also sent a "masakaki" ritual offering of evergreen twigs on Saturday.

Land Minister Tatsunori Ibayashi and the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's Election Strategy Committee Chairperson Nishimura Yasutoshi separately visited the shrine, which honors "convicted war criminals" along with millions of war dead.

Previous visits to the shrine by Japanese leaders have prompted strong criticism from China and South Korea. Japan occupied a wide area of China by the end of World War II, and South Korea was under Japanese colonial rule between 1910 and 1945.

China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Beijing “firmly opposes and strongly condemns” the “negative moves” by Japan.

Beijing has “lodged serious and strong protests with the Japanese side,” Mao told reporters in Beijing.

“The war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarist war of aggression,” Mao said, recalling that it “honors 14 convicted Class A war criminals responsible for Japan's aggression.”

“Japanese leaders and politicians, despite knowing this quite well, still pay respect to the war shrine. This reveals their deep-seated wrong view on historical issues and malicious intention to erase the criminal record of those war criminals, reverse the verdict on aggression and clear the path for remilitarization,” Mao alleged.

Noting that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, Mao said Beijing calls on Japan to “recognize history, repent for historical crimes, stop the retrogressive moves on historical issues and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the wider world with concrete actions.”

Ties between Tokyo and Beijing have been strained since last November following Takaichi's comments suggesting that an attack on Taiwan could prompt a response by Japan's Self-Defense Forces in support of the US.

China considers Taiwan its breakaway province to be unified with the country, while Taiwan insists on its independence.

# Typhoon Champi to turn away from Taiwan, will still bring heavy rain

10/19/2026 07:53 PM

[](jsvscript:)[](jsvscript:)[](javascript:void(0))[Listen](javascript:)

[Link](javascript:)[Whatsapp](javascript:)[Reddit](javascript:)[Line](javascript:)[Email](javascript:)

CNA graphic

Taipei, Oct. 19 (CNA) Typhoon Champi will turn northward earlier than previously forecast, sparing Taiwan a direct hit but still bringing heavy rain to the north of the country on Friday and Saturday, according to the Central Weather Administration (CWA).

CWA forecaster Cheng Chieh-jen (鄭傑仁) told CNA Typhoon Champi had strengthened and increased in size over the past 12 hours, and as of Monday afternoon was packing sustained winds of 198 kilometers per hour near its center.

Due to the weakening of a Pacific high-pressure system, however, the storm is now expected to turn northward earlier than initially forecast, likely around Japan's Ishigaki Island, Cheng said.

As Champi brushes past northeastern Taiwan, it will likely be a strong "moderate" typhoon or weak "intense" typhoon per the CWA's classification system, which defines the latter as having sustained winds above 184 kph, Cheng said.

Based on current forecasts, the CWA could issue a sea warning on Wednesday night or Thursday at the earliest, and a land warning on Thursday evening or Friday, Cheng said.

The warning will likely apply to northern and eastern Taiwan, with the north and Yilan, in particular, facing possible heavy or extremely heavy rain on Friday and Saturday, he added.

As for this week's weather, Cheng said the CWA forecast mostly cloudy to clear skies on Tuesday, with high temperatures of 30-32 degrees Celsius in the eastern half of the country and 31-34 degrees in the west.

On Wednesday, a northeasterly wind system will bring slightly cooler temperatures to the north, with daytime highs reaching 27-30 degrees and a chance of scattered showers in Yilan and areas north of Hsinchu, Cheng said.

As the typhoon approaches on Thursday, there will continue to be scattered rain showers in Yilan and northern Taiwan. Those areas could see heavy or extremely heavy rain on Friday and Saturday, while scattered showers are forecast for other regions, Cheng said.

As Typhoon Champi weakens and moves away from Taiwan on Sunday, cloudy to clear weather conditions will prevail in most regions, with the exception of lingering rain showers in the east and on the Hengchun Peninsula in the south, Cheng said.

(By Chang Hsiung-feng and Matthew Mazzetta)

title: 花旗預測 陸AI企業赴港上市維持穩健
summary: [udn](https://udn.com/)[兩岸](https://udn.com/news/cate/2/6640)[陸港經貿](https://udn.com/news/story/7333/9822648) 聽新聞 0:00 / 0:00 2026-10-19 03:21 聯合報／ 記者[謝守真](https://udn.com/news/reporter/MDY5OTg=)／綜合報導 香港 [**中國大陸**](https://udn.com/search/tag
content:
[udn](https://udn.com/)[兩岸](https://udn.com/news/cate/2/6640)[陸港經貿](https://udn.com/news/story/7333/9822648)

聽新聞

0:00 / 0:00

2026-10-19 03:21 聯合報／ 記者[謝守真](https://udn.com/news/reporter/MDY5OTg=)／綜合報導  香港

[**中國大陸**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9C%8B%E5%A4%A7%E9%99%B8)ＡＩ產業今年掀起上市潮，[**香港**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E9%A6%99%E6%B8%AF)成為相關企業重要的融資市場。據路透，[**花旗**](https://udn.com/search/tagging/2/%E8%8A%B1%E6%97%97)銀行高層預期，儘管市場對企業估值的疑慮升高，大陸ＡＩ供應鏈企業赴港上市趨勢仍將維持穩健，明年香港股權資本市場的焦點，有望從硬體供應商轉向ＡＩ模型及應用開發商。

路透報導，花旗中國投資銀行及亞太區金融機構業務主管袁崢怡在曼谷出席國際貨幣基金（ＩＭＦ）會議期間受訪，談及大陸ＡＩ供應鏈企業赴港上市前景。她提到，儘管市場對估值的疑慮升高、審查日益嚴格，ＡＩ供應鏈企業仍將持續赴港上市。

袁崢怡指出，近期資料中心企業的估值回落主要源自美國市場，但ＡＩ供應鏈企業仍將繼續赴港上市。

她表示，計畫在香港上市的大陸企業，投資需求大致一半來自大陸境內、一半來自國際市場，有助於緩衝市場波動的影響。香港市場也有本地資金支持，持續增加的大陸南向資金正成為重要買盤。

不過，袁崢怡警告，如果美國整個ＡＩ產業周期出現反轉，全球市場都將受到影響，香港也不例外。他並指出，過去幾周市場已出現一些波動。

在供應鏈布局方面，袁崢怡表示，許多大陸硬體業者已主動在大陸以外建立生產據點，有助於服務全球客戶，並降低地緣政治摩擦帶來的影響。

他指出，大陸硬體供應商受惠於全球ＡＩ基礎設施建設熱潮，銷售量成長，產品單價也有所提高。

展望明年，袁崢怡預期，香港股權資本市場的焦點將從純硬體企業，轉向大陸ＡＩ模型及應用開發商。

title: Shame About the Hypersonics: Why the United States Needs More Missile Defenses in the Indo-Pacific

content:
By. Diego Arrendondo

DOI. 10.57912/34692192

On September 3, 2025, China held a Victory Day Parade to mark the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II. As is done annually, the display unveiled a range of new weapons, including [laser defense systems](https://nextgendefense.com/china-naval-laser-weapon/), [a stealth fighter](https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/f-35i-adir-vs-china-s-new-j-35-stealth-fighter-who-wins-in-summed-up-in-4-words/ar-AA1LYgoC?ocid=BingNewsSerp), and [missiles](https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/what-weapons-china-put-display-its-military-parade-2025-09-03/), signaling a modernization of China’s military that will force a change in U.S. posture and operations in the Pacific. The new weapons will expand China’s strike-force capabilities to include both the First and Second Island Chains in the Indo-Pacific, two U.S.-aligned arcs of archipelagos including Japan, Taiwan, Indonesia, and the Philippines in the First, and Guam and other strategic islands in the Second. The American military facilities on these island chains allow the U.S. to project its forces in the Pacific, enabling it to deter and respond to opposing forces quickly, restrict Chinese naval access, and form a defensive barrier. With China’s modernization of its military and shifting approach to Pacific hegemony, the U.S. should increase its anti-ballistic missile systems to protect its bases in Guam, South Korea, and Japan, and reassure its allies of its continued capability of stabilizing the region.

Military analysts and defense officials [widely agree](https://www.war.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/4150802/chinas-military-buildup-threatens-indo-pacific-region-security/)that the main purpose of China’s evolving weapons systems is to counter U.S. military assets, especially the U.S. naval hegemony in the region. Beijing also understands that in the era where drones can overwhelm traditional defenses, a rapid and cost-effective response is critical. The Liaoyuan-1([LY-1](https://nextgendefense.com/china-naval-laser-weapon/)) was one of the weapons on display designed for this purpose. It is [intended](https://nextgendefense.com/china-naval-laser-weapon/)for shipboard self-defense, specifically to disrupt and destroy optical sensors of enemy platforms that detect drones and missiles. Direct-energy weapons (DEW) like the LY-1 offer near-instant engagement at a low cost per shot, providing a financial advantage and an efficient means of countering saturated volumes of incoming threats.

All of these expanding weapons capabilities showcase China’s ambition to be seen as a leader among military powers and challenge American hegemony. The most significant and worrying are the [hypersonic missiles](https://www.eurasiantimes.com/china-hails-yj-21-hypersonic-ship-launched-missile/), most notably the Yingji 21 and DongFeng-26D (DF-26). The Yingji 21 can reach a terminal velocity of roughly Mach 10, making it difficult for missile-defense systems to intercept and earning it the title of an “aircraft carrier killer.” The base DF-26 is an intermediate-range ballistic missile (IRBM) [designed](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/china-df26d-guam-killer-missile-threatens-us-carriers-bases-pacific/)to deliver conventional and nuclear strikes. The “D” variant specifically has a 5,000-kilometer strike radius, making it able to hit [Guam](https://defencesecurityasia.com/en/china-df26d-guam-killer-missile-threatens-us-carriers-bases-pacific/), an important military base for the United States. These new weapons highlight a central gap in the current U.S. defensive posture in the Indo-Pacific by sending a signal that Beijing not only intends to match the U.S. in stealth but also in navy force projection.

Against this growing threat, the U.S. and its regional allies need to rely on layered missile-defense systems to strengthen deterrence and to counter potential attacks. At this moment, [Guam](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region)has a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) battery, each with 6 launchers and 8 interceptors per launcher, capable of intercepting missiles in their terminal phase. [South Korea](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region)additionally has one THAAD battery in Seongju, positioned to defend both Seoul and US troops in the Port of Busan. While [Japan](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region)does not have a battery, its defenses consist of 8 Aegis BMD ships, with five U.S. Aegis BMD ships permanently stationed in Japan. Defending all three of these territories is critical for the U.S. to manage the region and its global credibility because together, they serve as a multi-tiered system strategically important to the U.S. posture in the Indo-Pacific.

The U.S. should increase its land-based Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense System (ABMD) facilities and its THAAD in Guam, South Korea, and Japan. A layered missile defense increases the probability of intercept by creating multiple engagement windows. While it does not make defended regions invulnerable, it does raise the number of missiles required to achieve a successful hit, thereby lowering the cost-benefit ratio of an attack for China. Complicating the missiles’ reach deters China from employing missiles by reducing confidence in the ability to achieve reliable effects. However, the United States should also develop more cost-effective countermeasures, as it costs the U.S. about[$1 billion](https://www.thepricer.org/how-much-does-a-thaad-missile-cost/)for a THAAD battery, about $13 million for each interceptor, and [$637 million](https://www.forecastinternational.com/budget_site/pdf/FY2024/0300D%5FLineItem%5FMD73%5FLI%2D40%2DAegis%5FAshore%5FPhase%5FIII%5FFY2024%2Epdf)to deploy an Aegis Ashore.

Increasing ABMD and THAAD presence in Guam is essential because it provides the U.S. with a gateway to Asia, as it is home to important Navy and Air Force bases that [support](https://defensefeeds.com/analysis/geopolitics/guam-military-base/)the Air Force’s heavy bomber force, nuclear-powered submarines, the U.S. Pacific Fleet, and all long-range aircraft. Unlike the sea-based Aegis destroyers, which must divide time between escort and maintenance cycles, a land-based Aegis Ashore site provides continuous coverage. Similarly, enhancing South Korea's defenses is critical because of the US bases located within its borders. [South Korea](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan)currently operates 8 Patriot Advanced Capability (PAC-3) systems and its own MDS known as the Korean Air and Missile Defense; both [systems](https://www.missiledefenseadvocacy.org/defense-systems/patriot-advanced-capability-3-missile/)have a short range and cannot effectively engage IRBMs, giving opposing forces the possibility to neutralize U.S. bases and air operations. If the ROK Armed Forces are not able to delay opposing forces due to missiles, it will allow the enemy to neutralize U.S. bases, delaying U.S. reinforcements and disrupting air operations. In addition to holding[50,000](https://www.usfj.mil/About-USFJ/)U.S. military personnel and the [only](https://www.airpac.navy.mil/Organization/USS-George-Washington-CVN-73/About-Us/)forward-deployed aircraft carrier, the USS Geroge Washington, Japan also maintains [6 destroyers](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan), 5 of which are permanently-stationed, one cruiser equipped with [13 Aegis BMD destroyers](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan), and U.S.-operated PAC-3 systems in[Okinawa](https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/us-and-allied-ballistic-missile-defenses-asia-pacific-region#Japan). That being said, U.S. vessels or Japanese destroyers cannot be counted on to defend Japan if conflict breaks out, as ships would likely prioritize protecting U.S. [carrier strike groups](https://defensefeeds.com/analysis/weapons/carrier-strike-group/#:~:text=This%20layered%20formation%20defines%20standard%20carrier%20strike%20group,and%20operate%20together%20as%20a%20seamless%20combat%20system.). Deploying Aegis Ashore batteries in Japan will keep U.S. bases protected, freeing up ships to protect the USS George Washington, conduct patrols, and perform maintenance.

Although expanding layered missile defense would strengthen the U.S. ability to protect its forces in the Indo-Pacific, advocating for this policy is unlikely to be politically or economically feasible in the near term. The Iran War has shown that American [missile defense](https://sfg.media/en/a/us-patriot-thaad-missile-stockpiles-iran-war/#:~:text=The%20war%20with%20Iran%20has%20significantly%20depleted%20US,Patriot%20missiles%20and%20about%20250%20THAAD%20interceptors%20remaining.)is too [costly](https://jinsa.org/jinsa_report/missile-and-interceptor-cost-estimates-during-the-u-s-israel-iran-war/)and has drained that stockpile as well. Making a large expansion of missile defense in the Indo-Pacific more difficult to sustain. Domestically, the[American public](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/opinion-poll-iran-war/#:~:text=Americans%20do%20want%20the%20Iran%20war%20to%20end,interests%20and%20has%20not%20been%20worth%20the%20costs.)does not want to spend more on the military budget. Washington has also [reduced](https://www.armyrecognition.com/news/army-news/2026/trump-orders-reduction-us-south-korea-military-exercises-north-korea-iran-war#:~:text=On%20August%2016%2C%202026%2C%20U.S.%20President%20Donald%20Trump,before%20the%2011-day%20maneuvers%20were%20scheduled%20to%20begin.)the scale of some U.S.-South Korean military exercises. Japan is more favorable to military buildup, as its government has continued to [increase defense spending](https://blog.modeldiplomat.com/japan-military-spending-2026-budget-strategy)and invested in missile defense, drones, and other capabilities. The United States should instead develop cheaper defensive technologies, investing in [laser technology](https://www.defensenews.com/newsletters/daily-news-roundup/2026/04/28/what-we-know-about-the-us-militarys-new-joint-laser-weapon-system/)or other cost-effective countermeasures.

With the growing threat of China’s advancing military, the U.S. should consider focusing missile defense system expansion on strategic bases critical for combating Chinese regional influence. Guam, South Korea, and Japan are vital to the US for these reasons in stabilizing and maintaining its presence in the region. Additionally, placing defense systems in both Korea and Japan would reassure allies of the U.S.’s continued capability to defend against encroaching Chinese airstrike capabilities.  Deploying defense systems to these three locations will allow the United States to strengthen its naval deterrence as China continues to challenge the U.S.-led international order.

Taiwan has confronted and driven away 16 Chinese coastguard, research and fishing vessels that it said were involved in simultaneous “maritime harassment” operations.

An “unusually large” number of Chinese vessels took part in coordinated operations around Taiwan’s main island and Pratas (also known as Dongsha), a disputed island to the southwest, the Taiwanese coastguard said in a statement on Sunday.

zh_title: 公众投票评选低碳菜肴 九名厨师晋级香港比赛
summary: 香港 九名决赛选手在香港2026年绿色可持续全电动烹饪比赛中晋级。 11月2日至21日期间，公众可以在JW万豪酒店品尝并投票选出他们最喜欢的菜肴。比赛推广低碳烹饪技术和食材，推动香港朝着 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 17 日， 10:04 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 九名决赛入围者已进入 2026 Gr 的公众投票阶段
content:
香港
九名决赛选手在香港2026年绿色可持续全电动烹饪比赛中晋级。 11月2日至21日期间，公众可以在JW万豪酒店品尝并投票选出他们最喜欢的菜肴。比赛推广低碳烹饪技术和食材，推动香港迈向低碳生活

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 17 日，香港时间 10:04 · 阅读 2 分钟

主办方表示，经过厨师和业余厨师在第一轮测试低碳烹饪技术后，9名决赛入围者已进入2026年绿色可持续全电烹饪大赛的公众投票阶段。

此次比赛由中国香港女厨师协会和香港国际烹饪艺术协会主办，在国际烹饪学院举行。参赛者在青年厨师、业余厨师和专业厨师三个类别中进行角逐，使用全电动烹饪设备和当地食材制作菜肴，并根据味道、摆盘、营养、可持续性、创造力和烹饪技术进行评估。

每个类别的前三名选手被选出进入下一阶段。他们的菜肴种类繁多，从环保家禽三重奏和惠灵顿鸭，到釉面猪肉、四川风味虾菜和醋鱼子酱熏鳕鱼。
比赛还鼓励参赛者减少食物浪费，充分利用食材，将节能减碳理念融入烹饪中。渔农自然护理署旗下的“港丰”品牌的食用花卉是指定成分之一。

中国香港女厨师协会的成员首次参加比赛，在公开组和专业组的六个奖项中赢得了四个奖项，每个类别获得两个奖项。商务及经济发展局副局长陈百里表示，这项比赛汇聚了创新科技、可持续发展和低碳烹饪，推动香港努力实现2050年前的碳中和目标。

中国香港女厨师协会创会主席萧凯蒂表示，整体水平超出了她的预期，尤其是年轻和业余参赛者。 “专业组的菜品超乎专业，不仅展现了强大的厨艺和创意，而且在食材的选择和烹饪过程中也融入了环保理念。”萧说。
她希望比赛能增强参赛者对餐饮业的信心，并鼓励业界和公众了解低碳烹饪的好处，将绿色饮食习惯融入日常生活。萧女士还鼓励参赛者多参加烹饪比赛，积累经验，树立信心。九款入围菜肴将于 11 月 2 日至 21 日在香港 JW 万豪酒店的酒廊供应，让食客品尝参赛菜肴并投票选出他们最喜欢的绿色和可持续菜肴。

Hong Kong
Nine finalists have advanced in Hong Kong's 2026 Green & Sustainable All-Electric Cooking Competition. The public can taste and vote for their favourite dishes at JW Marriott Hotel from 2 to 21 November. The competition promotes low-carbon cooking techniques and ingredients as Hong Kong works toward

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

17 Oct 2026 at 10:04 HKT · 2 min read

Nine finalists have advanced to the public voting stage of the 2026 Green & Sustainable All-Electric Cooking Competition after chefs and amateur cooks put low-carbon cooking techniques to the test in the first round, the organisers said.

The competition, organised by the Hong Kong China Women Chefs Association and the Hong Kong International Culinary Arts Association, was held at the International Culinary Institute. Contestants competed in young chef, amateur cook and professional chef categories, using all-electric cooking equipment and local ingredients to create dishes assessed on taste, presentation, nutrition, sustainability, creativity and cooking techniques.

The top three contestants from each category were selected for the next stage. Their dishes range from an eco-friendly poultry trio and duck Wellington to glazed pork, Sichuan-style prawn creations and smoked cod with vinegar caviar.

The competition also encouraged contestants to reduce food waste, make fuller use of ingredients and incorporate energy-saving and carbon-reduction concepts into their cooking. Edible flowers under the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department's Hong Kong Harvest brand were among the designated ingredients.

Members of the Hong Kong China Women Chefs Association entered the competition for the first time and won four of six awards across the open and professional divisions, taking two awards in each category. Under Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Bernard Chan Pak-li said the competition brought together innovation and technology, sustainable development and low-carbon cooking as Hong Kong works toward its carbon-neutrality target before 2050.

Hong Kong China Women Chefs Association founding president Chef Kitty Siu said the overall standard had exceeded her expectations, particularly among younger and amateur contestants. "The professional group's dishes were beyond professional. They not only demonstrated strong culinary skills and creativity, but also incorporated environmental concepts into their choice of ingredients and cooking processes," Siu said.

She said she hoped the competition would strengthen participants' confidence in the catering industry and encourage both the trade and the public to understand the benefits of low-carbon cooking and incorporate greener eating habits into everyday life. Siu also encouraged contestants to take part in more culinary competitions to gain experience and build confidence. The nine finalist dishes will next be served at The Lounge at JW Marriott Hotel Hong Kong from 2 to 21 November, allowing diners to taste the entries and vote for their favourite green and sustainable dish.

title: 20 conservation interns face one remaining obstacle
summary: Only one barrier stands in the way of 20 young and passionate environmentalists’ dreams of joining the ranks of South Africa’s dedicated conservationists and becoming stewards of South Africa’s diverse ecosystems. Laptops. The recent gradua
content:
Only one barrier stands in the way of 20 young and passionate environmentalists’ dreams of joining the ranks of South Africa’s dedicated conservationists and becoming stewards of South Africa’s diverse ecosystems.

Laptops.

The recent graduates are part of a 12-month placement programme with Nature Connect, a Cape Town-based NGO that connects people with nature, trains young people for green jobs and supports community-led conservation projects.

Nature Connect’s new cohort of interns were inducted into the job placement on Thursday, 8 October 2026. (Photo: Nature Connect)

Each of the 20 graduates holds a conservation qualification and, through the internship, will gain access to what they need to turn that qualification into a career: a mentor who knows the sector and on-the-ground practical experience. They only lack the tools needed to do the work.

“Nature Connect is asking individuals, businesses and institutions in South Africa to donate working laptops so that every intern has one,” the organisation said in a media statement.

### **The need for trained conservationists in SA**

South Africa is one of only 17 megadiverse countries in the world, ranking in the top 10 globally for plant species richness and third for marine species endemism. But like the rest of the world, the country’s biodiversity is deteriorating.

According to the South African National Biodiversity Institute’s (Sanbi’s) latest biodiversity assessment, 986 ecosystem types assessed in the country were under threat.

The report found that:

*   More than half of all assessed species were of concern, with the most fragile being freshwater and cartilaginous species.

*   Estuaries, rivers and wetlands were the most threatened and least protected, a critical concern for a water-scarce country.

*   Both ecosystem (terrestrial biomes) and species (species groups) Red List Indexes showed declining trends, indicating increasing threat levels.

Speaking to Daily Maverick, Nature Connect CEO Dr Anthony Roberts said that to protect that nation’s biodiversity, South Africa needed more trained conservationists working on the ground.

“There are numerous environmental challenges we’re facing across the country, from rural to urban challenges, but at the same time, funding for conservation in the country is very low. We’re dealing with a lot of social and economic challenges in the country, but we also need to find the justification space within that to support nature conservation as well,” Roberts said.

Nature Connect CEO Anthony Roberts says South Africa needs more conservationists to protect ecosystems and provide vital services like water management and pollution and climate mitigation. (Photo: Nature Connect)

Roberts added that interns in the programme had already done the hard work of completing their studies and finding their first job opportunities. They just need the right tools to get them past the finish line.

### **Nature Connect trains young conservationists**

The placement programme is made possible through a decade-long partnership between the NGO and CATHSSETA (Culture, Arts, Tourism, Hospitality and Sport Sector Education and Training Authority). The partnership has resulted in the placement of 198 graduate interns since 2016. However, Roberts said the CATHSSETA funding mainly covered stipends, which graduates mostly used for transport.

Over the course of the year, the conservation interns will work in schools, on nature camps, in training programmes, at urban conservation sites and with partner organisations across Cape Town.

From Nature Connect’s side, buying laptops for the interns is not feasible at the moment because the expense would divert funds from the organisation’s other beneficiaries and projects.

The laptops are a necessity for the interns. Without the tools, the graduates’ work – which, in addition to fieldwork, requires computer-based research, keeping daily timesheets, writing monthly logbooks and developing a portfolio of evidence that counts towards the completion of the internship – will be hindered.

Recent graduates Cheynne Williams and Tina Msutwana are part of the 2026/27 cohort of Nature Connect’s internship programme.

“I didn’t really know what conservation is and what protecting the environment is about. I was always surrounded by buildings and growing up in the townships. Nature is something that is there, but you are not really familiar with it, what it is and why it is important for us,” said Cape Peninsula Technical University graduate Msutwana.

Tina Msutwana, a graduate from Cape Peninsula University of Technology, is one of the 20 graduates who are part of Nature Connect’s conservation internship. (Photo: Nature Connect)

Msutwana added that her love for conservation and the environment grew as she went deeper into her studies.

For Williams, a University of the Western Cape graduate, her love for the environment started when she was a child and only grew as she did.

“My childhood sparked an interest that grew up with me as I went to university. When I got into university at UWC, I was like, okay, biodiversity conservation, first year, let’s do this,” Williams said.

Cheynne Williams, a graduate from the University of the Western Cape, is one of the 20 graduates who are part of Nature Connect’s conservation internship. (Photo: Nature Connect)

Currently working on the sustainable schools programme, Williams and Msutwana are passionate about supporting teachers to educate learners on environmental sustainability, hoping to spark interest in future conservationists.

Roberts said the organisation was looking for working laptops with a charger, ideally less than three years old.

“Every device will be securely wiped before it is issued and recorded on the organisation’s asset register, and donors will be thanked by name where they are happy to be,” the organisation assured. **DM**

**How to donate**

_Laptops can be dropped off or delivered at the following address:_

_Nature Connect, Unit 3B, Tokai On Main Office Park, 2 Burchell Street, Tokai,Cape Town, 7966_

content:
欧盟领导人正在考虑制定一项新的贸易管控工具，当某个外国公司的产品可能在欧盟泛滥成灾并对欧盟经济造成严重冲击之际，可以运用这一工具，迅速将这家公司踢出欧盟市场。

彭博社星期四(10月15日)报道说，欧盟已决定推动建立一项贸易应对机制，该机制有权完全阻止中国等地的外国制造产品进入欧盟单一市场。

《南华早报》援引知情消息人士的话说，欧盟委员会主席乌尔苏拉·冯德莱恩(Ursula von der Leyen)星期四在在欧盟委员会一场会议的开场致辞中提出了这一被称为“死亡开关”(kill switch)的方案。

这一方案有可能让欧盟在应对与中国的贸易争端时，除了关税和其他贸易限制等手段之外，又掌握一个威力巨大的新武器。

报道说，这表明欧盟委员会的贸易团队可能会着手开发该这一贸易工具。不过有关该工具的具体设计、适用范围及使用条件目前都尚未确定。

美国之音向欧盟委员会发言人办公室发出置评请求，但截至发稿前，还未收到回应。

彭博社报道说，欧盟领导人在比利时布鲁塞尔举行的峰会上讨论了新的贸易工具的问题，并要求欧盟委员会在年底前制定相关措施。此举旨在使欧盟能够在极端情况下——例如当中国等竞争对手冲击欧盟经济时——通过彻底关闭欧盟市场来做出回应。

近年来，布鲁塞尔常常为与中国的贸易失衡而伤脑筋。

欧盟2025年从中国进口了价值5594亿欧元的商品，而对华出口总额仅为1996亿欧元，由此产生了3598亿欧元的贸易逆差。

与2024年相比，欧盟自中国进口的商品增长了6.4%，而对中国的出口则下降了6.5%。

欧洲制造商日益担忧来自中国同行的激烈竞争，这种竞争波及汽车、化工和机械等多个行业。中国企业凭借成本优势和强大的制造能力占据上风，而欧洲企业则在市场份额、盈利能力和就业岗位方面面临压力，甚至节节败退。

欧盟过去在与中国发生贸易争端时，通常把重点放在推动中国对欧洲开放市场之上，也就是通过增加对中国的出口来平衡双边的贸易。但是这一策略收效甚微。欧盟产品进入中国市场增速缓慢，而中国产品涌入欧洲市场的势头极为迅猛。

因此，欧盟对华贸易谈判的策略发生了变化，从施压北京开放市场，转变成限制中国厂家和商品进入欧盟市场，从而对欧盟的制造商提供保护。德国过去对欧盟限制中国商品的举措反应审慎，因为担心德国的对华出口会受到波及。不过现在德国的态度也已经改变，常常强烈主张限制中国商品进入欧盟市场。

所谓“死亡开关”措施，在一定程度上是德国与法国共同推动的结果。

与此同时，欧盟并未放弃与中国通过谈判化解分歧。10月9日，中国商务部长王文涛和欧盟贸易与经济安全专员马罗什·谢夫乔维奇(Maros Sefcovic)在北京经过历时两天的谈判后达成共识，在未来四年内将中国向欧盟出口的混合动力和插电式混合动力汽车数量减少一半以上，年度最高数量为35万辆。

有分析指出，中欧如果没有达成这一共识，中国今年向欧盟出口的混合动力和插电式混合动力汽车数量就有可能突破80万辆。

谢夫乔维奇当时表示，中欧达成的这项“共同谅解”只是贸易再平衡的“关键第一步”。布鲁塞尔目前酝酿的“死亡开关”可能就是欧盟的后续安排。

立陶宛总统吉塔纳斯·瑙塞达(Gitanas Nausėda)星期四会后向记者表示，“如果中国采取某些不公平贸易做法，我们可以限制中国产品进入欧洲市场，甚至彻底关闭欧洲市场。”

针对欧盟峰会酝酿的“死亡开关”措施，中国商务部发言人以答记者问的方式作出回应，呼吁欧盟打消“以施压换取好处”的幻想。

“中欧经贸磋商的目的就是要通过对话协商妥处分歧，照顾彼此关切。双方都要拿出解决问题的诚意，”中国商务部发言人说。“欧方不能幻想以施压换取好处，更不要低估中方维护自身利益的决心和能力。”
