content:
下载全文 PDF 台湾积体电路制造公司 (TSMC，台湾积体电路制造公司) 生产 90% 以上的先进芯片，为人工智能开发提供动力，显着提升了台湾在全球事务中的战略重要性。近年来，认知影响力行动仍然加剧了许多台湾老年人的担忧，担心台积电的海外扩张可能会损害台湾的经济利益、战略影响力和才华横溢的工程师。然而，像我这样的台湾年轻人可能会认为这些担忧被夸大了。台积电一再强调，其最先进的研发能力将留在台湾，台湾将继续作为公司技术开发和全球生产网络的核心。台湾人不应该担心台积电在美国扩大生产，主要有以下三个原因。首先，此次扩张使台积电能够更好地服务美国领先客户并增加其商机。其次，将生产从台湾转移出去有助于减少环境压力和地缘政治风险，并增强半导体供应链的稳定性。最后，台积电的国际发展计划增强了台湾的全球影响力，并加强了与世界各地合作伙伴的联系。
市场准入、政府补贴和下游供应链效益尽管人们对台积电在美国工厂建造和生产半导体的高成本存在合理的担忧，但值得承认这项活动的长期好处：使台积电能够更快地接触全球客户。尽管在海外建立业务需要更高的成本，但这种扩张在财务上已被证明是可行的，正如台积电亚利桑那州所证明的那样。仅 2025 年，亚利桑那州晶圆厂的净利润就达到新台币 42.​​32 亿元（1.358 亿美元），乍一看似乎是全年数据，但实际上仅在一个季度内就实现了这一收入。台积电亚利桑那州取得成功的关键原因之一是全球芯片市场的变化。美国主要依赖台湾制造尖端逻辑芯片。通过在美国建设更多晶圆厂，台积电能够更好地满足其主要客户的产能需求，其中包括AMD、苹果、英伟达和高通等美国公司。这可以实现更快、更个性化的客户服务，从而与大公司建立信任和亲和力，并鼓励他们将来从台积电购买产品。除了贴近客户之外，美国政府还积极利用立法来鼓励半导体公司在国内建设。
美国商务部根据 CHIPS 和科学法案向台积电提供 66 亿美元的直接拨款资金，并获得 50 亿美元的低息联邦贷款。这笔资金有助于抵消美国比台湾更高的建设和运营成本。此外，台积电在美国的扩张不仅建立了跨行业联系，还为长春集团和三立化学等台湾重要供应商在美国运营铺平了道路，从而推动了广泛的芯片生态系统。当这些主力晶圆厂搬迁到新的土地时，整个材料供应网络也随之移动，从而带来更多的商机。通过授权这些供应商扩展到全球市场，此类行动最终会改变

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Producing more than 90 percent of the advanced chips powering AI development, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC, 台灣積體電路製造公司) has significantly elevated Taiwan’s strategic importance in global affairs. In recent years, cognitive influence operations have nonetheless fueled fears among many older Taiwanese that TSMC’s overseas expansion could cost Taiwan economic benefits, strategic leverage, and talented engineers. Younger Taiwanese like myself, however, may see these concerns as overstated. TSMC has repeatedly emphasized that its most advanced research and development (R&D) capabilities will remain in Taiwan, and that the island will continue to serve as the heart of the company’s technology development and global production network. Taiwanese should not be concerned about TSMC expanding its production in the United States for three main reasons. Firstly, this expansion allows TSMC to better serve leading-edge US customers and grow its business opportunities. Secondly, diversifying production away from Taiwan helps reduce environmental strains and geopolitical risks, and strengthens the stability of the semiconductor supply chain. Finally, TSMC’s international development plans enhance Taiwan’s global presence and strengthen connections with partners around the world. Market Access, Government Subsidies, and Downstream Supply Chain Benefits Although there are valid concerns about the high cost of building and producing semiconductors at TSMC facilities in the United States, it is worth acknowledging the long-term benefit of this activity: providing TSMC with quicker access to customers worldwide. Even though establishing operations abroad entails higher costs, this expansion has proven financially viable, as demonstrated by TSMC Arizona. In 2025 alone, the Arizona fab recorded a net income of NTD 4.232 billion (USD 135.8 million) —income that, at first glance, may appear to have been full-year data, but was actually made in just one quarter. One key reason why TSMC Arizona has been successful has been changes in the global market for chips. The United States relies primarily on Taiwan for the fabrication of leading-edge logic chips. By building more fabs in the United States, TSMC is better able to satisfy the capacity demands of its key customers, including American companies such as AMD, Apple, Nvidia, and Qualcomm, among others. This enables faster, more personalized customer service, which builds trust and affinity with large companies and encourages them to buy from TSMC in the future. Beyond customer proximity, the United States government has actively employed legislation to encourage semiconductor companies to build domestically. The US Department of Commerce has awarded TSMC USD 6.6 billion in direct grant funding under the CHIPS and Science Act , along with access to USD 5 billion in low-interest federal loans. This funding helps offset the higher costs of construction and operation in the US compared to Taiwan. Furthermore, TSMC’s American expansion not only builds cross-industry connections, but it also drives a broad chip ecosystem by paving the way for critical Taiwanese suppliers such as the Chang Chun Group and Sunlit Chemical to operate in the United States. When these anchor fabs move to new land, the entire material supply network also moves with them, leading to more business opportunities. By empowering these suppliers to expand into global markets, such actions ultimately transfer international investment back into Taiwan’s domestic economy. Therefore, continued expansion in the United States represents a strategic investment in TSMC’s long-term financial future. Image: TSMC Fab 21 under construction in Phoenix, Arizona (November 2023). (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) Environmental Risks and Geopolitics In order to maintain satisfying relationships with customers, TSMC must operate a stable and unbroken semiconductor production line. Some Taiwanese believe that this stability can be maintained at home, yet growing environmental risks and geopolitical realities indicate that relying on production in Taiwan alone is increasingly fragile. Within this context, TSMC’s expansion to the United States can help maintain a stable semiconductor production line. As TSMC continues to expand its production capacity, Taiwan is gradually reaching the limits of its environmental carrying capacity. Semiconductor fabs consume vast amounts of water and electricity. Building more and more fabs in Taiwan will put too much pressure on the power grid. Increasing load will risk energy shortages and infrastructure strain, thus destabilizing production lines not only for TSMC but also for other businesses in Taiwan. By contrast, locations for TSMC’s expansion, such as Arizona, possess far more abundant resources. Arizona has one of the biggest energy grids in the United States, operating over 6,551 megawatts (MW) of installed solar capacity alongside nearly 3,900 megawatts (MW) of battery energy storage systems. Beyond electricity, water is also essential for the semiconductor industry; a single advanced chip factory can consume up to 38 million liters of water per day (an amount approximately equivalent to the daily water usage of a medium-sized city). As a small island with finite resources, Taiwan simply lacks the physical capacity to sustain such immense environmental pressure. Crowding the nation with dozens of new factories would push its fragile water supply to a dangerous breaking point, placing a burden on the everyday lives of Taiwanese citizens. Moreover, an earthquake that hit eastern Taiwan in 2024 caused TSMC factories in Tainan to shut down temporarily, as chip fabs are designed to automatically cease production when any tremors occur. For instance, EUV chipmaking machines possess sensors that detect infinitesimal movements that cannot be noticed by humans; if the EUV machine senses the floor moving, it will shut down completely. Indeed, continuing to print during tremors can blur the circuit lines and potentially result in significant financial losses as wafers must be discarded. Hence, moving factories to locations like Arizona helps mitigate natural disaster risks such as earthquakes and provides a more controllable environment, rendering chip production lines more efficient. Given the relative availability of land, water, and electrical resources in North America, building factories in the United States may ultimately be beneficial for maintaining the stability of the Taiwanese production lines. By expanding its manufacturing capacity overseas, TSMC can reduce its exposure to geopolitical risks – and, in the event of war, help sustain the industrial capacity of the “arsenal of democracy.” For more than seven decades , Taiwan has faced persistent tensions across the Taiwan Strait, which have intensified in recent years and created significant geopolitical uncertainty. A war in the Taiwan Strait could severely disrupt global semiconductor supply chains, triggering shortages of advanced chips and inflicting trillions of dollars in economic losses worldwide. If key fabs in Taiwan are damaged or destroyed, rebuilding the lost production capacity could take years. By expanding its manufacturing capacity into the United States, TSMC can help key geopolitical partners like America maintain access to chips during wartime situations. Soft Power and Continuity Many Taiwanese argue that TSMC is the “ silicon shield ” protecting Taiwan against China. Therefore, they claim that the protection of this shield would be forfeited should TSMC build more factories in the United States. However, I believe TSMC’s global expansion can also help Taiwan garner greater international recognition by building stronger connections with local communities overseas. One example is the collaboration between Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing (JASM) and the TSMC Education and Culture Foundation, which brought Taiwan’s OneSong Orchestra to Kumamoto for a cultural concert . When locals connect with Taiwanese culture through these activities, it transforms Taiwan from an unfamiliar chip supplier into a culturally rich nation that bonds with local communities on a personal level. Such community bonds naturally encourage local communities to support strong diplomatic ties between their government and that of Taiwan. Additionally, these community investments extend into classrooms, where local universities partner with TSMC to build a new generation of semiconductor professionals who have been trained through Taiwanese resources. In the context of Japan, cultural exchanges between TSMC and the local community not only strengthen the company’s ties with Kumamoto residents, but also help build public support for its overseas expansion. In this sense, TSMC’s overseas expansion does more than diversify production—it can also expand Taiwan’s international presence and strengthen its ties with key partners around the world. Many Taiwanese refer to TSMC as the nation’s “Guardian Mountain” (護國神山) because of its crucial role in safeguarding Taiwan’s economic prosperity and national security. TSMC’s global expansion can strengthen the resilience of the semiconductor supply chain, bring production closer to its customers, expand its business opportunities, create new possibilities for young Taiwanese, and enhance Taiwan’s international presence. Some Taiwanese elders may worry that sending engineers to the United States represents a loss of human resources for Taiwan. However, these Taiwanese engineers are not abandoning Taiwan. Instead, they are stepping into global leadership roles and establishing important cross-border industry networks. When these professionals eventually return to Taiwan, they will be able to train the next generation of engineers preparing to go overseas and advance Taiwan’s economic prosperity. Expanding into the United States, therefore, does not mark the end of TSMC’s role as Taiwan’s “Guardian Mountain.” Rather, it is a pragmatic step toward ensuring that TSMC can continue to fulfill that role in a rapidly changing world. One Youth’s Perspective As a junior in the International Bilingual School at Hsinchu-Science-Park, many of my classmates’ parents are employed at TSMC. Drawing inspiration from their parents, some have also decided to pursue a career at TSMC. The establishment of TSMC Arizona has encouraged even more of them to pursue this track, and many of my peers are excited about the new job opportunities abroad that have been created. Indeed, these new job opportunities appeal to Taiwanese teenagers who had never yet been able to imagine their part in the “American Dream.” Ironically, according to a 2024 ABC News/Ipsos survey of US adults, public confidence in the American Dream has significantly eroded. Yet, new TSMC subsidiaries in the United States not only stabilize the production chain but also help revive the long-faded “American Dream” for Taiwanese youth. The main point: While many commentators in Taiwan suggest that TSMC’s expansion to the United States weakens Taiwan’s economic and national security, the business decisions may actually prove more economically viable, and relieve pressure on Taiwan’s grid and water supply. Meanwhile, the opportunities to work in the United States revive the long-faded “American Dream” among Taiwanese youth. The post A Taiwanese Youth’s Perspective: TSMC’s US Expansion and the American Dream appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

律政司司长林定国周一启程前往文莱出席第十六届中国-东盟检察长会议，会上将探讨如何保障数码时代的儿童。他将讨论跨境合作打击针对青少年的网络犯罪，并介绍香港的经验

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 19 日 16:53 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

文莱政府宣布，律政司司长林定国周一下午启程前往文莱，出席第十六届中国-东盟检察长会议及相关区域会议。

林郑月娥作为中国官方代表团的一员出席此次高级别会议，并计划在一场致力于保护数字时代儿童的全体会议上发表讲话。他与东南亚国家联盟成员国代表的讨论将集中于加强国际合作，应对针对青少年的网络犯罪威胁。
此次访问之际，人们越来越担心影响全球年轻人的数字威胁。技术的快速进步为年轻人创造了广泛的发展机会，但同时也带来了前所未有的安全风险，特别是未经同意的亲密图像传播和深度换脸技术的滥用。由于针对儿童的非法在线活动很容易跨越国界，区域执法和司法机构认为跨境伙伴关系至关重要。

在会议期间，林郑月娥将介绍香港现有的旨在保护儿童免受网络伤害的法律架构，同时概述该市未来旨在应对新兴数字危险的政策措施和监管举措。除全体会议外，林郑月娥还将与中国代表团成员和东盟官员一起参加双边讨论，以扩大相互交流并促进跨司法管辖区更紧密的工作关系。

陪同林郑月娥正式出访的有刑事检控专员周天行及数名政府律师。律政司司长预计于10月23日结束任期返港。在他缺席期间，律政司副秘书长张国钧代理律政司司长。

He will discuss cross-border cooperation against cybercrime targeting youth and present Hong Kong's le

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 16:53 HKT · 2 min read

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam Ting-kwok departed for Brunei on Monday afternoon to participate in the 16th China-ASEAN Prosecutors-General Conference and related regional meetings, the government announced.

Lam is attending the high-level gathering as part of the official Chinese delegation, where he is scheduled to address a plenary session dedicated to safeguarding children in the digital era. His discussions with representatives from member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations will centre on strengthening international collaboration to counter cybercrime threats directed at youth.

The visit comes amid growing concern over digital threats affecting young people globally. While rapid technological progress has created extensive developmental opportunities for youth, it has simultaneously introduced unprecedented safety risks, notably the non-consensual distribution of intimate images and the misuse of deepfake technology. Because illicit online activities targeting children easily cross national borders, regional law enforcement and judicial bodies view cross-border partnerships as critical.

During the conference, Lam will present Hong Kong's existing legal architecture designed to shield children from online harms, while outlining the city's future policy measures and regulatory initiatives aimed at tackling emerging digital dangers. In addition to the plenary sessions, Lam will join bilateral discussions alongside members of the Chinese delegation and ASEAN officials to broaden mutual exchanges and foster closer working relationships across legal jurisdictions.

Lam is accompanied on the official trip by Director of Public Prosecutions Anthony Chau Tin-hang and several government counsel. The justice secretary is scheduled to wrap up his engagements and return to Hong Kong on October 23. During his absence, Deputy Secretary for Justice Horace Cheung Kwok-kwan is assuming the role of acting secretary for justice.

title: China’s Rise and Central Asia: What Will Next Ten Years Look Like?
summary: For much of my time as a journalist, the story of China’s rise has come with a familiar undertone of alarm. China is either becoming the next great global power, challenging the West, rewriting the rules of international politics or quietly
content:
For much of my time as a journalist, the story of China’s rise has come with a familiar undertone of alarm. China is either becoming the next great global power, challenging the West, rewriting the rules of international politics or quietly building a parallel system that the rest of the world will eventually have to adapt to. All of these arguments have some basis. But I sometimes wonder whether we make the China story too simple, especially from Central Asia, where China is not some distant geopolitical competitor, but a country next door, a major trading partner and an increasingly visible part of our economic landscape.

Jiyang Dong. Photo credit: Nazarbayev University

So I wanted to ask a broader question: if China continues to gain economic and geopolitical weight over the next 10 years, what will that power actually look like by 2035, and what will it mean for Central Asia? I spoke to several experts and their answers were more nuanced than the usual China-versus-the-West narrative. The most interesting conclusion was not that China will necessarily replace the existing international order. It may not have to.

**China may reshape the order without replacing it**

Jiyang Dong, assistant professor at Nazarbayev University’s Graduate School of Business, made a point that immediately shifted the question for me. “Ironically, the key variables impacting China’s future role in the international system are not necessarily within China,” he said.

China’s policies, he said, are already laid out in successive five-year plans and implemented with consistency. What matters just as much is what happens elsewhere: whether the United States (U.S.) continues to retreat from multilateralism and whether institutions such as the World Bank and IMF continue to meet the development needs of the Global South.

If they do not, Dong believes, institutions in which China plays a central role could gradually become more important. He points to the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank as one example. That means China’s rise may not depend entirely on Beijing building a new system from scratch. It may also depend on whether existing institutions leave enough space for China and other emerging powers to build something alongside them.

> Gulnar Shaimergenova, director of the China Studies Center in Kazakhstan, sees the process in similar terms. “I would rather speak not about the creation by China of a completely alternative world order, but about an attempt to change the balance and rules within the existing international system,” she said.

By 2035, she expects a more polycentric system in which China becomes one of the key centers of economic, technological and political influence. The real question, she said, is not whether one world order will simply replace another, but which institutions and norms will adapt to the new balance of power.

Ken-Moriyasu-Hudson. Photo credit: nationalinterest.org

Deputy Chairman of the Institute of Foreign Policy Studies under Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs Amangeldy Tazhenov reaches a similar conclusion. China, he said, is not trying to “break” the existing system. It is pushing for its transformation and reform so that it better reflects current realities and the changing distribution of power.

But Ken Moriyasu, a senior fellow at Hudson Institute, offered a sharper interpretation of the same trend. For much of the post-Deng Xiaoping era, he noted, China largely adapted to an international system shaped by Western powers. Under Xi Jinping, the ambition is different.

“It is less about reforming China to fit the existing order and more about changing the order to fit China,” Moriyasu said.

At the same time, he cautions against assuming Beijing is confident it can simply build the order it wants. China also knows that its rise generates resistance and suspicion. That, he said, helps explain why Beijing continues to emphasize the UN and existing institutions while simultaneously promoting BRICS, the SCO and a more multipolar system.

> “Beijing will preserve institutions that reinforce China’s status, seek to reshape institutions where Western influence remains predominant, and simultaneously build organizations, relationships and economic networks that give Beijing alternatives,” he said.

I find that distinction more useful than the familiar question of whether China is trying to become “the next U.S.” Perhaps China does not need to replace the system. It may simply need to become powerful enough to change the way the system works around it.

**Central Asia is becoming more important for a different reason**

Amangeldy Tazhenov. Photo credit: sszi.kz

This is where the discussion becomes more interesting for Central Asia. For years, China’s relationship with the region was discussed largely through the familiar vocabulary of trade, energy, resources and transport corridors. Those things still matter. But the strategic logic appears to be changing. Moriyasu calls the emerging logic “strategic resilience.” Much of China’s trade and energy still moves through maritime routes exposed to American naval power. Central Asia gives Beijing something the South China Sea cannot: a vast continental hinterland connecting China westward across Eurasia. “Central Asia matters to Beijing not only because of the energy, minerals and markets within Central Asia, but increasingly because of what lies beyond it. It connects China westward across the Eurasian landmass,” he said.

His forecast is striking: “I would expect Central Asia to move from China’s economic periphery toward the strategic center of China’s relationship with Eurasia.”

That changes the question because Central Asia’s value for China is no longer simply what Beijing can obtain from the region. It is also what the region allows China to reach. Jiyang Dong approaches this from a more economic perspective. “Central Asia’s greatest strategic significance hinges on its potential as a connectivity hub in the heart of Eurasia,” he said.

Without sufficient connectivity infrastructure, he notes, trade volumes remain limited, and resources remain effectively locked in the region. That is why projects such as the[expansion](https://astanatimes.com/2026/07/kazakhstan-uzbekistan-expand-strategic-partnership-through-trade-transport-and-regional-agreements/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) of the Aktau container hub and the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway matter beyond their immediate economic purpose. They are helping turn Central Asia’s geography into an asset. Perhaps this is where we should stop thinking of infrastructure simply as infrastructure.

**Infrastructure may be the new geopolitics**

Moriyasu said something that stayed with me: “Infrastructure becomes the new hinge of geopolitics.”

> “Once trade routes, pipelines, power grids and supply chains are built around particular networks, they begin to shape the economic choices available to countries using them,” Moriyasu said.

That is a much more subtle form of power than the geopolitics I grew up reading about. There is no flag going up. No alliance is announced. No military base appears. But the network changes. And once a country’s trade, logistics, power systems, digital infrastructure or industrial supply chains are deeply embedded in a particular network, those connections can begin shaping the choices available to it. This is also where my own perception of China has changed.

It is difficult to ignore the efficiency of some of the infrastructure projects I see around me. The LRT in Astana is a very concrete example. Whatever one’s broader political view of China may be, a functioning project creates a different impression than a political speech or diplomatic statement. This is where infrastructure can begin to operate as soft power. Not necessarily because Beijing tells people to admire China, but because people encounter its capabilities in practical ways: a railway, a road or a technology. Over time, that can produce something harder to measure but politically significant: familiarity, respect and, potentially, a certain degree of loyalty.

Tazhenov described China’s approach in similarly long-term terms, noting that Beijing tends to think in much longer horizons than many other countries. He also pointed to the growing visibility of Chinese economic activity in Kazakhstan: from infrastructure and roads to new enterprises and resource projects. That matters because soft power is usually discussed in terms of culture, education or films. Perhaps in the next decade, we will have to add infrastructure to that list.

**The next phase may be about technology, not concrete**

This is where the forecasts become even more interesting. Shaimergenova believes the development most underestimated today is the transition from physical infrastructure connectivity to technological and institutional connectivity. A few years ago, the China conversation in Central Asia focused on roads, railways, pipelines and energy. Today, she notes, the agenda increasingly includes AI, digital infrastructure, green technologies and critical minerals.

> “Central Asia will be not only a territory through which flows between China and Europe pass, but increasingly a space where different technological, production and regulatory systems will intersect,” she said.

That is probably the part of the China story that deserves more attention. Dong sees another underestimated area: cooperation in non-fossil energy. Solar panels, wind turbines, energy storage, flexible grids and nuclear power could all become increasingly important as Central Asian economies grow and demand more electricity. In other words, China’s future role in Central Asia may be less about simply connecting the region to China and more about helping shape the systems through which the region itself develops.

**More China: more choices, or fewer?**

This is where the experts stop agreeing. Dong sees growing competition among major powers as potentially useful for Kazakhstan because it creates more room to advance national interests through different partners and financial systems.

Shaimergenova is more cautious. “The strengthening of competition among major powers provides Kazakhstan with additional opportunities for investment, technology, transport projects and access to different markets. But at the same time, the risk increases that economic, technological and even logistical decisions will increasingly be viewed through the prism of geopolitical choice,” she said.

> Tazhenov is even more direct: “My opinion is that an aggravation of geopolitical rivalry is certainly unfavorable for Kazakhstan. It actually narrows the field for foreign policy maneuver.”

This may be the real paradox of the next decade. China’s rise can give Kazakhstan access to more capital, infrastructure, technology and markets. But if rivalry between China and the U.S. continues to harden, those same economic choices may increasingly be interpreted as political choices. The more interconnected Kazakhstan becomes with major external powers, the more important it is to remain capable of deciding where each connection leads.

**What we may be underestimating**

One idea kept returning throughout these conversations, even when the experts approached it from very different directions. It is not simply that China is becoming more present in Central Asia. The region and China are becoming more mutually interested in one another. Tazhenov believes this growing mutual interest, connectivity and economic complementarity is one of the least appreciated trends. For China, Central Asia offers transport routes, resources, energy and stability. For Kazakhstan and its neighbors, China increasingly offers markets, investment and technology. The relationship is therefore becoming more complicated than a simple story of a rising power expanding into a neighboring region.

It is also becoming a story of mutual dependence which is not automatically goo

content: 茉莉花评论 文 / 孔灵犀 西班牙人上街要求降租金、停止驱逐。限租能压低房租，可它多不出一套房，而西班牙缺的正是房子。纽约强制搬人要经法院，文中所引的中国两条规则讲提前通知：护着租客，和找得到房，是两回事。 10月3日，西班牙马德里、瓦伦西亚等城市举行了约50场住房游行，西班牙政府说，光是马德里就有约7万人上街。前一天，议会以178票对172票、184票对166票，否决了政府为平息抗议提出的两项法令，里面有把2028年前到期的租约延长两年。抗议者要求降租金、停止驱逐。可是，限租、延长租约这些办法，到底帮得了谁？ 我的看法是：限租能压低租金，短期内对已经住进去的人尤其有用，一些地方的新租约也设了上限；可限租多不出一套房，还在找房的年轻人租不租得到房，还要看新房建得够不够。纽约和中国正好可以对照：纽约有争议、没和解的驱逐案要由法官裁决，房东胜诉后签发驱逐令，中国下文的两条规则写的是提前通知；可在纽约，法律护着租客，租房照样难。 西班牙央行在2025年年报里算过：2021年到2025年，西班牙新建成的住房比新增的家庭少了约75万套。光是2025年，新增家庭就有24万户，新建成的住房只有9.2万套，缺口还在扩大。房子不够，租金就往上走：房产网站Idealista的统计显示，今年9月底，在西班牙租房每平方米要15.1欧元，比一年前贵5.6%。 央行把限租的好处和代价都说了：限租在短期内特别能减轻已签租约的租户的负担；可要是长期实行，房东的实际收入下降，投资出租房的劲头跟着下降，新出租的房子会比不限租时少。 纽约：强制搬人要经法院，空房却极少 纽约的法律尊重租客的权利：按规矩，把租客赶出门的只能是执行官或者警长，别人动手赶人，就是非法驱逐。纽约州的“正当理由驱逐”法（Good Cause Eviction）2024年4月20日生效，受这部法律保护的房子，房东没有正当理由不能结束租约，这部法律靠法院执行。美国宪法第十四修正案写着，各州不经正当法律程序，不得剥夺任何人的生命、自由或财产。在我看来，纽约这套先审后搬的程序，就是这条原则落在租房上的样子：租客的话要听，房东的诉求也要先由法官裁决。 一个驱逐案是这样走的：房东先向法院递交诉状，写明起诉的理由；案子先分到调解庭，法官要房东和租客谈着解决。租客的答辩，是向法院陈述抗辩理由和反诉；开庭日期可能改期；双方还可以提动议，请求法院采取某项行动。进入开庭审理的，双方当庭举证，由法官作出决定；房东胜诉的，法院判决房东有权让租客搬走，法官再签发驱逐令。房东雇执行官执行驱逐令的，执行官由市长任命；动手之前，接到驱逐令的官员还要至少提前14天书面通知租客。美国广播公司纽约台（ABC7）2024年11月的调查发现，纽约市的驱逐案平均要两年；房东们说，驱逐令至少要六个月才能执行。前者算整个案子，后者只是最后一步。案子拖成几年，部分原因是疫情以来法院积案多、资源有限，不全是程序要花的时间。ABC7报道的一位布朗克斯区房东，当了几十年护士，在法院打赢了官司，又等了一年多才等到法官签发驱逐令，到报道时还在等执行官去执行。这套程序两边都护着：租客不会被人直接赶出门，房东的权利也要经法官裁定、由官员落实；代价是慢，房东要等。 可在纽约找房一样难。纽约市住房保护与发展局2024年3月6日在市议会作证时说，2023年全市出租房的净空置率只有1.41%，供给跟不上需求。 中国：这两条规则靠提前通知保护租客 《民法典》第七百三十条规定，租期没有约定或者约定不明确，依据第五百一十条的规定仍不能确定的，视为不定期租赁，双方都可以随时解除合同，只要在合理期限之前通知对方。也就是说，依法算作不定期租赁的，房东在合理期限之前通知租客，就能解除合同，这一条没有要求房东说明理由，也没有要求房东先到法院起诉。2025年9月15日起施行的《住房租赁条例》加了一层保护：房东依法解除合同，要通知租客，给租客留出搬走的合理时间，不得用暴力、威胁或者其他非法方式逼租客解约、搬走。这两条保护租客的办法是提前通知和留出搬家时间，条文里没有先走法庭程序这一环，纽约那样要经法院裁决的程序，在这两条规则里找不到对应的东西。 三地比起来，西班牙和纽约相同的是缺房：西班牙新建成的住房赶不上新增的家庭，纽约空房极少。不同的是法律怎么护着租客：纽约靠法院走完程序，中国的这两条规则靠提前通知，西班牙连延长租约的法令都没通过。落到租房的人身上：在纽约，住进去的租客住得稳，想新租一套房的人却很难找到；在中国，依法算作不定期租赁的租客，房东在合理期限之前通知就能解除合同。 支持限租的人也有证据。西班牙央行说，加泰罗尼亚等地被定为住房紧张区的城镇，新租约的租金设了上限；央行引用的一项2023年的研究发现，加泰罗尼亚2020年到2021年的限租让租金下降了4%到6%，短期内没有减少出租房。我同意，限租能把租金压下来；可压低租金和多出房子是两回事，2025年西班牙新建成的住房，仍然赶不上新增的家庭。还在找房的年轻人要的，不只是一份便宜些的租约，而是先签得到一份租约。 所以我的答案是：限租帮得上已经住进去的人，可它补不上缺的房子；还在找房的年轻人租不租得到房，很大程度上要看新房建得够不够。对美国来说，要紧的是守住这套两边都护着的程序，同时多盖房，让空房多起来。 纽约的驱逐案，2024年的调查显示平均要两年；2023年全市出租房的净空置率，只有1.41%。法院的程序保得住已经住进去的人，保不住还在找房的人。 文中事实来自：BBC中文、路透社、西班牙央行2025年年报、Idealista、纽约市住房保护与发展局、美国广播公司纽约台、澎湃新闻政务号、司法部、美国国家档案馆、纽约州参议院、纽约房屋法庭解答中心

title: Chinese rental cars recorded military data during Norway exercise
zh_title: 中国租赁汽车在挪威演习期间记录军事数据
summary: 挪威中国士兵在奥斯陆机场进行安全演习时发现了中国制造的出租汽车内的摄像头录制的视频。这段视频捕捉到了军事设施的访问密码、路线和人员动向，引发了间谍活动的担忧。挪威家园卫队证实了这一发现，但可以 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 17 日 14:26 HKT · 2分钟读懂中国制造的租赁汽车在挪威期间记录敏感信息
content:
中国
挪威士兵在奥斯陆机场的一次安全演习中发现了中国制造的租赁汽车中摄像头录制的视频。这段视频捕捉到了军事设施的访问密码、路线和人员动向，引发了间谍活动的担忧。挪威国民警卫队证实了这一发现，但可能

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 17 日 14:26 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

据挪威报纸 Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) 报道，中国制造的租赁汽车在挪威军事演习期间记录了敏感信息，包括安全地点的访问代码和官员的出入，引发了人们对联网车辆带来的风险的担忧。

9 月 14 日至 18 日在奥斯陆机场举行的一次安全演习中，等候的士兵点击车辆屏幕发现了车载摄像机录制的视频。录音显示谁进出汽车、采取的路线，甚至用于打开军事设施大门或门的密码。

DN 表示，这些录音来自 Hertz Norge 向军队提供的租赁车辆，该公司间接由中国汽车集团吉利拥有。其中至少有两辆汽车是 Deepal 品牌的汽车，由中国国有汽车制造商长安汽车制造。
挪威国民警卫队发言人佩尔·古纳尔·格罗斯伯格豪根中校向法新社证实：“是的，国民警卫队的士兵发现了存储在他们系统中的车辆传感器的视频。”他表示，目前尚不清楚这些录音是否与第三方共享，尤其是在中国，但他不能排除这种可能性。

据 DN 报道，由于缺乏替代方案，军方继续使用这些车辆直到演习结束，士兵们删除了这些视频。军方表示，它更倾向于针对每个地点制定安全程序，可能会在当地禁止配备摄像头和传感器的车辆，无论其来源如何，认为全面禁止中国制造的车辆是不相称的。

Hertz Norge强调其遵守挪威和欧洲法规。该公司营销和传播总监 Hallvard Nerbovik 告诉法新社：“我们客户的数据在我们这里是安全的。” “没有明确的法律依据，我们不会与汽车制造商、我们的车主或其他第三方共享与我们租赁相关的个人数据。”他没有具体说明机上视频是否可能已被转移。长安集团没有回应法新社的提问。
挪威国家安全局（NSM）表示，现代车辆是“收集信息的滚动计算机”。 NSM 官员 Andreas Skjold-Lorange 告诉法新社：“我们不确定这些信息被发送到何处或用于什么用途。”他警告说，过度依赖单一国家的产品，尤其是不与挪威在安全问题上合作的国家，会使挪威变得脆弱。

China
Norwegian soldiers discovered videos recorded by cameras in Chinese-made rental cars during a security exercise at Oslo airport. The footage captured access codes, routes and personnel movements at military facilities, raising espionage concerns. Norway's Home Guard confirmed the findings but could

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

17 Oct 2026 at 14:26 HKT · 2 min read

Chinese-made rental cars recorded sensitive information during a Norwegian military exercise, including access codes at secure sites and officials' comings and goings, raising concerns about the risks posed by connected vehicles, Norwegian newspaper Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) reported.

During a security exercise at Oslo airport from 14 to 18 September, waiting soldiers tapping on a vehicle's screen discovered videos recorded by onboard cameras. The recordings showed who was getting in and out of the cars, the routes taken and even the codes used to open gates or doors to military facilities.

DN said the recordings came from rental vehicles supplied to the army by Hertz Norge, which is indirectly owned by the Chinese auto group Geely. At least two of the cars were Deepal brand vehicles, made by Chinese state-controlled automaker Changan.

"Yes, soldiers from the Home Guard found videos from the vehicles' sensors stored in their systems," Lieutenant Colonel Per Gunnar Grosberghaugen, Norwegian Home Guard spokesperson, confirmed to AFP. He said it was not known if the recordings were shared with a third party, notably in China, but he could not rule out the possibility.

The military continued to use the vehicles until the end of the exercise due to a lack of alternatives, and the soldiers deleted the videos, DN reported. The military said it preferred security procedures tailored to each site, with possible local bans on vehicles equipped with cameras and sensors regardless of their origin, judging that a general ban on Chinese-made vehicles would be disproportionate.

Hertz Norge stressed that it complies with Norwegian and European regulations. "Our customers' data is safe with us," Hallvard Nerbovik, its marketing and communications director, told AFP. "No personal data related to our rentals is shared with car manufacturers, our owners or other third parties without explicit legal grounds." He did not specify whether the onboard videos may have been transferred. Changan group did not respond to AFP's questions.

The Norwegian National Security Authority (NSM) said modern vehicles are "rolling computers that collect information". "We don't know for sure where the information is sent or what it's used for," NSM official Andreas Skjold-Lorange told AFP. He warned that excessive dependence on products from a single country, especially one that does not cooperate with Norway on security matters, makes Norway vulnerable.

title: 台湾拟收紧对中国芯片出口管制与美接轨，北京也宣布限制人工智能技术出口

content:
台湾经济部长龚明鑫在接受彭博社专访时表示，台湾准备收紧对中国人工智能(AI)芯片等尖端技术产品的出口管制，以便对焦美国政府对北京的芯片出口限制措施，与特朗普政府一道，联手打击将尖端半导体芯片走私到中国的行为。

彭博社星期五(10月16日)发表了这场在星期一进行的专访报道

台湾实际上已经对尖端半导体芯片出口中国实施了很多限制，并经常向出口商发出警告，提醒他们不要在对中方的出口业务中违反美国的法律或规定。但是赖清德政府尚未将未获授权的出口走私行为入罪。

根据台湾中央社的报道，龚明鑫在接受彭博社采访时表示，台湾准备将人工智能伺服器和尖端半导体纳入出口管制清单。一旦这些新的措施得以落实，未来向中国出口或走私受到管制的人工智能硬件，将会被依照“贸易法”追究刑事责任。

不过龚明鑫并未在受访时透露政府将在何时制定和实施新的出口限制措施。

“我们日后针对管制品相的部分措施将与美国保持一致，因为我们在《台美对等贸易协定》(ART)中作过相当程度的承诺，”中央社援引龚明鑫的话说。

台湾与美国今年2月12日签署一项对等贸易协定，美国把对从台湾进口的产品所征收的关税税率降低为15%，台湾方面则取消或减少99%的对美关税壁垒。

台湾行政院院长卓荣泰在协定签字后表示，台美谈判达成这项协定是“成功守护国家及产业利益，开启台美经贸及双边技术合作新页”。“双方承诺加强经济和国家安全合作，以增强供应链韧性，”伴随协定的事实清单指出。

中央社在报道中指出，一旦赖清德政府出台针对中国的新出口管制措施，这将标志着为维护台湾科技和国家安全利益所采取的最为严格的限制措施之一。由于两岸关系长期陷入僵局，赖清德政府正在对北京采取更为强硬的政策，此举也可以部分缓解来自美方在这个问题上的施压。

与此同时，中国商务部与科技部也于星期五联合发布了一份文件草案，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》公开征求意见。

计划限制或禁止出口的技术多达40项，涵盖人工智能、生物医药芯片和光伏三大领域，其中拟禁止出口技术14项，拟限制出口技术26项。

“此次修订亦是技术贸易管理的常态化工作，依法依规进行，不针对任何特定国家、地区或实体，”中国商务部发言人说。

近年来，在美国主导的限制措施下，中国无法获取全球最尖端的人工智能芯片以及制造这些芯片的先进设备。

根据中国商务部和科技部提出的草案，使用敏感国家数据训练的人工智能大模型核心技术将被禁止出口。此外，旨在应用于国防、关键信息基础设施等高度敏感领域的人工智能智能体，也将受到出口限制。

多项芯片设计技术——包括部分人工智能处理芯片和存储芯片的相关技术——也被纳入了此次拟议的出口限制范围。

修订目录中还涵盖了12项与太阳能相关的技术——包括涉及多晶硅(太阳能供应链核心原材料)生产的技术——以及5项生物医药技术(包括涉及细胞和基因疗法的技术)。

美联社援引科技研究与咨询机构Omdia的首席分析师苏廉节(Lian Jye Su)的话说，中方此举“可被视为是对西方国家就人工智能、机器人、电信及其他关键技术提出主权要求的回应”。他认为，其目的是为了更好地管控对这些中国技术的获取。

title: 为美国畅销减肥药制造原料，中国工厂爆严重卫生问题
summary: 美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)调查人员在两家为美国市场供应复方减肥药原料的中国工厂里，发现严重的卫生问题，包括在设备上发现黑霉菌和虫子污染。美国国会中国特设委员会表示，美国制药公司依赖中国生产，是把美国民众置于风险之中。 美国彭博社星期四(10月15日)[报道](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-15/compound-semaglutide-tirzepatide-plants-in-china-found-w
content:
美国食品药品监督管理局(FDA)调查人员在两家为美国市场供应复方减肥药原料的中国工厂里，发现严重的卫生问题，包括在设备上发现黑霉菌和虫子污染。美国国会中国特设委员会表示，美国制药公司依赖中国生产，是把美国民众置于风险之中。

美国彭博社星期四(10月15日)[报道](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-15/compound-semaglutide-tirzepatide-plants-in-china-found-with-black-mold-by-fda)， 美国FDA检查人员在中国成都圣诺生物制药有限公司(Chengdu Shengnuo Biopharm Co)和南京臣功制药有限公司(Nanjing Chengong Pharmaceutical Co)记录到严重违规情况。这两家中国工厂负责生产用于美国复方减肥药GLP-1的关键成分。

**黑霉、虫子和伪造文件**

根据彭博社通过《信息公开法》获得的报告显示，美国检查人员在其中一家工厂的设备上发现黑霉，地板上有“严重污染”。 检查人员还发现该厂员工试图在工厂里藏匿文件，并偷偷将产品样品倒掉；另一家工厂则存在伪造实验报告和文件的证据。

根据报告，今年八月，当美国FDA检查人员抵达成都圣诺时，工厂的质量控制人员拿着实验室的文件跑到一个房间里，并把文件塞进储物柜，同时还有员工把产品样品倒进水槽，“似乎是经过协调的行为”。美国检查人员无法取得那些被藏匿的文件。

美国检查员在报告中说，他们在成都圣诺工厂里，除了发现霉菌和肮脏的地板外，还注意到天花板上有“明显的虫子活动”。

而在南京臣功制药的工厂，检查员发现他们一直在购买其他工厂生产的活性成分，并贴上南京臣功的认证章。但臣功的员工并没有审核其他工厂的检测信息以确认产品的安全性。

**专家：“一场随时可能爆发的严重事故”**

彭博社报道，食品药品监督管理局已经将两家中国公司列为出口警示名单，代表这些公司的产品可能被禁止进入美国。彭博社援引前FDA检查与调查副专员迈克尔·罗杰斯(Michael Rogers)的话说，检查结果看上去“像是一场随时可能爆发的严重事故”。

这两家中国工厂生产司美格鲁肽(semaglutide)和替西帕肽(tirzepatide)，用于未经监管机构批准贩售、也未经安全或有效性审查的定制版本。这是两家美国制药公司诺和诺德(Novo Nordisk A/S)和礼来公司(Eli Lilly & Co.)生产的畅销减肥药的活性成分。

司美格鲁肽是一种长效胰高糖素样肽-1(GLP‑1)受体激动剂，广泛用于2型糖尿病和肥胖症的治疗；替西帕肽是一种新型双受体激动剂(GLP‑1 + GIP)，也用于2型糖尿病治疗，并显示显著减重效果。

彭博社报道，一些所谓的复方药物制造商(drug compounders)用相对便宜的畅销减肥药仿制品充斥市场，而中国是这些药品活性成分的重要供应国。

美国众议院中国特设委员会星期四在X上转推了彭博社的这篇文章，并发文说，FDA检查员在两家生产复方GLP-1药物活性成分的中国工厂发现了设备上的黑霉、天花板里大量虫子以及其他严重问题。贴文中说，美国制药公司依赖中国生产药物，“实际上是在把美国公民置于风险之中。”

中国问题特设委员会长期关注美国公司对中国生产药物的依赖。今年3月，该委员会就美国对中国活性药物成分及尖端药物的依赖问题举行听证。听证会上，议员和专家们指出，中国正在垄断美国的药品市场，而且这是蓄意设计的结果。与会的议员和专家把该问题的重要性提升至与中国的战略竞争及美国国家安全问题的高度。

summary: 香港退休的新西兰最高法院法官阿诺德爵士被推荐任命为香港终审法院非常任法官。如果获得批准，他将把海外普通法法学家名册增加到六名法学家，从而增强法院的灵活性和国际地位。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 16 日香港时间 21:11 · 1 分钟阅读首席大法官 Andrew张建宗欢迎行政长官接受
content:
香港
退休的新西兰最高法院法官阿诺德爵士被推荐任命为香港终审法院非常任法官。如果获得批准，他将把海外普通法法学家名册增加到六名法学家，从而增强法院的灵活性和国际地位。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 16 日 21:11 · 阅读时间 1 分钟

终审法院首席法官张家明欢迎行政长官接受建议，委任新西兰最高法院退休法官阿诺爵士为终审法院非常任法官。该建议由司法人员推荐委员会提交，政府现将在根据《基本法》和《香港终审法院条例》作出任命前，寻求立法会的正式批准。

此次任命将使最高法院中来自其他普通法司法管辖区的非常任法官人数从五名增加到六名，从而在管理上诉法院的案件日历方面提供更大的操作灵活性。根据香港终审法院条例，法院备有本地非常任法官和海外普通法司法管辖区法官的名册，法定法官人数合计上限为30人。
随着最新成员的加入，海外特遣队将由来自新西兰、澳大利亚和英国的六名杰出法学家组成，与四名当地非常任法官一起服务。

终审法院的实质性上诉由一个五人小组审理并作出裁决，该小组由首席法官、三名常任法官和一名从本地或海外名册中选出的非常任法官组成。

特伦斯爵士曾担任新西兰副检察长，之后担任新西兰上诉法院和最高法院法官，直至 2017 年从常任法官退休，为新西兰带来了数十年的高级普通法司法经验。司法当局指出，他的加入加强了法院的国际地位，并有助于确保有效处理复杂的最终上诉。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Retired New Zealand Supreme Court judge Sir Terence Arnold has been recommended for appointment as a non-permanent judge of Hong Kong's Court of Final Appeal. If approved, he would raise the overseas common law roster to six jurists, enhancing the court's flexibility and international standing.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

16 Oct 2026 at 21:11 HKT · 1 min read

Chief Justice Andrew Cheung has welcomed the Chief Executive's acceptance of a recommendation to appoint retired New Zealand Supreme Court judge Sir Terence Arnold as a non-permanent judge of the Court of Final Appeal. The recommendation was submitted by the Judicial Officers Recommendation Commission, and the government will now seek formal endorsement from the Legislative Council before the appointment is made under the Basic Law and the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal Ordinance.

The appointment would increase the number of non-permanent judges from other common law jurisdictions sitting on the top court from five to six, providing greater operational flexibility in managing the appellate court's case calendar. Under the Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal Ordinance, the court maintains rosters for both local non-permanent judges and those from overseas common law jurisdictions, capped at a combined statutory ceiling of 30 judges.

With the latest addition, the overseas contingent would comprise six distinguished jurists from New Zealand, Australia, and the United Kingdom, serving alongside four local non-permanent judges.

Substantive appeals before the Court of Final Appeal are heard and decided by a five-member panel comprising the Chief Justice, three permanent judges, and one non-permanent judge selected from either the local or overseas rosters.

Sir Terence served as Solicitor-General of New Zealand before sitting on the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court of New Zealand until his retirement from the permanent bench in 2017, bringing decades of senior common law judicial experience to the territory. Judicial authorities noted that his inclusion on the bench strengthens the court's international standing and helps ensure the efficient handling of complex final appeals.

title: 李靖宇：从蔡康永遭封杀看两岸的“游戏规则”
summary: 资深主持人蔡康永日前低调现身民进党台北市长参选人沈伯洋竞总成立大会，引发关注。资料照。（宋碧龙／大纪元） 【大纪元2026年10月16日讯】近期，蔡康永低调现身沈伯洋竞选活动引发中共与小粉红痛批、抵制，对比有艺人在天安门广场高举五星旗向中共输诚而遭台湾球迷抵制，取消职棒开球活动，引发许多讨论。 有台湾网红指出：“在哪里玩就要遵守那里的游戏规则”、“所谓的自由，就是在不违法的前提下，我们能尽情说自己想说的话，做自己想做的事”、“民主自由是没有人需要为了自己的认同而道歉而付出代价
content: 资深主持人蔡康永日前低调现身民进党台北市长参选人沈伯洋竞总成立大会，引发关注。资料照。（宋碧龙／大纪元） 【大纪元2026年10月16日讯】近期，蔡康永低调现身沈伯洋竞选活动引发中共与小粉红痛批、抵制，对比有艺人在天安门广场高举五星旗向中共输诚而遭台湾球迷抵制，取消职棒开球活动，引发许多讨论。 有台湾网红指出：“在哪里玩就要遵守那里的游戏规则”、“所谓的自由，就是在不违法的前提下，我们能尽情说自己想说的话，做自己想做的事”、“民主自由是没有人需要为了自己的认同而道歉而付出代价。” 这些话乍听之下有一定的道理，人的本能就是趋利避害，追逐利益不是什么错……然而人之所以是万物之灵，就是我们还能在利害面前多一层思考──您确定民主社会的规则与极权体制的规则，真的可以放在一起比较吗？ 自由不是毫无代价：言论自由不等于免受抵制 这样的说法至少有四点明显的谬误： 第一，混淆了“政府封杀”与“市场选择”的差别。蔡康永在中国面临的是中共（公权力）的系统性封杀，是直接剥夺其工作权；而吴奇隆在台湾失去开球机会，并非台湾政府下令禁止，而是民间球团与消费者基于品牌形象和情感的自主决定。这是自由市场的选择，而不是国家机器剥夺自由。 第二，言论自由不等于“免于被市场抵制”。民主保障任何人都能尽情说想说的话，政府不会因为你的言论把你抓去关。但这并不保证你的言论不会引起大众反感。艺人有表态爱中共的自由，台湾民众同样也有“因为你的立场而选择不消费你”的自由。 第三，中华民国与中华人民共和国有本质上的不同。在中共治下，反对体制可能会面临人身安全与法律制裁；但在中华民国台湾，表态爱中共的艺人，其财产、家人依然受到台湾法律的完好保护，他们若想回台享受健保或置产，政府绝不会清算。台湾社会依然包容，让不认同这块土地的人安全生活。 第四，地缘政治下，认同往往伴随社会成本。当艺人选择认同一个对台具备军事威胁的政权时，引起被威胁群体（台湾大众）心理上的防卫与排斥，是自然的情感反应。这不是双标，而是民主社会维护自身主体性的防卫机制。 哈伯玛斯的解方：以“普世价值”取代“民族主义” 为了让爱国心不沦为狭隘的民族情绪，德国哲学家哈伯玛斯（Jürgen Habermas）在1980年代中期深入讨论了“宪政爱国主义”（Constitutional Patriotism）。 传统的爱国主义或国家认同，通常建立在“血缘、共同历史、民族文化或地理边界”（例如：我是中国人、我是德国人、我们流着相同的血）。 但哈伯玛斯沉痛地反思纳粹主义，得出一个结论，这种基于“血缘国族”的爱国心非常危险，极易走向排他、盲目与极权（就像小粉红的非理性爱国）。因此他主张，现代多元民主社会的公民，其共同认同不该是血统，而应是“自由、民主、人权、法治”等普世的“宪政原则与民主程序”。 白话来说：“我爱这个国家，不是因为我们有相同的血统，而是因为这个国家实行着保护每个人自由的‘民主宪政秩序’。我们对国家的忠诚，是对‘宪法所保障的自由体制’的忠诚。” 从神州大地到丛林社会：你真想遵守“权力逻辑”的狼性规则？ 目前中国大陆遭到共产党窃国，自1949年中共建政以来，中国因饥饿与各种政治迫害死亡的人数估计超过8千万，死亡数字超越了希特勒的纳粹德国与史达林的苏联，是人类历史上因单一政权死亡人数最多的案例，世界上没有任何一个政权这样残杀自己的同胞。 在精神文化方面，中华文化是神州大地的灵魂，五千年来，文化认同凝聚着中华民族的精神；而中共不遗余力地破坏中华传统文化，这不就是在毁灭中国人的灵魂吗？ 更糟的是，共产党毁掉了人的正常思考后，再借着洗脑教育，灌输了一套充满谎言、仇恨与斗争的党文化，使当今多数中国人的言行举止很失当。 毁掉中华文化信仰价值使中国大陆出现了一种什么现象呢？现代的中国人失去了信仰与价值信念，许多人完全以金钱欲望为人生目标，在追逐金钱的过程中，损害他人、为非作歹都毫无顾忌。 因此，有毒奶粉食品、产品假冒山寨、环境污染恶化、黑社会大行其道……为人师表者强奸幼女，老人跌倒无人敢搀扶，政匪一家、官员贪污腐败，拥有二奶、三奶、四奶……身在其中犹如置身狼窟。 国际特赦组织（Amnesty International）指出，习近平任内将政权稳定置于经济发展之上，消除任期限制、扩大数位集权统治。这套体制成功压制了社会的公开反抗，但代价却是“全体人民的财富缩水、阶级流动停滞、以及民众社会生活空间被高度限缩”，成了近年中国社会的普遍现状。 这种社会某种程度上已退回原始的丛林社会，遵循的是狼性规则，也就是“权力逻辑”──谁的拳头大谁就是老大，谁的靠山硬谁就能躺赢。许多中国人缺乏文明素养（没有排队等习惯），但是却对权力绝对服从，一有机会就欺压弱者，“拿普通人出气，对暴政屁也不敢放一个，欺软怕硬”。 你确定，真的想要遵守这样的游戏规则？ 当商业利益超越国家与尊严：所有人心中都有答案 即使从情感的角度上来看，拥抱一个用飞弹对着自己家乡的政权，还称之为“祖国”，不论用什么理由都说不过去；这样明目张胆的为了商业利益出卖自己的国家，会不会又为了钱出卖自己的至亲、合作伙伴，甚至出卖自己的灵魂？我想所有人都会有答案。 我们做人做事还是要有尊严、有原则，不要丢失了自己的品格与立场，才会赢得别人的尊重，才能获得真正公平对等的合作机会，这样的钱，赚得安心、赚得有价值。 人生是一场马拉松，而不是百米冲刺。不义之财来得快、去得急；真正能陪我们走到终点的，永远是正道与坚持，你说是吗？ （本文作者是台大社会学士、台大政治硕士，政治经济专栏评论员。专长是当代中国政治文化、社会文化与经济发展领域。）

title: Apple iPhone Duo pre-orders sell out in 15 minutes in Hong Kong
zh_title: Apple iPhone Duo 在香港预购 15 分钟内售罄
summary: 香港苹果公司于周五晚上启动了其首款可折叠智能手机 iPhone Duo 的预订。首发日商店提货位在 15 分钟内就被抢购一空。只有售价 27,999 港元的顶级 2TB 型号仍可当天领取。其他车型的送货上门时间被推迟到一月下旬。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 17 日香港时间 10:55 · 2 分钟阅读 Apple 推出官方备受期待的首部作品已接受预订
content:
香港
苹果公司于周五晚上启动了其首款可折叠智能手机 iPhone Duo 的预订。首发日商店提货位在 15 分钟内就被抢购一空。只有售价 27,999 港元的顶级 2TB 型号仍可当天领取。其他车型的送货上门时间被推迟到一月下旬。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 17 日，香港时间 10:55 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

苹果公司于周五晚间推出了备受期待的首款可折叠设备 iPhone Duo 的官方预订，引发了巨大的客流量，在不到 15 分钟的时间内就耗尽了上市当天的商店提货位。

这款豪华双屏智能手机是苹果迄今为止最昂贵的手机产品，于晚上 8 点开始接受预订。 《The Standard》的姊妹刊物《Sing Tae Headline》的测试人员证实，在开业后 30 分钟内，大多数标准型号的发货时间已被推迟至明年 1 月下旬。

为了准备晚间高峰，Apple 官方网站和 Apple Store 移动应用程序均于下午早些时候下线进行定期维护，并显示标准等待屏幕欢迎早期访客，并告知他们预订将于晚上 8 点准时开始。
潜在买家所面临的成功程度不同，具体取决于他们使用的平台。开场几分钟内进行的数字测试显示，桌面网站版本运行相对顺利，一些早期客户可以在晚上 8.04 点之前完成对标志性夜空配色入门级 256GB 存储型号的付款。

相比之下，那些尝试通过官方 Apple Store 移动应用程序购买的人遇到了严重的系统瓶颈。许多用户被置于虚拟队列中，遇到要求他们留在页面上的等待屏幕，然后系统通知表明他们的等待时间即将结束。当移动应用程序用户于晚上 8.18 左右成功绕过虚拟等候室时，他们收到通知，称完全无法提供当日商店取货服务。
由于库存迅速耗尽，迟到者如果希望在 10 月 23 日正式发布日收到设备，他们的选择非常有限。15 分钟后不久，发布日店内提货的唯一剩余库存是顶级 2TB 存储型号，其标价为 27,999 港元。对于所有其他存储容量，物理存储收集选项完全呈灰色。选择送货上门而不是商店提货的顾客面临着更长时间的延误，预计送货时间迅速缩短，导致许多晚上晚些时候下单的顾客预计到货日期会延长到一月下旬。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编

负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
Apple launched pre-orders for its first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, on Friday evening. Launch-day store pickup slots sold out in under 15 minutes. Only the top-tier 2TB model at HK$27,999 remained available for same-day collection. Home delivery for other models was pushed to late January.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

17 Oct 2026 at 10:55 HKT · 2 min read

Apple launched official pre-orders for its highly anticipated first foldable device, the iPhone Duo, on Friday evening, triggering a massive wave of traffic that exhausted launch-day store pickup slots in less than 15 minutes.

The luxury dual-screen smartphone, which marks Apple's most expensive mobile release to date, became available for reservation starting at 8pm. Testers from Sing Tae Headline, the sister publication of The Standard, confirmed that within 30 minutes of opening, shipping delivery times for most standard models had already been pushed back to late January of next year.

In preparation for the evening rush, both the official Apple website and the Apple Store mobile application went offline for scheduled maintenance earlier in the afternoon, displaying a standard holding screen welcoming early visitors and advising them that pre-orders would commence precisely at 8pm.

Prospective buyers faced varying levels of success depending on the platform they used. Digital tests conducted during the opening minutes revealed that the desktop website version operated relatively smoothly, allowing some early customers to complete their payments by 8.04pm for the entry-level 256GB storage model in the signature night sky colourway.

In contrast, those attempting to purchase through the official Apple Store mobile application encountered significant system bottlenecks. Many users were placed in a virtual queue, encountering holding screens that asked them to remain on the page, followed by system notifications indicating that their waiting times were almost over. By the time mobile app users successfully bypassed the virtual waiting room at approximately 8.18pm, they were met with notices stating that same-day store pickup was entirely unavailable.

The rapid depletion of stock left latecomers with highly limited options if they hoped to receive their devices on the official release day of October 23. Shortly after the 15-minute mark, the only inventory remaining for launch-day in-store pickup was the top-tier 2TB storage variant, which carries a premium price tag of HK$27,999. For all other storage capacities, the option for physical store collection was completely greyed out. Customers choosing home delivery instead of store pickup faced even longer delays, with estimated delivery windows rapidly slipping, leaving many who ordered later in the evening with projected arrival dates extending into late January.

summary: 香港海事处表示，根据新的南行游艇计划，五艘广东注册的游艇将于周五成为首批进入香港水域的游艇。海事处处长黄世发概述了监测、锚地和停泊安排，并驳回了对中国船舶影响的担忧 [![图 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:36 香港时间 · 2 分钟阅读 五艘广东注册游艇将率先入驻
content:
香港
海事处表示，根据新南行游艇计划，五艘在广东注册的游艇将于周五首批进入香港水域。海事处处长黄世发概述了监测、锚地和停泊安排，并驳斥了对中国船舶影响的担忧。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:36 香港时间 · 阅读 2 分钟

海事处表示，五艘在广东注册的游艇将于周五根据新南行游艇计划首批进入香港水域，标志着香港向大湾区游艇拥有者开放的重要一步。

海事处处长黄世发周四在电台节目中表示，五艘游艇已通过部门的电子商业系统成功注册。他补充说，已有23名操作员通过该系统注册，近300名大陆船长已通过所需的评估。
该计划要求申请人指定其锚地。动态跟踪系统将监控游艇的移动，该系统会向误入限制区域或自动识别系统发生故障的船只发出警报，以确保安全。我们会在五个指定碇泊处加强巡逻和执法：赤柱、大潭、浅水湾、西贡三噚湾和大澳。

黄说，有足够的停泊空间供预计抵达的旅客使用，无需限制每日访问。如果锚地已满，来访的游艇将被引导至其他地点。目前的锚地预计可容纳约115艘长度达40米的游艇。

虽然香港的游艇泊位总数约为 4,000 个，远低于该市 10,000 多艘游艇，但黄指出，并非所有游艇都需要立即停泊。目前正计划在红磡、南丫岛和机场附近增设泊位。

尽管这五个锚地缺水缺电，但来访的游艇将可以使用该市的七个售水亭和八个指定加油站。海事服务提供商和当地船只也可以提供补给。该部门将分发传单并在网上发布参观游艇的详细信息。
在回应对该计划对中华白海豚栖息地影响的担忧时，黄指出该地区已经有大量船只活动，并相信该计划对生态和交通的影响很小。海事局长强调，本地和来访的游艇将受到同等对待，任何违反法律的行为都将采取执法行动。

Five Guangdong-registered yachts will become the first to enter Hong Kong waters on Friday under the new southbound yacht scheme, the Marine Department said. Director of Marine Wong Sai-fat outlined monitoring, anchorage and berthing arrangements, and dismissed concerns about the impact on Chinese w

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 13:36 HKT · 2 min read

Five Guangdong-registered yachts are set to become the first to enter Hong Kong waters under the new southbound yacht scheme on Friday, marking a significant step in opening the city to yacht owners from the Greater Bay Area, the Marine Department said.

Speaking on a radio programme on Thursday, Director of Marine Wong Sai-fat said the five yachts had been successfully registered through the department's Electronic Business System. He added that 23 operators had registered via the system and nearly 300 mainland captains had passed the required assessment.

The scheme requires applicants to specify their anchorage. Yacht movements will be monitored by a dynamic tracking system, which ensures safety by alerting vessels that stray into restricted areas or whose automatic identification systems fail. Enhanced patrols and enforcement will be carried out at the five designated anchorages: Stanley, Tai Tam, Repulse Bay, Three Fathoms Cove in Sai Kung and Tai O.

Wong said there is enough berthing space for the expected arrivals and no need to limit daily visits. If an anchorage is full, visiting yachts will be directed to alternative sites. The current anchorage areas are expected to accommodate about 115 yachts of up to 40 metres in length.

While Hong Kong's total yacht berths number around 4,000, well below the city's more than 10,000 yachts, Wong noted that not all need berthing at once. Plans are underway for additional berths in Hung Hom, Lamma Island and near the airport.

Although the five anchorages lack water and electricity, visiting yachts will be able to use the city's seven water-selling kiosks and eight designated fuel stations. Marine service providers and local vessels can also supply provisions. The department will distribute leaflets and post details online for visiting yachts.

Responding to concerns over the scheme's effect on Chinese white dolphin habitats, Wong noted the area already had plenty of vessel activity, believing the scheme's ecological and traffic impact would be low. Stressing that local and visiting yachts would be treated alike, the marine chief said any breaches of the law would draw enforcement action.

title: Special Forces in China’s Nuclear and Missile Operations
zh_title: 中国核与导弹行动中的特种部队
source: Small Wars Journal by Arizona State Univ
summary: 摘要 人们对特种部队在管理核行动中的作用知之甚少，尤其是在国外。文章探讨了中国人民解放军火箭军特种作战部队的组织结构和任务。研究中国核行动和导弹行动中的特种部队如何帮助情报专业人员和政策制定者更清楚地了解中国的导弹生存能力以及使其导弹部队面临风险的选择。简介：从苏联手提箱核装置到美国陆军特种部队“绿灯队”
content:
摘要 人们对特种部队在管理核行动中的作用知之甚少，尤其是在国外。文章探讨了中国人民解放军火箭军特种作战部队的组织结构和任务。研究中国核行动和导弹行动中的特种部队如何帮助情报专业人员和政策制定者更清楚地了解中国的导弹生存能力以及使其导弹部队面临风险的选择。简介 从苏联手提箱核装置到冷战期间美国陆军特种部队“绿灯小组”，特种作战在核战略中的作用有着悠久且未被充分认识的历史。研究美国对手如何计划在核行动中使用特种部队的文章就更少了。然而，研究中国人民解放军火箭军（PLARF）如何运用特种作战揭示了党的优先事项、中国的核生存方法以及了解中国弹头管理实践的窗口。最后一个见解尤其重要，因为它可以表明准备情况、警戒状态以及从中央军事委员会（中国共产党的最高军事指挥部）授权使用核到在运载工具上放置弹头的时间表。外界对 PLARF 特种部队知之甚少。以下大多数评估必然是暂时的。
然而，来自中国的足够多的媒体报道、期刊文章和社交媒体帖子让分析人士能够拼凑出一幅关于解放军特种部队如何将特种部队融入其核行动的图景（尽管并不完整）。与冷战期间对核渗透的担忧不同，解放军特种部队构成的威胁并不那么引人注目。尽管未来可能会发生变化，但解放军特种部队的主要任务是反渗透、保卫弹头和“蓝队”（解放军中的敌方部队通常被称为蓝队或蓝军）。 PLARF特种作战部队的组织和任务 PLARF特种部队的总体目标是对中国导弹旅的生存能力和作战能力进行压力测试，反击对手的渗透和破坏，以及保护弹头和导弹阵地。用解放军一名旅长的话说，解放军训练和维持特种作战部队的主要原因之一是纠正“防御行动中的某些缺陷”和“拥有足够可信的自卫能力来防止敌人的渗透”。中国军队喉舌《解放军报》的另一篇文章指出，“尖刀”部队的任务之一是导弹发射支援和反击敌方特种作战攻击。
更广泛地说，2012年《中国战略导弹部队百科全书》指出，火箭军的前身第二炮兵需要为精确制导攻击、特种部队突袭以及攻击后的修复和恢复做好准备。事实上，用于训练解放军军官的2004年《第二炮兵作战科学》中有几段专门介绍敌方特种作战的破坏威胁和防御方法他们。尽管 22 年来，解放军的作战理念、生存能力和技术取得了长足进步，但最近的演习仍然表明，重点是使用特种部队进行反渗透

【原文 English Original】
Abstract Little is known about the role special forces have in managing nuclear operations, especially in foreign countries. The article examines the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force’s special operations units, their organizational structure, and missions. Studying how special forces in China’s nuclear and missile operations helps intelligence professionals and policymakers develop a clearer picture of China’s missile survivability and options to hold at risk its missile forces. Introduction From Soviet suitcase nuclear devices to U.S. Army Special Forces “ Green Light teams ” during the Cold War, the role of special operations in nuclear strategy has a long and underappreciated history. Even fewer pieces have examined how U.S. adversaries plan to employ special forces in nuclear operations. However, studying how the People’s Liberation Army Rocket Force (PLARF) employs special operations reveals Party priorities, China’s approach to nuclear survivability, and windows into China’s warhead management practices. The last insight is especially important, since it can indicate readiness, alert status, and timelines from when the Central Military Commission—the Chinese Communist Party’s supreme military command—authorizes nuclear use to the placement of warheads on delivery vehicles. Little is known about the PLARF’s special forces from the outside. Most of the following assessments are necessarily tentative. Yet, enough media reporting, journal articles, and social media posts from China exist for analysts to cobble together a picture–albeit incomplete–of how the PLARF integrates special forces in its nuclear operations. Unlike worries over nuclear infiltration during the Cold War, the threats posed by PLARF’s special forces are less dramatic. Although this may evolve in the future, PLARF special forces primarily focus on counter-infiltration, guarding warheads, and “blue-teaming” (an opposing force in the PLA is generally referred to as blue team or blue force). PLARF Special Operations Forces Organization and Missions PLARF special forces are generally oriented toward stress testing the survivability and operations of China’s missile brigades, countering infiltration and sabotage from adversaries, and protecting warheads and missile sites. In the words of one PLARF brigade commander, one of the main reasons for training and maintaining special operations forces (SOF) units in the PLARF is to rectify “certain shortcomings in defensive operations” and “have sufficient credible self-defense capabilities to prevent enemy infiltration.” Another article from the PLA Daily—the mouthpiece of the Chinese military— posits that one of the missions of the “Sharp Knife” unit is for missile launch support and countering enemy special operations attacks. More broadly, the 2012 China Strategic Missile Force Encyclopedia states that the Second Artillery Forces, the predecessor to the Rocket Force, need to be prepared for precision-guided attacks, special forces raids, and to conduct repairs and recover in the aftermath of an attack. Indeed, the 2004 Science of Second Artillery Campaigns, an operational manual used to train PLA officers, has several passages dedicated to threats of sabotage from enemy special operations and ways to defend against them. Although the PLA’s operational concepts, survivability, and technology have come a long way in 22 years, more recent exercises still suggest an emphasis on the use of special forces for counter-infiltration missions and the protection of launch sites and warheads. Within the PLARF, several special forces units are assigned to different bases and serve different missions. There are at least seven special operations units in some capacity within the PLARF with different yet overlapping missions. Each unit is normally subordinated to a corps-level base that corresponds with a particular geographic area within China, often hosting delivery vehicles or nuclear warheads. There is no unified special operations command in China, and different services and levels of command may have dedicated special forces units. Consequently, the PLARF’s special forces vary in size. Drawing upon Ma Xiu’s research from the China Aerospace Studies Institute and Chinese media reporting, the following table captures known PLARF SOF units, their key characteristics, and command structure. Table 1 : Known PLARF SOF Units PLARF Special Operations Forces Unit Name Chinese Name Key Characteristics Known Location Immediate Parent Unit Special Operations Security Training Team 特种警卫集训队 (Tèzhǒng jǐngwèi jíxùn duì) Approximately 200 personnel focused on anti-reconnaissance, anti-infiltration, and anti-raiding missions Base 61 Directly subordinate to Base 61 Sharp Knife Special Operations Team 利刃特战队 (Lìrèn tè zhànduì) 38-man unit referred to as “missile guardians” and potentially dedicated to counter-SOF and missile launch support One in Base 64; one in Base 67 Security Battalion (Base 67) Knife’s Edge Special Operations Team 刀锋特战队 (Dāofēng tè zhànduì) Base 67 headquarters site security Base 67 Security and Service Battalion Blue Team SOF Unit Unknown[BG3.1][AR3.2][BG3.3] Opposing force unit with a special operations capability focused on technical reconnaissance, electronic warfare, and sabotage to help the PLARF find weaknesses Base 69 Blue Team Unit in the 3rd Test and Training District Special Operations Squadron 特战中对 (Tè zhàn zhōng duì) Opposing force unit at the company level in a remote mountain environment with reconnaissance and surveillance, frequency jamming, SOF, and electronic countermeasure capabilities to help the PLARF find weaknesses Base 69 Blue Team Opposing Force Regiment in the 2nd Test and Training District Special Operations Reconnaissance Team 特种侦察队 (Tèzhǒng zhēnchá duì) Damage assessment and target reconnaissance Staff Department Operations Support Group Reconnaissance Regiment Base 67 is where the PLARF stockpiles its warheads. Within Base 67 is the “Knife’s Edge” Special Operations Team, a 38-man unit primarily focused on site security. The Knife’s Edge is part of the Security and Service Battalion, which itself is subordinated to Base 67 Operations Support Regiment. This team is responsible for physical security around Base 67’s headquarters. Established around 2004, the Sharp Knife Special Operations Team is subordinate to Base 67’s Security Battalion. It primarily focuses on protecting PLA Unit 96038, a unit responsible for warhead management and transportation of warhead stockpiles. Exercises in 2014 suggest that the Sharp Knife team contains snipers and has a role in escorting mobile missiles. Ma Xiu additionally notes that the Sharp Knife personnel are reportedly referred to as “missile guardians” within Base 64, consisting of intermediate-range and intercontinental ballistic missiles. Still, Ma Xiu points out that it’s unknown whether Sharp Knife teams are unique to specific units or if every single PLARF base possesses such a unit. The Sharp Knife team’s command level in Base 64 is also unclear. Located in Anhui province, Base 61 is a command unit that carries several missile brigades, consisting of short-range and medium-range ballistic missiles. Base 61 directly maintains a Special Operations Security Training Team, consisting of approximately 200 personnel for counter-reconnaissance, counter-infiltration, and counter-raiding missions. A 2024 social media post from China Youth Daily showcased approximately 100 trainees for this team, though it is unclear from this post alone how often this team takes in recruits or how many of these trainees become part of the Special Security Training Team. The post further notes that this team guards a “national treasure,” which is often a euphemism for warheads or important delivery vehicles. Within Beijing, the PLARF Headquarters comprises four major components: the staff, political work, logistics, and equipment departments. The PLARF Staff Department Operations Support Group has a reconnaissance regiment in charge of battlefield reconnaissance and intelligence support and a subordinate Special Operations Reconnaissance Team for target reconnaissance and damage assessment. The reconnaissance regiment is based in Beijing with two secondary garrisons in Qinghai and Fujian. The location of the Special Operations Reconnaissance Team is unknown. Stress Testing Missile Survivability The PLARF special operations community has an important role in red-blue exercises and stress testing missile survivability, especially during transit. These exercises pit missile brigades as the red side against a dedicated blue force. In fact, this emphasis on red-blue exercises comes from the top down. China’s 2013 defense white paper, for instance, directs the former Second Artillery Force to conduct red-blue exercises for reconnaissance and counter-reconnaissance, jamming and anti-jamming, and strengthening protection against nuclear, biological, and chemical threats. David C. Logan highlights that the PLARF established the creation of a Blue Army Teaching and Research Section, championed by Colonel Diao Guangming, to develop more difficult and complex training exercises. Within Base 69’s 3rd Test Training District is a PLARF blue force unit and a subordinate special operations unit. Little is known about its special operations capability, though the blue force unit does host PLARF units for exercises and training in plateau operations near the Gobi Desert region. Established in early 2018 as an experimental unit, Base 69’s 2nd Test and Training District also maintains a blue force regiment and a subordinate special operations squadron or company led by Zheng Yihang (some analysts refer to this unit as a squadron while other sources describe Zheng Yihang as a special operations company commander). A PLA Daily article traces the force from a 2004 tactical-confrontation team, through a Blue Force assembled from multiple units in 2012, to formal establishment in 2018, casting it as the missile force’s “first opponent.” From special operations raids to jamming, these exercises involve a variety of capabilities and are focused on preventing red team PLARF missile brigades from “arriving on time, launching on time, or launching accurately” to reveal potential weaknesses. The special operations element infiltrates and reconnoiters launch positions, command posts, and encampments, then raids launchers, transporter-erector-launchers on the move, convoys, and key personnel, often in severe cold, at night, or on the plateau. According to one account from Xinhua News, a PLARF special forces commander stressed non-contact play where “being discovered means failure.” Another PLA Daily article describes several blue force personnel conducting multi-means air reconnaissance while special troops raid from the ground, with blown bridges, ambushed launch vehicles, and jamming that leaves a battalion an “information island.” Red side missile brigades often will respond with camouflage, dispersal, light discipline against satellite passes, counter-reconnaissance, anti-infiltration, and rapid relocation and launch under harassment. After being discovered, red team missile brigades often must search for and apprehend blue force personnel to avoid failure in the exercise. The characteristics of these exercises underscore the PLA’s emphasis and heightened threat perceptions around the survivability of missile brigades. Conclusion and Policy Implications Although the role of special forces in managing nuclear operations is often underappreciated in the literature coming out of Western policy research institutions, the PLA invests significant resources in yearly exercises that test the survivability of missile brigades. Whether founded or unfounded, these exercises could also indicate that the PLARF and senior leadership see a variety of exquisite and unconventional ways in which the United States or other adversaries seek to disrupt the operation of China’s nuclear and conventional missile brigades. As U.S.-China military competition and nuclear competition intensify, the PLARF’s emphasis on protecting missile brigades from a variety of novel threats is unlikely to wane. Though their purview could evolve, the role of special forces in China’s nuclear strategy likely reflect a concern over protecting warheads and delivery vehicles rather than infiltrating an enemy’s forces. While the PLARF’s special forces generally stress-test the survivability of missile launch platforms, there are still many unknowns about the size, location, and number of PLARF SOF units. Future research should also examine in greater detail the organizational structure and command level of these units, the extent of sympathetic bureaucratic support within the PLA, and how they integrate with other components of the PLA. Do PLARF SOF have their own redundant reconnaissance systems, or are they primarily relying on intelligence from other services or organizations to inform their planning? For U.S. policymakers seeking damage limitation or left-of-launch options, researchers can attempt to track their specific routes, gaps in protecting delivery vehicles and warheads, and vulnerabilities in command and control. Ideally, policy entrepreneurs or military planners should find ways to disrupt PLARF mobile missile launcher operations and induce greater spending on internal security forces within the PLARF. This might involve credible and visible investment in long-range reconnaissance, special operations reach, and left-of-launch capabilities to reinforce existing fears over missile survivability and induce countermeasures to rectify perceived gaps. The PLARF has already shown that it takes the raids on its missile brigades seriously; in such a measure-countermeasure competition, every guard battalion, Blue Force detachment, and counter-reconnaissance drill draws money, personnel, and training time away from investing in increased offensive strike capabilities for a Taiwan campaign. Still, this course of action should be pursued only if the defensive burden on China exceeds the offensive investment by the United States, and forecasts of likely PLA countermeasures should be used to verify the soundness of the policy option. The post Special Forces in China’s Nuclear and Missile Operations appeared first on Small Wars Journal by Arizona State University .

title: FC Seoul on verge of clinching 1st S. Korean football title in 10 yrs
zh_title: 首尔FC有望夺得10年来首个韩国足球冠军
summary: 作者：Yoo Jee-ho 首尔 10 月 15 日（韩联社）——首尔 FC 队即将在 10 年来首次夺得韩国顶级足球联赛冠军，最早将于周日开香槟庆祝。进入周末比赛，首尔FC在12支球队的K联赛1中以20胜5平6负积65分稳居榜首。蔚山HD FC积47分排名第二。两家具乐部还剩七场比赛，如果蔚山HD FC周六没有获胜并且首尔FC周日获胜，那么FC首尔将获得第七个冠军。首尔FC球员在俱乐部K赛中庆祝1-0战胜仁川联队
content:
作者：柳智浩

首尔10月15日电（韩联社）——首尔FC最早将于周日开香槟庆祝，距离他们10年来在韩国顶级足球联赛中的首个冠军已经很近了。

进入周末比赛，首尔FC在12支球队的K联赛1中以20胜5平6负积65分稳居榜首。蔚山HD FC积47分排名第二。

两家具乐部还剩七场比赛，如果蔚山HD FC周六没有获胜并且首尔FC周日获胜，那么FC首尔将获得第七个冠军。

2026 年 9 月 5 日，首尔足球俱乐部球员在首尔世界杯体育场举行的俱乐部 K 联赛 1 场比赛中庆祝 1-0 战胜仁川联队（这张资料照片由韩国职业足球联盟提供）。球员们举着一条围巾，上面写着“走向第七颗星”，指的是为赢得联赛冠军而刻在球队队服上的一颗星星。 （照片非卖品）（韩联社）

蔚山HD FC将于下午4:30迎战富川FC 1995。周六，一场平局将使蔚山队的积分达到 48 分。如果首尔FC第二天击败金泉尚武FC，他们的积分将提高到68分。

在这种情况下，在还剩六场比赛的情况下，20分的差距将是难以逾越的。随后，首尔FC将与2018年和2025年的全北现代汽车队并列，成为在当前设置下最快夺得K联赛1冠军的俱乐部，在32场比赛后实现这一目标。
首尔FC是本赛季唯一一支没有连续输球的俱乐部。他们是联赛中进球数最多的球队，为 58 个，比蔚山队多 10 个；失球最少，为 26 个，比江原 FC 少 2 个。

前锋方面，波兰前锋帕特里克·克利马拉以14个进球领先，仅落后蔚山队的亚戈·卡里略1个，边锋郑承元则贡献了8个进球和6次助攻。

守门员具成润作为最后一道防线的稳定力量，首尔FC已经有13次不失球，排在联赛第二位，仅次于江原FC的14次。

主教练金基东终于享受到了首尔FC在2024赛季之前任命他时最初设想的成功。首尔FC在金的第一个赛季获得第四名，并在2025年跌至第六位，导致一些沮丧的球迷有时对金发出嘘声。但这位 55 岁的战术家现在带领首尔 FC 即将获得期待已久的冠军。

2026 年 10 月 10 日，首尔足球俱乐部主教练金基东在首尔世界杯体育场举行的 K 联赛 1 场比赛中观看球队对阵济州 SK FC 的比赛（这张照片由韩国职业足球联盟提供）。 （照片非卖品）（韩联社）

By Yoo Jee-ho

SEOUL, Oct. 15 (Yonhap) -- Nearing their first title in the top South Korean football league in 10 years, FC Seoul can pop champagne as early as Sunday.

Entering weekend play, FC Seoul are sitting pretty atop the tables of the 12-club K League 1 with 65 points on 20 wins, five draws and six losses. Ulsan HD FC are in second place with 47 points.

With seven matches left for both clubs, FC Seoul will clinch their seventh championship if Ulsan HD FC do not win Saturday and if FC Seoul themselves win Sunday.

FC Seoul players celebrate their 1-0 win over Incheon United in the clubs' K League 1 match at Seoul World Cup Stadium in Seoul on Sept. 5, 2026, in this file photo provided by the Korea Professional Football League. The players hold up a muffler that reads, "Toward the Seventh Star," referring to a star placed on a team's uniform for winning a league title. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

Ulsan HD FC will face Bucheon FC 1995 at 4:30 p.m. Saturday, and a draw will take Ulsan to 48 points. And if FC Seoul beat Gimcheon Sangmu FC the following day, they will improve to 68 points.

In that scenario, the 20-point gap will be insurmountable with six matches to go. FC Seoul would then tie the 2018 and 2025 Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors as the fastest club to clinch a K League 1 title under the current setup, doing so after 32 matches.

FC Seoul are the only club this season not to have lost consecutive matches. They have scored the most goals in the league with 58, 10 more than Ulsan, and have also conceded the fewest goals with 26, two fewer than Gangwon FC.

Up front, Polish striker Patryk Klimala has been leading the way with 14 goals, just one behind Yago Cariello of Ulsan for the league lead, and winger Jeong Seung-won had contributed eight goals and six assists.

Goalkeeper Gu Sung-yun has been a steady force as the last line of defense, with FC Seoul having recorded 13 clean sheets, the second most in the league behind Gangwon FC's 14.

Head coach Kim Gi-dong is finally enjoying the kind of success FC Seoul first envisioned when they appointed him before the 2024 season. FC Seoul finished fourth in Kim's first season and dropped to sixth place in 2025, leading some frustrated fans to boo Kim at times. But the 55-year-old tactician now has FC Seoul on the cusp of a long-awaited title.

FC Seoul head coach Kim Gi-dong watches his team play Jeju SK FC during the clubs' K League 1 match at Seoul World Cup Stadium in Seoul on Oct. 10, 2026, in this photo provided by the Korea Professional Football League. (PHOTO NOT FOR SALE) (Yonhap)

# 意大利南部与北部同时爆发抗议浪潮

JOSEPHINE DE LA BRUYÈRE 2026年10月20日

周六，警方在米兰与抗议者对峙。Stefano Porta/Lapresse, via Associated Press

上周末，两个互不相干的抗议浪潮震动了意大利：北部学生与南部农民、卡车司机分别要求政府出手遏制不断上涨的生活成本。

周六和周日，意大利北部多座城市有数千名学生示威者游行，抗议低工资、高税负、食品杂货和汽油价格上涨以及公共资金削减。部分游行酿成暴力事件：成群蒙面抗议者抢劫商店、纵火并向警察投掷物品，警方则以水炮和催泪瓦斯回应。

在意大利南部，农民和卡车司机自上周起封锁港口和主要高速公路，抗议伊朗战争引发的高油价，造成超市和加油站出现短缺。他们表示，价格上涨侵蚀了本已微薄的利润，并要求政府作出更强有力的回应。

总理乔治娅·梅洛尼一直将法律与秩序作为其政府的支柱。她周六在社交媒体发帖，表示对和平抗议者“高度尊重”，但谴责暴力：“抗议是一项权利。纵火焚烧我们的城市则不是。”

她周一与政府和执法官员会面，考虑对暴力抗议者施加更严厉的惩罚。

周日，米兰一家受损店铺内的警察。Reuters

南北两地的抗议是席卷欧洲的一波类似运动中的最新一起。上个月，马德里一名87岁老妇被[驱逐](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/24/world/europe/spain-eviction-sanchez.html)，促使西班牙人走上街头[抗议](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/08/world/europe/spain-protests-maricarmen-housing.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/08/world/europe/spain-protests-maricarmen-housing.html")房租上涨，使总理佩德罗·桑切斯的政府陷入政治危机。[阿尔巴尼亚](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/17/world/europe/albania-protests-what-to-know.html "Link: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/17/world/europe/albania-protests-what-to-know.html")民众对贾里德·库什纳计划中的豪华开发项目的 不满 已升级为对政治腐败和生活水平恶化的公开愤怒。在法国，学生抗议学校状况，释放出一股沮丧情绪，[席卷全国](https://cn.nytimes.com/world/20261019/france-student-protests-why/)，并在周末演变为该国[数十年来最严重的骚乱](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/17/world/europe/france-protest-riots-marseille.html)。

意大利的青年抗议规模要小得多，并于周日晚间结束。米兰警方称，约2000人在米兰示威，当地发生了最大规模的抗议。博洛尼亚、都灵、布雷西亚和贝加莫等城市也举行了游行。

广告

“我们的苦难没有选举解决方案，”本月早些时候创建、发出最初行动呼吁的匿名社交媒体账号发帖写道，敦促广泛的反政府示威“带来一个新意大利和一个新欧洲的诞生”。

尽管米兰多数抗议者和平游行，但与警方的冲突仍导致32人被捕，其中大多数是未成年人。警方称14名警察受伤，其中一人被鹅卵石击中头部。米兰一家商业协会周一估计，骚乱造成的损失超过100万欧元（约合人民币750万元）。

该市左翼市长朱塞佩·萨拉在一份声明中称，“我们周六和周日目睹的针对执法部门、公共空间和企业的行动和场景不可容忍，也不可辩护”。

骚乱的画面在全国引发强烈负面反应。“不可接受，”意大利全国性日报之一《信使报》周一头版写道。

但一些人敦促意大利人不要只盯着暴力。“年轻人很愤怒，”马尔科·巴斯切塔周六在意大利共产主义日报《宣言报》上写道。“一片水域若被忽视和堵塞数十年，就不能指望它不溢出。”

意大利主流媒体对北部抗议的报道明显多于较贫穷南部持续时间更长的抗议——这是另一个令农民、卡车司机及其支持者不满的地方。“新闻不谈意大利南部，因为政府对意大利南部不感兴趣，”在线杂志《Scomodo》的一则标题写道。

梅洛尼的交通和基础设施部长马泰奥·萨尔维尼已同意下周与南部卡车司机代表会面。但周末随着意大利媒体开始报道封锁的后果，他宣布将会议提前到周二。他在一次电台采访中表示，政府将“尽我们所能”安抚卡车司机。

美国芯片制造商英伟达（Nvidia）首席执行官黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）将是“投资德国峰会”重要嘉宾之一 图像来源: Jens Kalaene/dpa/picture alliance

广告

（德国之声中文网）为期两天的“投资德国峰会”将于周一晚间在[柏林](https://dw.com/zh/%E6%9F%8F%E6%9E%97/t-40351455)开幕。德国总理默茨将发表开幕致辞。预计约有200名德国及国际大型企业代表出席会议。

美国芯片制造商英伟达（Nvidia）首席执行官[黄仁勋](https://dw.com/zh/%E9%BB%84%E4%BB%81%E5%8B%8B%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%BB%88%E5%B0%86%E5%BC%80%E6%94%BEai%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E5%B8%82%E5%9C%BA/a-77207319)（Jensen Huang）将是峰会重要嘉宾之一。英伟达产品是当前[AI热潮](https://dw.com/zh/%E4%BA%BA%E5%B7%A5%E6%99%BA%E8%83%BD/t-69572979)的核心之一，德国政府希望借助双方合作，帮助德国在这一领域迎头赶上。

据德国《商报》（Handelsblatt）报道，德国总理默茨与黄仁勋计划在峰会上公布一项AI合作计划。据悉，德国联邦政府将投入数亿欧元，英伟达则将提供工程师和芯片。包括西门子和奥迪在内的约十家德国企业也将参与其中。

上周五晚间，黄仁勋在柏林强调了德国作为业务所在地的重要性。据《每日镜报》（Tagesspiegel）报道，黄仁勋表示：“德国是我们在欧洲最大的运营基地。”

他指出，能够独立运营自己的服务对于[实现“数字主权”至关重要](https://dw.com/zh/%E5%BE%B7%E5%9B%BD%E6%95%B0%E5%AD%97%E4%B8%BB%E6%9D%83%E8%B7%AF%E6%BC%AB%E6%BC%AB/a-73614719)。英伟达销售的是芯片而非终端应用，他认为终端应用程序应当由德国本土开发提供。

## 德国政府希望提振私人投资

德国联邦政府希望借助此次峰会调动更多私人资本。德国政府内部人士表示，仅靠公共资金无法推动国家实现现代化。

据安联研究（Allianz Research）的一项研究显示，2019年至2025年，德国投资额下降了6.4%。同期，欧元区其他国家的投资额增长了6.7%，美国增长了20.2%。该研究将德国投资下降的原因归结为能源成本高企、税费负担沉重以及官僚主义问题。

## 黄仁勋：对德国在技术领域明显落后表示痛心

黄仁勋近日在受访时，谈及[德国在AI等关键技术领域的发展现况](https://dw.com/zh/%E5%BE%B7%E8%AF%AD%E5%AA%92%E4%BD%93kimi%E6%97%B6%E5%88%BB%E5%88%B0%E6%9D%A5-%E8%A5%BF%E6%96%B9%E5%BF%85%E9%A1%BB%E6%AD%A3%E8%A7%86%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%9A%84%E6%88%90%E5%8A%9F/a-78052610)时表示：“没有什么比看到世界上技术最先进的国家之一，如今在技术领域远远落后，更让我感到痛心。”

黄仁勋认为，原因之一可能在于欧洲的行事方式。他说：“也许是因为欧洲人做事时，总是想得太多考虑得太复杂。”“德国拥有如此多的人才，行动起来就好。”他发表这番言论的视频于上周末在社交媒体上广泛传播。

## 德国经济研究所：勿对峰会抱有过高期待

德国经济研究所（IW）则警告称，不应对这场峰会抱有过高期待。该机构指出，德国的劳动力、能源和官僚行政成本居高不下，正在阻碍投资者进入德国市场。

IW所长迈克尔·许特尔（Michael Hüther）接受德新社采访时表示：“如果认为这场峰会能在短期内改变这一状况，那就太天真了。企业不会因为参加一场宣传活动就选择德国。关键在于能否在这里赚钱。”

他指出，如果政府能够迅速落实改革议程，效果会更好。
