Huang Qingchen has a Master of Law in International Relations from Beijing Foreign Studies University.

Published: 9:30am, 25 Sep 2026

Hong Kong’s first five-year plan marks an unprecedented milestone not only for its economic and social development, but also for how it governs itself. The plan, which drew on 16,000 public submissions – roughly 80 per cent from ordinary citizens – is a testament to the government’s commitment to long-term development, which shows an unusual convergence of public consensus and political will.

For a city long accustomed to letting the market hold the reins, crafting a [road map](https://www.scmp.com/topics/hong-kongs-first-5-year-plan?module=inline&pgtype=article) clear in aims, precise in methods and univocal in stance – and placing itself as the primary agent responsible for its execution – is an act of political self-reinvention. It betokens a willingness to embrace the role of direction setter and reform executor, to be held accountable for outcomes five years down the road rather than merely navigate short-term challenges at hand.

Hong Kong’s reorientation away from a market-led approach indicates not only an upgrade of policy tools, but also a recalibration of governance philosophy.

## Details

[Blood on the Clocktower (BotC)](https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/240980/blood-on-the-clocktower)is currently the #1 rated party game on [Boardgamegeek.com!](http://boardgamegeek.com!/) We are so pleased that the local community playing BotC at Spielbound has grown such that multiple simultaneous games are being run at each of our BotC meet ups!

In November, the BotC meetup is scheduled for Monday, November 2 from 5:30 - 10:30 PM ... and Spielbound is reserving the *entire* Annex (up to 50 attendees~) for this event! Halloween weekend just passed; you are welcome to attend in costume! Dress up as your favorite BotC character!!!!

* A day pass is required to join this special event ($6 per person on Mondays or current Spielbound member); please check in with the front cafe staff when you arrive.
 * Those who have never played 'Blood on the Clocktower' at Spielbound are welcome to attend this event for free to try it out!
 * Storytellers will be on hand to explain the game rules to novice players, starting at 5:30 PM~

_More on the game:_
 Blood on the Clocktower is a game of murder and mystery, lies and logic, deduction and deception for five-to-twenty courageous players and one devious storyteller.

A social game played in person, seated in a circle, each player receives either a ‘good’ or ‘evil’ token with their unique character on it. Good players share information to solve the mystery whilst evil players lie about who they are and what they know. The good team wins if they can piece together their knowledge, trust each other, and execute the demon. The evil team wins if the demon can sow distrust, evade detection, and wipe out the village.

## [Dual-Use Farms](https://www.thewirechina.com/2026/10/18/like-it-or-not-the-eu-and-china-are-already-engaged-in-a-trade-war/dual-use-farms)

China needs land for crops and solar energy installations. Rather than compete against each other, farmers and green energy companies are realizing that they can cooperate by using one piece of land for both purposes. They are also now exporting their newfound dual land-use expertise around the world.

## Details

**[Wake Up Together](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/community)**[](https://www.wakeuptogether.org/community)is an online meditation community that was established in 2020 by Trina Truong and partners. Our mission is to help support individuals in maintaining a solid meditation practice through practicing in an accessible and open-minded community. We meet every day, virtually. While we are rooted in the Vipassana-Insight tradition, our approach is also inclusive to all Buddhist meditation practices such as anapanasati (mindfulness of the breath), Metta (loving-kindness), body scans, Zen, ton glen, and others.

The space that our meditators come to know is one that expresses itself as welcoming and embodying all views and interpretations of spirituality.

We hold the commitment to remain humble and vulnerable in our role as the door openers to the individual's inner journey. We aspire to shape the experience for participants to experience serenity, clear-seeing and profound understanding of the mind, and the [no] self through the practices, the guidance, the teachings, and the reflections offered in group sharing.

To solidify this spiritual aspiration is to make a commitment to sit in community with a predetermined frequency or as often as you can.
 We welcome you to join our beloved community!

These guided meditations are offered daily and given freely. There
 are no up-front fees. Wake Up Together is 100% donation based,
 relying on your support and generosity.

title: 欧洲准备加强针对中国的贸易防御机制，先是汽车，现在是化工行业
summary: 费加罗报对中国的关注主要集中在两个话题：首先是中国邀请特朗普的（前）发言人再次访问中国，其次是中国考虑对人工智能技术实施出口管制。经济类回声报则大篇幅关注了欧洲准备加强针对中国的贸易防御，先是汽车，现在是化工行业。除此之外，10月17日本台订阅的法国主流日刊集中大篇幅关注与黄背心运动出现合流趋势的法国高中生运动。 中国和欧盟旗帜特写。 © REUTERS – Dado Ruvic摄影 首先来看中国邀请特朗普的发言人再次访华。费加罗报报道称，这是因为白宫新任发言人凯蒂·扎卡里亚
content: 费加罗报对中国的关注主要集中在两个话题：首先是中国邀请特朗普的（前）发言人再次访问中国，其次是中国考虑对人工智能技术实施出口管制。经济类回声报则大篇幅关注了欧洲准备加强针对中国的贸易防御，先是汽车，现在是化工行业。除此之外，10月17日本台订阅的法国主流日刊集中大篇幅关注与黄背心运动出现合流趋势的法国高中生运动。 中国和欧盟旗帜特写。 © REUTERS – Dado Ruvic摄影 首先来看中国邀请特朗普的发言人再次访华。费加罗报报道称，这是因为白宫新任发言人凯蒂·扎卡里亚表示，她在中国的时候，中国“没有真正的厕所”。在扎卡里亚就中国厕所表达不满后，北京邀请她“更加频繁地来中国”看看。中国外交部发言人毛宁带着一丝微笑，在一场例行记者会上对扎卡里亚发出了邀请。费加罗报称，她可能会在11月陪同特朗普前往中国访问。今年9月，特朗普和习近平在华盛顿举行的峰会上讨论了人工智能、贸易问题、伊朗战争等。双方确认，将在今年再次会面。 费加罗报指出，现年41岁的凯蒂·扎卡里亚曾经在2010年代初在中国生活过。她在刚刚过去的星期四播出的一则采访中宣布，她在中国生活的时候，中国没有“真正的厕所”。扎卡里亚刚刚被特朗普任命，任命没多久就已经受到了批评，前一日爆出已不再任发言人一职。她被指在没有律师资格的情况下，自称为律师。有关中国，她表示，“（当时）所有人都在对我们反复说，希拉里（克林顿）会赢、美国的黄金时代、美国的光荣都已经结束了、中国将会崛起”…她表示，自己对这些信息记得非常清楚。但她当时刚从中国回来，于是认为，“中国怎么可能成为下一个崛起的国家呢？他们甚至没有真正的厕所”。 此外，费加罗报还报道称，凯蒂·扎卡里亚经常在社交网络和媒体频道上自诩为律师。但“没有任何迹象表明她在加州佩波代大学拿到法律学位后，曾成功考下美国律师资格证”。几天前，她表示，自己曾经报名参加律师资格证的考试，但“接下来因为需要搬到中国和配偶团聚，因此分了心、不堪重负”。 费加罗报还关注了中国宣布正在考虑对人工智能相关的部分技术、生物技术、太阳能相关技术实施出口管制一事。当中指出，中国和美国正在就技术创新展开激烈竞争。在这一背景下，双方互相指责彼此盗取人工智能相关技术。 中国商务部日前公布了一项草案，当中规定，“禁止出口14项技术”。受禁止的技术包括“利用人工智能生成、修改恶意代码”，“使用中国的战略性和敏感数据训练的人工智能模型”。该文件还建议，对另外26项技术的出口进行限制，其中包括有可能被用于数据入侵的技术。 费加罗报还关注到，中国商务部在另一份声明中，对上述限制性提议背后的理由做了阐释。当中指出，“与人工智能相关的各种固有风险以及衍生风险，正受到世界各国的高度关注”。中国政府正在实施的，是“必要的监管”，为的是防止这些技术被滥用、或被用于恶意的目的。相关草案刚刚进入了为期一个月的大众咨询窗口期。 经济类回声报则大篇幅关注了欧洲准备加强针对中国的贸易防御，先是汽车，现在是化工行业。当中报道称，欧盟不愿触发和中国爆发贸易战。在这一前提下，欧盟认为，保护自身免受中国进口浪潮冲击的办法，就是团结起来，开发新的贸易政策性工具，“纠正全球宏观经济的失衡”。年底之前，欧委会需要对这一“新的工具”进行更详尽的开发和阐释。回声报称，本周四和周五的欧洲理事会会议上，人们并没有明确提到中国。“但显然，针对的就是中国”。欧盟对华贸易逆差天天超10亿欧元，而且仍在以前所未有的速度持续扩大着。 10月初，欧盟促请中方同意限制向欧洲出口电动汽车。现在，欧洲还希望把这种限制，扩展到其他行业。法国特别提到了化工、塑料、机床以及金属硅等行业。其他国家也提到了医疗设备等相关领域。回声报指出，在这些行业中，中国企业近年来已取得了主导性的地位。 不过，中国商务部近期强调，“欧洲不应该幻想，通过施加压力就能获得好处，也不能低估中国保护自身利益的决心和能力”。 在法德敦促下，回声报认为，包括那些历来不愿限制对华自由贸易的国家，也开始加入对华贸易限制性自我防卫机制的开创倡议。回声报引述欧洲对外关系委员会的安德鲁·斯莫尔的分析称：“如今欧洲人认识到，中国构成的是一个系统结构性的问题，而不是仅仅影响少数几个工业部门而已”。 作者： 呢喃

## Details

Four different teachers will rotate talks with a Dharma talk, meditation, sutra, and metta practices. 🙏

>>>> ZOOM ID/Link <<<<
[https://us02web.zoom.us/j/5093952030](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/5093952030)

All are welcome to be a part of our evening service. Experience not necessary. Those of any faith or lack thereof are welcome. All that is required is an open mind to learn how to promote wellness, happiness, love, and peace to oneself and all sentient beings. Typically a service will include the following:

*   Check in. (How you’re doing.)
*   Silent meditation, seated on cushion, chair, or one of the pews.
*   Dharma talk from either Thay Kozen or one of five other teachers. (Buddhist teaching on how to alleviate suffering and promote happiness and peace.)
*   Metta practice. (Loving kindness.)
*   Sutra recitation and discussion. (Sutras are the written Dharma teachings.)
*   Much love and laughter.

summary: **6:00 - 7:00 pm (EST) AND 7:15 - 8:15 pm (EST), weekly on Monday in the HEALING room at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd, The Mezzanine Suite 228 in Mt. Pleasant. We have a NEW dedicated space for private WellBEing sessions in the HEALING ro
content:
**6:00 - 7:00 pm (EST) AND 7:15 - 8:15 pm (EST), weekly on Monday in the HEALING room at bliss, 1007 Johnnie Dodds Blvd, The Mezzanine Suite 228 in Mt. Pleasant. We have a NEW dedicated space for private WellBEing sessions in the HEALING room at bliss available M-SU 8AM-8PM. We have implemented an in-house scheduling calendar that Practitioners may reference to determine an available mutually beneficial time if the recommended time below is not convenient for you.**

**This is a private 1-hour session. Please RSVP directly to the Practitioner to book the session time and then go to [givetobliss.com](http://givetobliss.com/) to make a $33 donation via VENMO (no fees), PayPal or credit card. Thank you!**

**Reiki** is a Japanese energy healing technique developed in the early 1900’s by Mikao Usui to stimulate health and vitality through channeling life force energy. While promoting a deep state of relaxation, Reiki therapy may reduce stress, anxiety, and pain through gentle touch and transferring of energy. The practitioner delivers this energy through their hands to assist in improving the recipients biofield flow and balance on the physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual levels. By having a tranquil effect on the mind and body, Reiki promotes healing and restoration while having a favorable influence on the parasympathetic and autonomic nervous systems.

**Access Bars** was developed by Gary Douglas as a set of tools and processes applied to facilitate more consciousness. As a restorative modality, Access Bars involves the practitioner connecting with 32 points on participants head through gentle touch. This contact facilitates the release of negative energetic thought forms, ideas, beliefs, emotions, and considerations that create barriers. As energetic blockages are discharged, a rebalancing occurs making room for improved thought patterns. Results may include a more peaceful mind, relaxed body, improved outlook, stress relief, more energy, and feeling replenished. Measurements of electrical activity of the brain conducted after an Access Bars treatment were shown to have literally calmed brain activity down.

**Facilitator: Lisa Ann Helmly,MS,RDN,LDN, [lisa@lisahelmly.com**](http://lisa@lisahelmly.com**/)

*   Holy Fire III/Karuna Reiki Master
*   Certified Kundalini Reiki Practitioner
*   Certified Access Bars Practitioner
*   Passionate about inspiring people to optimize their health and wellbeing.
*   Small changes yield big results.

As a Low Country Native, Lisa is enthused to share complimentary integrated healing and restorative modalities to promote optimal health and well-being. Holding a Bachelor of Arts in Business Administration equipped Lisa to gain experience in the corporate environment, flip residential housing properties, and continue managing her rental property business. Completing a Master of Science in Nutrition as a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist prepared Lisa for working in the medical sector assisting patients with a variety of illnesses, disease states, and conditions. During this time to the present, Lisa pursued further studies in alternative and integrative health practices attaining multiple credentials. While working in these areas, Lisa continued serving in her roles as a mother, daughter, sister, and friend.

**Sounds Productive Right? Does Being More Productive Support Health and Well-Being?**

“Getting busier does not necessarily make you better…affectively managing your stress does!”

You really didn’t think all of that activity was done perfectly with complete ease and grace, did you? Of course not. As Lisa was stressed out creating elevated levels of cortisol and adrenaline, this lack of balance was in opposition to a positive state of health and well-being. How ironic is that behavior? Lisa more fully understands how stress and being out of balance can have a negative impact on the mind and body. Sometimes the vehicle that drives a person to do, may eventually run them over. Hypothetically speaking, imagine being in a hit and run accident driven by yourself in your very own car. Can you relate now? The coping mechanism of burning the candle at both ends is comfortable because it is familiar. However, the candle may eventually burn out.
 If there is one commonality that we all have in this human experience, it’s managing our own life stressors. Add a dose or two of trauma along the way and what do you get…**Amplified Stress with Triggers.** The well-being sessions are offered here for interested participants to explore complementary and integrative approaches on processing and managing stress to ultimately feel and function better. You are invited to take this peaceful exploration on optimizing your own health and happiness.

title: Energy transition faces critical-minerals crunch by 2035: report
zh_title: 报告称，到 2035 年，能源转型将面临关键矿产短缺
summary: GEM Mining Consulting 表示，到 2035 年，能源转型将面临关键矿产紧缩，这种紧缩超出了矿商所能开采的材料量，因为加工瓶颈和不可靠的项目预测威胁着供应。这家总部位于智利圣地亚哥的咨询公司估计，到 2035 年，预计供应量只能满足锂需求的 68%，而钴和铜的需求分别为 74% 和 75%。然而，预计产量似乎更为充足的石墨和稀土面临着更大的供应链风险，因为加工能力主要集中在中国。 “储备金变得具有战略意义
content:
GEM Mining Consulting 表示，到 2035 年，能源转型将面临关键矿产紧缩，这种紧缩超出了矿商所能开采的材料量，因为加工瓶颈和不可靠的项目预测威胁着供应。这家总部位于智利圣地亚哥的咨询公司估计，到 2035 年，预计供应量只能满足锂需求的 68%，而钴和铜的需求分别为 74% 和 75%。然而，预计产量似乎更为充足的石墨和稀土面临着更大的供应链风险，因为加工能力主要集中在中国。 GEM 在报告中表示：“只有当储备能够通过弹性供应链融资、许可、开采、加工、合格和交付时，它才具有战略意义。”该分析对评估矿产安全的常用方法提出了挑战：将公布的采矿能力与预计需求进行比较。 GEM 认为，这些数字可能大大夸大了制造商实际可用的材料，因为矿山面临许可和融资延迟、产能问题、冶金损失和客户资格要求。供应现实 为了应对这些风险，GEM 制定了两项衡量指标：追踪供应与初级需求之间差距的数量稀缺指数，以及衡量加工集中度、技术依赖性和地理风险等因素的供应链脆弱性指数。
锂成为按数量计算最受限制的矿物，在 GEM 稀缺指数中得分为 80 分（满分 100 分）。钴得分为 65 分，而铜得分为 62 分。当考虑到供应链脆弱性时，情况会发生变化。尽管预计到 2035 年供应量将分别满足其需求的 107% 和 96%，但稀土磁体在 GEM 的脆弱性指数中得分为 95 分（满分 100 分），电池级石墨得分为 89 分。由 Gem Consulting 提供。钴的脆性得分为 78，而镍则达到 66，因为加工集中在印度尼西亚和中国。尽管铜的实物短缺迫在眉睫，但其得分相对较低，为 36。这种区别意味着最大的矿山供应赤字不一定是最大的战略脆弱性。对于锂、钴和铜，GEM 认为首要任务是让可靠的新矿生产投入运营。对于石墨和稀土来说，在主要生产国之外实现炼油和加工多元化更为重要。稀土就说明了这个问题。 GEM 估计，中国以外的多元化磁体供应仅能满足全球需求的 15%，即使全球总产量看起来足够，消费者也将面临风险。 GEM 表示，公布的项目产能也会给政策制定者和投资者带来对未来矿产供应量的误导性印象。
该咨询公司计算出，一个设计年产量为 10 万吨的假设项目在对开发和运营风险进行调整后，最终只能提供约 60,200 吨可靠的可销售产量，减少了近 40%。损失可能会在整个项目的开发和生产链中累积。许可和融资可能会推迟建设，调试可能会推迟产量，矿山需要时间才能达到铭牌产能，冶金回收会减少生产的可用材料量。离开加工厂的材料可能面临另一个障碍：满足电池、磁铁和其他制造商要求的化学和技术规格。由宝石咨询公司提供。研究结果表明政府

【原文 English Original】
The energy transition faces a critical-minerals crunch by 2035 that extends beyond how much material miners can extract, as processing bottlenecks and unreliable project forecasts threaten supplies, according to GEM Mining Consulting. The Santiago, Chile-based consultancy estimates projected supply will meet just 68% of lithium demand in 2035, compared with 74% for cobalt and 75% for copper. Yet graphite and rare earths, where projected volumes appear more adequate, face greater supply-chain risks because processing capacity is heavily concentrated in China. “A reserve becomes strategically relevant only when it can be financed, permitted, extracted, processed, qualified and delivered through a resilient supply chain,” GEM said in its report. The analysis challenges a common way of assessing mineral security: comparing announced mining capacity with projected demand. GEM argues that those figures can substantially overstate the material actually available to manufacturers because mines face permitting and financing delays, ramp-up problems, metallurgical losses and customer qualification requirements. Supply reality To account for those risks, GEM developed two measures: a Volume Scarcity Index tracking the gap between supply and primary demand, and a Supply Chain Fragility Index measuring factors including processing concentration, technological dependence and geographic risk. Lithium emerges as the most constrained mineral by volume, scoring 80 out of 100 on GEM’s scarcity index. Cobalt scores 65, while copper registers 62. The picture changes when supply-chain vulnerability is considered. Rare-earth magnets score 95 out of 100 on GEM’s fragility index and battery-grade graphite scores 89, despite projected supply covering 107% and 96% of their respective demand in 2035. Courtesy of Gem Consulting. Cobalt scores 78 for fragility, while nickel reaches 66 because processing is concentrated in Indonesia and China. Copper, despite its looming physical deficit, scores a comparatively low 36. That distinction means the biggest mine-supply deficit is not necessarily the greatest strategic vulnerability. For lithium, cobalt and copper, GEM sees the priority as bringing dependable new mine production into operation. For graphite and rare earths, diversifying refining and processing outside dominant producing countries is more important. Rare earths illustrate the problem. GEM estimates diversified magnet supply outside China would cover only 15% of global demand, leaving consumers exposed even if aggregate worldwide production appears sufficient. Capacity gap Announced project capacity can also give policymakers and investors a misleading impression of future mineral availability, GEM said. The consultancy calculates that a hypothetical project designed to produce 100,000 tonnes annually may ultimately provide only about 60,200 tonnes of reliable, saleable output after adjusting for development and operating risks — a reduction of nearly 40%. The losses can accumulate throughout a project’s development and production chain. Permitting and financing can delay construction, commissioning can push back output, mines need time to reach nameplate capacity and metallurgical recoveries reduce the amount of usable material produced. Material that leaves a processing plant may face another hurdle: meeting the chemical and technical specifications required by battery, magnet and other manufacturers. Courtesy of Gem Consulting. The findings suggest governments seeking secure critical-mineral supplies may need to look beyond headline resource estimates or planned mine capacity. Processing infrastructure, financing, permitting, technical performance and the ability to deliver qualified material all determine whether underground resources become usable supply. For miners and investors, GEM argues that this changes how projects should be valued. A smaller deposit with proven processing, infrastructure and customers may carry greater strategic importance than a much larger resource without a reliable route to market. The energy transition’s mineral race, in other words, may be decided as much by what happens after the ore leaves the ground as by how much miners can extract.

title: HKIC shifts AI investment focus to downstream applications; BOC Investment eyes cross-border industrialisation
zh_title: HKIC将人工智能投资重点转向下游应用；中银投资着眼跨境工业化
summary: 人工智能 HKIC 表示，其超过 70% 的资本都针对早期和成长期公司，250 家投资组合公司中有 11 家在香港上市，今年计划上市的公司有 30 多家。其首席执行官概述了人工智能应用和开源创新的重点。中银投资计划跨境工业化 [![图 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:17 HKT · 2 分钟读香港投资公司 (HKIC) 行政总裁 C
content:
人工智能
HKIC 表示，其超过 70% 的资本都针对早期和成长阶段的公司，250 家投资组合公司中有 11 家在香港上市，今年还有 30 多家计划上市。其首席执行官概述了人工智能应用和开源创新的重点。中银投资计划跨境产业化

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 15 日 13:17 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港投资公司（HKIC）行政总裁陈嘉敏表示，公司70%以上的资金投放于早期和成长期的企业，目前投资已初见成效。她在活动上表示，在250个投资项目中，已有11家公司已在香港上市，超过30家公司计划今年上市或提交上市申请。

陈表示，未来的技术应该满足不同人群的需求，易于获取且价格实惠。以人工智能为例，她表示HKIC正在逐步将投资重点转向人工智能价值链的中下游部分，包括实际应用场景。她强调了对开源人工智能的特别关注，她说开源人工智能可以显着降低创新成本，让年轻一代和小型初创企业能够快速创新、蓬勃发展和竞争。
中银集团投资副总裁王军在同场活动中表示，公司正在实施以早期投资、小额投资和硬技术投资为重点的转型战略，以支持香港的研究成果商业化。他表示，该公司已投资超过10只科技基金和9个香港科技项目，重点关注人工智能、生物材料制造和新材料等领域。

王先生表示，中银投资将优先选择香港特区政府支持的项目，并积极探索香港科研与大湾区转型相结合的跨境产业化路径。他主张推广香港研发、内地验证的模式。

王毅表示，中银投作为立足香港的全球投资平台，将发挥国家风险资本、耐心资本和长期资本的作用。他表示，公司在能源、航空、半导体、先进制造等领域投资了一批行业影响力大、金额大、回报丰厚的重大项目。三年来，大湾区科技贷款已突破7000亿元。
王强调，公司将利用全球机构网络和跨境金融服务，助力科技走出去，推动科技创新链与制造产业链无缝对接。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

【原文 English Original】
Artificial Intelligence
HKIC says over 70 per cent of its capital targets early and growth-stage firms, with 11 of 250 portfolio companies listed in Hong Kong and over 30 planning listings this year. Its CEO outlined a pivot to AI applications and open-source innovation. BOC Investment plans cross-border industrialisation

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 13:17 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong Investment Corporation (HKIC) Chief Executive Clara Chan said more than 70 per cent of the company's capital is placed in enterprises at early and growth stages, and the investments are already showing results. Speaking at an event, she said that among 250 portfolio projects, 11 companies have listed in Hong Kong, and over 30 plan to list or submit listing applications this year.

Chan said future technology should serve the needs of different groups of people, be easy to access and affordable. Taking artificial intelligence as an example, she said HKIC is gradually shifting its investment focus to the middle and downstream parts of the AI value chain, including practical application scenarios. She highlighted particular attention to open-source AI, which she said can significantly lower innovation costs and allow younger generations and small startups to innovate quickly, thrive and compete.

Wang Jun, deputy chief executive of BOC Group Investment, said at the same event that the company is implementing a transformation strategy focused on investing early, investing small and investing in hard technology, to support the commercialisation of research in Hong Kong. He said the firm has invested in more than 10 technology funds and nine Hong Kong technology projects, focusing on sectors including artificial intelligence, biomaterials manufacturing and new materials.

Wang said BOC Investment will give priority to projects supported by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government and is actively exploring a cross-border industrialisation pathway that combines Hong Kong research with Greater Bay Area conversion. He argued for promoting a model of Hong Kong research and development with mainland verification.

As a global investment platform based in Hong Kong, Wang said BOC Investment will play the role of national risk capital, patient capital and long-term capital. He said the firm has invested in a number of major projects with significant industry influence, large amounts and attractive returns in energy, aviation, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing. Over the past three years, technology loans in the Greater Bay Area have exceeded 700 billion yuan.

Wang stressed that the company will use its global institutional network and cross-border financial services to help technology go global, and promote seamless connection between the technology innovation chain and the manufacturing industry chain.

## Details

I have lived in 6 countries, traveled to 45 and all 7 continents, and checked everything off my very extensive travel bucket list by the age of 36.

Ask me anything.

Whether you would like to travel more, are itching to live the digital nomad life, or just want to hear some cool stories from around the globe, join me to chat about life, travel, and the pursuit of happiness.

If you’d like to know more about me and my story in the meantime, check out [https://www.nicoleelysejourneys.com](https://www.nicoleelysejourneys.com/) and my talk on “Why getting robbed at gunpoint in Colombia is the best thing that’s ever happened to me.”

This is not a sales pitch. I do do travel coaching if you want more targeted help getting started, but that’s not what we’re here to talk about. I just like meeting fellow travelers and wannabe travelers.

# Support Pie Formosa’s Independent Work

I sometimes describe myself as a refugee from WeChat to Instagram — but I am also, quite literally, a refugee from China. I am a political dissident, human rights activist, non-binary person and independent writer living with invisible disabilities, now continuing my work in Europe. I write and create public work about censorship, authoritarianism, political memory, democracy, queer and trans freedom, refugee experiences, neurodiversity, and the cultural spaces where resistance survives. For years, WeChat was one of the places where I published my work. Readers could easily support independent creators with small tips. Then the Chinese Communist Party shut down my account. I lost not only a platform, but also an audience, an archive, and a simple way for people to support my work. This fundraiser is part of rebuilding that independence. Living with invisible disabilities also means that conventional employment structures and constant high-intensity workloads are not always accessible or sustainable for me. I need a modest and stable income to make independent research, writing and human-rights work sustainable. Your support will help cover: * research, writing and documentation * travel to human-rights, democracy and civil-society events * digital tools and publishing costs * accessibility-related working needs * basic living costs that allow me to continue this work independently My first goal is €3,500. If something I have written, documented or created has informed, helped or inspired you, even €1, €5 or €10 helps me keep this work alive. If donating is not possible, sharing this fundraiser also makes a real difference. Authoritarianism depends on silence and forgetting. Independent voices survive because people choose to keep them alive. Thank you for supporting my work. Pie Formosa (they/them) https://linktr.ee/pieformosa

**Alan Wan**

Dear Friends,

My name is Alan, and I am writing this with a sincere and humble heart.

I am a Chinese political dissident living in Houston, Texas. Because of my beliefs and my willingness to speak openly about freedom, human rights, and justice, I have faced serious threats and intimidation from the Chinese government. These pressures have made it impossible for me to safely return to China, where my family still lives. Every day, I carry the pain of being separated from my loved ones, uncertain when—or if—I will ever be able to reunite with them again.

Beyond the emotional suffering, I am now facing severe financial hardship. Due to restrictions and complications surrounding the transfer of my personal funds from abroad, I have been unable to access resources that I once depended on for survival. My savings are rapidly disappearing, and I am now struggling simply to cover basic daily necessities such as food, housing, transportation, and medical care.

This situation has left me feeling isolated and vulnerable. I never imagined that standing by my principles would lead to such profound personal sacrifice, but I continue to hold onto hope.

Today, I am reaching out with deep humility to ask for your support. Any assistance—whether financial help, practical resources, or connections to organizations that aid individuals in political exile—would mean more than words can express. Your kindness could help me maintain stability during this incredibly difficult chapter of my life and allow me to continue moving forward with dignity.

I am not asking for luxury, only for the chance to live safely and meet my most basic needs while I navigate these extraordinary challenges.

Thank you for taking the time to read my story. Your compassion, understanding, and support would be a lifeline during one of the hardest periods of my life.

With deepest gratitude,

Alan

Momo Crawlers, we’re asking for your help.

The disaster at the Nepal-Tibet border has left thousands displaced from their homes, and the full scope of the crisis is still being realized. Many Momo Crawl vendors and volunteers remain concerned for loved ones who are still missing.

Through friends and family, we’ve established contact with mutual aid networks on the ground in Nepal. They are also providing us with live updates on the aid groups they’re seeing, what those groups are accomplishing, and where additional support is most needed.

Our plan is to allocate funds according to the feedback we receive from our contacts in Nepal. In addition to mutual aid groups and NGOs, we anticipate directing a significant portion of proceeds to the Nepali government’s [Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund](https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np/). This fund accepts digital payments, and we encourage you to donate directly if you prefer: [](https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np/)[https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np](https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np/)

We established this GoFundMe primarily for ease of use and to help us track the impact of the Momo Crawl community. We expect to keep the drive active until Momo Crawl on September 13th, 2026, but donations received now will be allocated to relief efforts on a rolling basis. We will share updates about the use of funds as information becomes available.

With love and gratitude,

The Momo Crawl team

**Note: This meeting is hosted on Zoom, please RSVP for the passcode.**

Some of the activities we may do include:

*   Watch Korean videos with English captions.
*   Translate Korean blog posts/news articles to English.
*   General discussion.

The meeting is scheduled for every week, but feel free to attend when you can.

title: 62 岁华人母亲因长期照护压力崩溃，杀害 25 岁自闭症儿子后跳桥
summary: 纽约皇后区近日发生一起令人震惊的家庭悲剧。 一名患有严重自闭症、无法通过语言交流的25岁华裔男子，在其25岁生日当天被父亲发现陈尸家中，颈部及手腕有多处致命刀伤。而就在遗体被发现前数小时，其母亲被发现重伤倒卧于高速公路桥下。 警方目前正全力调查两起事件的关联，并怀疑妈妈可能涉嫌杀害儿子后企图自杀。 案发于10月14日上午8时55分左右。警方接获911报警后赶往皇后区木边（Woodside）59街的一处公寓，发现25岁的华裔男子黄布莱恩（Bryan Wong）倒卧在客厅的沙发床
content: 纽约皇后区近日发生一起令人震惊的家庭悲剧。 一名患有严重自闭症、无法通过语言交流的25岁华裔男子，在其25岁生日当天被父亲发现陈尸家中，颈部及手腕有多处致命刀伤。而就在遗体被发现前数小时，其母亲被发现重伤倒卧于高速公路桥下。 警方目前正全力调查两起事件的关联，并怀疑妈妈可能涉嫌杀害儿子后企图自杀。 案发于10月14日上午8时55分左右。警方接获911报警后赶往皇后区木边（Woodside）59街的一处公寓，发现25岁的华裔男子黄布莱恩（Bryan Wong）倒卧在客厅的沙发床上，身上有多处严重外伤，现场急救人员赶到后当场宣布其死亡。 令人无比痛心的是，10月14日恰好是Bryan的25岁生日。警方确认，Bryan患有严重自闭症且无语言能力，平时生活完全依赖家人照料。 事发当天，Bryan的父亲回家后目睹了这一惨状并迅速报警。 警方在案发现场搜获了数把刀具，并在客厅发现了一封疑似遗书的纸条。警方虽然尚未正式公布遗书的具体内容，但执法部门消息人士透漏，该纸条疑似由其母亲留下的绝笔信。 就在Bryan的遗体被发现前约5小时，即10月14日凌晨4点左右，警方曾在范威克高速公路（Van Wyck Expressway）下方的 Harper Street 发现一名重伤倒地的62岁女子。该女子骨盆及双腿多处骨折，随后被送往纽约长老会皇后医院抢救。警方初步判断，其伤势系从高速公路高架桥跳下所致。 调查人员很快证实，这名重伤女子正是Bryan的母亲，也是长期以来负责照料他日常起居的主要照顾者。 据执法部门消息，调查人员目前正将此案朝“杀人后企图自杀”（Murder-Suicide）的方向进行深入调查。10月15日，纽约市法医办公室已正式将Bryan的死因定性为他杀（Homicide）。 这起惨剧让周围的邻居感到难以置信。 据了解， Bryan一家来自中国香港，已经在当地生活多年。邻居们形容，这家人平日里十分安静有礼，从来没有听到过争吵声，与周围相处融洽。 不少看着Bryan长大的邻居回忆，其母亲平时非常爱护儿子，经常带他去附近的公园散步，但近年来母亲看起来越来越憔悴和疲惫，似乎承受着常人难以想象的照料压力。 这起发生在华裔家庭的悲剧，也让社区再次聚焦于特殊需求家庭（Special Needs Families）长期面临的绝境与心理危机。 华策会皇后区特需家庭服务部相关专家指出，长期照顾患有严重残疾或自闭症的成年子女，往往会让家长在生理、经济和心理上面临三重极限挤压。 特别是当特殊需求儿童成年、脱离了学校体系的公共资源支持后，许多家庭会陷入极度的孤立与无助中。照顾者若长期缺乏喘息时间（Respite Care）与心理干预，极易萌生绝望情绪。 一个年轻的生命在生日当天戛然而止，留下的是一个支离破碎的家庭，以及对特殊照顾者心理健康支持机制的深刻拷问。

summary: 引自 https://www.instagram.com/p/DeixtHwk_qg/ IG: @hkhrftw : 當香港的人權狀況每況愈下，極權政府甚至將打壓的黑手伸向其他民主國家，試圖噤聲海外的異見者。作為自由的捍衛者，我們必須做得更多。我們有責任讓大眾看見極權打壓的真實面貌，並喚醒社會的關注，共同守護我們目前所身處、得來不易的自由國度。 為了讓這段歷史與抗爭精神不被抹煞，「第三屆香港人權作品展（高雄站）」正式登場。本次展覽以宏觀與微觀的雙重奏視角，透過雙展場同步呈現，
content:
引自 https://www.instagram.com/p/DeixtHwk_qg/ IG: @hkhrftw :

當香港的人權狀況每況愈下，極權政府甚至將打壓的黑手伸向其他民主國家，試圖噤聲海外的異見者。作為自由的捍衛者，我們必須做得更多。我們有責任讓大眾看見極權打壓的真實面貌，並喚醒社會的關注，共同守護我們目前所身處、得來不易的自由國度。

為了讓這段歷史與抗爭精神不被抹煞，「第三屆香港人權作品展（高雄站）」正式登場。本次展覽以宏觀與微觀的雙重奏視角，透過雙展場同步呈現，深刻串連起香港抗爭的集體記憶與個人經驗：

高雄歷史博物館匯聚特邀藝術家與公開徵件的得獎作品，勾勒出時代的輪廓；明德新村則延伸展出香港政治犯的獄中書信，以及首獎得主劉學成精緻的木雕創作，引領觀眾立體感受抗爭者的內心世界。

現場亦同時展出一批珍貴畫作——包含繪於《蘋果日報》上的政治人物肖像，以及多部在港遭禁的書籍。

雙展區相互呼應，讓觀眾在理解歷史脈絡之餘，也能透過創作、書信與禁書，貼近高牆內的生命經驗，進而反思言論與出版自由面臨的嚴峻限制。

【展覽資訊】
展區一：明德新村 轉角壹貳壹
* 地址： 高雄左營區明德新村12-1號
* 展期： 2026年11月8日 至 2027年1月10日
* 時間： 星期二至五 11:00-17:00 ｜ 星期六及日 10:00-18:00
展區二：高雄歷史博物館
* 地址： 高雄市鹽埕區中正四路272號
* 展期： 2026年11月15日 至 2027年1月10日
* 時間： 星期二至日 10:00-17:00

合辦組織： 香港人權陣線、華人民主書院協會

自由需要每個人共同發聲與守護，誠摯邀請您走入展場，與我們一同見證並延續這份不屈的意志。

title: Songwriter Support Group - Zoom Edition, Wed, Oct 21, 2026, 7:00 PM   | Meetup
summary: Hello songwriters! We are continuing our Songwriter Support Group over Zoom and hope you will join us! This is a great chance to connect with fellow songwriters and hear what others are creating. And, as we have discovered over the past yea
content:
Hello songwriters!

We are continuing our Songwriter Support Group over Zoom and hope you will join us! This is a great chance to connect with fellow songwriters and hear what others are creating. And, as we have discovered over the past year, you can log in and share from almost anywhere!

The Zoom room will open at 6:50pm and we will start promptly at 7:00pm. Plan to login at least a couple minutes early to make sure you are there for the start of the meeting. We will post the Zoom link a day or two before the meeting.

Please read the "Virtual Rules" below as there are some minor and important requirements in order for you to participate and for this to be effective. Also, if you are new, please make certain your meetup setting allows you to receive private messages as that is how I communicate initially. If you have it turned off, you WILL NOT BE ABLE TO RECEIVE MESSAGES AND I WILL REMOVE YOU FROM THE LIST TO ALLOW A WAITLISTED MEMBER TO ATTEND.

Looking forward to hearing your beautiful songs.

The requirements for your song:

A) Have your lyrics ready to share with the group. This can be done by sharing your computer screen or pasting your lyrics into the chat. If you have any questions, please send us a note and we'll be happy to help out.

B) You need to be able to perform it live OR have a recording of it that you can play over Zoom. If you have questions about this please contact me at least 48 hours ahead of the meeting.

Also…

Tell us what you’d like critiques of and we’ll verbally discuss only what each writer would like to hear about. It's not up to anyone in the group to make value judgements on anyone's work (it's good, it's not good). We're here to consider our songs from where they're at, with respect to the artistic work we're helping to nurture and grow.

The event is limited to 11 people. You must stay for the duration of the event as you would if you came in person. After 11 have signed up, a ‘yes’ rsvp goes on a wait list, so please don't RSVP yes to hold a spot if it's only a 50-50 chance you'll make it. NO SHOWS AND LAST MINUTE CANCELS WILL NOT HAVE PRIORITY FOR FUTURE CIRCLES.

New people and all genres and levels of music are welcome!

title: Why is retirement boring?
summary: FOR most Filipinos, retirement is something we look forward to. After decades of working, raising a family, paying the bills and meeting deadlines, we see retirement as a reward. No more alarm clocks. No more traffic. No more office politic
content:
FOR most Filipinos, retirement is something we look forward to. After decades of working, raising a family, paying the bills and meeting deadlines, we see retirement as a reward. No more alarm clocks. No more traffic. No more office politics. Finally, we can sleep late, travel, enjoy hobbies, spend time with our family and do the things we never had time to do.

That was exactly how Miguel imagined his retirement.

At 62, after almost four decades of chasing business goals, Miguel was ready. He had saved enough to feel reasonably comfortable. His children were grown, his house was fully paid and he had been looking forward to retirement for years.

“I can finally enjoy life,” he told his friends.

During the first few months, he did. He played golf during weekdays, watched movies and enjoyed leisurely breakfasts with his wife. They went on trips. He visited friends. For the first time in many years, he had nowhere he needed to be.

Get the latest news
 delivered to your inbox

Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters

By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the [Terms of Service](https://manilatimes.net/terms-of-service "Terms of Service") and [Privacy Policy](https://manilatimes.net/privacy-policy "Privacy Policy").

It was wonderful. Until it wasn’t.

After a while, the days began to look the same. Monday no longer felt different from Saturday. His golf games became routine. Some of his friends were still working, while his children were busy with their own careers. His wife had her own activities and interests.

One morning, Miguel woke up and realized something uncomfortable. He had plenty of time, but he didn’t know what to do with it.

Miguel was bored. This may sound surprising. After all, isn’t having more free time what we all dream about? But perhaps we have misunderstood retirement.

We often think of work as something that takes time away from us. We forget that work also gives us many things beyond a salary. It gives us purpose, people and structure. It gives us responsibilities, relationships and a sense of achievement. It makes us feel that we are valued.

For 40 years, Miguel knew what he was supposed to do every Monday morning. People depended on him. He had colleagues to talk to, problems to solve and goals to achieve.

Then, suddenly, all of that disappeared.

Miguel had prepared to retire from work. He had not prepared to retire to something.

This is an important lesson in retirement planning.

We spend years asking, “How much money do I need to retire?” That is certainly an important question. We need enough money to pay for food, housing, health care, travel and the many years that may lie ahead.

We have become very good at calculating how much money we need to retire, and surprisingly, poor at imagining what we will retire to.

AARP, the American Association of Retired Persons, reported in a US study that 14 percent of retirees felt bored, while 13 percent felt isolated and another 13 percent lacked a sense of purpose. These figures are not representative of Filipino retirees, but they point to a challenge we should not ignore: Financial security alone does not guarantee a fulfilling retirement.

We should also ask: What will I do with my time? Who will I spend it with? What will give me a reason to get up in the morning?

Retirement does not have to mean doing nothing. A fulfilling retirement may require us to become more intentional about how we spend our time.

For some, it may mean mentoring younger people. After decades of experience, retirees have something valuable to give. For others, it may mean volunteering, teaching, joining a church organization or supporting a cause close to their hearts.

For some, retirement may be the opportunity to finally pursue a passion postponed because of work and family responsibilities — painting, writing, traveling or learning something completely new.

And for others, retirement may include working, but on their own terms. Part-time consulting, entrepreneurship or board work can provide both income and purpose, without the demands of a full-time career.

Relationships also matter.

During our working years, we often have hundreds of people around us. Then retirement comes and that circle suddenly becomes smaller. Our children may live in another country. Friends may still be working. Some relationships may have faded simply because schedules no longer align.

For Filipinos, there is an added reality. We naturally look to our children and grandchildren as an important part of our later years. But our children have their own careers, families and responsibilities. They can enrich our retirement, but they cannot be our entire retirement plan.

That is why we should build our social life before retirement, not wait until after we retire.

We also need structure. Freedom sounds wonderful, but too much unstructured time can become difficult. A retirement filled with exercise, family, friends, learning, hobbies, travel, service and rest can feel very different from simply having nothing to do.

This is the irony of retirement, we spend our working lives wishing we had more time, and when we finally get it, we discover that time itself needs to be planned.

Miguel eventually understood this.

He did not need another full-time job. He needed a reason to look forward to Monday.

He began mentoring younger professionals. He volunteered with a church organization. He committed to exercising regularly and made time for his family. He continued playing golf, but it became only one part of his retirement rather than the whole of it.

Slowly, retirement became interesting again.

Miguel’s experience reminds us that retirement planning should not begin and end with money.

Yes, we need to know whether our savings and investments can support us for the rest of our lives. But we also need to prepare for the life we want to live when the paycheck stops.

We should ask ourselves: What am I retiring to?

Because it is possible to have enough money and still have an empty retirement. It is possible to have financial security but no sense of purpose. It is possible to have all the time in the world and still wonder what to do with it.

Retirement should not simply be the end of our working years. It should be the beginning of a new chapter where we have greater freedom to choose how we spend our time, whom we serve and what gives our life meaning.

So, before you retire, don’t just plan your finances. Plan your life.

Because someday, you will retire. And when that day comes, the question may not be, “Do I have enough money?”

It may be an even more important one: “What will I do with all this time?”

content: 巴黎的示威活动在过去一个月中升级。 (路透社：Abdul Saboor) 抗议活动席卷欧洲，数十万人在欧洲大陆的数十个城市走上街头。 最初的示威活动始于上个月在法国，此后，骚乱已蔓延至六个国家。 虽然存在一些共同的抱怨（特别是生活成本），但问题也会因地点不同而有显著差异。 巴黎和里尔部分地区已宣布宵禁，因为一些集会演变为暴力，导致数百人被捕，并造成商店和公共建筑的广泛破坏。 现在，分析师警告称，不满情绪可能在接下来的几周内在更多国家蔓延。 以下是您需要了解的内容。 人们为何抗议？ 示威活动可以追溯到 9 月 17 日，当时巴黎东南部一所高中的教师因人员短缺问题而抗议。 随后学生也加入进来，骚乱并未花多长时间就蔓延到全国其他学校。 最初关于教育的问题已经扩大，涵盖了普遍的生活成本问题和公共部门的削减。 法国的集会变得越来越暴力，周末数万人走上街头，遍布全国。 在某些地区，商店被洗劫，历史建筑被破坏甚至纵火。 抗议者在法国各地的城市与防暴警察发生冲突，并袭击政府大楼。 法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙在周日晚上的电视讲话中谴责了“无节制的暴力”，并将责任归咎于激进左翼破坏者，他们劫持了一场拥有合理担忧的运动。 在法国抗议活动开始的同时，马德里的人们也开始示威，因为一家投资公司强行将一位居住了 70 年的老人的租金提高了 230%，并将其赶出了家。 马里卡门·阿巴斯卡尔，87 岁，在被强制从公寓中移走后两周死于医院。 骚乱已经蔓延，现在多个国家的集会正在进行。以下是首次示威活动发生的时间和地点： 这张地图显示了抗议活动规模最大的地区。 我们是如何走到这一步的？ 法国拥有欧元区第二大经济体。但政府正面临高债务、巨额预算赤字和不断上升的借贷成本。 今年，它将花费比国防或教育更多的钱来偿还债务。 虽然学校和教学资源的状态在法国一直是焦点（特别是点燃了最初的集会），但大陆各地吸引人们走上街头的问题不止一个。 大多数问题都与生活成本上升有关。以下是概述： 示威活动的影响实际上取决于您身在何处。 在法国，巴黎的官员周一鼓励其地区 counterparts 实施宵禁。与此同时，西班牙正面临 11 月 29 日的突然选举，这是首相佩德罗·桑切斯在住房改革（旨在遏制公众抗议）被立法者拒绝后不久宣布的。 阿尔巴尼亚的问题与西欧略有不同。政府腐败是吸引人们要求改变首都地拉那局势的主要原因之一，那里有政客被指控使用狡猾的手段批准与特朗普家族相关的豪华沿海开发项目。 马德里抗议者在本月初发出他们的声音。 (路透社：Violeta Santos Moura) 接下来可能发生什么？ 在法国，政府已举行危机会议，巴黎和里尔部分地区宣布宵禁。这是在抗议者承诺在未来几天升级行动之后。 该国距离总统选举不到六个月，各政党互相指责煽动暴力。 例如，极右翼政治领袖玛丽娜·勒庞将责任完全归咎于政府，称法国处于“暴力与无助之间，甚至被挟持”。 事实上，欧洲正面临一些专家所称的“超级选举周期”，这可能加剧紧张局势，因为多个国家将在未来 12 个月内进行选举。 与此同时，阿尔巴尼亚总理埃迪·拉马承诺留任，尽管面临辞职呼吁，因此那些已经使警察陷入困境的抗议活动可能会再次爆发。 意大利、葡萄牙和比利时的政府都谴责了日益增长的暴力行为，并未提供任何让步。 过去几周，希腊、奥地利、爱尔兰和德国也记录了较小的示威活动。

title: Hong Kong hairy crab shops struggle as more shoppers head north
zh_title: 随着越来越多的购物者北上，香港大闸蟹店陷入困境
summary: 香港 由于跨境购物和网上竞争，香港传统大闸蟹店的生意面临 10% 至 20% 的下降，铜锣湾一家零售商报告订单下降和游客减少。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 19 日 18:16 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 Hong香港历史悠久的大闸蟹店正面临跨境采购和网上购物日益激烈的竞争，铜锣湾零售商之一
content:
香港
由于跨境购物和网上竞争，香港传统大闸蟹店的生意面临 10% 至 20% 的下降，铜锣湾一家零售商报告订单下降和游客减少。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 19 日 18:16 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港历史悠久的大闸蟹店正面临来自跨境购买和网上购物的日益激烈的竞争，铜锣湾的一家零售商报告今年的业务下降了 10% 至 20%。

《英文虎报》的姊妹刊物《星岛头条》走访了两家传统大闸蟹店，发现随着时令美食重返市场，销量参差不齐。一家店的老板表示，今年新顾客很少，主要靠老顾客，生意比去年同期下降了10%至20%。

她表示，体型较小、价格更实惠的螃蟹销量下降了 20% 至 30%，部分原因是经济压力、网上购物以及大陆购买大闸蟹的趋势日益增长。往年旺季，有顾客订购了1000多只螃蟹作为礼物。但她表示，今年的订单数量和规模均有所下降。
她还指出，过去在离开香港之前购买螃蟹的酒店客人和游客已基本消失。十一月通常是生意最繁忙的月份，她说她有些担心销售情况。

然而，对五至六两或以上的中型螃蟹的需求保持稳定，而对较大螃蟹的订单则略有增加。重阳节前夕，该店增加了9至10两螃蟹的订单，以满足顾客寻求更丰盛的时令大餐的需求。

与此同时，另一家已经经营了50至60年的商店的老板表示，货源充足，价格与往年相似，而且质量也有所提高。他表示，该店的业务基本保持稳定，部分原因是在线销售约占其收入的 30% 至 40%。他说，虽然团体聚会的大订单已不再常见，但购买螃蟹在家吃的顾客的小订单却有所增加。

尽管越来越多的香港人前往内地购买大闸蟹，但他警告说，质量并不总是有保证。他说，香港出售的大闸蟹质量普遍较好。他补充说，大多数顾客更喜欢在购买前亲自检查螃蟹，只有在对零售商产生信心后才转向网上购买。

Hong Kong
Traditional hairy crab shops in Hong Kong face a 10 to 20 per cent drop in business due to cross-border shopping and online competition, with one Causeway Bay retailer reporting declining orders and fewer tourists.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 18:16 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong's long-established hairy crab shops are facing growing competition from cross-border purchases and online shopping, with one Causeway Bay retailer reporting a 10 to 20 per cent drop in business this year.

A visit by Sing Tao Headline, a sister publication of The Standard, to two traditional hairy crab shops found mixed sales as the seasonal delicacy returned to the market. The owner of one shop said it had attracted few new customers this year and was relying mainly on regulars, with business down 10 to 20 per cent from the same period last year.

She said sales of smaller, more affordable crabs had fallen by 20 to 30 per cent, partly due to economic pressures, online shopping and the growing trend of buying hairy crabs on the mainland. In previous peak seasons, some customers had ordered more than 1,000 crabs as gifts. But both the quantity and size of orders had declined this year, she said.

She also noted that hotel guests and tourists who used to buy crabs before leaving Hong Kong had largely disappeared. November is usually the busiest month for the business, and she said she was somewhat concerned about sales.

However, demand for medium-sized crabs weighing five to six taels or more remained stable, while orders for larger crabs had edged up. Ahead of the Chung Yeung Festival, the shop increased orders for crabs weighing nine to 10 taels to meet demand from customers seeking a more substantial seasonal feast.

Meanwhile, the owner of another shop, which has been operating for 50 to 60 years, said supplies were plentiful and prices were similar to previous years, while quality had also improved. He said the shop's business had remained broadly stable, partly because online sales accounted for around 30 to 40 per cent of its revenue. While large orders for group gatherings had become less common, smaller orders from customers buying crabs to eat at home had increased, he said.

Although more Hongkongers were heading to the mainland to buy hairy crabs, he cautioned that quality was not always guaranteed. He said hairy crabs sold in Hong Kong were generally of better quality. He added that most customers preferred to inspect crabs in person before buying, switching to online purchases only after they had developed confidence in a retailer.

香港浸会大学于 10 月 16 日至 18 日举行首届 AI-TEM 2026 会议，聚集了 200 多名国际学者，讨论人工智能的伦理挑战。该活动与波士顿大学、高丽大学和维也纳大学合作，重点关注扩大响应

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

香港时间 2026 年 10 月 19 日 22:12 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

香港浸会大学（HKBU）于10月16日至18日主办首届AI-TEM 2026：人工智能、科技与新兴媒体国际会议，云集了200多名国际学者、教师和研究生。该活动由波士顿大学、高丽大学和维也纳大学合作举办，主题是“扩展负责任的人工智能通信”。

演讲者和与会者讨论了人工智能带来的伦理挑战，包括隐藏的不平等、不平衡的采用和新形式的排斥。演讲和辩论的重点是传播研究如何帮助建立一个更具包容性和对社会有益的未来。香港浸会大学传理学院院长钟布在会议开幕式上表示：“人工智能的未来不仅仅是技术的问题，更是人类的问题。工程师可以告诉我们算法有多高效，但只有传播学者才能解释社会为何存在。
波士顿大学的 James E. Katz 强调了国际合作的重要性，并指出四所大学的目标是在快速变化的人工智能和媒体领域促进探究自由和独立思想。此次活动邀请了香港大学的 Michael Chau Chiu-lung、波士顿大学的 Yang Sung-Un、维也纳大学的 Jörg Matthes、智利天主教大学的 Ingrid Bachmann 和高丽大学的 Jennifer Ihm 等顶尖学者发表主题演讲，提供有关人工智能、传播和新兴媒体的全球视角。

一个亮点是互动会议，将来自当地几所中学的学生与国际学者联系起来。学生们就人工智能的伦理影响、其在日常生活中的作用以及对就业市场的未来影响进行了讨论，将年轻人的声音带入有关负责任人工智能的全球辩论中。会议还包括研究论文展示和三场专门小组会议。

会议结束时，香港浸会大学、波士顿大学、高丽大学和维也纳大学承诺继续合作并倡导以人为本、对社会负责的人工智能通信研究。

Hong Kong
Hong Kong Baptist University held the inaugural AI-TEM 2026 conference from October 16 to 18, gathering over 200 international scholars to discuss ethical challenges of AI. The event, in partnership with Boston University, Korea University, and the University of Vienna, focused on extending responsi

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

19 Oct 2026 at 22:12 HKT · 2 min read

Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) hosted the first AI-TEM 2026: AI, Technology & Emerging Media international conference from October 16 to 18, gathering more than 200 international scholars, faculty, and graduate students. The event, organized in partnership with Boston University, Korea University, and the University of Vienna, focused on the theme of 'Extending Responsible AI Communication'.

Speakers and participants discussed ethical challenges posed by AI, including hidden inequalities, uneven adoption, and new forms of exclusion. Presentations and debates centered on how communication research can help build a more inclusive and socially beneficial future. Zhong Bu, Dean of HKBU's School of Communication, opened the conference by stating: 'The future of AI isn't just about technology, it is a human question. Engineers can tell us how efficient an algorithm can be, but only communication scholars can explain why society exists as it does.'

James E. Katz of Boston University highlighted the importance of international collaboration, noting that the four universities aim to promote freedom of inquiry and independent thought in the rapidly changing field of AI and media. The event featured keynote presentations from leading academics including Michael Chau Chiu-lung from the University of Hong Kong, Yang Sung-Un from Boston University, Jörg Matthes from the University of Vienna, Ingrid Bachmann from the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, and Jennifer Ihm from Korea University, offering global perspectives on AI, communication, and emerging media.

A highlight was an interactive session connecting students from several local secondary schools with international scholars. Students engaged in discussions on AI's ethical implications, its role in daily life, and future implications for the job market, bringing youth voices into the global debate on responsible AI. The conference also included research paper presentations and three specialized panel sessions.

The conference concluded with HKBU, Boston University, Korea University and the University of Vienna pledging to continue their collaboration and champion research into human-centered, socially responsible AI communication.

# Sean dineen's mission to get my dissertation published

Support My Mission to Empower the Exceptionality Community As a person with cerebral palsy and many years advocating for people with exceptionalities, I’ve seen firsthand how society often dismisses their potential. Many are denied opportunities and classified in ways that stifle their growth, creating dependency instead of independence. This is not just morally unacceptable—it holds society back from innovation and progress. When my wheelchair got mislaid, I crawled through the streets. My research challenges these norms. By exploring how nondemocratic societies like Taiwan and apartheid South Africa engaged with the exceptionality community, I’ve uncovered surprising insights. These nations, despite their flaws, prioritized accessibility and genuine inclusion, consulting directly with the communities they aimed to serve. My work highlights how these approaches can inform global policies to create more inclusive and thriving societies. Now, I need your help to complete this vital research. I’ve traveled extensively, gathering data from South Africa, Australia, and the U.S. But key documents are located in one South African city, while interviews with 13 political leaders are required in another. As someone with cerebral palsy, I also need two assistants to make my travel and research possible. I’ve raised $1,500 toward my $10,000 goal, but I still need $8,500 to finish. Completing this dissertation is not just a personal milestone—it’s a step toward improving opportunities for the exceptionality community worldwide. Your support, no matter the amount, will make a difference. Together, we can replace outdated perceptions with true inclusion, unlocking the potential of millions. Thank you for joining me in this mission.

**Help Me Study Abroad in Taiwan – A Journey of Language, Culture & Growth**

Hi everyone,

I’m excited to share that I’ve been given an incredible opportunity to study abroad in Taiwan (June 3 - July 1)! This program will allow me to fully immerse myself in a new culture while studying Mandarin Chinese and engaging in meaningful cross-cultural experiences.

Studying abroad in Taiwan is more than just travel for me — it’s a chance to grow academically, professionally, and personally.

Why Taiwan?

Taiwan is known for its rich history and welcoming communities. By living and studying there, I will:

Strengthen my Mandarin Chinese language skills

Build cross-cultural communication skills

Study alongside local and international students

Experience Taiwanese traditions, festivals, and daily life firsthand

Develop independence, adaptability, and global awareness

**Why I’m Fundraising**

While I’ve worked hard to prepare for this opportunity, studying abroad comes with significant expenses, including:

Program tuition and fees

Housing

Flights

Cultural excursions and educational activities

Any contribution — big or small — will help make this life-changing experience possible.

**Your support is not just helping me travel — you are investing in my education, personal growth, and future.** I’m so grateful for any encouragement, donations, or shares. I can’t wait to share updates, photos, and stories from Taiwan along the way! Thank you for being part of this journey with me!

title: Volta doubles Springer rare earths, eyes 2027 study
zh_title: Volta 将 Springer 稀土产量翻倍，着眼 2027 年研究
summary: Volta Metals (CSE: VLTA) 已将其位于安大略省的 Springer 矿床的指示稀土资源量增加了一倍多，随着 2027 年经济评估的进展，该项目按测量和指示资源吨位跻身北美五个最大的项目之列。更新后的矿产资源估算将指示资源量增加了 116%，达到 1.224 亿吨，总稀土氧化物 (TREO) 品位为 0.59%。另外 1.975 亿吨品位 0.53% TREO 被归类为推断。独立准备的估算还包括该项目的第一次镓资源评估。 “我们相信
content:
Volta Metals (CSE: VLTA) 已将其位于安大略省的 Springer 矿床的指示稀土资源量增加了一倍多，随着 2027 年经济评估的进展，该项目按测量和指示资源吨位跻身北美五个最大的项目之列。更新后的矿产资源估算将指示资源量增加了 116%，达到 1.224 亿吨，总稀土氧化物 (TREO) 品位为 0.59%。另外 1.975 亿吨品位 0.53% TREO 被归类为推断。独立准备的估算还包括该项目的第一次镓资源评估。 Volta 总裁兼首席执行官凯雷姆·乌斯梅兹 (Kerem Usenmez) 在一份声明中表示：“我们相信，在市场为中国以外的供应支付溢价之际，斯普林格正在成为北美少数几个大型、可通过公路获取的磁铁稀土和潜在镓来源之一。”萨德伯里首席执行官表示，萨德伯里在“披萨外卖区”举办了大型稀土项目，此次扩张正值西方政府寻求减少对中国的依赖，中国在全球稀土加工和镓生产中占据主导地位。这两种商品都具有重要的战略意义，稀土用于电动汽车和风力涡轮机的永磁体，而镓对于某些半导体技术至关重要。
高品位扩张 Springer 表示，高品位核心产量增长了 140%，达到 2,760 万吨，TREO 品位为 1%，预计金属净收入为每吨 384 加元（272 美元），相当于原地金属总价值 106 亿加元（75 亿美元）。推断的高品位核心产量增加了九倍，达到 2,670 万吨，TREO 品位为 0.94%，估计金属净收入为每吨 333 加元（236 美元），或原地总价值 89 亿加元（63 亿美元）。该区域仍然开放以进行扩张。该矿床在其指示资源范围内还含有估计 4,427 吨原位镓，其中包括 1,480 万吨的高品位区域，平均每吨 56 克。镓可以提供额外的收入来源，尽管 Volta 尚未确定这种金属是否可以经济地回收。该公司正在进行冶金研究，以评估回收方法和潜在的商业可行性。磁铁稀土（钕、镨、镝和铽）约占指定资源稀土氧化物总含量的 22.4%，Volta 表示这一比例是北美最高的之一。北美稀土项目按测量和指示吨位排名，包括报告的储量。推断吨位单独显示以供上下文参考，不用于排名。 （标普全球市场情报数据库，2025 年 5 月；施普林格于 2026 年 9 月 30 日 MRE。
根据该公司引用的标准普尔全球市场情报数据，按实测和指示资源吨位计算，施普林格在北美稀土项目中排名第五。不过，该排名衡量的是资源规模而不是经济潜力，也没有考虑品位、冶金、开发成本或项目成熟度的差异。发展前景 Springer 位于萨德伯里以东约 70 公里处，受益于直接的高速公路、现场电力以及附近的天然气和铁路基础设施。该矿床的低剥采率也可以支持未来的矿山开发，尽管该项目的经济性尚未经过测试。 Volta 计划进行额外钻探以扩大和提炼资源，同时推进稀土冶金工作

【原文 English Original】
Volta Metals (CSE: VLTA) has more than doubled the indicated rare earth resource at its Springer deposit in Ontario, placing the project among North America’s five largest by measured and indicated resource tonnage as it advances toward an economic assessment in 2027. The updated mineral resource estimate increased indicated resources by 116% to 122.4 million tonnes grading 0.59% total rare earth oxides (TREO). A further 197.5 million tonnes grading 0.53% TREO are classified as inferred. The independently prepared estimate also includes the project’s first gallium resource assessment. “We believe Springer is shaping up as one of the few large, road-accessible sources of magnet rare earths, and potentially gallium, in North America, at a time when the market is paying a premium for supply from outside China,” Volta president and CEO Kerem Usenmez said in a statement. Sudbury hosts major rare earth project ‘in a pizza delivery zone,’ CEO says The expansion comes as Western governments seek to reduce their dependence on China, which dominates global rare earth processing and gallium production. Both commodities are strategically important, with rare earths used in permanent magnets for electric vehicles and wind turbines, while gallium is essential to certain semiconductor technologies. High-grade expansion Springer’s indicated high-grade core grew 140% to 27.6 million tonnes grading 1% TREO, with an estimated net metal revenue of C$384 ($272) per tonne, equivalent to C$10.6 billion ($7.5 billion) in gross in-situ metal value. The inferred high-grade core increased ninefold to 26.7 million tonnes grading 0.94% TREO, with an estimated net metal revenue of C$333 per tonne ($236), or C$8.9 billion ($6.3 billion) in gross in-situ value. The zone remains open for expansion. The deposit also contains an estimated 4,427 tonnes of in-situ gallium within its indicated resource, including a higher-grade zone of 14.8 million tonnes averaging 56 grams per tonne. Gallium could provide an additional revenue stream, although Volta has yet to establish whether the metal can be economically recovered. The company is conducting metallurgical studies to assess recovery methods and potential commercial viability. Magnet rare earths — neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium — account for about 22.4% of the indicated resource’s total rare earth oxide content, a proportion Volta says is among the highest in North America. North American rare earth projects ranked by Measured and Indicated tonnage, including Reserves where reported. Inferred tonnage is shown separately for context and is not used in the ranking. ( S&P Global Market Intelligence database, May 2025; Springer at the September 30, 2026 MRE. ) Springer ranks fifth among North American rare earth projects by combined measured and indicated resource tonnage, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data cited by the company. However, the ranking measures resource size rather than economic potential and does not account for differences in grade, metallurgy, development costs or project maturity. Development outlook Located about 70 km east of Sudbury, Springer benefits from direct highway access, on-site power and nearby natural gas and rail infrastructure. The deposit’s low strip ratio could also support future mine development, although the project’s economics remain untested. Volta plans additional drilling to expand and refine the resource while advancing metallurgical work on rare earth and gallium recovery. The company is targeting a preliminary economic assessment (PEA) in the first half of 2027, which would provide an initial evaluation of potential mining costs, processing requirements and project economics.

【原文 English Original】
New imagery circulating on social media has revealed a second new naval auxiliary vessel for PLAN. Observers speculate the design serves as a Chinese UUV mothership, capable of supporting very large drones through onboard equipment. Naval News provides a brief outline on what the pictures in question add to our existing knowledge of this intriguing development for the Chinese Navy. The photos in question are stills taken from two very short video reels shared originally on Chinese social media, specifically Weibo. The new pictures quickly spread onto other sites and forums, including “X”, formerly Twitter. The authenticity of these reels remains to be confirmed. Checks with multiple AI detection tools suggest the material is genuine, although superficial “enhancements” cannot be ruled out. The footage shows several tugboats towing the new auxiliary vessel. The ship carries extensive scaffolding and is still missing all sensor and communication equipment. The location is the Pearl River in Guangzhou, specifically a section near the Panyu district, as the distinct GAC HQ for research and development, known as GAEI headquarters, is visible in the background. One plausible origin of this new vessel is the COMEC shipyard associated with Huangpu Wenchong, on Longxue Island further downstream. However, both the identity of the builder and the destination for further fitting-out work need to await additional imagery for confirmation. At least two other yards belonging to Huangpu further up-river are plausible candidates to finish the fitting-out work. One of these is Huangpu’s primary yard for a wide range of naval vessels, including frigates, surveillance vessels, the Zubr-class LCAC designated as the Type 728 in China, and a recently revealed trimaran submersible . View from the stern, with the amphibious payload bay clearly visible. Six masts possibly serve as a lifting mechanism for a cradle to launch and retrieve underwater vehicles below the hull. Image via Sinodefenceforum, originally Chinese social media. Naval News previously reported on a new type of presumed Chinese UUV mothership under construction at Hudong, Shanghai. That ship, with a length slightly exceeding 200 metres , features twelve distinct lifting masts at the stern. The assumed purpose of this mechanism is to vertically move a cradle integrated into the ships’s welldeck-like stern. Notional dimensions of this cradle as observed at the yard in Shanghai would enable the device to carry large payloads with a length of up to 50 metres for launch and recovery at sea. Satellite imagery suggests that China is evaluating at least two very large UUV designs between 35 and 45 metres. Such a size renders these vessels the largest known military UUVs in the world. Similar role but different design for the two suspected motherships The new ship now seen in Guangzhou does differ from the unit in Shanghai in several points. The hull appears shorter and narrower, producing an overall smaller vessel. Initial observation suggests a length closer to 150 metres. The jack-up masts at the stern are of a different configuration. Instead of twelve masts, two abreast, at different height like on the Shanghai-built ship the Guangzhou unit only features six extended masts of similar height in a similar two abreast-layout. Both ships share a raised forward deckhouse accommodating the bridge at the front and a large opening leading into a hangar-like area at the rear. The first design, then still under construction at Hudong on Changxing Island in Shanghai. This vessel appears to be notably larger than the unit in Guangzhou, and includes several design differences. Image via Chinese social media. Propulsion mirrors the Shanghai-unit, with side by side smokestacks for diesel engines at the rear of the forward deckhouse. The appearance of the engine exhausts shows minor differences between both vessels, likely owing to differences in total installed power. The Guangzhou-built design includes a relatively conventional hull with an inward cant on the upper hull limited to the deckhouse. Meanwhile the vessel in Shanghai shows a distinctly inwards angled upper hull beginning near the bow and extending over the entire length of the ship. Both ships feature an opening similar to a well deck gate at the stern. Guangzhou shipyard busy supplying a wide range of support vessels to PLAN The suspected shipyard for the second Chinese UUV mothership is COMEC, formerly known as GSI. The yard has engaged in significant activity building a range of auxiliary vessels for the Chinese Navy over the last few years. Most notable among these are two sets of amphibious barges the yard assembled since around 2024. Observers associate these designs with a support role for a notional amphibious invasion of Taiwan. COMEC also continues to build fleet replenishment ships for PLAN, including a second batch of Type 903A AOR. Most recently the yard launched the first hull of a new design of supply vessel. This AOR is similar to but larger than the two Type 901 fleet replenishment ships supporting Chinese carriers. A second hull of this type with a displacement of around 65,000 tons now appears to be under construction at the yard as well. Other recent projects include two new types of submarine support vessels, an experimental carrier-like flattop hull apparently intended for evaluation of UAVs and the third unit of the Type 920 hospital ship, commissioned in 2025. The purpose of this new auxiliary is likely going to leave room for speculation for a considerable time. The Chinese military is rarely in the habit of sharing significant amounts of information on new construction projects. This is particularly the case for more dedicated or unusual roles. Further assessment needs to await more detailed imagery in order to clarify the intended purpose of these bespoke vessels with the Chinese Navy. title: AIT Director Raymond Greene’s Remarks at the Joint Press Conference of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau and the Taiwan Coast Guard
zh_title: AIT局长雷蒙·格林在司法部调查局与海巡署联合记者会上的发言
summary: AIT 局长雷蒙德·格林 (Raymond Greene) 在司法部调查局与台湾海巡署联合新闻发布会上的讲话 OT-2613 2026 年 10 月 17 日 AIT 局长雷蒙德·格林 (Raymond Greene) 在司法部调查局与台湾海巡署联合新闻发布会上的讲话 2026 年 10 月 17 日（准备中） 赵总理、陈局长和海洋事务委员会部长，早上好！很荣幸再次与大家一起庆祝美台执法合作的又一项重大成就。今天，我们齐聚一堂，共同认识精津
content:
AIT 局长雷蒙德·格林 (Raymond Greene) 在司法部调查局与台湾海岸警卫队联合新闻发布会上的讲话 OT-2613 2026 年 10 月 17 日 AIT 局长雷蒙德·格林 (Raymond Greene) 在司法部调查局与台湾海岸警卫队联合新闻发布会上的讲话 2026 年 10 月 17 日（已准备） 赵总理、陈局长和海洋事务委员会部长，早上好！很荣幸再次与大家一起庆祝美台执法合作的又一项重大成就。今天，我们齐聚一堂，确认在台湾周边海域查获1,577公斤氯胺酮。如果没有司法部调查局和台湾海岸警卫队管理局的专业精神、技能和合作伙伴的努力，这一行动是不可能实现的。 AIT与台湾人民一起对MJIB和台湾海岸警卫队与DEA密切合作，完成此次调查和扣押的辛勤工作表示感谢。美国和台湾一次又一次地表明，我们在执法方面的伙伴关系确实发挥了作用——使我们的社会更加安全。但我们并不是这种出色的执法伙伴关系的唯一受益者；国际社会也是如此。近年来，我们捣毁了一个总部位于台北的跨国诈骗集团，涉及700多个诈骗网站。
我们共同揭露了一起价值超过1亿美元的重大欺诈和洗钱案件，受害者大多是老年人。我们甚至在印太地区树立了重要的执法先例，支持台湾在出口压片机上加盖序列号的要求，加强防止毒贩获取设备的措施。台湾还拥有丰富的知识、技能和资源，可以帮助国际社会的伙伴确保该地区和全球免受威胁和危机。因此，美国将继续支持台湾寻求有意义的国际参与。包括台湾在内可以加强全球合作，确保所有有能力和负责任的伙伴都能为解决世界上最紧迫的挑战做出贡献，包括打击跨国犯罪。我想再次对 MJIB 和 TCGA 的同事表示诚挚的谢意，感谢你们的专业精神和合作伙伴关系。我们很自豪能与你们站在一起，为我们的社区和家庭创造台湾、美国和印度太平洋地区的安全。 《美国在台协会》首发美国在台协会时任处长雷蒙德·格林在司法部调查局与海巡署联合记者会上的讲话。

【原文 English Original】
AIT Director Raymond Greene’s Remarks at the Joint Press Conference of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau and the Taiwan Coast Guard OT-2613 October 17, 2026   AIT Director Raymond Greene’s Remarks at the Joint Press Conference of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau and the Taiwan Coast Guard October 17, 2026 (As Prepared ) Premier Cho, Director General Chen, and Ocean Affairs Council Minister Kuan, good morning! It is an honor to join you once again to celebrate yet another major achievement in U.S.-Taiwan law enforcement collaboration.   Today, we gather to recognize the seizure of 1,577 kilograms of ketamine from the coastal waters around Taiwan.   This action would not have been possible without the professionalism, skill, and collaborative effort of our partners at the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau and the Taiwan Coast Guard Administration.   AIT joins the Taiwan people in expressing our gratitude for the hard work by MJIB and the Taiwan Coast Guard, in close cooperation with the DEA, to complete this investigation and seizure.   Time and again, the United States and Taiwan have shown that our partnership in law enforcement delivers – making our societies safer and more secure. But we’re not the only beneficiaries of this excellent law enforcement partnership; the international community does as well.   In recent years, we’ve dismantled a Taipei-based transnational fraud syndicate involving more than 700 fraudulent websites.   We’ve jointly exposed a major fraud and money laundering case exceeding $100 million, with victims mostly being elderly individuals. We’re even setting vital law enforcement precedents in the Indo-Pacific, supporting Taiwan’s requirement for serial numbers to be stamped on exported tablet press machines, strengthening measures against preventing narco-traffickers from accessing equipment.   Taiwan also has extensive knowledge, skills, and resources that help partners in the international community ensure that the region and the globe remain free from threats and crises. So, the United States will continue to stand by Taiwan in its pursuit of meaningful international participation. Including Taiwan enhances global cooperation, ensuring that all capable and responsible partners can contribute to solving the world’s most pressing challenges, including countering transnational crime.   I want to once again express my sincere gratitude to our colleagues at MJIB and TCGA for your professionalism and partnership. We are proud to stand with you to make Taiwan, America, and the Indo-Pacific safe for our communities and our families. The post AIT Director Raymond Greene’s Remarks at the Joint Press Conference of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau and the Taiwan Coast Guard appeared first on American Institute in Taiwan .

content: 韩连潮  X  @lianchaohan  ·  17h 【神圣的拥枪权】我属于把美国宪法规定的拥枪权视为最为神圣的个人权利之一的人。 世界上没有一部宪法像美国宪法这样规定这项“人民的权利”，并由美国最高法院在释宪判决中明确加以肯定。极少数国家宪法中虽规定可以拥枪，但又限制在住家和自卫时才能使用。只有美国宪法将人民拥枪权和反对极权暴政挂钩，这就是 美国250年来形成的独有国魂 ，我为此深感自豪。 但是，公权力的本性决定它总会找借口一点点侵蚀个人权利，对拥枪权更是如此。他们表面上说并不禁枪、只控枪，实际上就是在温水煮青蛙，等发现时，你已经失去了这项权利。 美国的控枪举措主要是在民主党执政期间进行的。从上世纪20年代30年代开始，先通过税收和商业条款对枪支进行全国性限制，后又规定禁止购枪的特定类别人口、禁止自动武器以及把半自动改为自动、启动购枪全国即时犯罪背景调查系统、禁止所谓“攻击性武器”（如AR-15步枪）和大容量弹匣、实行登记注册制度、允许法院暂时没收被认为对自己或他人具有危险性的人的枪支等等。各州的限制更是名目繁多，让人无所适从。比如我在弗吉尼亚买枪并不需要注册，搬到马里兰后不注册就成了非法。最近，马里兰州出台了一项针对格洛克（Glock）及类似手枪的出售禁令，定于2027年1月1日正式生效。这种变相剥夺宪法规定拥枪权的做法只会越来越多。 有人把所谓中国历朝都承认人民拥有武器和美国宪法规定的拥枪权进行类比，这是完全错误的。禁兵禁武一直是中国历朝历代维护皇权和极权统治的重要手段。为了巩固皇权、防止民间起义和反抗，历代统治者几乎都对民间武器实行了严格的管制甚至全面的禁绝。这种政策被称为“禁武令”或“收天下兵”。 党国：让我们从当下说起。中共党国对枪支管制之严厉前所未有。记得有人买玩具手枪被判刑的事吧？新疆模式的刀具购买实名化、上锁安铁链，似已在全国推行。所以袁腾飞能够在自由世界买枪玩枪显摆一下也无可厚非。 清朝：为防汉人造反，禁兵禁武长达数百年。它作为外族侵入中原的政权，满洲贵族对汉族社会的反抗极其敏感，其武器禁令贯穿整个朝代。其中包括严禁民间私造、私藏火器弩弓，甚至多次颁布严旨，禁止汉人教拳习武。因为山高皇帝远，边远民间非法拥有火器存在，但这和美国宪法规定的拥枪有着本质的不同。 历代的情况大同小异，从秦朝收缴天下兵器、铸“十二金人”，到宋代禁读兵书兵法，不一而足。 算了，我不想浪费时间写下去了。人一旦有了身份和意识形态立场认同，先入为主，很难用事实和道理去说服他们。希望搞清问题的推友自己去查吧。

[https://www.eventbrite.com/e/the-september-2026-jobs-reportinflation-updates-tickets-1994107871323?aff=ideatoipo](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/the-september-2026-jobs-reportinflation-updates-tickets-1994107871323?aff=ideatoipo)
 The US economy is constantly evolving, influenced by employment numbers, the rise and fall of inflation, foreign policy, domestic economic agendas, and movement of citizens between different regions. As a job seeker, all of these effects working in tandem can impact the inner workings of a job search.

Join Colin Mo of Albert's List and Dr. Reilly White, Professor of Finance at the University of New Mexico for a monthly webinar where they'll discuss how these factors are impacting your career, particularly for those who work in tech and reside in the San Francisco Bay Area. You'll learn about:

*   The most recent month's jobs report, including its biggest takeaways, silver linings, and potential warning signs.
*   The most recent month's CPI report and how the rising cost of goods and money are impacting the flow of investments or consumer spending.
*   What to expect in the weeks and months ahead as economic conditions evolve.
*   How the economic numbers are impacting those in the San Francisco Bay Area and the technology industry!
*   How Trump's recent policies are affecting the job market and economy.
*   Other notable trends moving the market, including bonds, housing prices, quit rates, and more!
*   And much more!

Join us with your questions, comments, and concerns.

ABOUT DR. REILLY S. WHITE, PhD
 Dr. White is the Associate Dean of Teaching and Learning and an Associate Professor of Finance with tenure at the University of New Mexico. Dr. White also serves on the board of the CFA Society of New Mexico, advisor for the $4.7 Million student-run UNM Regent’s Portfolio, and leads a series of financial literacy projects in the community. Prior to his career in academia, Dr. White worked as an analyst for a large Boston-based bank, where he learned a great deal about company analysis, funding, and maintaining ethical corporate leadership. He has consulted with investment managers and municipalities on maintaining optimal portfolio strategies, particularly in response to economic challenges. Dr. White was also awarded the 2022 Paul Bartlett Ré Emerging Promotor of Peace Award and serves on the of board Voz Collegiate Preparatory School.

In addition to his PhD from the University of Connecticut, Dr. White graduated summa cum laude from the University of Massachusetts-Dartmouth with a degree in Finance. Dr. White has published nineteen articles in finance and financial technology in the last few years, including articles in Physica A, Journal of Corporate Finance, IEEE, Technological Forecasting and Social Change, and the Journal of Banking and Finance. With his students, he co-authored Financial Literacy for Immigrants and Refugees, a free financial literacy handbook that has been translated into Spanish, Arabic, and Dari. Since 2020, Dr. White has been interviewed over 150 times by local and national media outlets on various economic and finance topics.

Visit his website at [https://www.reillywhite.com/](https://www.reillywhite.com/).

title: Ancient love poems show romance timeless across millennia
zh_title: 古老的爱情诗展现了跨越千年的永恒浪漫
summary: 香港大学的一位学者强调，古代美索不达米亚和埃及的爱情诗揭示了从神圣的仪式到世俗的崇拜，浪漫的渴望在 4000 多年来一直没有改变。 [![图片 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk) 作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编 2026 年 10 月 15 日 00:05 HKT · 2 分钟阅读 远在现代之前浪漫，在古代近东，人心剧烈跳动。穿越美索不达米亚肥沃的平原和埃及阳光普照的沙滩
content:
香港
香港大学的一位学者强调，古代美索不达米亚和埃及的爱情诗揭示了从神圣的仪式到世俗的崇拜，浪漫的渴望在 4000 多年来一直没有改变。

[![图片1：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

作者：[Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)，主编

2026 年 10 月 15 日 00:05 香港时间 · 阅读时间 2 分钟

早在现代浪漫之前，古代近东的人们的心跳就剧烈。香港大学阿拉伯语项目主任阿姆贾德·雷法伊 (Amjad Refai) 表示，穿过美索不达米亚肥沃的平原和埃及阳光普照的沙滩，早期文明将他们最深切的渴望刻在粘土和纸莎草上，证明爱是一种永恒的、通用的语言。

在古代美索不达米亚，浪漫的渴望与神圣的传统交织在一起。几个世纪以来，圣经中的《所罗门之歌》被认为是历史上最古老的情诗，直到考古学家发现了写于公元前 2000 年左右的《舒辛情歌》。拉法伊于 2026 年 10 月 15 日在《标准》专栏中写道，虽然最初是由一位女祭司在神圣的生育仪式上背诵的，以确保土地的繁荣，但这块泥板却揭示了女性原始、热情和世俗的奉献。
这首诗是一位被国王迷住的新娘深深的个人忏悔：“新郎，让我爱抚你，我珍贵的爱抚比蜂蜜更美味，在充满蜂蜜的卧室里，让我享受你的美丽，狮子，让我爱抚你，我珍贵的爱抚比蜂蜜更美味。”

几个世纪后，大约公元前 1300 年，古埃及人捕捉到了一种不同但同样迷人的浪漫色彩。新王国的世俗诗歌读起来就像艺术家欣赏杰作，呼应了法老拉美西斯二世对其心爱的王后奈菲尔塔丽的传奇般的热爱。在这些现存的诗歌中，情人怀着幻想般的钦佩崇敬着心上人独特的美丽，将她比作最稀有的宝石和太阳：“最美丽的！”像晨星一样升起，在快乐的一年开始时，闪闪发亮，皮肤白皙，她的眼睛可爱，她的嘴唇甜美，她没有说太多的话。

雷法伊写道，这些文本并排放置，编织出一幅人类情感的挂毯。美索不达米亚歌曲充满了肉体渴望的颤抖温暖，而埃及诗歌则呈现出对灵魂伴侣深深浪漫的崇拜。数千年来，他们共同耳语着一个令人欣慰的真理：帝国衰落，但坠入爱河的惊心动魄的体验却从未改变。

[![图片3：Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

主编
负责 CLB.org.hk 报道和编辑标准的主编。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong
A University of Hong Kong academic highlights how ancient Mesopotamian and Egyptian love poems reveal that romantic longing has remained unchanged for over 4,000 years, from sacred rituals to secular adoration.

[![Image 1: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)

By [Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk), Editor in Chief

15 Oct 2026 at 00:05 HKT · 2 min read

Long before modern romance, the human heart beat fiercely in the ancient Near East. Across the fertile plains of Mesopotamia and the sun-drenched sands of Egypt, early civilizations etched their deepest desires onto clay and papyrus, proving that love is a timeless, universal language, according to Amjad Refai, director of the Arabic Programme at the University of Hong Kong.

In ancient Mesopotamia, romantic longing was intertwined with sacred traditions. For centuries, the biblical Song of Solomon was considered history’s oldest love poem, until archaeologists discovered the Love Song for Shu-Sin, written around 2000 BCE. Although originally recited by a priestess during sacred fertility rituals to ensure the land’s prosperity, the clay tablet reveals a woman’s raw, passionate, and earthly devotion, Refai wrote in a column for _The Standard_ on 15 October 2026.

The poem is a deeply personal confession of a bride captivated by her king: 'Bridegroom, let me caress you, My precious caress is more savory than honey, In the bedchamber, honey-filled, Let me enjoy your goodly beauty, Lion, let me caress you, My precious caress is more savory than honey.'

Centuries later, around 1300 BCE, the ancient Egyptians captured a different, yet equally enchanting, shade of romance. Echoing the legendary devotion Pharaoh Ramses II held for his beloved Queen Nefertari, secular poetry from the New Kingdom reads like an artist admiring a masterpiece. In these surviving poems, the lover reveres his sweetheart's unique beauty with starry-eyed admiration, comparing her to the rarest precious gems and the sun: 'Most beautiful of all! Rising like the morning star, At the start of happy year, Shining bright, fair of skin, Lovely the look of her eyes, Sweet the speech of her lips, She has not a word too much.'

Placed side by side, these texts weave a tapestry of human emotion, Refai wrote. While the Mesopotamian song pulses with the trembling warmth of physical longing, the Egyptian poem presents a deeply romantic adoration of a soulmate. Together, they whisper a comforting truth across millennia: empires fall, but the breathtaking experience of falling in love remains unchanged.

[![Image 3: Adam](https://clb.org.hk/en/static/img/editors/clb-adam-192.png)](https://clb.org.hk/en/desks/clb-desk)
